# Bootwright code audit against its specifications

Revision 1, dated 2026-11-05. Repository: `bootwright` at commit `f8b15669f`
on `main`, clean tree. Requested by the repository owner. Orchestrated and
written by Claude Fable 5.1 with Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and
Claude Haiku 5.5 agents, each sub-task routed to the model its difficulty
needs ([method](#7-method-and-verification-record)). Scope: the Go code under
`api/v1alpha1`, `internal/` and `cmd/bootwright`, the Ansible collection
under `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core`, the fitness
suite under `test/architecture` and the cases under `e2e/`, each judged
against the specification page or section that owns it. Out of scope: the
specifications' own consistency (audit 001 covers it), the add-on design
(audit 002), operator documentation under `docs/`, live runs, and any command
with effects. This file and its navigation page are the only repository
changes the audit makes; it changes no product code, contract, milestone
state or specification, and authorizes no implementation.

## How to read this report

The report is long because the owner asked for a full audit and for verified
findings rather than impressions. Each reader can stop early.

| If you want | Read |
| --- | --- |
| The verdict and what to fix first | [Section 1](#1-executive-assessment), then [section 4](#4-ordered-remediation-roadmap) |
| Every High and Medium finding in one table | [Section 2](#2-findings-by-severity) |
| The patterns behind the findings, with the one structural remedy for each | [Section 3](#3-cross-cutting-themes) |
| How each domain holds up, bounded by what was examined | [Section 5](#5-domain-assessments) |
| The full record of one lane: assessment, entries, tracked items, coverage ledger, limits, refuted candidates | [Section 6](#6-lane-reports) |
| How the findings were produced and verified, the models each sub-task ran on, the gates, and the limits of the method | [Section 7](#7-method-and-verification-record) |
| Every entry, including Low and tracked ones, in one table | [Section 8](#8-complete-catalog) |

Finding identifiers carry a three-letter lane code and a number (`CPR-01`
is the first finding of the Ceph ingress and removal lane); the lane table in
section 7 maps codes to lanes. Severity is Blocking, High, Medium or Low on
the scale section 7 defines, and every entry carries a kind: defect, gap,
drift, unsafe, test-gap, doc-stale or improvement. Every entry survived
three independent verifications, or an arbitration where they split, and
cites the file and lines it rests on at the audited commit.

## 1. Executive assessment

Bootwright's code does what its specifications say on the paths that
matter most. Every lane found the destructive refusals (disk ownership,
removal ordering, controller-host protection, physical erase, uninstall) and
the secret-handling rules (keyring format, custody, stdin reads, masking)
enforced before the effect they guard, and the state machine, the frozen
request bounds, the refusal tables and the architecture fitness suite are
held by tests that read the spec's own tables. No finding is Blocking. The
discrepancies cluster where one rule has more than one copy, where admission
and the later stages disagree about a valid document, where an adapter folds
different answers into one outcome, and where a delivered decision moved the
code and left the owning spec behind.

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Lanes, spec pages and lines | 36 lanes over 33 pages, 29,734 lines |
| Clauses registered | 12,925 |
| Candidate findings proposed | 354 |
| Confirmed after three-lens verification | 313: 0 Blocking, 3 High, 64 Medium, 246 Low |
| By kind | 146 defects, 64 doc-stale, 52 drift, 29 test gaps, 10 gaps, 7 unsafe, 5 improvements |
| Confirmed but already recorded as open work | 3 (B248, B412, B99) |
| Duplicates merged across lanes | 9 pairs |
| Refuted by the verifiers | 29 |
| Splits decided by an arbiter | 41 |
| Headline findings re-verified independently | 10 of 10 held; 1 raised to Medium, 1 reclassified from unsafe to drift |

**What to fix first.** Six items stand above the rest, in this order.

1. [CLI-01](#cli-01) (High, unsafe): `render` is classified privileged, so a
   non-root invocation re-executes as root and the publisher creates
   directories and writes `effective-state.yaml` with root's credentials at
   whatever path the operator names, while `--sensitive` checks that the
   directory is owned by root instead of by the invoking account. Under sudo
   the operator's own private directory is refused and a directory render
   creates is unreadable to them. Every other operator-named path in an
   elevated process goes through the invoking-account opener; this one does
   not.
2. [MOI-04](#moi-04) (Medium, unsafe): the installer's private host key pair
   and the LUKS recovery passphrase are copied into the served private
   directory at a umask-derived mode before `chmod 0640` and the SELinux
   label are applied. A probe against the pinned ansible-core read the
   passphrase during that window in 20 of 20 runs, and the directory token is
   visible in an earlier `mv` argument vector, so a local account on the
   artifact-server host can find the file.
3. [SEC-07](#sec-07) (High, defect): the controller-side SSH policy parser
   refuses the `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` line every FIPS crypto-policy back end
   carries, while the tunnel parser, repaired under B1011, admits it. On a
   FIPS controller, an accepted configuration, every Ceph host, cluster and
   SMB block and the physical erase refuse before contacting a host, and the
   only workaround weakens FIPS.
4. [SEC-01](#sec-01), [PRJ-03](#prj-03), [RCP-11](#rcp-11),
   [SCR-05](#scr-05) (Medium and Low): the remaining ambient-trust paths.
   Three root-run exec sites skip the root-ownership qualification that
   sudo, rpm and dnf get; the adapter's ansible-core still searches the
   system-wide plugin directories the distribution package creates; two
   adapters write scratch outside the root-only child; and a sudo option list
   that does not parse is read as naming no input logging.
5. [RCS-02](#rcs-02) (Medium, unsafe): an agent-installed bare-metal node may
   select its root disk by a kernel name such as `/dev/sda`, against the
   physical disk safety rule, and cannot use the durable by-id form at all.
   The repository's own physical fixture declares `/dev/sda` on three nodes.
   This must land before the bare-metal agent path is qualified.
6. [ADD-01](#add-01) (High, defect): on the exact install policy that five of
   the six built-in packages use, a pending upgrade InstallPlan, the normal
   state once the pinned CSV falls behind the catalog head, makes a healthy
   instance read unknown with a destroy remedy and makes a continued apply
   refuse. It fails safe, which is why it follows the exposure fixes.

**What is sound.** The counterevidence matters as much as the findings. Ceph's
partial-OSD clear records intent before it zaps and re-proves the disk
afterwards; uninstall resolves with `openat2` and `RESOLVE_BENEATH` and
package removal fails closed; the keyring v4 format has golden, fuzz and
tamper suites; the physical firmware step and the libvirt host apply are the
best-defended code the lanes read; the RAM erase worker binds every chunk to
the disk identity; `diff` is read-only by construction; the CLI's command
and flag catalog, parsing bounds, JSON envelope and diagnostic order match
the spec and are pinned by goldens; and every test the security spec names
exists. The prior add-ons audit's remediation is in place.

**What the findings mostly are.** 246 of 313 are Low: a refusal with the
wrong name, a remedy that names no exit, output that bypasses the shared
renderer, a Not yet met line whose item is delivered, a version number copied
into prose. They cost operators time and mislead readers of the specs; they
do not damage anything. The 64 Medium findings are where validated input
fails late with a generic refusal, where a safety rule is enforced but has no
test, where a resumed operation misreads its own earlier effect, and where an
adapter classifies an answer wrongly. [Section 3](#3-cross-cutting-themes)
names the ten patterns behind them and the one structural remedy for each;
[section 4](#4-ordered-remediation-roadmap) orders the work.

**What this audit does not claim.** It is a source and test assessment with
effect-free probes; no host or cluster was reached and no live run was made,
so every clause that only a live run can prove is marked unverifiable in the
lane ledgers rather than passed. Coverage is bounded by those ledgers: each
lane states what it examined and what it left. Verification defaults to
omission, so the catalog understates rather than overstates, and the final
severity of a split verdict is the lowest a real-voting verifier gave unless
an arbiter decided it. Every citation was checked against the baseline by a
separate pass that repaired 219 line references and left 8 sentences for the
author to correct by hand.

## 3. Cross-cutting themes

Ten patterns account for most of the catalog. Each names the findings that
instantiate it and the one structural change that would close the pattern
rather than each instance. The lists are representative, not exhaustive;
section 8 holds every entry.

### 3.1 Privileged work is not confined to the invoking account or to root-owned inputs

[CLI-01](#cli-01), [CLI-02](#cli-02), [CLI-03](#cli-03), [CLI-04](#cli-04),
[SEC-01](#sec-01), [PRJ-03](#prj-03), [MOI-04](#moi-04), [RCP-11](#rcp-11),
[SCR-05](#scr-05).

The privilege model holds on the paths the security lane read, and several
elevated paths leave it. `render` publishes to operator-named paths as root
with its ownership check held to root. Bare `render` and
`preflight container-cluster` with `--ssh-*` flags elevate before a help or
usage outcome, and the sudo-entry environment guard runs ahead of the
no-effect contracts of help, version and completion. Root-run exec sites for
`getent`, `firewall-cmd` and the SSH client skip the root-ownership
qualifier that sudo, rpm and dnf get. Adapter ansible-core still searches the
system-wide plugin directories. Private installer files are published at a
umask-derived mode before their final mode. Two adapters write scratch
outside the root-only child. A sudo option list that does not parse is read
as naming no input logging. Each instance is narrow; together they show a
boundary enforced call site by call site rather than by construction.

Remedy: derive the root requirement from each command's declared effects
after parsing and help resolution; route every operator-named path in an
elevated process through the invoking-account opener; run every root exec
through one qualified-executable helper with a fixed working directory; pin
every Ansible plugin path to the bundle; publish every private file by
write-then-rename at its final mode; and add an architecture test that fails
when an elevated package opens a path or execs a binary outside those
helpers.

### 3.2 One rule, several disagreeing copies

[SEC-07](#sec-07), [SEC-01](#sec-01), [RCS-01](#rcs-01), [SBP-02](#sbp-02),
[SBP-09](#sbp-09), [CPR-04](#cpr-04), [CRA-01](#cra-01), [CRA-02](#cra-02),
[CRA-06](#cra-06), [CRA-10](#cra-10), [OCN-01](#ocn-01), [RCD-07](#rcd-07),
[RCD-01](#rcd-01), [RCD-05](#rcd-05).

Where a predicate is implemented more than once, the copies drift. Three SSH
crypto-policy parsers disagree on the `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` line every FIPS
back end carries, and only the tunnel parser was repaired. The physical
MAC-set proof shared by the RAM erase worker and the Ceph host runtime omits
the management-controller host-interface exception the kickstart applies. The
controller-host power guard reads live sysfs addresses while the installer
reads permanent ones. Go preflight and the worker select IPv6 interfaces
differently. The cluster default replica pair reaches planning by three
routes. `diff` re-implements the scheduler's throttle and the runner's
lent-material screen and covers less. Taint comparison in `diff` does not
normalize the way placement does.

Remedy: give each predicate one owning module (SSH policy reduction, the
physical MAC set, durable disk identity, the cluster default replica pair,
the lent-material set, the admission throttle), make every consumer import
it, and where Go and Python must both hold it, drive both from one shared
test corpus as the ingress firewall rules already are.

### 3.3 Admission accepts what planning or the worker then refuses

[CPC-01](#cpc-01), [CEA-08](#cea-08), [CPN-04](#cpn-04), [CPN-02](#cpn-02),
[CRA-02](#cra-02), [CRA-08](#cra-08), [CRB-01](#crb-01), [CRB-02](#crb-02),
[CRB-07](#crb-07), [CPL-06](#cpl-06), [CPC-07](#cpc-07), [MCH-04](#mch-04),
[MCH-08](#mch-08), [CPR-04](#cpr-04), [CLI-03](#cli-03), [ENV-06](#env-06).

`validate`, `plan` and `apply` disagree about what a valid document is, mostly
in Ceph. Admitted `spec.mgrModules` and `singleHostDefaults` refuse at plan
with a generic `lifecycle.unsupported`. An admitted NVMe-oF service with
`enable_auth: true` can never be planned. `count_per_host` and service-name
spellings admission accepts are refused at plan, while decorated host tokens
are silently narrowed. Worker name and list bounds that Go admission no
longer applies refuse only at apply with an opaque request reason, after the
cluster and its prerequisites have run. `addressRef` and a keyless root
cluster SSH key pass the API and refuse at plan. Kernel-name and WWN-only root
devices pass `validate` and fail at plan. Every instance fails before an
effect, so the cost is a late, generic refusal rather than damage, but it is
the class the refusal tables exist to prevent.

Remedy: carry every bound and accepted-value set from one Go declaration into
the frozen request so workers check the same numbers, and add a parity test
that runs every admitted fixture through planning and fails on any
`lifecycle.unsupported` or worker request refusal that has no admission rule
or refusal-table row.

### 3.4 External answers are classified wrongly

[ADD-01](#add-01), [ADD-02](#add-02), [ADD-09](#add-09), [ADD-11](#add-11),
[INF-01](#inf-01), [INF-05](#inf-05), [SBP-11](#sbp-11), [MON-01](#mon-01),
[CTS-01](#cts-01), [OCI-02](#oci-02), [SBV-08](#sbv-08), [CTS-10](#cts-10).

Adapters map a transport failure, a native refusal and a proven mismatch onto
the same outcome. A pending upgrade InstallPlan turns a healthy instance into
unknown and an apply into a refusal. `oc`'s text error is parsed as a JSON
Status, so the webhook-window retry never fires, and a placed Secret's
transient failure fails at once. Readiness classification is inverted at the
managed-service probe: an unanswered listener fails the attempt while a
certificate mismatch is unknown. An unanswered Redfish system read becomes a
hardware mismatch, an unreadable checkpoint listing becomes "the network cut
the controller off", and a certificate failure is told to set `HTTPS_PROXY`.
The libvirt apply proceeds without proving the hypervisor answered. The
result is wrong remedies, including a destroy remedy for a healthy add-on.

Remedy: define one closed answer classification per adapter family (no
answer, transport failure by cause, native refusal, answered and mismatched,
answered and matching), implement it once per language, map each class to
its specified outcome and remedy, and require a unit test per class at each
call site that reads a remote system.

[API-02](#api-02), [OCA-02](#oca-02), [CPC-10](#cpc-10), [CRA-03](#cra-03),
[CPD-07](#cpd-07), [OUT-07](#out-07), [SBP-06](#sbp-06), [ADD-09](#add-09),
[PRJ-01](#prj-01), [PRJ-02](#prj-02), [OCI-01](#oci-01), [OCI-06](#oci-06),
[OCN-02](#ocn-02), [OCN-03](#ocn-03), [MCH-02](#mch-02), [MCH-03](#mch-03),
[CTS-02](#cts-02), [CPN-06](#cpn-06), [CEA-01](#cea-01), [CPR-03](#cpr-03),
[ADD-04](#add-04), [SEC-03](#sec-03), [SEC-05](#sec-05), [ENV-02](#env-02),
[MON-03](#mon-03), [MON-13](#mon-13), [MOI-05](#moi-05), [CTH-08](#cth-08),
[MON-04](#mon-04).

The largest class, 64 doc-stale and 52 drift findings, is spec text a
delivered item or decision made false. The re-judged tracked items show the
mechanism: X263, D199, D183, B514, B719, B1004 and B1122 changed code on
purpose and closed without editing the owning spec. Not yet met lines outlive
their items, and request-format version numbers copied into prose go stale.
None changes behavior, but a reader acting on the owning spec gets the wrong
contract, which is the role the specs claim for themselves.

Remedy: make closing a delivered item require the owning-spec lines it
changed (a docs-check rule that a delivered record cites spec anchors edited
in the same commit), have docs-check refuse a Not yet met line whose item is
delivered, and replace version literals in prose with the Go constant's name
or a generated table.

### 3.6 Refusal tables and fitness tests check one direction only

[OCI-03](#oci-03), [SBV-14](#sbv-14), [CPL-04](#cpl-04), [RCC-02](#rcc-02),
[CPC-03](#cpc-03), [SBV-02](#sbv-02), [ARC-01](#arc-01), [ARC-08](#arc-08),
[ARC-09](#arc-09), [ARC-10](#arc-10), [CPL-03](#cpl-03), [OCN-10](#ocn-10).

The refusal-table guard tests are a real strength, but several check only
that each table row matches the code, not that every refusal the code emits
has a row, or they skip a kind or a table. Architecture fitness checks are
narrower than the clauses they are cited for: field paths, the `requests.go`
convention, ports in domain roots and package-global mutable state. This is
how the plan-time refusals of theme 3.3 escaped notice.

Remedy: make each table guard bidirectional by enumerating the refusal codes
and reasons `Unsupported` can emit and failing on any without a row, extend
the guards to every kind and table the spec says they hold, and widen the
architecture fitness checks to the clause text they back or narrow the
clause.

### 3.7 Enforced safety refusals with no test

[CEA-05](#cea-05), [ENV-05](#env-05), [RCS-05](#rcs-05), [CPR-02](#cpr-02),
[ADD-15](#add-15), [CRB-04](#crb-04), [OCA-03](#oca-03), [OCA-09](#oca-09),
[OCA-11](#oca-11), [OCN-07](#ocn-07), [OCN-08](#ocn-08), [MON-09](#mon-09),
[MOD-01](#mod-01), [MOD-02](#mod-02), [CPL-09](#cpl-09), [RCC-08](#rcc-08),
[CEA-09](#cea-09), [ADA-11](#ada-11).

29 test-gap findings name refusals the code enforces today that nothing
pins: cluster SSH key separation, the RAM image's installer-isolation
refusals (whose only test mocks the isolation), the tiebreaker
`authorized_keys` changed-since-read refusal, the Secret placement type
refusal, the thin-pool and LVM RAID clear refusals, attempt exhaustion before
running is recorded, and boundaries such as 128 against 129 services. The
scale rates an untested safety clause Medium because a refactor can remove it
silently.

Remedy: add a docs-check or Go fitness rule that every named refusal token
and reason in a spec refusal list appears in at least one test that asserts
it, with boundary rows on both sides of every numeric limit.

### 3.8 Interrupted and resumed work loses its own record

[CTH-01](#cth-01), [CTH-02](#cth-02), [CPD-01](#cpd-01), [INF-02](#inf-02),
[CTX-01](#ctx-01), [CTX-02](#ctx-02), [MOI-01](#moi-01), [RCP-01](#rcp-01),
[RCC-05](#rcc-05), [OUT-10](#out-10), [SCR-03](#scr-03).

Paths that resume after an interruption treat their own earlier effects as
foreign or pre-existing. A re-setup or a resumed package install records
Bootwright-installed packages as present before Bootwright, so uninstall
keeps them. A completed DB/WAL allocation is refused `device-not-empty` on
the next apply with a clear-the-disk remedy. An `init` killed mid-way leaves
a name that neither a retry nor `delete --purge` can clear, and an abandoned
publication stage blocks a prompted update and delete. An artifact server can
resolve completed on stale configuration (tracked as B248). A setup run that
cannot be numbered fails the whole install.

Remedy: apply the intent-before-effect rule uniformly: every multi-step
effect records what it is about to create before creating it, a resume
reconciles against that record before any foreign or pre-existing
classification, and each such path gets an interruption test at every step
boundary.

### 3.9 Remedies that do not carry the operator to an exit

[SCR-01](#scr-01), [SCR-04](#scr-04), [RCC-04](#rcc-04), [PRJ-05](#prj-05),
[RCS-04](#rcs-04), [RCS-06](#rcs-06), [CRB-03](#crb-03), [CPN-03](#cpn-03),
[CLJ-03](#clj-03), [CTH-06](#cth-06), [CLI-11](#cli-11), [MCH-05](#mch-05),
[SBV-05](#sbv-05).

Many refusals fire correctly but name no exit, the wrong cause, or a command
that refuses again: corrupt-store refusals without the two required exits, a
literal placeholder where a context name belongs, rebind and `lifecycle.live`
remedies that drop the invocation's flags, consumer prerequisite refusals that
name no prerequisite, and conflicts that name only one side. The spec usually
states the remedy; the code attaches it on one of several paths that raise
the same refusal.

Remedy: build remedies from one template per refusal code that takes the
invocation's flags and the conflicting objects, and test that every path
raising a given code produces the same remedy.

### 3.10 Human output bypasses the shared renderer

[OUT-01](#out-01), [OUT-05](#out-05), [OUT-09](#out-09), [OUT-13](#out-13),
[OUT-02](#out-02), [OUT-15](#out-15).

The JSON envelope and the diagnostic contract match the spec, but several
human writers skip the shared renderer and its width, ASCII, color and
stacking rules, and `apply` and `destroy` blocks always report an empty
outcome with zero attempts.

Remedy: route every human table through the shared renderer with identity and
state metadata, fill the block outcome from the operation record, and add a
golden per command that writes a table.

## 4. Ordered remediation roadmap

The order is the one a principal engineer would follow: exposure and
privilege first, then fail-closed defects that block accepted configurations,
then wrong outcomes on qualified paths, then the spec repairs that mislead
readers, with the two guards that stop the largest classes from growing.
Each step names its findings; the entries in section 6 carry the smallest
change and the exit evidence. A step marked "owner decision" changes a
contract and needs a recorded decision before implementation; this report
authorizes none.

1. **Stop `render` from writing as root.** [CLI-01](#cli-01),
   [CLI-02](#cli-02), [CLI-03](#cli-03), [CLI-04](#cli-04). Classify
   context-free and bare `render` as unprivileged, inject the invoking
   account's UID into the render publisher and resolve and publish through
   the invoking-account opener, and move elevation after the help, usage and
   raw-bound outcomes. First because any non-root render through sudo
   reaches it.
2. **Publish private installer files at their final mode.**
   [MOI-04](#moi-04). Write `identity`, `identity.pub` and `recovery` to the
   work area, set mode, owner and label, then rename into the private
   directory, as the image is already published; add a test that asserts the
   mode before exposure. Second because it is secret exposure, narrower than
   step 1 only because it needs a local shell on the artifact-server host.
3. **Reduce, not refuse, the FIPS SSH back end in the controller parser.**
   [SEC-07](#sec-07). Share one reduction function between the tunnel and
   controller parsers and add FIPS back-end fixtures to both parsers' tests.
   An accepted configuration cannot run Ceph until this lands.
4. **Close the remaining ambient-trust paths.** [SEC-01](#sec-01),
   [PRJ-03](#prj-03), [RCP-11](#rcp-11), [SCR-05](#scr-05). Route `getent`,
   `firewall-cmd` and the SSH client through the root-owned executable
   qualifier with a fixed working directory; pin every ansible-core plugin
   path to the bundle; confine adapter scratch to the root-only child; make
   an unparseable sudo option list refuse `secret.input`.
5. **Require a durable root selector on physical agent nodes.**
   [RCS-02](#rcs-02), [MCH-04](#mch-04), [MCH-08](#mch-08). Owner decision:
   the agent path cannot use a by-id hint, so either require a WWN hint, or a
   serial-number hint with an exact size, for a physical node, or lift the
   by-id refusal; move the kernel-name refusal into Machine admission;
   reconcile `openshift-clusters.md` with the physical disk safety rule. Must
   land before the bare-metal agent path is qualified.
6. **Define the physical MAC set once.** [RCS-01](#rcs-01),
   [SBP-02](#sbp-02), [SBP-09](#sbp-09). Permanent addresses, the
   CDC/RNDIS host-interface exception and bond slaves, used by the RAM erase
   worker, the Ceph host runtime, the controller-host power guard and the
   Redfish target proof, with tests for a CDC interface, a bond and a cloned
   MAC.
7. **Fix the cluster object engine's OLM edges.** [ADD-01](#add-01),
   [ADD-02](#add-02), [ADD-11](#add-11), [ADD-03](#add-03). Accept a pending
   upgrade plan once `installedCSV` is the `startingCSV` (and clarify
   `add-ons.md:334-336` so the plan rule applies only until then); read
   `oc`'s create failure reason from JSON output so the webhook retry fires;
   retry transient Secret placement until the deadline; read
   `maxOpenShiftVersion` from the real annotation.
8. **Make admission, planning and the Ceph workers agree.**
   [CPC-01](#cpc-01), [CEA-08](#cea-08), [CRB-01](#crb-01),
   [CRB-02](#crb-02), [CRB-07](#crb-07), [CPN-04](#cpn-04),
   [CRA-08](#cra-08), [CRA-02](#cra-02), [CPL-06](#cpl-06),
   [CPC-07](#cpc-07). For each input planning or a worker refuses today
   (`mgrModules`, `singleHostDefaults`, NVMe-oF `enable_auth` bindings,
   `count_per_host`, name and list bounds, the replica floor, `addressRef`),
   either realize it or refuse it at admission with a field-named diagnostic
   and a refusal-table row (owner decision per input); carry the bounds into
   the frozen request; add the admitted-fixture-through-plan parity test.
9. **Correct answer classification at the remote reads.**
   [INF-01](#inf-01), [INF-05](#inf-05), [INF-07](#inf-07),
   [INF-08](#inf-08), [SBP-11](#sbp-11), [CTS-01](#cts-01),
   [MON-01](#mon-01). The managed-service readiness probe, the Redfish,
   wheel-fetch and checkpoint reads; make DNS readiness and chrony binds
   cover every declared address family (B412 already records the wildcard
   bind).
10. **Record intent before effect on resumable paths.** [CTH-01](#cth-01),
    [CTH-02](#cth-02), [CPD-01](#cpd-01), [CTX-01](#ctx-01),
    [CTX-02](#ctx-02), [OUT-10](#out-10). Setup package installs, DB/WAL
    allocation and context init record what they are about to create and
    reconcile against it on resume; a setup run that cannot be opened
    discards dnf output instead of failing the install.
11. **Settle the NFS security default and add the missing safety tests.**
    [CEA-10](#cea-10), [CEA-05](#cea-05), [RCS-05](#rcs-05),
    [CPR-02](#cpr-02), [ADD-15](#add-15). Owner decision: `ceph.md:434`
    (sys only) against `ceph-resources.md:988` and `:1001-1002` (no default,
    never added); the shipped NFS examples omit `sectype`. Then pin the
    enforced refusals that have no test, starting with cluster SSH key
    separation, the RAM image isolation and the tiebreaker changed-since-read
    check.
12. **Repair the spec text delivered decisions left stale, and add the two
    guards.** [API-02](#api-02), [OCA-02](#oca-02), [CPC-10](#cpc-10),
    [CRA-03](#cra-03), [CPD-07](#cpd-07), [OUT-07](#out-07),
    [SBP-06](#sbp-06), [ADD-09](#add-09), [OCI-01](#oci-01),
    [PRJ-01](#prj-01), [PRJ-02](#prj-02), [OCI-03](#oci-03),
    [SBV-14](#sbv-14) and the other doc-stale and drift entries of section 8.
    A delivered record must cite the owning-spec lines it changed, and every
    refusal-table guard must be bidirectional. Last because nothing here
    changes behavior, and first among the cheap items because the guards stop
    the largest finding class from growing.

Milestone carriers are the owner's call. The items above map onto the
existing pages: steps 1 to 4 and 7 are M3 and M4 defects on delivered
paths; steps 5, 6 and 11 gate the physical and Ceph acceptance rows they
touch; steps 8 to 10 are M2 and M1 defects; step 12 is a docs and gates
slice.

## 5. Domain assessments

One judgment per domain, bounded by what the lanes examined (their coverage
ledgers are in section 6). Counts are confirmed findings after merging.

| Domain | Lanes | Confirmed | High | Medium | Low |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desired-state API | api-grammar, api-environment-secrets, api-machines, api-openshift, api-ceph, api-addons | 58 | 0 | 9 | 49 |
| Command line | cli-parsing, cli-journeys, cli-output | 33 | 1 | 6 | 26 |
| Project, architecture and security | project-glossary, architecture, security | 23 | 1 | 5 | 17 |
| Controller, contexts and secrets | controller-host, controller-stage, contexts, secrets | 31 | 0 | 7 | 24 |
| State reconciliation | reconciliation-core, reconciliation-plan, reconciliation-diff, reconciliation-safety | 37 | 0 | 5 | 32 |
| Infrastructure services and substrates | infra-services, substrates-virtual, substrates-physical | 32 | 0 | 6 | 26 |
| Managed operating system | managedos-media-install, managedos-network-fips-physical, managedos-day2 | 16 | 0 | 3 | 13 |
| Container clusters | openshift-install, openshift-nodes-coverage | 15 | 0 | 2 | 13 |
| Ceph storage | ceph-lifecycle, ceph-devices-resources, ceph-ingress-removal, ceph-native-api, ceph-resources-a, ceph-resources-b, ceph-coverage | 53 | 0 | 17 | 36 |
| Add-ons | addons | 15 | 1 | 4 | 10 |

**Desired-state API.** Sound in structure: the kind catalog, the retired and
unrealized tables, the strict-YAML refusals, the input ceilings and the
Machine schema match their pages and are held by tests. Weak at the edges of
admission: it accepts Ceph and Machine inputs that planning refuses
([CPC-01](#cpc-01), [CEA-08](#cea-08), [MCH-04](#mch-04)); the image grammar
admits a reference with no repository, which a container runtime then
resolves through short-name policy ([API-01](#api-01)); the MetalLB
held-address check misses Ceph ingress virtual IPs ([ADA-09](#ada-09));
kind-default inheritance treats an authored empty arm as a selection and does
not suppress TLS behind an HTTP listener ([ENV-06](#env-06),
[ENV-08](#env-08)); and the key-separation refusals have no test
([CEA-05](#cea-05)).

**Command line.** The command and flag catalog, the parsing bounds, the JSON
envelope, the diagnostic order and the authorization order match the spec
and are pinned by goldens. Weak at the privilege boundary, where `render`
runs its output side as root ([CLI-01](#cli-01)) and help and usage outcomes
elevate first ([CLI-02](#cli-02), [CLI-03](#cli-03), [CLI-04](#cli-04)), and
in human output that bypasses the shared renderer or reports empty outcomes
([OUT-01](#out-01), [OUT-05](#out-05), [OUT-13](#out-13)). Private
operation logs are flushed only on the next write, so a wedged adapter's
last lines stay in memory ([OUT-11](#out-11)).

**Project, architecture and security.** Dependency direction, effect grants
and protocol bounds are held by exact fitness tests, and every test the
security spec cites exists. Weak where one rule has several copies
([SEC-07](#sec-07), [SEC-01](#sec-01)), in the ambient plugin path
([PRJ-03](#prj-03)), in missing redirect revalidation and the absent
internal-error boundary ([SEC-06](#sec-06), [SEC-02](#sec-02)), and in
fitness checks narrower than the clauses they back ([ARC-01](#arc-01),
[ARC-08](#arc-08), [ARC-10](#arc-10)). The project scope and non-goals hold
in code; the glossary terms are the identifiers the code uses.

**Controller, contexts and secrets.** Destructive paths are well defended:
uninstall resolves beneath its root, package removal fails closed, tool
location answers only from a completed proof, and only normalized proxy
variables cross sudo. Registry formats, locks, the two-hold media protocol,
deletion order and the keyring v4 format match the spec with golden, fuzz
and tamper suites. Weak in resume bookkeeping, where a re-setup or a resumed
install records Bootwright's packages as pre-existing ([CTH-01](#cth-01),
[CTH-02](#cth-02)), in recovery over half-finished store states
([CTX-01](#ctx-01), [CTX-02](#ctx-02), [SCR-01](#scr-01)), in transport
diagnostics ([CTS-01](#cts-01)), in the sudo option-list fail-open
([SCR-05](#scr-05)), and in spec text X89 left behind ([CTS-02](#cts-02)).

**State reconciliation.** The state machine and its transition tables are
driven from the spec, plan freezing enforces every bound, `diff` is
read-only by construction, and the RAM erase worker binds each chunk to the
disk identity. Weak where `diff` re-implements scheduler and runner checks
([RCD-07](#rcd-07), [RCD-01](#rcd-01)), in the stored-plan bound the store
caps below the spec ([RCC-06](#rcc-06)), and in the physical root-disk and
MAC-set predicates ([RCS-01](#rcs-01), [RCS-02](#rcs-02)).

**Infrastructure services and substrates.** The refusal tables, placement and
reservation refusals, serving-certificate proof and host-key pinning match
the spec; the physical firmware step and the libvirt host apply are the
best-defended code examined, and the KubeVirt bounds match. Weak at the
Ansible boundary of the managed services, with inverted readiness
classification ([INF-01](#inf-01)), DNS readiness on the first record only
([INF-05](#inf-05)) and wildcard sockets of one family
([INF-07](#inf-07), [INF-08](#inf-08), tracked as B412); in Redfish answer
handling ([SBP-11](#sbp-11), [SBP-05](#sbp-05)); in the controller-host MAC
guard ([SBP-02](#sbp-02)); and in SSH-placed emulated BMC claims
([SBV-11](#sbv-11)). The infrastructure-services lane has the highest share
of Medium findings of any lane. vSphere is unrealized by design under B99.

**Managed operating system.** Network convergence, the RHSM foreign
registration refusal, the physical clear and the FIPS proof are precise and
tested, and the day-2 update and firewall workers have closed vocabularies.
Weak at the installation role's edges: private files published before their
final mode ([MOI-04](#moi-04)), a marker not compared before convergence
([MOI-01](#moi-01)), serial-root and host-key ordering in the kickstart
([MON-02](#mon-02), [MON-11](#mon-11)), and a budgets section that no
longer describes the physical arm ([MOI-05](#moi-05)). Some encryption and
update clauses rest on live qualification not yet run.

**Container clusters.** The refusal table is held to both capabilities, the
install token and sweep discipline, kubeconfig custody and node placement
with uid-pinned patches trace to tests. Weak in the physical and boot-media
paths B67 delivered but operators have not accepted ([OCI-02](#oci-02)), in
taint comparison in `diff` ([OCN-01](#ocn-01)), and in coverage text that
still says physical nodes refuse ([OCI-01](#oci-01), [OCN-02](#ocn-02)).
The secondary-network admission findings sit in the API domain
([OCA-05](#oca-05)).

**Ceph storage.** Destructive ownership is sound: the partial-OSD clear
records intent first and re-proves before zap, deadlines and refusal tables
are read from the spec by tests, and secrets stay on stdin or in private
files. Weak in admission-to-plan-to-worker parity ([CPC-01](#cpc-01),
[CEA-08](#cea-08), [CRB-01](#crb-01), [CRB-07](#crb-07),
[CRA-08](#cra-08)), in cross-host disk comparison ([CPD-03](#cpd-03)), in a
missing management-gateway digest check ([CPD-04](#cpd-04)), in the
placement-group budget's width for an unauthored pool ([CRA-01](#cra-01)),
and in refusal vocabulary and version numbers in the spec. This is the
largest domain and holds the largest Medium count, with no High.

**Add-ons.** The trust boundary, package selection, namespace exclusivity,
frozen-request guards and Secret handling match, and the remediation of the
prior add-ons audit is in place. Weak in the Python cluster object engine's
OLM and observation edges: a pending upgrade plan makes healthy instances
unknown ([ADD-01](#add-01)), the webhook retry never fires
([ADD-02](#add-02)), transient Secret failures fail at once
([ADD-11](#add-11)), and evidence fields are empty or truncated
([ADD-03](#add-03), [ADD-13](#add-13)).

## 6. Lane reports

Each lane section opens with its assessment, lists its confirmed findings, gives one entry per finding in the house shape (evidence, impact, counterevidence, correction and exit evidence), then its tracked discrepancies, coverage ledger, observations, limits and the candidates its verifiers refuted. Entry ids carry the lane code. Citations are links to the file at the baseline; the line numbers are the baseline's.

### Group: Desired-state API

### API: Desired-state grammar, input discovery, YAML decoding, kind catalog, graph validation, defaults, native fields and custom playbooks

Lane `api-grammar`. Spec range: `specs/api.md` lines 1-724; `specs/api/input.md` lines 1-196; `specs/api/custom-playbooks.md` lines 1-48. Register: 471 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 12; confirmed: 10; tracked: 2; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

This lane covers [api.md:1-724](../../specs/api.md), [input.md:1-196](../../specs/api/input.md) and [custom-playbooks.md:1-48](../../specs/api/custom-playbooks.md), a register of 471 clauses, over three rounds. The structural core matches its specification. The kind catalog in [object.go:49](../../api/v1alpha1/object.go) holds the 34 kinds in the spec's canonical order. The retired-field, retired-value, retired-kind and unrealized tables match their spec rows one for one and are held to the data by tests. Every strict-YAML refusal the spec names has a probe row in `TestEveryStrictYAMLRuleRefusesWithItsCode`. All 12 fixed input ceilings in [input.go:25-40](../../internal/desiredstate/input.go) match the input page, and discovery's symlink, hard-link, type and enumeration rules are in place. No finding is Blocking or High. One Medium defect remains: the `image` lexical rule admits a reference with no repository component. The other confirmed findings are Low and fall into three groups. The first is diagnostic detail: no permitted-field list for a non-identifier key, invalid object names repeated in message text, and `api.unrealized` absent from plan and apply. The second is bounds and spelling detail: the secrets-directory check budget and number canonical form. The third is spec text that lags intentional code: native-map inertness, add-on list sorting, the forbidden controller host groups, and the `serviceID` reference class. The ledger gives the limits of this assessment. About 40 clauses in the first round were marked unverifiable because another lane owns them, including owner-specific normalizations, context-store retention, cross-build continuation and per-class reference resolution. Rounds 2 and 3 closed only the subset the critic named. Most "met" verdicts come from reading source at the baseline, not from a probe run.

| ID | Severity | Kind | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [API-01](#api-01) | Medium | defect | The image grammar admits a reference with no repository component, such as `squid:6.10` or `registry.example.test:5000` |
| [API-03](#api-03) | Low | defect | An unknown key that is not a schema identifier gets no list of permitted fields and no rename offer |
| [API-04](#api-04) | Low | defect | The secrets-directory check gives each skipped secrets directory a fresh 65,536-entry budget and ignores entries of unreported type |
| [API-05](#api-05) | Low | defect | Canonical number output pads exponents (`1e-05`) and tags integral values `!!float 1` |
| [API-06](#api-06) | Low | defect | Some compiler diagnostics repeat an object name that is not a DNS label |
| [API-07](#api-07) | Low | defect | `plan` and `apply` never emit the `api.unrealized` warning the spec and delivered record promise; only `validate` does |
| [API-09](#api-09) | Low | defect | CustomPlaybook forbids host groups that do not exist and admits the real controller inventory group |
| [API-10](#api-10) | Low | defect | `CephNFSExport.spec.serviceID` is not a typed native-service reference and is resolved by kind admission with `api.invariant` |
| [API-11](#api-11) | Low | drift | api.md says native maps stay inert during compilation except NMState, but Ceph admission inspects and normalizes native NFS export maps |
| [API-12](#api-12) | Low | drift | ClusterAddon normalization sorts `provides`, `requires`, `inputs` and other set lists that the owning page never declares sorted |

#### API-01

**Medium, defect.** Image grammar admits a reference with no repository component, such as a short name `squid:6.10` or `registry.example.test:5000`.

**Evidence.** [api.md:596-603](../../specs/api.md) defines an image reference as "a registry `host[:port]`, then `/`-separated repository components each matching ..., then either `:<tag>` ... or `@sha256:<64 hex>`". Line 603 applies "the same host and path rule" to registry and registry-base values, so a bare host is valid for those two rules but not for an image. [lexical.go:361-371](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go) implements `validImage` by checking only that the text before the last colon passes `validRegistry(value[:colon])`, and in the digest branch at [lexical.go:362-363](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go) that the base passes `validRegistry(base)`. `validRegistry` at [lexical.go:332-350](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go) leaves its component loop on `if u.Path == "" { break }` ([lexical.go:341-343](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go)), so a host with no path is accepted. `validDNS` and `validHost` at [lexical.go:166-184](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go) accept a single label such as `squid`. As a result `squid:6.10`, `squid@sha256:<64 hex>` and `registry.example.test:5000` are all admitted as images. A temporary probe at the baseline confirmed all three, and confirmed that `squid:latest` is refused. `TestImageAndRegistryPathsFollowTheOCIGrammar` at [lexical_test.go:219-240](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical_test.go) admits only `registry.example.test/<component>` image forms and has no refused row for a reference without a repository. The `image()` shape ([schema.go:120](../../api/v1alpha1/schema.go)) is used for managed-service `image.local` and `image.public` ([infrastructure_services.go:13](../../api/v1alpha1/infrastructure_services.go)), the OLM catalog source image ([addons.go:55](../../api/v1alpha1/addons.go), with a second image site at [addons.go:152](../../api/v1alpha1/addons.go)) and the OpenShift release image ([openshift_clusters.go:60](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go)).

**Impact.** Admission accepts an unqualified short name in fields that the spec requires to be fully qualified. What follows depends on the host's `registries.conf` short-name mode. Under the enforcing or prompting defaults common on RHEL, the likely outcome is a pull failure after admission instead of a refusal at `validate`. Under a permissive mode, the runtime may resolve the name through unqualified-search registries the operator never named. A `host:port`-shaped value is read as a repository named after the host with a numeric tag, which is ambiguous more than unsafe.

**Counterevidence.** The digest form still requires `sha256:` and 64 hex characters, and `latest` is refused. The `registry` and `registry-base` rules correctly allow a bare host. No other admission layer was found that requires a `/` in these fields, and no milestone item, Not yet met line or decision tracks this.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In `validImage`, require at least one `/`-separated repository component after the host in both the tag and digest branches. Check the host and port with the host rule and each component with `ociPathComponentPattern`. One-component shapes such as `quay.io/squid:1` must stay admitted. Exit: `TestImageAndRegistryPathsFollowTheOCIGrammar` refuses `squid:6.10`, `registry.example.test:5000` and `squid@sha256:<64 hex>`, still admits every current admitted row, and the `api/v1alpha1` suite passes.

#### API-03

**Low, defect.** An unknown key that is not a schema identifier gets no list of permitted fields and no rename offer.

**Evidence.** The strict-decoding paragraph at [api.md:152-161](../../specs/api.md) says "Any other unknown key is reported at its containing field and is not repeated. The diagnostic names the fields its containing field permits, and offers a rename when exactly one of them equals the key ignoring case or ... is nearest to the key within at most two edits." `unknownField` at [decoding.go:320-324](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/decoding.go) returns early for a key that fails `schemaIdentifier`, with the fixed message "a field name that is not a schema identifier is not permitted here" and the remedy "remove the field". The permitted-name list and the `nearestName` rename are built only after that return, at [decoding.go:352-364](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/decoding.go). The string "not a schema identifier" appears only at [decoding.go:322](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/decoding.go), so no test covers the branch. The kind-defaults path has the same early return at [decoding.go:372-374](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/decoding.go), where the spec does not clearly require a kind list.

**Impact.** A key such as `image.tag`, `typ e`, a quoted name with a trailing space, or a key longer than 64 bytes is refused with only "remove the field". The operator is not told which fields are allowed or which one was likely meant. A plain YAML scalar loses trailing whitespace, so `spec :` decodes to `spec` and does not reach this branch.

**Counterevidence.** The key is correctly not echoed, and the refusal is at the containing path. "The diagnostic" can be read as covering only identifier keys, so the spec is mildly ambiguous. No tracking record was found.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In the non-identifier branch, list the permitted fields with `boundedList(names)` and run `nearestName` against them, without echoing the key. Alternatively, tighten the spec sentence so it limits the list to identifier keys. Exit: a compilation test whose probe carries `typ e: opaque` under a Secret spec asserts one `api.field` at `$.spec` whose message lists the permitted fields and whose remedy offers `rename it to type`. A row for a 65-byte key asserts the field list too.

#### API-04

**Low, defect.** The secrets-directory check gives each skipped secrets directory a fresh 65,536-entry budget and ignores entries of unreported type.

**Evidence.** medium confidence. Each half of this finding is contested by one verifier. [input.md:76-79](../../specs/api/input.md) says the check warns `input.secrets-directory` for a YAML file "at any depth" and "lists names within the entry and depth ceilings, opens no file". [input.md:101](../../specs/api/input.md) sets the entry ceiling at "65,536 across all visited directories". [input.md:113-117](../../specs/api/input.md) says "skipped subtree descendants are not enumerated or counted". Discovery charges its listings against the aggregate: [reader_linux_amd64.go:249-254](../../internal/desiredstate/inputfs/reader_linux_amd64.go) lists with `desiredstate.MaxEntries-s.entries+1` and adds the count to `s.entries`. The secrets check at [reader_linux_amd64.go:281-286](../../internal/desiredstate/inputfs/reader_linux_amd64.go) starts every skipped `secrets` directory with `budget := desiredstate.MaxEntries`, and `holdsYAML` at [reader_linux_amd64.go:328-355](../../internal/desiredstate/inputfs/reader_linux_amd64.go) never adds what it lists to `s.entries`. `holdsYAML` classifies entries only as `DT_REG` or `DT_DIR` ([reader_linux_amd64.go:347-352](../../internal/desiredstate/inputfs/reader_linux_amd64.go)). Discovery's own walk resolves `DT_UNKNOWN` by opening the child through the session, as [input.md:44-46](../../specs/api/input.md) requires. The only test, `TestASkippedSecretsDirectoryHoldingYAMLIsReportedUnread` at [directory_linux_amd64_test.go:133-160](../../internal/desiredstate/inputfs/directory_linux_amd64_test.go), covers neither a budget nor untyped entries.

**Impact.** Listing work for the check can reach the number of `secrets` directories times 65,536 names, not one aggregate 65,536. Each check stops at its first YAML hit. On a filesystem that does not report `d_type`, such as some network or FUSE mounts, YAML misplaced under `secrets` produces no warning and no Secret-reference remedy.

**Counterevidence.** The check opens no regular file, refuses nothing, and fails quiet on a listing error, as the spec allows. Depth is bounded, and discovery's own entry ceiling is enforced. The budget half rests on reading "within the entry and depth ceilings" as the one aggregate ceiling. A per-check ceiling is also a valid reading given [input.md:113-117](../../specs/api/input.md). The `DT_UNKNOWN` half conflicts with "opens no file" if the remedy is to open untyped entries, so one verifier classed it as an improvement.

**Correction and exit evidence.** First, decide in the spec whether the check's entry ceiling is per check or shared with discovery, and whether an `O_PATH` probe of an untyped entry counts as opening a file. If shared, pass the remaining budget `MaxEntries - s.entries` or one budget shared by all secrets directories. For untyped entries, either resolve them as discovery does or treat a `DT_UNKNOWN` entry with a `.yaml` or `.yml` name as a hit. Exit: an inputfs test with two secrets directories whose combined listings exceed the chosen budget asserts the check stops without a warning, and a test through the untyped-entries harness asserts the warning still fires.

#### API-05

**Low, defect.** Canonical output of a finite-number field is not the plain shortest spelling: an integral value emits `!!float 1`, a small one `1e-05`.

**Evidence.** [api.md:131-133](../../specs/api.md) says "Canonical output uses the shortest base-10 spelling, including exponent form when needed, that round-trips to the same binary64 value." Decoding stores a Number as `strconv.FormatFloat(n, 'g', -1, 64)` at [decoding.go:443](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/decoding.go). Go's `'g'` format pads the exponent to two digits, giving `1e-05` and `1e+21`. The shortest spellings are `1e-5` and `1e21`. The YAML encoder writes the text unchanged with tag `!!float` at [encoding.go:176-182](../../internal/desiredstate/encoding/encoding.go), and the JSON path at [encoding.go:235-238](../../internal/desiredstate/encoding/encoding.go) carries the same padding. The module in use is `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` v3.0.5 ([go.mod:9](../../go.mod)), whose encoder keeps an explicit tag when the plain text resolves to another tag, so an integral value prints as `!!float 1` or `!!float 100`. Non-integral values such as `2.5` print plain. A temporary probe at the baseline confirmed each of these outputs. [effective_roundtrip_test.go:37](../../internal/desiredstate/encoding/effective_roundtrip_test.go) admits `NumberValue("1")` but checks only that the value decodes back.

**Impact.** `render effective` and the effective-state file show `1e-05`, one byte longer than the canonical spelling, and `targetSizeRatio: !!float 1` for an integral ratio. The effect is cosmetic, and the value round-trips.

**Counterevidence.** The exponent padding contradicts the spelling clause literally. The `!!float` tag does not: the digits `1` are already the shortest spelling, `!!float` is an admitted tag, and [api.md:700-701](../../specs/api.md) makes encoder golden fixtures normative for encoder details the spec does not fix. No golden in the repository carries `!!float`, so the intended tag is unrecorded.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Trim exponent zero-padding and the `+` sign when spelling a Number, in decoding or encoding. Record the intended tag for integral Numbers in an encoder golden. Exit: an encoding golden with `targetSizeRatio` values `1` and `0.00001` shows the chosen integral spelling and `1e-5` in YAML and JSON, and `validate` over that output admits it.

#### API-06

**Low, defect.** Some compiler diagnostics repeat an object name that is not a DNS label.

**Evidence.** [api.md:168-187](../../specs/api.md) shows the object "as its kind and name" only when `metadata.name` is a DNS label. It also says a diagnostic carries "no authored scalar value", repeating only "an unknown key that is a schema identifier, a reference name that is a DNS label, a repeated entry's name that is a DNS label, and a Secret's declared type". The sink attaches the object identity only under `api.ValidLexical("name", ...)` at [diagnostics.go:142](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/diagnostics.go). An invalid name only withholds the identity at decode time ([decoding.go:114-116](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/decoding.go)), and the object goes on through the later phases. The message text is not guarded. The cross-kind cluster-name collision builds its message and remedy from `record.object.Identity()` and the other records' identities at [selection.go:41-43](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/selection.go). `unrealizedIssue` at [phases.go:305-313](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go) starts its message with `object.Identity() + " declares "`. Nothing skips it after the name refusal at [phases.go:270-275](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go). In environment selection, excluded objects never reach the name check, and their text repeats the name at [selection.go:56](../../internal/environment/selection.go), [selection.go:63](../../internal/environment/selection.go), [selection.go:72](../../internal/environment/selection.go) and in `excludedRoot`'s remedy at [selection.go:86-87](../../internal/environment/selection.go) (`"add " + object.Name() + ...`). Those problems pass into the sink through record matching in `closeGraph` at [phases.go:151-159](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go). A temporary probe compiled an OpenShiftCluster and a CephCluster both named `Bad_Name` plus an excluded OpenShiftCluster named `Bad_Name`. Both the `api.duplicate` and the `api.selection` diagnostics repeated `Bad_Name`.

**Impact.** An authored `metadata.name` outside the label grammar is repeated in diagnostic text, against the rule that bounds which authored values a refusal may repeat. The practical risk is low, because a credential rarely lands in `metadata.name` and a correct grammar refusal appears alongside.

**Counterevidence.** The name refusal itself does not echo, and the environment package already guards names elsewhere ([selection.go:301-302](../../internal/environment/selection.go)), so these sites look like omissions rather than policy. Backlog B464 covers a different point. No tracking record was found.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Build these messages through one helper that writes the identity only when the name is a DNS label and otherwise writes the kind and "this object". Apply the same guard in `environment.Select` for excluded objects. Exit: a compilation test with two cluster kinds named `Bad_Name`, a managed object named `Bad_Name` that declares an unrealized field, and an excluded OpenShiftCluster named `Bad_Name` asserts that no diagnostic message or remedy contains `Bad_Name`.

#### API-07

**Low, defect.** plan and apply never emit the api.unrealized (or api.deferred) warnings the spec and delivered record promise; only validate does.

**Evidence.** [api.md:40-42](../../specs/api.md) says "`validate`, `plan` and `apply` warn `api.unrealized` at the path of each declaration below", and [delivered.md:9022-9024](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) records "`api.unrealized` warns at `validate`, `plan` and `apply`". The compiler emits the warning at [phases.go:296-300](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go). The lifecycle service compiles through `compileSources` at [planning.go:41-49](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/planning.go), which uses the report only for a nil check and returns only `state`. Every lifecycle path shares that helper. Plan warnings come only from `s.removalWarnings` at [presentation.go:29](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/presentation.go), and apply warnings come only from convergence at [executor.go:217](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/executor.go). The only CLI reader of compile advisories is the validate writer at [output.go:157-170](../../internal/cli/output.go), together with the context admission paths. `TestUnrealizedTableMatchesUnsupported` at [unrealized_linux_amd64_test.go:145-160](../../cmd/bootwright/unrealized_linux_amd64_test.go) checks the compile advisories and the plan refusals but never plan or apply output.

**Impact.** Every row the warning covers is refused at plan with `lifecycle.unsupported`, which the test proves row by row. So at plan and apply the operator already gets a stronger signal, and the missing warning has no behavioral consequence. The spec and the delivered record still state output the code does not produce.

**Counterevidence.** The spec is inconsistent with itself. [custom-playbooks.md:42-43](../../specs/api/custom-playbooks.md) names only `validate` for `api.unrealized` and names no command for the disabled playbook's `api.deferred`. The advisories appear in validate's JSON only per [output.md:398](../../specs/cli/output.md), and decision record Q85 ([backlog.md:3339](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)) asked only about `validate`. No item tracks the plan and apply gap.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Decide which side moves. Either carry the compile report's warning diagnostics into `PlanResult.Warnings` and the operation's warnings, or narrow [api.md:40-42](../../specs/api.md) and the delivered record to `validate` and context admission. Exit for the code path: a lifecycle test asserts that a plan preview over each unrealized fixture lists `api.unrealized` at the row's path. Exit for the spec path: `make docs-check` with the narrowed wording.

#### API-09

**Low, defect.** CustomPlaybook forbids host groups that do not exist (bootwright_controller_hosts, bootwright_ocp_hosts) and accepts the real controller identities and the controller Machine as targets.

**Evidence.** [custom-playbooks.md:24-27](../../specs/api/custom-playbooks.md) says "the controller is never a target: its inventory identities are forbidden host groups". The code's list at [validation.go:66](../../internal/desiredstate/customplaybooks/validation.go), inside `validateTargetsAndTags` ([validation.go:62-68](../../internal/desiredstate/customplaybooks/validation.go)), is `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `bootwright_ocp_hosts` and `bootwright_controller_hosts`. The real controller inventory at [runner_linux_amd64.go:151](../../internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go) is group `bootwright_controller` with host `controller`, and [setup.yml:3](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/playbooks/controller/setup.yml) reads `hosts: bootwright_controller`. The two stale group names appear only in [validation.go:66](../../internal/desiredstate/customplaybooks/validation.go), its test rows at [validation_test.go:138-141](../../internal/desiredstate/customplaybooks/validation_test.go), and the deferred detail page at [custom-playbooks.md:92-94](../../specs/deferred/custom-playbooks.md). That page lists the same four identities verbatim, so the code follows a stale detail spec, and both need the fix.

**Impact.** A CustomPlaybook targeting `hostGroups: [bootwright_controller]` is admitted. The kind never executes: an enabled one is refused at plan and a disabled one only warns `api.deferred`, so no effect reaches the controller today. The reserved-shape rule meant to keep operator code off the controller is not enforced, and admitted declarations would carry into any executable schema under B102.

**Counterevidence.** The candidate also claimed that admission must refuse `target.machines` naming the controller Machine. That half does not hold. The deferred page assigns the controller exclusion to the future executor ("A qualified executor must expand the declaration to an exact non-empty Machine set ... the controller is never a target", [custom-playbooks.md:94-96](../../specs/deferred/custom-playbooks.md)), and no spec field names the controller as a Machine for admission to compare against. No tracking record was found for the stale names.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Replace the forbidden list in both [custom-playbooks.md:92-94](../../specs/deferred/custom-playbooks.md) and [validation.go:66](../../internal/desiredstate/customplaybooks/validation.go) with the real inventory identities `bootwright_controller`, `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`, and optionally `controller`, which is a host alias, not a group. Derive them from the inventory builder's constants and drop the two names that do not exist. Exit: a `validation_test.go` row probes `hostGroups: [bootwright_controller]` and is refused at its index, and `make docs-check` passes.

#### API-10

**Low, defect.** CephNFSExport.spec.serviceID is not a typed native-service reference; kind admission resolves it again with api.invariant instead of the shared api.reference.

**Evidence.** [api.md:290](../../specs/api.md) lists `serviceID` in the Native service class beside `mdsServiceRef` and `serviceRef`. [api.md:293](../../specs/api.md) says the schema types every reference field with its class, and [api.md:299-307](../../specs/api.md) says such a reference "resolves through the same `api.reference` diagnostic" and that "no kind's admission resolves such a reference again". [ceph.md:54](../../specs/api/ceph.md) gives the field's namespace as "native service registry, exactly `nfs.<serviceID>`". [ceph-resources.md:46-49](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) allows the bare ID because the owning field fixes the type, which settles the spelling but not the class. The schema at [storage.go:153](../../api/v1alpha1/storage.go) types it `required("serviceID", nonempty())`, while the siblings use `nativeServiceOf("clusterRef")` ([scope.go:87-93](../../api/v1alpha1/scope.go)). CephCluster admission resolves it by hand at [nfs_export.go:184-186](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export.go) and issues `api.invariant` at `$.spec.serviceID`. Tests pin that code at [nfs_export_test.go:231](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export_test.go) and [nfs_export_test.go:330](../../internal/storage/ceph/nfs_export_test.go). `TestEveryNestedReferenceNamesWhereItResolves` at [scope_test.go:75](../../api/v1alpha1/scope_test.go) examines only shapes that carry a scope, so it never sees this field.

**Impact.** A dangling NFS service ID is refused with `api.invariant`, not `api.reference`, and it skips the shared suppression and echo rules. Tooling keyed on `api.reference` misses it. The refusal itself fires at the right field and names the cluster, so the operator still gets a usable diagnostic.

**Counterevidence.** The planner check at [nfs_export.go:124-125](../../internal/storage/ceph/nfs_export.go) runs on the frozen request. It is defense in depth, not a second admission resolution. The fix is larger than a call-site change: `Scope` ([scope.go:5-15](../../api/v1alpha1/scope.go)) has no fixed-type field, and `nativeServiceOf` keys on both `service_type` and `service_id`. Audit 001 F03-07 settled only the field's naming. No tracking record was found.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Extend `Scope` with a fixed native service type, type `serviceID` with a native-service scope fixed to `nfs` that keeps the bare spelling, and drop the hand-written resolution in CephCluster admission. Moving `serviceID` out of the Native service row would weaken the spec and is not recommended. Exit: `TestEveryNestedReferenceNamesWhereItResolves` holds `serviceID`, and a refusal golden in which a CephNFSExport names an undeclared nfs service yields one `api.reference` at `$.spec.serviceID`, with the two pinned tests updated.

#### API-11

**Low, drift.** api.md says native maps stay inert during compilation except NMState, but Ceph admission inspects native ServiceSpec and NFS export documents.

**Evidence.** [api.md:719-721](../../specs/api.md) says "Native maps remain inert during desired-state compilation, except for the explicit NMState composition subset needed to validate Machine declarations." CephCluster rules are bound into compilation at [wiring_desiredstate.go:53](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_desiredstate.go). The CephNFSExport `native` map is an open map ([storage.go:153](../../api/v1alpha1/storage.go), `required("native", native())`). Admission refuses named members inside it at [nfs_export.go:18-26](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export.go), including `export_id`, `cluster_id`, `fsal.user_id` and `fsal.cephx_key`. It also requires `protocols` and compares `fsal.fs_name` with the bound filesystem at [nfs_export.go:186-197](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export.go). Normalization writes `fsal` and `clients` defaults into the map at [normalization.go:168-186](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/normalization.go). The Ceph pages specify this deliberately at [ceph-resources.md:1004-1012](../../specs/ceph-resources.md), which lists the refused members and the frozen defaults. The api.md sentence is therefore stale against its sibling owners, and the code is correct.

**Impact.** A reader of the API contract would expect the compiler never to refuse on, or rewrite, native content outside NMState. In fact `validate` refuses fixed Ceph native members and normalization fills in defaults. The two spec pages disagree about where native validation lives. There is no behavioral consequence.

**Counterevidence.** The native ServiceSpec part of the candidate is overstated. `storageNativeService` at [storage_native.go:10](../../api/v1alpha1/storage_native.go) is a closed record whose only open member is `spec`, and [ceph-native-api.md:375](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md) describes those documents as closed records. The NFS export map is decisive by itself, and the CephSMB `native` maps are also inspected. [input.md:186-187](../../specs/api/input.md) is not violated, because the diagnostics name a fixed, documented key list, not arbitrary native keys. No tracking record was found.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Reword [api.md:719-721](../../specs/api.md) to say that native maps stay uninterpreted by the compiler except where an owning page specifies admission or normalization of named members, and link the NMState subset, [ceph-resources.md:1004-1012](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) and the Ceph native service pages. Exit: `make docs-check` passes with the new links.

#### API-12

**Low, drift.** ClusterAddon normalization sorts provides, requires, inputs and step secretRefs, but the owning page never says the effective list is sorted.

**Evidence.** [api.md:350-353](../../specs/api.md) says set-valued lists reject duplicates and "normalization sorts one only when that schema says the effective representation is sorted", and [api.md:655-656](../../specs/api.md) repeats the rule. The owning page calls `provides` and `requires` a "Set of add-on capability tokens" ([addons.md:42-43](../../specs/api/addons.md)) and gives `inputs` "set semantics keyed by author-defined `name`" ([addons.md:67](../../specs/api/addons.md)). It never says these lists are sorted, and its normalization section ([addons.md:677-697](../../specs/api/addons.md)) defers to "the common API rules" at line 696, which send the question back to the owning schema. The normalizer sorts `provides` and `requires` at [admission.go:18-20](../../internal/addons/admission.go), `inputs` at [admission.go:28](../../internal/addons/admission.go), each step's `secretRefs` at [admission.go:72](../../internal/addons/admission.go), and, beyond the original candidate, ClusterAddonBinding `addonConfigs[].inputs` at [admission.go:82](../../internal/addons/admission.go) and `addonConfigs` at [admission.go:85](../../internal/addons/admission.go). The helpers are at [admission.go:255-265](../../internal/addons/admission.go). Other owning pages state such sorts explicitly, for example [ceph.md:337](../../specs/api/ceph.md) and [secrets.md:133](../../specs/api/secrets.md).

**Impact.** `render effective` reorders these add-on lists, and the API contract gives no reason for it. The lists are sets, so meaning does not change.

**Counterevidence.** The sorting is plainly intentional and gives a canonical order. The step `secretRefs` row is owned by [add-ons-design.md:238](../../specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md), not by addons.md, and no consumer reads a step today. No tracking record was found.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Replace the circular sentence at [addons.md:696](../../specs/api/addons.md) with an explicit statement that the effective `provides`, `requires`, `inputs`, `addonConfigs` and `addonConfigs[].inputs` lists are sorted, and add the same statement for `secretRefs` to [add-ons-design.md:238](../../specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md). Exit: `make docs-check` passes.

#### API-02

**Low, drift.** api.md still lists node labels and taints and a stretch topology without a tiebreaker as api.deferred warnings, but D199 removed the first and admission now refuses the second. Re-judged from tracked: D199 clause (9) at specs/milestones/backlog.md:5772-5773 ("The `api.deferred` warning for node labels and taints is removed") is the decision that moved the code, not open work that records the stale api.md text, and no open item in specs/milestones/ mentions api.deferred or the tiebreaker warning. specs/api.md:76-81 still lists node labels and taints and a Ceph stretch topology without a tiebreaker as api.deferred warnings, so the code changed on purpose and the spec text is stale, which makes this a confirmed drift.

**Evidence.** api.md:76-81: "`api.deferred` stays the warning for a declaration that plans but changes nothing: an OpenShift endpoint `dnsName` and node `labels` and `taints` ..., a disabled `CustomPlaybook`, and a Ceph stretch topology without a tiebreaker." backlog.md:5772 D199: "(9) The `api.deferred` warning for node labels and taints is removed." openshift/admission.go:314-325 inertDeclarations emits api.deferred only for `endpoints.<slot>.dnsName`. topology.go:270-271: `if textOf(tie, "node") == "" { a.invalid("$.spec.topology.stretch.tiebreaker.node", "native stretch mode needs a tiebreaker MON at a third site", ...)`, and a.invalid issues api.invariant. A grep for `"api.deferred"` across internal/ finds only machine, openshift dnsName and the CustomPlaybook emitters. Spec: `specs/api.md:76-81`, `specs/openshift-clusters.md:50-53`, `specs/openshift-clusters.md:990-1000`, `specs/ceph-coverage.md:482`. Code: `internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go:314-325`, `internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go:270-273`, `specs/milestones/backlog.md:5772-5773`.

**Impact.** An operator or a later agent reading api.md expects a warning for labels and taints, which are now applied, and expects a warning-only outcome for a stretch topology without a tiebreaker, which validation refuses. This is documentation drift only.

**Counterevidence.** The other three entries (dnsName, root-device hints, disabled CustomPlaybook) still match the code. The owning pages (openshift-clusters.md node placement, ceph-coverage.md U01) already state the current behavior.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Edit api.md:76-81 so the api.deferred list names only the endpoint `dnsName`, an OS-ready Machine's root-device hints other than `deviceName` and `wwn`, and a disabled `CustomPlaybook`. Exit: specs/api.md lists only the three remaining api.deferred cases; `make docs-check` passes.

#### API-08

**Low, defect.** The api.unrealized message always says 'plan refuses it', but plan refuses the dependencyVersions.libvirt row only when the controller selects the libvirt client. Re-judged from tracked: B676 (specs/milestones/backlog.md:2228-2237) covers only the libvirt NEVRA pin, meaning it must either be honoured through host dnf or removed from the grammar. It does not mention that the api.unrealized warning says "plan refuses it" without condition. specs/api.md:40-42 makes that same unconditional promise, while specs/api.md:73-74 says the row "is refused when the controller selects the libvirt client", so the warning is wrong on paths with no libvirt client and no record tracks that mismatch.

**Evidence.** phases.go:307: `message := object.Identity() + " declares " + declaration.Declaration() + ", which this build admits but does not realize, so plan refuses it with lifecycle.unsupported"`. DeclaredBy (unrealized.go:36-55) checks only that `value.Text() != u.Except`. The plan side, selection.go:303: `if environments := catalog.OfKind(api.Environment); len(environments) == 1 && requiresLibvirtClient(catalog, machine) {` and only then appends the dependencyVersions.libvirt shape. Spec 73-74: "The `dependencyVersions.libvirt` row is refused when the controller selects the libvirt client." Rows refused on a selecting Machine or binding (spec 67-70) show the same pattern: a profile, Entitlement or ClusterAddon that nothing selects is warned with the same words. Spec: `specs/api.md:40-42`, `specs/api.md:67-74`, `specs/cli/output.md:1010`. Code: `internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go:305-313`, `api/v1alpha1/unrealized.go:31-55`, `internal/controller/selection.go:288-308`.

**Impact.** Take an Environment whose controller needs no libvirt client (for example bare-metal or vSphere only) and that pins `dependencyVersions.libvirt: 10.0.0`. validate tells the operator plan will refuse it, plan then succeeds, and the pin is silently ignored. The diagnostic is misleading either way.

**Counterevidence.** No effect is wrong: the pin has no consumer when libvirt is not installed. The test fixture for this row (host-variants) selects libvirt, so the test passes.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Word the message conditionally ("plan refuses it with lifecycle.unsupported where it is consumed"), or give Unrealized a condition predicate that is shared with the plan-side refusal, so the warning fires only when plan would refuse. Exit: A compilation test in which an Environment pins libvirt and its controller has no libvirt-client need asserts either no 'plan refuses it' wording or no api.unrealized warning, and that lifecycle.Unsupported matches it.

#### Observations

- The kind catalog matches the spec exactly: 34 kinds in canonical order, each with one schema registration.
- The retired-field, retired-value, retired-kind and unrealized tables match their spec rows one for one, and data-driven tests hold them to the data.
- The strict-YAML probe ledger covers every refusal the spec names and has an empty known-deviation ledger.
- All 12 input ceilings match. Byte reads are bounded to the remaining budget plus one, and files are re-verified after reading.
- The diagnostic sink deduplicates before counting and reserves one slot for the source-free `input.limit` sentinel.
- The dependent-check suppressions (Secret type, undecodable references, add-on expansions, unresolved provider) each have a dedicated test.
- The expansion budget is charged at inheritance, authored defaults and normalization, and stops at the first excess.
- Schema integers go through big-integer and big-rational arithmetic, so an oversized integer gets an `api.value` range refusal, not an overflow.
- The family-neutral allowlist is empty, with ceiling 0, as specified.
- The retired-kind continuation clause and block identity hashing each have dedicated tests, including the 63-byte name boundary.
- The encoder's plain-string predicate is stricter than the spec requires and also quotes C1 controls, the byte-order mark and non-BMP characters.
- The compiler folds "validate authored-only grammar" into the step after inheritance. Behavior looks equivalent because inheritance never overwrites authored values.

#### Limits

Most verdicts rest on reading source and tests at the baseline. Temporary probes were run only to confirm API-01, API-05 and API-06, and each probe file was removed afterwards. About 40 first-round clauses are unverifiable because another lane owns them: owner normalizations (MAC, IP, CIDR, Secret source literal) beyond the round-2 spot checks, context-store retention, Environment cluster-selection indexing, per-class reference resolution for endpoint and external references, and schema-wide conventions such as closed-vocabulary maps and enablement semantics. Rounds 2 and 3 examined only the clauses the critic named. IP compression was checked for Machine addresses and CIDR fields, not every IP-typed field. The cross-family node-binding check was judged generic from the code and has no cross-family test. Normalizer sorts were compared with their owning pages only for add-ons, Ceph and secrets. Inspection of add-on values maps was not traced. Whether the diagnostic sink keeps exactly 1,000 entries after reference retraction drops items once the limit has fired was not checked. `jsonschema.go` and the `cmd/bootwright` admission tests were not reviewed in depth.

#### Refuted candidates

No candidate was refuted in this lane. All twelve candidates across three rounds were confirmed or found tracked, though verifiers narrowed several: the controller-Machine half of API-09 was dropped, the ServiceSpec half of API-11 was found overstated, and the `!!float` tag half of API-05 was reduced to a presentation question.

### ENV: Environment kind (dependency versions, domains, sites, cluster selection, access defaults, kind defaults, mirrors, controller Machine, rescue, aggregate invariants) and the Secret and Entitlement kinds

Lane `api-environment-secrets`. Spec range: `specs/api/environment.md` lines 1-505; `specs/api/secrets.md` lines 1-238. Register: 323 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 10; confirmed: 10; tracked: 0; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

The audit read [specs/api/environment.md](../../specs/api/environment.md) lines 1-505 and [specs/api/secrets.md](../../specs/api/secrets.md) lines 1-238 against the code at commit f8b15669f. The core of the lane is sound. The Environment schema, the dependency-version and mirror grammars, the cluster-selection closure, the controller Machine refusals and their table, the rescue refusal, the fleet-key rule, the Secret source union, the Entitlement arm closure and the RHSM and registry checks each have cited code that matches the owning clause, and the controller refusal table is held to the code by a test that parses the spec. The discrepancies are ten, none Blocking or High: three Medium and seven Low. They cluster in three places. The first is the kind-defaults algorithm, where inheritance is driven by schema declarations: a recipient that selects a variant by an authored arm or an HTTP-only listener meets a spec sentence that the schema does not implement (ENV-06, ENV-08), and a typeless Secret default escapes grammar checks (ENV-04). The second is spec text that has gone stale against delivered work (ENV-02, ENV-07, ENV-10, and the ENV-08 sentence). The third is missing tests for safety-relevant refusals that the code does enforce today (ENV-03, ENV-05). The assessment is bounded by the ledger below: the adapter and controller-stage clauses (dependency resolution and freezing, mirror archive layout, container runtime install, registration effects, materialization) were left to other lanes and are unverified here.
