#### Observations

- The API schema in `api/v1alpha1/machines.go`, `machines_install.go`, `machines_clear.go` and `machines_erase.go` matches every field record in the spec, including the arm-specific fields.
- Suppression entries in the schema control kind-default inheritance only ([defaults.go:44](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/defaults.go)). The refusals they imply are enforced separately in `substrate.validateLibvirtAttachment` and `validateControllerTrust`.
- Several refusals the spec places on install-profile fields fire at plan in `managedos/installation`: ssh.passwordAuthentication true, FIPS Ed25519 keys, the encryption endpoint IP literal, the repository proxy credential, the recovery passphrase length and the durable root-disk form. Each is refused before registration, and the spec wording names no tier for most of them.
- A libvirt capacity-reserve disagreement between providers sharing one host and pool surfaces only as an Unknown capacity check at the apply gate, never at validate ([reserves.go:23-26](../../internal/substrate/capacity/reserves.go), [budget.go:280-282](../../internal/substrate/capacity/budget.go)). It still refuses before registration.
- Tests cover most safety refusals: BMC address grammar, host-key credential collisions, managed prefix overlap and port bounds, erase and clear targets, and the 20-attachment bound.
- The host-key cross-credential check reads cluster node logins through one layout table ([families.go:166-178](../../api/v1alpha1/families.go)), so a new cluster kind is covered once registered there.
- The virtual-media trust paths have tests that every refusal fires before any write, including the case where the manager switch overrides a read-only false device flag.
- A BMC CA bundle replaces the system trust store, and a bundle beside verification off is refused in the adapter as well as at admission.
- Erase target WWNs are compared as raw text where clear targets normalize case and the 0x prefix. Erase stays safe: serial numbers must also be distinct, the worker refuses duplicate devices, and the WWN match fails closed.
- Substrate validators keep default branches that the decoder makes unreachable (the BIOS-attribute value branch is one). They are defense in depth for Machines built in Go.
- `imageEndpointIsIPLiteral` ([encryption.go:68-76](../../internal/managedos/installation/encryption.go)) returns true when the endpoint cannot be resolved; endpoint resolution is refused elsewhere.
- In the physical erase worker, device-mapper holders are released before `probe.identify` runs (lines 446-460), with a comment that the read-only probe proves identity first. This belongs to the physical erase lane and was not judged here.

#### Limits

Adapter and execution clauses were traced only in part. Rounds one and two left about 40 register clauses unverifiable: the Ansible Redfish plugins, the Kickstart templates, sushy-tools emulator apply, network convergence and the session `trust.identity` check; round three then traced twelve of those targets. No Go tests were run in rounds one and two and none in round three by the finder; verifiers ran single tests and `bin/bootwright validate` on scratch copies of `examples/machines/lab-rhel` and `lab-baremetal`, and that binary may not be built from the baseline commit. The cross-lane owners of the bridge-use shared key, the 63-byte identity hashing and the Environment kind-default path remapping beyond `ValidatePartial` were not verified. The kind-default phase ordering was not traced end to end. The `bmcPortRange` count of `os.provided: false` Machines was not reopened. Whether the Proxy admission refuses userinfo in `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy` belongs to the Proxy lane, and the session host-key port, as against the address, was not compared with the installation evidence.

#### Refuted candidates

- MCH-06, non-scalar BIOS attribute values refused by the schema as `api.type` without the entry's position: refuted by one of three verifiers. The decoder refuses the value at the YAML node, so the diagnostic carries the entry's source line and column and names the field; the spec names no diagnostic code, and the value is refused before anything reaches the BMC. What remains is a possible improvement, an end-to-end validate test for these values, not a spec violation.

### OCA: ContainerCluster kind: shape, distribution and release, install selection, endpoints, credentials and certificates, networking, security, nodes, cross-object invariants

Lane `api-openshift`. Spec range: `specs/api/openshift-clusters.md` lines 1-534. Register: 235 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 11; confirmed: 7; tracked: 1; refuted: 3.

#### Assessment

Lane key api-openshift, code OCA. Spec range: [specs/api/openshift-clusters.md](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) lines 1-534, audited at commit f8b15669f.

#### Assessment

The ContainerCluster admission code is close to its owning spec. The schema in `api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go`, the normalization and validation in `internal/containercluster/openshift`, the topology table and its spec-parity test, the endpoint source and ownership rules, the trust projection and the credential rules were each read against the clauses of the register (235 clauses) and met them, apart from the three `vcenterCredentials` clauses that the Not yet met line tracks as B733 and the KubeVirt attachment kind proof that B87 tracks. The package tests under `internal/containercluster/openshift` pass at the baseline. No finding is Blocking or High. Seven findings are confirmed: one Medium defect, one Low defect or drift that needs an owner decision, one Low drift in the secondary-network bridge rule, three Low test gaps and one Low doc-stale record. One further discrepancy is tracked. The discrepancies cluster in two places. The first is secondary-network admission (OCA-05, OCA-10, OCA-11), where the install interface is derived from the default route alone, a reserved-name list is enforced but not specified, and three numeric and lifecycle limits have no test. The second is the boundary between spec wording and admission strictness for encryption roles (OCA-01). The remaining findings are missing tests for refusals that fail closed through another check (OCA-03, OCA-09) and milestone text in B733 that still uses the retired `openshift` source and `platform.type` vocabulary (OCA-04). Clauses at the adapter and execution boundary were not traced and are listed under Limits.

#### Confirmed findings

| ID | Severity | Kind | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [OCA-01](#oca-01) | Low | defect | Encryption role admission requires each selected role to be declared by exact name, while the spec resolves a selection through the worker and infra pool fold |
| [OCA-03](#oca-03) | Low | test-gap | No test proves the refusal of a `node` endpoint source on a cluster with more than one node |
| [OCA-04](#oca-04) | Low | doc-stale | B733 contract text still uses the retired `openshift` endpoint source and `platform.type` (tracked as B733) |
| [OCA-05](#oca-05) | Medium | defect | Secondary-network uplink checks find the install interface from the default route, so a node with no default route escapes the install-interface and br-ex VLAN refusals |
| [OCA-09](#oca-09) | Low | test-gap | No test covers the `node` endpoint source refusal for a missing or ambiguous installation address |
| [OCA-10](#oca-10) | Low | drift | Secondary-network bridge admission refuses an OVN-reserved name list and existing node interface names that the spec never states |
| [OCA-11](#oca-11) | Low | test-gap | No test proves the secondary-network MTU ceiling, the 25-entry `excludeSubnets` limit or the lifecycle-without-Enabled refusal |

#### OCA-01

**Low, defect.** Disk-encryption role admission requires every selected role to have a node of that exact role, contradicting the spec's 'resolves to at least one declared node' with infra/worker pool folding.

Owner decision required. Not tracked.

**Evidence.** [openshift-clusters.md:436-439](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) states: "An authored role selection resolves to at least one declared node. `infra` folds into the worker machine-config pool: selecting `worker` or `infra` targets that pool, and selecting both produces one configuration." Admission instead builds a set of exact node role names ([admission.go:388-390](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go)) and refuses each selected role that is not in it ([admission.go:408-411](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go)): "every selected encryption role must have a declared node". The empty selection is refused at [admission.go:404-407](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go), as the spec requires. The effect side already folds the two roles ([encryption.go:37-43](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/encryption.go) and [pushed_admission.go:65-75](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/pushed_admission.go), both testing `(role == "worker" || role == "infra") && (slices.Contains(roles, "worker") || slices.Contains(roles, "infra"))`). Two tests pin the strict rule: the "unrepresented role" case at [admission_test.go:330](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission_test.go) (`roles: [infra]` on a control-plane and worker roster) and the "encryption undeclared role" case at [admission_contract_test.go:103](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission_contract_test.go). The first was run and passes because the refusal fires: `./scripts/go test ./internal/containercluster/openshift/ -run TestReleaseCredentialsSecurityAndPlacement`.

**Impact.** Validation refuses selections that the spec reading through the fold admits: `roles: [infra]` on a roster of control-plane and worker nodes, `roles: [worker]` on a roster whose compute nodes are all `infra`, and a mixed selection such as `[controlPlane, infra]` with no `infra` node. The pool each of these selects holds declared nodes, and the projection would install it correctly. The operator has to rename the role to match the node roles. A workaround exists and nothing unsafe is admitted.

**Counterevidence.** "Resolves to at least one declared node" can be read per role, which is what the code does. The stricter rule fails closed, its remedy text names the fix, and two tests make it deliberate. No decision, delivered record or Not yet met line accepts it, so the only evidence of intent is the tests. Because of the ambiguity, the reproducing and specification reviews rated it Low drift and the refuting review rated it Medium defect. It is reported as a defect because the spec's next sentence defines resolution through the fold.

**Correction and exit evidence.** The owner chooses one rule. Either resolve each selected role through the pool fold in `validateNodes` (a selected `worker` or `infra` resolves when any worker or infra node exists) and change both pinning tests, or reword [openshift-clusters.md:437](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) to say that each selected role names a role some declared node has and that folding applies only to targeting. Exit: a unit test for `roles: [infra]` on a control-plane and worker roster that asserts the chosen outcome, the matching spec sentence, and `make docs-check`.

#### OCA-03

**Low, test-gap.** No test proves the multi-node VIP equalities (api-int equals api, ingress differs from api) or the node-source one-node refusal.

Not tracked. The finding as first stated also covered the multi-node VIP equalities; the verifiers showed that half is tested, so it is narrowed here.

**Evidence.** [openshift-clusters.md:224](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) states "`node` is valid only for a one-node cluster". Admission refuses it at [admission.go:437-439](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go) with "node endpoint source requires exactly one cluster node" at `<slot>.source.type`. No `*_test.go` file contains the message, and no test sets `source.type: node` on a roster of two or more nodes. Every node-source fixture is single-node: the helper at [admission_test.go:71-73](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission_test.go) uses a node source only when the count is 1, and [admission_test.go:308](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission_test.go) builds one node. The VIP rules of [openshift-clusters.md:248-249](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) ("`api-int` resolves the `api` address, and the `api` and `ingress` addresses differ") are enforced at [admission.go:557-562](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go) and are already pinned by field: TestInstallerEndpointPlatformOwnership sets `api-int.address` to 192.0.2.4 and `ingress.address` to the API address on a three-node derived baremetal roster and requires an issue at each field ([endpoint_ownership_test.go:93-100](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/endpoint_ownership_test.go)). That test asserts the field and not the message.

**Impact.** A regression in the one-node check could go unnoticed. The operator would then see the generic missing-address refusal at `api.address` instead of a diagnostic at the slot's source.

**Counterevidence.** A multi-node `node` cluster is also refused at the effective API address ([admission.go:538-540](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go)), because node resolution yields no address for a roster that is not one node ([admission.go:512-515](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go)). The cluster still fails closed.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a case to `admission_test.go` with a three-node roster and `source.type: node` on the API slot, asserting the issue at `$.spec.install.endpoints.api.source.type` and the "exactly one cluster node" message. Optionally assert the message text in the existing VIP cases. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/containercluster/openshift/ -run <new test>` fails when the check at admission.go:437-439 is removed.

#### OCA-04

**Low, doc-stale.** B733 contract text still uses retired vocabulary: the `openshift` endpoint source and `platform.type`.

Tracked as B733: the stale text is B733's own contract.

**Evidence.** The Not yet met line at [openshift-clusters.md:190](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) ("the vSphere arm admits no `vcenterCredentials`; tracked as B733") is accurate: the vSphere arm in [openshift_clusters.go:19-24](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go) admits only `nodeNetworking`. The item it points to describes the cluster in a retired shape. [m3.md:1704-1710](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) says the three slots "resolve from the `openshift` source only" and that a cluster behind an operator load balancer "authors `platform.type: none`"; [m3.md:1697](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) says the refusal "lifts for `platform.type: vsphere`"; the M3f outcome at [m3.md:388-389](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) repeats `platform.type: vsphere` and `platform.type: none`. The same vocabulary appears in [m3.md:1466](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) ("refusals for `openshift` sources on `none`, for a non-`openshift`") and [m3.md:1743](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) ("non-`openshift` slot on `vsphere`"). The API has an `installer` source ([openshift_clusters.go:6](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go): `enumeration("installer", "external", "loadBalancer", "node")`) and a presence-union platform with no `type` field (`choice(field("baremetal", ...), field("vsphere", ...), field("none", ...), field("external", ...))`), as [openshift-clusters.md:147](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) states.

**Impact.** An implementer of B733 who follows the item would author or test against field values that admission refuses.

**Counterevidence.** The spec page and the code agree with each other. Only milestone text is stale, and the retirement is intentional: [specs/api.md:408](../../specs/api.md) records `spec.install.platform.type` as replaced by the arm.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Reword B733, the M3f outcome and the exit evidence at m3.md:1466 to use `installer` sources and `platform: {vsphere: {}}` and `platform: {none: {}}`. Exit: `grep -n 'platform.type\|`openshift` source\|non-`openshift`' specs/milestones/m3.md` returns nothing, and `make docs-check` passes. The grep must include the "non-`openshift`" phrasings, which a narrower pattern would miss.

#### OCA-05

**Medium, defect.** Secondary-network uplink checks find the install interface from the default route, so a node with no default route escapes the install-interface and br-ex VLAN refusals.

**Evidence.** [openshift-clusters.md:390](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) requires `uplink.interface` to be an interface every node declares, "other than its install interface". [openshift-clusters.md:416-421](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) refuses a `vlan` on `br-ex` "where a node's install interface is itself a `vlan` interface". [machines.md:419-421](../../specs/api/machines.md) defines the install address: "select the unique eligible address whose interface carries a default route for that address family; if there is none, select the sole eligible address". A Machine with no default route therefore has an install interface. The code takes it from the default route alone: [network_admission.go:61](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) sets `install := defaultRouteInterface(native, familyBits)`, and [network_admission.go:131-137](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) returns the empty string unless exactly one default-route interface exists. With `install` empty, the br-ex VLAN refusal at [network_admission.go:174](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) (`interfaceType(native, install) == "vlan"`) and the install-interface arm at [network_admission.go:204](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) (`iface == install`) cannot match. The cluster MTU limit ([network_admission.go:61-66](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go)) and the br-ex MTU ceiling ([network_admission.go:173](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) and 216-217) fall back to an interface MTU of 1500 for the same reason. [node_network.go:28-37](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/node_network.go) compares the install address with the default route only when a route exists, and no OpenShift rule requires one. The tests at network_admission_test.go:160-199 cover the default-route case only. No probe was run.

**Impact.** Take a node without a default route, one static install address on a VLAN interface, `hostAddresses: bridge` and `uplink.interface` set to the interface that carries the install address. That network validates and plans, although the spec refuses it. A tagged br-ex network over a VLAN install interface is likewise admitted. In the second case OVN-Kubernetes would build br-ex on the VLAN interface and the access tag would ride inside its tag, which is the outcome the spec says admission prevents. The consequence in the second case is inferred from the spec's own rationale and was not reproduced.

**Counterevidence.** The path is narrow. OpenShift nodes almost always declare a default route, and OVN-Kubernetes builds br-ex on the default-gateway interface, so a node without one may not get a working br-ex at all. With `hostAddresses: none`, a statically addressed install interface is still refused by the "carries an address" arm. When a default route exists, `NodeNetworkIssues` already refuses an install address on any other interface, so `install` equals the install address's interface in every routed case.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Derive each node's install interface from the Machine selection, `machine.InstallAddress(bound, c).Get("interface")`, and fall back to the default-route interface only when no address is selected. Use it at network_admission.go:61, 173-174 and 204. Exit: a `network_admission_test.go` case with a Machine that has no default route and one static install address on `eth0.100`, with (a) `uplink.interface: eth0.100` and `hostAddresses: bridge` refused at `uplink.interface`, and (b) a br-ex network with `vlan: 10` refused at `vlan`.

#### OCA-09

**Low, test-gap.** No test covers the node endpoint source refusal for a missing or ambiguous installation address.

**Evidence.** [openshift-clusters.md:224-228](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) states: "Effective normalization resolves that node Machine's `network.installAddressRef` using the Machine selection rules ... Missing or ambiguous installation candidates are errors." In [admission.go:511-531](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go), when `machine.InstallAddress` returns issues, each is rewritten to `path + ".source"` with the message "node endpoint source requires one eligible static installation address" (lines 520-526). The ambiguity rule itself is tested in the machine package ([admission_test.go:106-127](../../internal/machine/admission_test.go), TestInstallAddressSelectionHasNoOrderFallback). No test file contains the cluster-side message, and the node-source cases in the openshift tests are the happy path ([admission_test.go:72](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission_test.go)) and a missing Machine ([admission_test.go:308](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission_test.go)), which returns early without issues. The per-node message at [admission.go:265-270](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go) ("node Machine requires one eligible static installation address") is untested as well. The materialized address drops its prefix at admission.go:527-528, also untested.

**Impact.** A regression in the path rewrite, the ambiguity rule as seen from the cluster, or the prefix stripping would go unnoticed. The operator would still receive the per-node diagnostic from admission.go:265-270, so the cost is a diagnostic at the wrong field.

**Counterevidence.** When the network configuration or composition is missing, `InstallAddress` returns no issue and the empty address is caught by the "installation requires an effective API endpoint address" refusal at [admission.go:539](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go). A missing candidate still fails closed.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a case to `admission_test.go`: a single-node cluster with `source.type: node` whose Machine has two eligible addresses and no `installAddressRef`, asserting the issue at `$.spec.install.endpoints.api.source` and its message, plus a case for the node entry at admission.go:265-270 and one that asserts the address is materialized without its prefix. Exit: the new tests pass and fail when the rewrite is removed.

#### OCA-10

**Low, drift.** Secondary-network bridge admission refuses an OVN-reserved name list the spec never states.

Not tracked. No D, X or delivered record accepts the discrepancy; the list is recorded only in delivery history ([m3.md:1084-1085](../../specs/milestones/m3.md)), and the rule is intentional and tested.

**Evidence.** [openshift-clusters.md:389](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) describes `uplink.bridge` as "`br-ex`, sharing the default bridge, or a new OVS bridge name: 1 to 15 bytes of letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `+` or `-`." Admission also refuses a name that `reservedOVNInterface` lists ([network_admission.go:84](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go), `bridge != "br-ex" && reservedOVNInterface(bridge)`; the list at [network_admission.go:328-337](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go)): `lo`, `br-ext`, `br-int`, `br-local`, `br-nexthop`, `br0`, `ext-vxlan`, `ext`, `int`, `tun0` and the prefixes `genev_sys_`, `k8s-`, `ovn-k8s-`, `patch-br-` and `vxlan_sys_`. It refuses a bridge name equal to an interface the node declares ([network_admission.go:210-213](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go): "bridge ... already names a node interface"). The same list refuses a reserved `uplink.interface` ([network_admission.go:204](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go)), which row 390 does not mention either. TestSecondaryNetworkReservedNames pins all sixteen names (network_admission_test.go:82-100) and passes. The behavioral spec states the reserved-name rule only in general terms for node interfaces ([openshift-clusters.md:326](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md): "an interface named as OVN-Kubernetes reserves refuses") and lists no names.

**Impact.** An operator who picks the spec-valid name `k8s-tenant` receives an "invalid or reserved bridge name" refusal, and the owning field record does not explain why. The remedy text names the cause.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal is protective, tested and explained in its remedy. The word "new" in the spec row arguably already excludes a name equal to an existing node interface. Only the unlisted OVN-Kubernetes names and prefixes are a clear gap in the spec.

**Correction and exit evidence.** List the reserved set once in its owning place and link it from [openshift-clusters.md:326](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md) and from the `uplink.bridge` and `uplink.interface` rows, and state the rule that a new bridge name must not equal a declared node interface. Exit: `make docs-check` passes and the spec names the set that `reservedOVNInterface` encodes.

#### OCA-11

**Low, test-gap.** No test proves the secondary-network MTU ceiling (at most the uplink's, or the install interface's for br-ex).

**Evidence.** [openshift-clusters.md:393](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) requires a secondary-network `mtu` "at most the uplink interface's declared MTU"; line 396 requires `ipam.excludeSubnets` "At most 25, inside `subnets`"; line 397 requires `ipam.lifecycle` to be "`Persistent`, with `Enabled` only". The code enforces all three: the MTU ceiling, measured against the install interface for br-ex, at [network_admission.go:171-173](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) and [216-218](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) ("MTU exceeds its uplink MTU"), with `interfaceMTU` defaulting to 1500 ([network_admission.go:154-162](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go)); the 25-entry limit at [network_admission.go:283-284](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) ("more than 25 excluded subnets"); the lifecycle refusal in the disabled-IPAM branch at [network_admission.go:261-262](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go) (`ipam.Has("lifecycle")`). The table test ([network_admission_test.go:20-33](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission_test.go)) has no row for any of them: its only MTU rows are "ipv6 mtu" (below 1280) and the cluster MTU case. A search of the test files for "exceeds its uplink", "uplink MTU" and "more than 25" finds nothing. The schema does not bound the list either ([openshift_clusters.go:75](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go) declares `field("excludeSubnets", array(cidr()))` with no maximum).

**Impact.** A regression could admit a localnet MTU above the uplink's into the cluster network block, which fragments or drops frames at runtime, or admit more than 25 exclusions.

**Counterevidence.** The code paths exist. The "disabled subnet" row (network_admission_test.go:29) already reaches the line 261 branch through `subnets`, so that branch is covered but the lifecycle trigger is not. The 1500 default in `interfaceMTU` is a conservative code choice that the spec does not state.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add three table rows: `mtu: 9000` on br-ex with an install interface that declares no MTU or 1500; 26 `excludeSubnets`; and `ipam` with `lifecycle: Persistent` and no `mode: Enabled`, declaring only the lifecycle so that it proves that trigger. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/containercluster/openshift/ -run TestSecondaryNetwork` passes with the new rows and each row fails when its check is removed.

#### OCA-02

**Low, drift.** Cluster MTU range and the default-route-MTU-minus-100 refusal are enforced but absent from the owning spec. Re-judged from tracked: B719 (specs/milestones/m3.md:1131-1136) lists only MachineConfig projection and Secret-part substitution as open, and says X123 delivered the typed OVN settings. Its contract line at m3.md:1165-1167 ("A declared cluster MTU must be at least 100 below each node's default-route interface MTU") is the delivered rule the code enforces, not a record that the spec still lacks it. specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:358 does not give the 576..65536 range or the minus-100 refusal, and no spec outside milestones states either one, so the spec is stale against code that changed on purpose.

**Evidence.** Spec 358: "`ovnKubernetesConfig` | object | no | absent; `mtu`, `gatewayConfig.routingViaHost`, `gatewayConfig.ipForwarding` (`Restricted` or `Global`), each written into the install-time `Network` only when set." No range and no limit are stated. Code openshift_clusters.go:72 `field("mtu", integer("576", "65536"))`; network_admission.go:63-65 `limit := interfaceMTU(native, install) - 100; if mtu > limit { ... "cluster MTU %d exceeds the default-route interface MTU minus 100"`. m3.md:1165: "A declared cluster MTU must be at least 100 below each node's default-route interface MTU (1,500 when undeclared)". Spec: `specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:358`. Code: `api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go:72`, `internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go:42`, `internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go:61-67`, `specs/milestones/m3.md:1165-1167`.

**Impact.** An operator reading the API spec cannot predict a refusal that admission emits. The rule's single owner is a delivery record, not the spec.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal itself is correct and names its remedy. B719 is in progress, so the rule's text exists in a tracked item, just not in the spec.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add the 576..65536 range and the 'at most each node's default-route interface MTU minus 100 (1500 when undeclared)' rule to the `ovnKubernetesConfig` row, or as a sentence after the table, in specs/api/openshift-clusters.md. Exit: Spec text names the rule; `make docs-check`; the existing MTU refusal test continues to pass.

#### Observations

- `./scripts/go test ./internal/containercluster/openshift/...` passes at f8b15669f.
- The platform presence union is enforced generically (schema_validation.go validateArms) as api.invariant at `$.spec.install.platform`, and an inherited default never introduces a second arm (defaults.go blocked arms).
- Endpoint address ownership (endpoint_ownership.go) covers other clusters, Machines, managed libvirt attachments, emulated BMC bind, managed services (bind, endpoint and addressRef) and LoadBalancer binds. Wildcard binds are excluded, as the spec says.
- Kind defaults are inherited before ValidateAuthored and before built-in defaults (phases.go:104,132). So `additionalTrustBundleRefs: []` clears inheritance, and an omitted field still inherits.
- Schema Suppress drops inherited endpoint addresses for node and loadBalancer sources, and inherited bootArtifacts in connected mode, so a default cannot trip the authored-address refusal.
- Image-only releases skip the control-plane count rule at admission and are refused at plan (selection.go:118-120). A test pins this intentionally.
- The KubeVirt baremetal-platform installer-source refusal (pushed_admission.go:24-31) duplicates the generic VIP-platform refusal (admission.go:573-575) for the same field, so an operator sees two issues for one fault.
- After round 1 the critic noted that about 20 clauses are unverifiable, all at the adapter or execution boundary (the SSH key projection, Always trust, the bridge move, TPM2 effect checks and platform.external), and that the registries non-atomic merge reads as a possible conflict with the spec's "complete policy" and "do not implicitly create each other" clauses. Spot checks confirmed these are met: infra folding in the vTPM check (pushed_admission.go:65-75), the enableOn mapping after the roles default (admission.go:32-33, agentinstall/encryption.go), node labels and taints validation (admission.go:392-399), the authored-address ban (admission.go:204-216) and the VIP equality checks (admission.go:554-562).
- Kind-default inheritance runs before ValidateAuthored (phases.go:94-131), and Suppression rules strip an inherited endpoint address when the authored source is node or loadBalancer, so the authored-address refusal cannot be bypassed through defaults.
- A wildcard LoadBalancer bind claims no address (endpoint_ownership.go:26), but an endpoint resolved to a wildcard is still refused by machine-network containment at `.address`.
- The agent path rejects malformed or multi-line SSH public material before the adapter, naming the Secret (internal/secrets/material/authorized_key.go:19-20).
- Machine binding uniqueness is enforced kind-agnostically through containercluster.MemberMachines in compilation/selection.go:49-60.
- After round 2 the critic again found about 17 clauses unverifiable at the execution and adapter boundary (post-install labels, taints and bridge moves, trust under Always, TPM2 effect checks, the nodeSSH split form with the public-only SSH refusal). Spot checks confirmed the OKD channel and FIPS refusals (admission.go:359-363), the bridge grammar (lexical.go:45), the numeric limits for secondary networks and the enableOn mapping (encryption.go:16-43).
- The OKD distribution is refused wholesale at agentinstall selection (selection.go:115-116); B748 tracks it as parked through the refusal row in specs/openshift-coverage.md:63.
- Additional trust projection uses only the cluster's own additionalTrustBundleRefs; Proxy and Registry trust never leak into install-config additionalTrustBundle (projection.go:66-73).
- TPM2 enforcement is layered: admission refuses a KubeVirt profile with no persistent vTPM, selection refuses a profile without tpm, and effect-time preboot or Redfish checks require a positive TPM 2.0 read.
- Node placement after install patches only what each node lacks, guarded by test operations, and never removes another manager's labels or taints.
- The adapter caps placement at 64 labels and 64 taints per node (containercluster_node_placement.py:24,45) with no admission bound. It is a narrow effect-time failure and is not reported as a finding.

#### Limits

Reading covered admission and normalization in `api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go` and `internal/containercluster/openshift`, the topology tests, and the parts of `agentinstall/selection.go` and `encryption.go` that the clauses lead to. Adapter and execution behavior was not traced: SSH authorized-key projection, the post-install bridge move, TPM2 effect checks, trust propagation, post-install placement wiring and the agent-install role's `argument_specs`. Probe tests could not be added because tracked files are read-only, so the test-gap findings and OCA-01 and OCA-05 rest on code reading and search; the only probes run were existing tests. Unique node binding, Machine and provider rules and the openshift-clusters.md selection table belong to other lanes and were not judged. The vSphere and B733 targets were out of scope for round 3. Round 2 and round 3 examined only the critic's targets and did not re-read the full spec range.

#### Refuted candidates

- OCA-06, topology admission skips the general control-plane count rule when `release.version` is absent. Two of three reviews found the code as described ([topology.go:70](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/topology.go) guards the count on `version != ""`), but the decisive review showed the spec ties the count to "the declared release" ([openshift-clusters.md:498-499](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md)) and says an image-only release gets only the release-independent rules (lines 77-79); selection refuses every image-only cluster, so the skip is intended and pinned by a test.
- OCA-07, `install.registries` inherits field by field, so a cluster that authors only `imageDigestSources` gains a default mirror. The behavior follows the general inheritance rule for non-atomic records (environment.md rule 4); the spec phrase "do not implicitly create each other" concerns derivation, not inheritance from an explicit Environment default, and a registries-specific test would pin behavior the general rule already decides.
- OCA-08, no test proves "the installer owns all three endpoint slots or none". TestInstallerEndpointPlatformOwnership sets only the API slot to `installer` on a three-node roster and requires an issue at `$.spec.install.endpoints` ([endpoint_ownership_test.go:86-91](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/endpoint_ownership_test.go)); a mutation that disabled the check made it fail.

### CEA: Storage kinds: references, CephCluster field record, complete-graph invariants

Lane `api-ceph`. Spec range: `specs/api/ceph.md` lines 1-486. Register: 235 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 11; confirmed: 11; tracked: 0; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

Lane key `api-ceph`, code `CEA`. Specs audited: [specs/api/ceph.md:1-486](../../specs/api/ceph.md), at commit f8b15669f. The register holds 235 clauses; three rounds examined them.

The lane is largely sound. Of the 210 clauses the first round examined, 177 are met, 7 are partially met, 2 are not met and 24 could not be judged from this page alone (they belong to adapter, execution and planning lanes). References, Normalization and the listener, VRRP, stretch, SMB-address and object-user checks of the complete-graph invariants match the code and carry exact-message tests. No finding is Blocking or High. The discrepancies cluster in three places. First, the CephCluster page lags the code: stale version numbers, a stale bucket-name limit, a binding list that omits oauth2-proxy, and a package-repository rule that omits the query and traversal refusals (CEA-01, CEA-02, CEA-04, CEA-07). Second, admitted input that planning cannot realize: `spec.mgrModules` and `singleHostDefaults` refuse at planning with no recorded row (CEA-03), and an `nvmeof` service with `enable_auth: true` plans into an unrealized-binding refusal although the native record and a delivered record require it (CEA-08). Third, the NFS export security flavor is left to the native default, which contradicts the page's "sys security only" invariant (CEA-10). Safety-relevant admission rules for cluster SSH key separation have no test (CEA-05). Nothing was tracked beforehand and nothing was refuted. The coverage is bounded by the ledger below: the SMB graph rules were skimmed, and adapter behavior was not examined.

| ID | Severity | Kind | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CEA-01](#cea-01) | Low | doc-stale | specs/api/ceph.md names request and evidence version numbers (v11, v2, v3) that no longer match the Go constants |

#### CEA-01

**Low, doc-stale.** specs/api/ceph.md names request and evidence version numbers (v11, v2, v3) that no longer match the Go constants.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:270-274](../../specs/api/ceph.md) reads "Core request v11 refuses continuation of v10 operations, image request v2 and package request v2 refuse continuation of older operations, and core evidence v3 and host request v2 refuse continuation of operations an earlier build made". The constants differ: [requests.go:19](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go) `const Version = "ceph-core-v41"`, [image.go:22](../../internal/storage/ceph/image.go) `ImageVersion = "ceph-image-v4"`, [package_sources.go:14](../../internal/storage/ceph/package_sources.go) `PackageVersion = "ceph-packages-v3"`, [evidence.go:14](../../internal/storage/ceph/evidence.go) `EvidenceVersion = "ceph-core-evidence-v14"`, [host.go:21](../../internal/storage/ceph/host.go) `HostVersion = "ceph-host-v13"`. [host.go:22](../../internal/storage/ceph/host.go) also defines `HostEvidenceVersion = "ceph-host-evidence-v4"`, which the paragraph's host evidence wording covers. The repository rule at [.claude/rules/guidance.md:10-11](../../.claude/rules/guidance.md) says "A spec names the Go constant of an internal version, never its number."

**Impact.** A reader judging whether an old context can continue gets version numbers that the code does not carry, so the clause cannot be checked against the code. No operator-visible behavior is wrong.

**Counterevidence.** The behavioral rule still matches: [specs/api/ceph.md:273-277](../../specs/api/ceph.md) states, without numbers, that an operation an earlier build planned is finished or destroyed with that build. Only the first sentence is stale. The backlog records later version moves.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Delete the first sentence or replace the numbers with the constant names (`Version`, `ImageVersion`, `PackageVersion`, `EvidenceVersion`, `HostVersion`, `HostEvidenceVersion`) and state the rule once. Exit: `make docs-check` passes and `grep -n 'v11\|request v2\|evidence v3' specs/api/ceph.md` returns nothing. To reproduce, run `grep -n 'Version = "' internal/storage/ceph/requests.go internal/storage/ceph/image.go internal/storage/ceph/package_sources.go internal/storage/ceph/evidence.go internal/storage/ceph/host.go`.

#### CEA-02

**Low, doc-stale.** Complete-graph invariants still say a bucket name has 3 to 44 characters; the field record and code use 3 to 63.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:427-431](../../specs/api/ceph.md) keeps "its name has 3 to 44 characters" (the decisive line is 428). The field record says "a DNS label of 3 to 63 characters under the one name rule" at [specs/ceph-resources.md:1626](../../specs/ceph-resources.md), and its admission text at [specs/ceph-resources.md:1652-1655](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) refuses only "a name shorter than 3 characters, the S3 minimum". [specs/api/ceph.md:17](../../specs/api/ceph.md) says "no limit depends on a block prefix". The code at [object.go:188-192](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/object.go) checks only `if len(name) < 3`; the 63 upper bound comes from the shared name rule at [jsonschema.go:43](../../api/v1alpha1/jsonschema.go) (`"maxLength": 63`).

**Impact.** The two owning pages contradict each other. A bucket name of 45 to 63 characters is admitted, which is the intended behavior, while this page says it refuses.

**Counterevidence.** The code and the field record agree with each other and with D183 (Q86 answered b, [backlog.md:3340](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)), which removed the block-prefix budget behind the 44 limit. Only this page's sentence is stale. [m2.md:858](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) and [m2.md:1736](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) record the earlier rule as delivered history and stay unchanged.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Change [specs/api/ceph.md:428](../../specs/api/ceph.md) to "its name is at least 3 characters (a DNS label of at most 63 under the one name rule)" and keep the field-record link. Exit: `grep -n '3 to 44' specs/api/ceph.md` returns nothing.

#### CEA-04

**Low, doc-stale.** The list of service bindings planning realizes leaves out oauth2-proxy bindings that the code realizes.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:120-124](../../specs/api/ceph.md) says a `spec.serviceBindings` entry is left to the gateway block, or to the credential bindings of a grafana or snmp-gateway service and the TLS binding of the management gateway, and that "any other entry refuses at planning". The same page says at lines 109-111 that oauth2-proxy realizes through the management gateway unit. The code realizes its bindings: [service_unit.go:445-459](../../internal/storage/ceph/service_unit.go) accepts `grafana`, `snmp-gateway`, `mgmt-gateway` and `oauth2-proxy`, the leaf table at [service_unit.go:419-423](../../internal/storage/ceph/service_unit.go) lists the oauth2-proxy leaves, and the refusal message at [service_unit.go:459-462](../../internal/storage/ceph/service_unit.go) names "the credential, TLS and CA bundle bindings of its oauth2-proxy". The caller is [requests.go:374-378](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go). The owning leaf table is [ceph-native-api.md:846-850](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md): `client_secret`, `cookie_secret`, `ssl_cert`, `ssl_key` and the `custom_configs/0` CA bundle.

**Impact.** Read literally, the page says a valid oauth2-proxy binding refuses at planning. The code plans it. There is no behavioral consequence.

**Counterevidence.** The owning native page documents the leaves, and the code's own message lists them. Only this summary sentence is stale.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add the oauth2-proxy credential, TLS and CA bundle bindings to the management gateway unit clause at [specs/api/ceph.md:122-124](../../specs/api/ceph.md). Exit: the sentence names oauth2-proxy and matches the `unrealizedBinding` message.

#### CEA-05

**Medium, test-gap.** Cluster SSH key separation refusals in CephCluster admission have no test.

**Evidence.** [topology.go:114-133](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go) refuses a cluster SSH key that equals the fleet install key ("cluster SSH key must differ from the fleet install key", line 118), equals a Machine access key ("cluster SSH key must differ from Machine access keys", line 123), or is reused by another CephCluster ("each storage cluster requires a distinct cluster SSH key", line 129). The spec requirement is [specs/api/environment.md:230-233](../../specs/api/environment.md): "The fleet key must differ from every Machine access key and every `CephCluster.spec.cephadm.clusterSSH.keyRef`. Each cluster SSH key must also differ from every Machine-authored private key." A search of every test file for these messages finds none. [fleet_key_admission_test.go](../../internal/environment/fleet_key_admission_test.go) covers the Environment and Machine side only, [hostkey_credentials_test.go:27](../../internal/machine/hostkey_credentials_test.go) covers the host-key credential collision, and the cephcluster tests set `clusterSSH` without a `keyRef`.

**Impact.** The fleet-versus-cluster check exists only on the CephCluster side, since the Environment admission does not read cluster keys. A regression could let one key work both as effect material on Ceph hosts and as an operator access credential with no failing test.

**Counterevidence.** The refusals are present and correct today. [specs/api/ceph.md:349-350](../../specs/api/ceph.md) only says cluster-login declarations agree, and the per-cluster distinctness rule at topology.go:127-132 has no spec clause. The spec says "Machine-authored private key" while the code checks only `access.ssh.auth.privateKeyRef`.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a table test in `internal/storage/cephcluster` that drives validation through the three collisions and asserts the field, message and remedy. State the per-cluster distinctness rule in [specs/api/environment.md](../../specs/api/environment.md) or the CephCluster field record, and settle whether other Machine-authored private key fields must be checked. Exit: the test passes and fails when topology.go:116-132 is removed. Reproduce the gap with `grep -rn 'cluster SSH key must differ' --include=*_test.go internal cmd`.

Also reported as [ENV-03](#env-03); the entries are merged here.
#### CEA-06

**Low, drift.** With no networks.publicCIDRs, the 'declared public CIDR' rules quietly use the topology Machines' address prefixes instead.

**Evidence.** The ingress virtual IP, SMB public address, management gateway virtual IP and service-network rules require the address inside a declared public CIDR ([specs/api/ceph.md:367-371](../../specs/api/ceph.md), [specs/api/ceph.md:444-447](../../specs/api/ceph.md), [specs/ceph-native-api.md:445](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md), [specs/ceph-native-api.md:488-495](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md)). `declaredPublicNetworks` at [services.go:87-109](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/services.go) returns the masked `publicCIDRs`, and when none are declared it returns the masked address prefix of every topology node's Machine ([services.go:94-107](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/services.go): `if len(out) != 0 { return out }` then the node loop). `publicCIDRs` is optional in the schema ([storage.go:101](../../api/v1alpha1/storage.go)). The fallback reaches the ingress check ([native_ingress.go:222-253](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/native_ingress.go)), `gatewayVirtualIP` ([native_ingress.go:264](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/native_ingress.go)), the SMB check ([smb.go:697-707](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/smb.go)), [observability.go:211-214](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/observability.go), the keepalived router networks ([endpoints.go:360](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/endpoints.go)) and `serviceNetworks` ([services.go:110-126](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/services.go)). No spec text states the substitution, and every cephcluster test fixture declares `publicCIDRs` ([admission_test.go:51](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/admission_test.go)).

**Impact.** A cluster without `publicCIDRs` admits a virtual IP in any network a Ceph host is addressed on, including one that is not the public network, and the diagnostics still point at `spec.networks.publicCIDRs`. `serviceNetworks` and the management gateway check skip the test entirely when the declared list is empty, so with no CIDRs and no Machine prefixes those addresses pass unchecked.

**Counterevidence.** The fallback looks deliberate and approximates the public network cephadm derives. The other rules still apply: no Machine address, not the network or broadcast address, no reuse. The MON address rule is skipped when `publicCIDRs` is empty ([topology.go:200-203](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go)), which is related but is a separate gap against [specs/api/ceph.md:455-456](../../specs/api/ceph.md).

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either state in the field record that an omitted `publicCIDRs` makes the topology Machines' address prefixes the declared public networks, and adjust the diagnostics, or require `publicCIDRs` whenever a service with a virtual IP is declared. Exit: the spec sentence exists and a test covers a virtual IP with `publicCIDRs` omitted, or admission refuses it.

#### CEA-07

**Low, doc-stale.** packageRepository refuses a query string, which its field rule does not mention.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:191-193](../../specs/api/ceph.md) says `packageRepository` is "an HTTPS RPM repository without userinfo or fragment, of at most 1798 bytes". The grammar at [lexical.go:119-121](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go) also requires `u.RawQuery == ""` and `plainURLPath(u.Path)`, which refuses "." and ".." segments and a backslash ([lexical.go:157-164](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go)). The sibling `packageRepositoryKey` rule at [specs/api/ceph.md:209-212](../../specs/api/ceph.md) already lists "userinfo, query, fragment or traversal". The refusals are pinned by `TestPackageRepositoryAdmitsOnlyWhatTheGuestAcquisitionFetches` ([lexical_test.go:273-277](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical_test.go)).

**Impact.** A repository URL with a query or a dot segment is refused although the field rule does not say so. The refusal is the safe direction; the spec is incomplete.

**Counterevidence.** The code behavior is intended and tested, and no other spec section sets a general rule for the field.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Change [specs/api/ceph.md:191-192](../../specs/api/ceph.md) to "without userinfo, query, fragment, dot segments or backslashes". Exit: the text matches lexical.go:119-121 and plainURLPath.

#### CEA-08

**Medium, defect.** An admitted nvmeof service with enable_auth: true and its five required mTLS bindings refuses every plan of its cluster as an unrealized service binding.

**Evidence.** [ceph-native-api.md:528](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md) says `enable_auth` "true requires the five protected gateway mTLS service bindings", and [ceph-native-api.md:982-990](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md) says "For `enable_auth`, all five native leaves are mandatory service bindings". [m2.md:1001-1003](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) records as delivered that "`enable_auth: true` uses the explicit certificate mode and its declared custody bindings". Admission requires the bindings: [native_bindings.go:32-36](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/native_bindings.go) declares the five `nvmeof` slots as required when `enable_auth` holds, and [nvmeof.go:66-80](../../internal/storage/ceph/nvmeof.go) freezes them into the unit through `gatewayBindings`. Planning refuses first: [requests.go:374-378](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go) returns `unrealizedBinding(ref)` unless `gatewayExecuted` or `unitBinding` holds. `gatewayExecuted` ([services.go:198-214](../../internal/storage/ceph/services.go)) has cases only for `ingress` and `rgw`. `unitBinding` ([service_unit.go:445-457](../../internal/storage/ceph/service_unit.go)) accepts only `grafana`, `snmp-gateway`, `mgmt-gateway` and `oauth2-proxy`, so `nvmeofLeaves` ([service_unit.go:426-442](../../internal/storage/ceph/service_unit.go)) is unreachable. [specs/api/ceph.md:119-123](../../specs/api/ceph.md) matches the code and says "any other entry refuses at planning". The refusal message at [service_unit.go:459-462](../../internal/storage/ceph/service_unit.go) names no nvmeof binding. Every `nvmeof` planning test uses `enable_auth: false`; [nvmeof_test.go:74](../../internal/storage/ceph/nvmeof_test.go) and :228 call `nvmeofUnits` directly and bypass `baseRequest`.

**Impact.** An operator who follows the example README (`libvirt-5-nodes-ceph-nvmeof`, lines 22-23) and sets `enable_auth: true` with all five bindings passes `validate`, and every plan of that CephCluster and its children then refuses with "Bootwright does not realize the service binding of nvmeof.`<id>`". The certificate mode recorded as delivered under X58 can never plan.

**Counterevidence.** The default and example path, `enable_auth: false`, has no bindings and plans. B480 still awaits operator acceptance, so the path is not live-qualified. The pages contradict each other, so which side is wrong is an owner decision. The phrase "`enable_auth` (`false` only)" at [m2.md:1014](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) sits under historical admission delivery and is out of date as well.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either add `nvmeof` to the realized binding types (its leaves are in `nvmeofLeaves`), list the nvmeof mTLS bindings at [specs/api/ceph.md:119-123](../../specs/api/ceph.md) and update the refusal message, or refuse `enable_auth: true` at admission and correct ceph-native-api.md:528 and 982-990, m2.md:1001-1003 and the example README. Until then a "Not yet met" line tracked by an item is missing at ceph-native-api.md:982. Exit: a planning test in `internal/storage/ceph` with `enable_auth: true` and the five bindings that plans the unit and the subsystem with the bindings frozen, or an admission test that refuses `enable_auth: true`.

Also reported as [CPN-01](#cpn-01); the entries are merged here.
#### CEA-09

**Low, test-gap.** No test proves that the packageRepositoryKey origin check compares hosts case-insensitively.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:209-213](../../specs/api/ceph.md) requires "Its scheme, host (case-insensitive) and effective port must match the repository; omitted HTTPS ports mean 443." `samePackageOrigin` ([topology.go:321-334](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go)) returns `strings.ToLower(u.Hostname()) + ":" + port`, with one caller at [topology.go:77](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go). The table in `TestPackageRepositoryKeyIsRequiredAndSharesRepositoryOrigin` ([repository_trust_test.go:33-42](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/repository_trust_test.go)) has the cases missing, mirror, explicit default port, foreign host and foreign port. No case differs only by host letter case. [storage_trust_test.go:25](../../api/v1alpha1/storage_trust_test.go) covers the lexical refusals (query, fragment, userinfo, traversal, control characters) and not the origin comparison.

**Impact.** A regression that dropped `ToLower` would refuse a valid mixed-case mirror key URL and no test would fail. There is no safety consequence, because it fails closed.

**Counterevidence.** The current code is correct.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a case with the repository fixed as lowercase `packages.example.test` and the key `https://PACKAGES.Example.test/ibm.asc`, expected admitted. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/storage/cephcluster/ -run TestPackageRepositoryKeyIsRequiredAndSharesRepositoryOrigin` passes with the new case.

#### CEA-10

**Medium, drift.** An omitted CephNFSExport native.sectype is admitted, so NFS-Ganesha's default security flavors (including AUTH_NONE) apply instead of sys only. Re-verification narrowed the consequence: NFS-Ganesha's default SecType is (none, sys), so omission adds AUTH_NONE only, which grants nothing beyond what AUTH_SYS already allows the same client addresses; the shipped NFS examples omit sectype, and ceph-resources.md:988 and :1001-1002 specify the omission, so this is one spec contradicting another.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:434](../../specs/api/ceph.md) states the invariant that an export's "native record is closed and serves NFSv4 over TCP with `sys` security only". The field record treats the two members differently. For `protocols`, [ceph-resources.md:986](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) refuses omission because "an omitted list would serve NFSv3 and NFSv4". For `sectype`, [ceph-resources.md:988](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) says "`[sys]` when present", with default "None" and "native `none` is not a supported option", and [ceph-resources.md:1000-1002](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) says `protocols`, `sectype` and a subvolume binding's `path` are never added. The code follows the field record: [nfs_export.go:191-193](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export.go) refuses only an omitted `protocols`; [nfs_export.go:62-70](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export.go) refuses only an authored krb5 token, and its remedy says "set spec.native.sectype: [sys] or omit spec.native.sectype"; [normalization.go:172](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/normalization.go) defaults transports and not `sectype`; [nfs_export.go:71-73](../../internal/storage/ceph/nfs_export.go) sends `sectype` only `if native.Has("sectype")`; the adapter at [ceph_native_nfs.py:47](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_nfs.py) lists it as optional and [ceph_native_nfs.py:273](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_nfs.py) accepts `"sectype" not in native`. The test at nfs_export_test.go:256-258 pins that normalization does not freeze `sectype`. The NFS-Ganesha default list for an omitted `SecType` includes `none` alongside `sys`; this comes from the native tool and cannot be verified from this tree.

**Impact.** If the default holds, an export written without `sectype`, which the remedy itself suggests, accepts AUTH_NONE (and krb5 flavors if the host ever has them) from allowed clients. That contradicts the sys-only invariant and the statement that native `none` is unsupported.

**Counterevidence.** Client address lists still limit who can mount, and an authored `none` or krb5 token refuses ([nfs_export_test.go:295-300](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export_test.go)). If the cephadm ganesha configuration or the manager NFS module sets a `sys` default, the impact disappears. This is a conflict between the invariant at specs/api/ceph.md:434 and the field record, with the code following the field record.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Decide in the spec first. Either default `sectype` to `[sys]`, freeze it, send it in the native request and drop it from the never-added list, or refuse an omitted `sectype` as `protocols` does. Then change ceph-resources.md:988, ceph-resources.md:1000-1002, the remedy at nfs_export.go:69 and the test at nfs_export_test.go:256. Exit: a cephcluster test that admits an export without `sectype` and asserts the effective native record is `[sys]`, or that it refuses at `$.spec.native.sectype`. Verify the native default on a real Ganesha before choosing.

#### CEA-11

**Low, improvement.** An unknown spec.mgrModules entry refuses at unindexed $.spec.mgrModules while every other module refusal names its entry.

Arbitrated: two reviewers disagreed on kind, and the spec sets no location for this refusal, so it is not a defect.

**Evidence.** The loop at [services.go:53-66](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/services.go) refuses the nfs family (line 58), smb (line 60) and mirroring (line 62) at `indexed("$.spec.mgrModules", i)`, and prometheus through `prometheusModule` ([observability.go:81](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/observability.go)). The final branch at line 64 calls `a.invalid("$.spec.mgrModules", "manager module requires its qualified service owner", ...)`, and `invalid` ([admission.go:32](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/admission.go)) only wraps `a.issue` with the field as given. [specs/api/ceph.md:131-132](../../specs/api/ceph.md) says "every other module refuses until its service owner" and sets no location. [ceph-native-api.md:498-503](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md) says nfs, prometheus and mirroring refuse "at its entry", which the code honors.

**Impact.** With several modules authored, the operator cannot tell from the field path which entry refused, and two unknown modules produce issues with the same field and message.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fires as the spec requires, and [native_nfs_test.go:108-111](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/native_nfs_test.go) proves it while pinning the unindexed path.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Use `indexed("$.spec.mgrModules", i)` at services.go:64 and name the module in the message, and change the assertion at native_nfs_test.go:108-111. Exit: a test with two unknown modules asserts one issue at each of `$.spec.mgrModules[0]` and `[1]`.

VRRP (endpoints.go:356-406) is cross-cluster, includes virtual_interface_networks and defaults to 50, and endpoints_test.go:92-123 tests it. Ingress requires virtual_ip (storage_native.go:38) and frontend_port and monitor_port for HAProxy (native_ingress.go:103-107), so no listener drops out. The clash message names the host and the other listener, and endpoints_test.go:188-197 covers range listeners. The tiebreaker refusals (topology.go:279-300) use ResolveServicePlacement, so label and host_pattern placement are covered. The stretch HA count rule is in stretch_services.go:85-96. NVMe-oF, NFS, NFS-export and SMB stretch refusals are tested at nvmeof_test.go:216 and stretch_test.go:294-303. Reserving the messenger range on the tiebreaker matches 'every storage host'. The bucket-name ceiling is already a known finding and is not repeated. |
| round 3: ## CephCluster | 89-91, 110-114, 127-134, 218, 263-264, 278-280 | 12 | 12 | 11 | 1 | 0 | 0 | External management: normalizeCluster returns before any managed default (normalization.go:57-60). partial.go:57-58 forbids each managed field at $.spec.`<field>` through forbid (admission.go:55-63), and the schema suppresses them (storage.go:105). Frozen request: ClusterSSHTransport (requests.go:348-353, requests_test.go:85), PackageRepositoryKey with its default (requests.go:343-346), and Delegated services carried only in the core Request, not in ClusterScope or the host request. Host request: no resource payload (host_test.go:524, :554). Retired fields refuse with their replacement path or reason (native.go:637-714). mgrModules: each case is refused and tested; the unindexed catch-all is partially met (CEA-11). |

The same-service exemption at endpoints.go:317 is backed by in-service checks (native_ingress.go:118-135 for distinct ingress ports, observability.go:147 for alertmanager 9094), and loki port 8080 is admitted by design (b479_listeners_test.go:80). #### Observations

- Root admission is layered well: lexicalValues, then intrinsic (also used for partial defaults), then cluster() or per-kind graph checks. External clusters forbid every CephManagedFields entry at its path (partial.go:57-58), and Suppress stops kind defaults from introducing those fields (compilation/defaults.go:44-54).
- The listener registry matches the spec's port table closely, including the 9283, 29443, loki and promtail fixed listeners, NFS QoS 31311 and the NFS HAProxy peer 1024 default. Same-service self-clashes are exempted only for ingress, alertmanager, loki and promtail.
- packageRepository's 1798-byte bound is derived as 2048 - len('/repodata/') - 240 ([lexical.go:200](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go)), and samePackageOrigin compares lowercased host and effective port, defaulting to 443 (topology.go:321-335).
- No version allowlist exists: Supported() only checks NativeVersion bounds, a nonempty image base and the verifiedTunnel transport (internal/storage/ceph/contracts.go:61-63).
- clusterAccess requires clusterSSH.keyRef unless the user is root (topology.go:108-110); the spec never states this exemption.
- Stretch child refusals (NFS export, SMB) run in Validate before the kind switch (admission.go:163-166); nvmeof is refused as deferred to B935 (nvmeof.go:57-58).
- The code the lane lists as root files under internal/storage (admission.go, normalization.go and others) sits in internal/storage/cephcluster/.
- The listener registry, the VRRP check and the SMB address checks all compare across every CephCluster in the catalog, which matches the "any CephCluster" wording.
- Tests for listener-clash diagnostics assert the full message and remedy text, including range listeners and the NFS QoS listener.
- Planning-time refusals for auxiliary images, both missing and unneeded, include CephSMBResource-driven samba images, and auxiliary_test.go:252 tests them.
- nvmeofLeaves (service_unit.go:426) and the nvmeof unit's Bindings field are unreachable at the baseline because baseRequest refuses first (CEA-08).
- Spot checks confirmed as met: the stretch 4/2, erasure and placement-policy refusals (pools.go:138-140, 210-211, 265-267, 306-307), the packageRepositoryTrustBundleRef caBundle type and its required repository (storage.go:98, topology.go:83-86), the reserved native transport refusal (topology.go:111-112), ibm.packages.source vendor only (storage.go:89), the osd_memory_target range (config.go:63) and the mgrModules refusals (services.go:53-66).
- Most refusals in this lane have exact-message tests: listeners (b479_listeners_test.go), serial OSD paths, object users and mgrModules.
- The host request takes ClusterScope only; the delegated auxiliary services list (name and hosts) lives only in the core Request, as the spec requires.
- oauth2-proxy always reserves 4180 whatever https_address names, which matches the spec wording.
- When networks.publicCIDRs is empty, the MON address proof returns without checking (topology.go:200-203); this is related to CEA-06 and is not a separate finding.
- The verifiers noted, outside this lane, that examples/full-platforms/multidc-platform/clusters/ceph/cluster.yaml:63-66 declares mgrModules balancer, pg_autoscaler and devicehealth, which admission refuses (services.go:63). The examples lane owns it.

#### Limits

No test or probe runs were part of the finding rounds: every judgment comes from reading the code and tests at f8b15669f, except that one verifier ran `./scripts/go test ./internal/storage/cephcluster/ -run NFSExport`, which passed. How planning treats an externally managed CephCluster in Capability.Unsupported was not traced, and which planning lane owns it is unclear. The per-kind field records of the ceph-resources pages were not checked beyond the references and invariants this page owns. Adapter and Ansible behavior behind the execution and adapter clauses was not examined: call home, key fingerprint pinning, trust bundle use, OSD effective config verification, digest freezing. The SMB graph rules (public addresses, share and subvolume exclusivity, identity resolution) were only skimmed. Round 2 and round 3 examined only the targets the critic named. The nvmeof refusal was traced by reading the code and its history; no probe test was run because one would need a test file inside the repository. The core-request listing and the request-level evidence for monitoring and management-gateway units were checked only through the routing code, not the frozen request goldens. The NFS-Ganesha default security flavors are a native fact this tree cannot prove, so CEA-10 has medium confidence.

#### Refuted candidates

None. All eleven candidates across the three rounds were confirmed (round 1: seven; round 2: two; round 3: two, one of them settled by arbitration to kind improvement).

### ADA: ClusterAddon, ClusterAddonProfile and ClusterAddonBinding kinds, admission diagnostics, built-in package schemas, MetalLB pool admission, normalization

Lane `api-addons`. Spec range: `specs/api/addons.md` lines 1-697. Register: 336 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 12; confirmed: 12; tracked: 0; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

Lane key api-addons, code ADA. Specs examined: [specs/api/addons.md:1-697](../../specs/api/addons.md). Baseline: commit f8b15669f, 2026-11-05.

#### Assessment

The lane is largely sound. Of the 336 register entries, the ledger records the kind schemas, the OLM arm, the executable-shape admission, the binding and ordering rules, the registry reader proof, the nmstate, kubevirt, metallb and gitops packages, and normalization as met in code, with tests that pin most pool and shape refusals. Twelve discrepancies were confirmed and none is blocking or high. One is Medium: the MetalLB held-address check does not see the virtual addresses a CephCluster declares (ADA-09). The other eleven are Low and cluster in three groups. Seven concern diagnostic quality where the refusal fires correctly but the text, field or count departs from the spec table (ADA-02, ADA-03, ADA-04, ADA-06, ADA-07, ADA-10, ADA-12). Three are spec text that is stale against intentional code (ADA-01, ADA-05, ADA-08). One is a test gap (ADA-11). No candidate was already tracked, and none was refuted. The two Not yet met lines in the lane ([B767 at specs/api/addons.md:598](../../specs/api/addons.md) for `certmgr` and [B93 at specs/api/addons.md:642](../../specs/api/addons.md) for `gitlab`) match the code, because neither package is in the built-in registry. The ledger bounds this assessment: the step-content rules owned by customplaybooks, the execution-side MetalLB and gate behavior, and the managed CephConsumer clause were not verified in this lane.

#### Confirmed findings

| ID | Severity | Kind | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ADA-01](#ada-01) | Low | drift | Executable shape admits a subscribe-only authored OLM add-on although the spec requires an owned catalog with an explicit priority |
| [ADA-02](#ada-02) | Low | defect | One package configuration fault yields two or three diagnostics at the same field, one with an empty catalog name |
| [ADA-03](#ada-03) | Low | defect | An empty ClusterAddonProfile is refused with the binding's message and a remedy naming spec.packages, a field profiles do not have |
| [ADA-04](#ada-04) | Low | defect | acm single-node remedy text differs from the spec |
| [ADA-05](#ada-05) | Low | drift | fdf subscription.source is defaulted from catalogSource.name although the spec says it is required with no default |
| [ADA-06](#ada-06) | Low | defect | Overlapping entries inside one MetalLB pool are reported as "pool X overlaps pool X" |
| [ADA-07](#ada-07) | Low | defect | Nested missing-profile diagnostic is suppressed when a nested profile shares the binding's name |
| [ADA-08](#ada-08) | Low | doc-stale | "The four rows above" no longer points at the rows it qualifies |
| [ADA-09](#ada-09) | Medium | defect | MetalLB held-address check omits CephCluster ingress, NFS and management-gateway virtual_ip addresses |
