#### ADA-01

**Low, drift.** Executable shape admits a subscribe-only authored OLM add-on although the spec requires an owned catalog with an explicit priority.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:154-158](../../specs/api/addons.md) defines the executable shape as including "an owned catalog with an explicit `priority`" and ends "Every other shape validates and is refused at `plan`." The X235 outcome repeats the wording at [specs/milestones/m4.md:1815-1819](../../specs/milestones/m4.md) ("an owned catalog with an explicit `priority` following the package Subscription rules"). The code has no catalog condition. [AuthoredShapeRefusal](../../internal/addons/authored.go) refuses only a non-ClusterAddon, a manifest set or missing OLM arm, steps, inputs, an external namespace, a missing OperatorGroup and a target other than own or all ([authored.go:30-51](../../internal/addons/authored.go)). `Authored` requires only a non-empty subscription package, channel, `startingCSV`, source and sourceNamespace ([authored.go:94-98](../../internal/addons/authored.go)). The six shape rows have no catalog row ([instance/selection.go:13-20](../../internal/addons/instance/selection.go)). The test removes `catalogSource` and still expects an instance ([authored_selection_test.go:148-170](../../internal/addons/authored_selection_test.go)), and a subscribe-only add-on from `redhat-operators` yields no issue (lines 172-175). The probe `./scripts/go test ./internal/addons/ -run TestACatalogCollisionIsReportedOnTheLaterAddOnWhicheverSideOnlySubscribes` passes.

**Impact.** A reader of the shape sentence believes an add-on without an owned catalog is refused at plan. It is instead synthesized as an instance and installs from the catalog it names, under exact `startingCSV` approval. This is a documentation inconsistency, not a safety gap. The spec contradicts itself: [specs/api/addons.md:114-117](../../specs/api/addons.md) make `catalogSource` optional with `name`, `image` and `priority` required only when the block is present; [lines 351 and 362-367](../../specs/api/addons.md) give a remedy for "an add-on that only subscribes"; [specs/add-ons.md:103-107](../../specs/add-ons.md) define the shape as a managed namespace and an OperatorGroup only. The delivered record is X235 ([specs/milestones/delivered.md:10627](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)). Only the sentence at line 156 and its X235 copy are outliers.

**Counterevidence.** The catalog priority rule exists only for owned catalogs ([specs/api/addons.md:165-168](../../specs/api/addons.md)). The refusal table in [specs/add-ons.md:552-562](../../specs/add-ons.md) has no missing-catalog row, and the X235 refused list at [m4.md:1828-1830](../../specs/milestones/m4.md) omits catalogs. Adding a refusal row would contradict the subscribe-only diagnostics.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Reword [specs/api/addons.md:155-156](../../specs/api/addons.md) to "an owned catalog, when declared, with an explicit `priority`", and the matching X235 outcome text. No `ShapeNoCatalog` row is needed. Exit: the shape sentence matches `AuthoredShapeRefusal`; `make docs-check` passes.

#### ADA-02

**Low, defect.** One package configuration fault yields two or three diagnostics at the same field, one with an empty catalog name.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:330-333](../../specs/api/addons.md): "Each fault is reported once, as its own diagnostic". The schema already refuses a missing fdf `subscription.source` and a non-positive duration ([api/v1alpha1/addons_storage.go:10-18](../../api/v1alpha1/addons_storage.go); the duration lexical accepts only a positive value at [lexical.go:137-139](../../api/v1alpha1/lexical.go)). `ValidatePackages` repeats both checks: `budget <= 0` at [instances.go:240-251](../../internal/addons/instances.go) and `source == ""` at line 249; the pollInterval check at [instances.go:263-267](../../internal/addons/instances.go) has the same shape. `admitFDF` fires for an empty source because `!sub.Has("catalogSource") && !slices.Contains(addons.DefaultCatalogs(), source)` is true ([packages/fdf.go:22-24](../../internal/addons/packages/fdf.go)). The same `budget <= 0` pattern is at [admission_olm.go:198-205](../../internal/addons/admission_olm.go). Probes over scratch copies of `examples/add-ons/lab-compact-df`, validated with `--output json --context none`: with fdf `subscription.source` and `catalogSource` removed, three errors at `$.spec.packages.fdf.subscription.source` (`api.invariant` "package fdf subscribes from catalog , which no cluster Bootwright installs serves", `api.required` "required field is absent", `api.value` "package fdf has no catalog source"); with `timeout: 0s`, two errors (`api.value` "package fdf timeout must be positive and at most 5h50m" and `api.value` "value does not match the required duration grammar"). The `api.required` diagnostic comes from the desiredstate compiler, not internal/addons.

**Impact.** Redundant diagnostics, one of which prints an empty catalog name in both message and remedy ("declare subscription.catalogSource named  with ..."). The input is still refused; this is noise.

**Counterevidence.** The row at [specs/api/addons.md:522](../../specs/api/addons.md) ("The catalog is neither owned nor a default catalog") covers an empty source literally, so the empty-name message follows the spec text. The clause at 330-333 is aimed at distinct faults not merging; "reported once" is read literally here. The `readiness.timeout` and pollInterval duplicates are inferred from code shape and were not probed.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In `ValidatePackages` and the readiness check, leave the positive and parse checks to the schema lexical and keep only the ceiling and whole-second checks. Make `admitFDF` return nothing for an empty source, or amend the spec. Exit: a compiler test asserts exactly one diagnostic for a missing fdf `subscription.source` and one for `timeout: 0s`.

#### ADA-03

**Low, defect.** An empty ClusterAddonProfile is refused with the binding's message and a remedy naming spec.packages, a field profiles do not have.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:279](../../specs/api/addons.md): "At least one list is non-empty." The profile case in `Validate` calls `expandSelection` ([admission.go:117-118](../../internal/addons/admission.go)), which reaches `expandIndexed`. Its empty check sums `profileRefs`, `addonRefs` and `packages` and returns the binding text without branching on kind ([bindings.go:28-31](../../internal/addons/bindings.go)). The profile schema has only `profileRefs` and `addonRefs` ([api/v1alpha1/addons.go:94-96](../../api/v1alpha1/addons.go)). A probe test over an empty `ClusterAddonProfile` returned `Code:api.invariant Field:$.spec Message:the binding selects no profile, add-on or package Remediation:add a package to spec.packages, a profile to spec.profileRefs or an add-on to spec.addonRefs`. Only a binding test covers the wording ([cmd/bootwright/package_kind_defaults_test.go:115](../../cmd/bootwright/package_kind_defaults_test.go)).

**Impact.** The diagnostic names the wrong kind and suggests a field the profile does not have, so following it produces a second error.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fires at the right field with the right code. The table row at [specs/api/addons.md:353](../../specs/api/addons.md) is written for the binding only, so a profile wording is new spec text, and the style rule at [lines 330-331](../../specs/api/addons.md) ("names what it concerns") is what the reused text breaks.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Branch on `owner.Kind()` at [bindings.go:29-31](../../internal/addons/bindings.go) and emit "the profile selects no profile or add-on" with the remedy "add a profile to spec.profileRefs or an add-on to spec.addonRefs". Add the row to the diagnostics table. Exit: a unit test in internal/addons asserts the profile message and remedy.

#### ADA-04

**Low, defect.** acm single-node remedy text differs from the spec.

**Evidence.** The remedy in [specs/api/addons.md:560](../../specs/api/addons.md) is `set hub.availabilityConfig to Basic`. The code emits `Remediation: "set hub availabilityConfig to Basic"` ([packages/acm.go:25-26](../../internal/addons/packages/acm.go)). The test asserts only the issue count, `len(admitACM(i, f)) != 1` ([hub_test.go:101-110](../../internal/addons/packages/hub_test.go), line 105). A grep over Go, Markdown and Python finds the string only in the spec and in acm.go.

**Impact.** The remedy loses the dotted field path, and a documented diagnostic text drifts with no test pinning it. The Field already carries the path, so the operator still learns which field to edit.

**Counterevidence.** Code, message and code value match the spec. The Field is `.hub.availabilityConfig` in the code against `$.spec.packages.acm.hub.availabilityConfig` in the spec; whether the pipeline prefixes the path was not traced.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Change the remedy to `set hub.availabilityConfig to Basic` and assert code, message and remedy in `TestACMSingleNodeAndDependentApproval`. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/addons/packages/ -run TestACMSingleNodeAndDependentApproval` passes with those assertions.

#### ADA-05

**Low, drift.** fdf subscription.source is defaulted from catalogSource.name although the spec says it is required with no default.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:513](../../specs/api/addons.md): "`source` is required, with no default"; [lines 685-687](../../specs/api/addons.md): normalization materializes `subscription.source` "(except for `fdf` and `gitlab`, which require it)". `NormalizePackages` sets the source to `catalogSource.name` whenever the block is present and defaults it for every OLM package, with no exemption for fdf ([instances.go:149-163](../../internal/addons/instances.go), decisive lines 151-161). The fdf schema marks `source` required ([api/v1alpha1/addons_storage.go:12-15](../../api/v1alpha1/addons_storage.go)), but normalization runs first in the compile pipeline ([cmd/bootwright/wiring_desiredstate.go:44-50](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_desiredstate.go)), so the required check does not fire when a `catalogSource` is declared. Probe: a scratch copy of `examples/add-ons/lab-compact-df` with only the `source:` line removed validates with `"ok":true` and no diagnostics.

**Impact.** A reader expects a refusal that does not fire. The spec disagrees with itself: the shared Subscription table at [specs/api/addons.md:406](../../specs/api/addons.md) says the source defaults to "the package's documented catalog, or `catalogSource.name` when present".

**Counterevidence.** The defaulted value equals the owned catalog, the only valid value, so no wrong installation follows. Without a `catalogSource`, fdf's empty default source leaves the requirement in force and [instances.go:249](../../internal/addons/instances.go) refuses. The `gitlab` package does not exist ([B93](../../specs/milestones/m4.md#b93)), so the exception for it could not be checked against code.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Edit [specs/api/addons.md:513](../../specs/api/addons.md) and [685-687](../../specs/api/addons.md) to say fdf's source has no package default but follows `catalogSource.name` when an owned catalog is declared, matching line 406 and the code. The same wording applies to `gitlab` at its row near line 613. Alternatively, skip the `catalogSource.name` default for packages whose descriptor requires the source. Exit: spec text aligned and `make docs-check` passes.

#### ADA-06

**Low, defect.** Overlapping entries inside one MetalLB pool are reported as 'pool X overlaps pool X'.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:669](../../specs/api/addons.md): the "Overlapping pools" row reads `pool <pool> overlaps pool <other> at <address>`, and [line 480](../../specs/api/addons.md) says "A pool also overlaps no other pool". In `admitPoolEntries`, `previous` is shared across pools ([pools.go:109](../../internal/addons/packages/pools.go)), each entry is set to `pool.Name` ([line 257](../../internal/addons/packages/pools.go)), checked, then appended: `previous = append(previous, r)` ([pools.go:298-299](../../internal/addons/packages/pools.go)). `checkPoolConflicts` then emits `pool %s overlaps pool %s at %s` ([pools.go:229-236](../../internal/addons/packages/pools.go), function at 192-238). Two overlapping entries of one pool therefore produce "pool a overlaps pool a" with the remedy "make the addresses of a and a disjoint". The existing tests cover only two distinct pools ([pool_refusals_test.go:49](../../internal/addons/packages/pool_refusals_test.go), [registry_test.go:39](../../internal/addons/packages/registry_test.go)).

**Impact.** A self-overlap gets a confusing message and remedy.

**Counterevidence.** Refusing intra-pool overlap is reasonable, and the row is literally satisfied with the two names equal. The refusal fires; only the wording and the spec coverage are wrong. The spec does not say whether entries of one pool may overlap, so part of this is a spec gap.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Decide the rule in the spec first. If entries must be disjoint, add a row and emit a distinct message when `other.pool == pool.Name`, for example "address `<entry>` of pool `<pool>` overlaps its entry <other entry>". Otherwise skip same-pool intervals. Exit: a test in pool_refusals_test.go with a pool `a` holding `192.0.2.80-192.0.2.90` and `192.0.2.85-192.0.2.95`.

#### ADA-07

**Low, defect.** Nested missing-profile diagnostic is suppressed when a nested profile shares the binding's name.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:342](../../specs/api/addons.md) requires an `api.reference` diagnostic at `$.spec.profileRefs[<i>]` when "A profile reaches a missing add-on or profile". `expandIndexed` decides whether the missing profile was referenced directly by comparing names, `if current.object.Name() != owner.Name()` ([bindings.go:66-75](../../internal/addons/bindings.go), guard at 72). The add-on branch uses the structural test `current.root >= 0` ([bindings.go:94-95](../../internal/addons/bindings.go)). Names are scoped per kind ([specs/api.md:574-576](../../specs/api.md)), so `ClusterAddonBinding/core` and `ClusterAddonProfile/core` can coexist. A probe test with binding `core` (profileRefs `[core]`) and profile `core` (profileRefs `[missing]`) returned no binding issues; the control with the profile named `other` returned `api.reference` at `$.spec.profileRefs[0]`.

**Impact.** The binding is left incomplete with no diagnostic of its own, so the per-binding row the spec requires is missing in the same-name case.

**Counterevidence.** The profile's own reference diagnostic still fails the compile; this path was read from [admission.go:118](../../internal/addons/admission.go) and not probed. A profile owner is not affected, because a profile that returns to itself is refused through the `active` map before this branch.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Use `current.root >= 0` at line 72, as line 94 does. Exit: a unit test with binding `core`, `profileRefs: [core]`, and profile `core` with `profileRefs: [missing]` reports at `$.spec.profileRefs[0]` on the binding.

#### ADA-08

**Low, doc-stale.** 'The four rows above' no longer points at the rows it qualifies.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:359](../../specs/api/addons.md): "The four rows above apply to an add-on of the executable shape only, because only that shape becomes an instance." The four executable-only rows (built-in name, namespace, OLM package, CatalogSource) are at [lines 348-351](../../specs/api/addons.md); six general rows follow at [352-357](../../specs/api/addons.md): unselected configuration, empty binding, profile expansion loop, afterRefs of another cluster, afterRefs cycle, authored ordering cycle. The code agrees with the narrower intent: shadows and shared identities are set only when `Authored(a)` succeeds ([instances.go:58-65](../../internal/addons/instances.go), guard at 58), while `afterRefs` is set on every selected member at line 57 ([authored_selection.go:8-26](../../internal/addons/authored_selection.go) reports the identity rows).

**Impact.** A reader can take the afterRefs and cycle rows, which sit directly above the sentence, as executable-only.

**Counterevidence.** Code behavior is correct; the wording only is wrong. The paragraph that follows (lines 360-367) describes only the identity rows, which confirms the intent.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Name the rows ("The built-in-name, namespace, OLM package and CatalogSource rows apply ...") or move the six general rows above the four identity rows. Exit: spec edit and `make docs-check`.

#### ADA-09

**Medium, defect.** MetalLB held-address check omits CephCluster ingress, NFS and management-gateway virtual_ip addresses.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:473-477](../../specs/api/addons.md): "A pool includes none of these addresses: ... an address another declared object holds"; the Held address row at [line 666](../../specs/api/addons.md) reads "held by `<holder>`". `checkPoolConflicts` builds holders from `f.Endpoints`, `f.Reserved`, node addresses and next hops only ([pools.go:192-211](../../internal/addons/packages/pools.go)). `f.Reserved` is filled only from `addressClaims` ([openshift/addon_facts.go:55-60](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/addon_facts.go)), whose switch covers OpenShiftCluster, Machine, InfraProvider, LoadBalancer and the managed DNSServer, NTPServer, Proxy, ArtifactServer and Registry kinds and has no CephCluster case ([endpoint_ownership.go:19-74](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/endpoint_ownership.go), switch 32-65). A CephCluster declares `virtual_ip` for its ingress, NFS and management gateway ([api/v1alpha1/storage_native.go:38-54](../../api/v1alpha1/storage_native.go)). The Ceph side compares an ingress `virtual_ip` only against declared Machine addresses and other ingress virtual IPs ([specs/ceph-native-api.md:488-492](../../specs/ceph-native-api.md), validated at [internal/storage/cephcluster/native_ingress.go:222-253](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/native_ingress.go)); nothing compares it against a MetalLB pool.

**Impact.** On a shared machine network, a MetalLB pool can include the address keepalived holds for the Ceph RGW or NFS ingress or the management gateway. MetalLB can then hand that address to a LoadBalancer Service and the two race on ARP, so the storage gateway or the Service becomes intermittently unreachable. The refusal the spec names does not fire. The same missing claim affects `endpointCollisions` ([endpoint_ownership.go:76-83](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/endpoint_ownership.go)), the second consumer of `addressClaims`, so an OpenShift endpoint equal to a CephCluster virtual IP is not flagged either.

**Counterevidence.** The holder list in the B727 item text is parenthetical and omits Ceph ([specs/milestones/m4.md:885-889](../../specs/milestones/m4.md)), and the code matches that list exactly, so the omission may have been a scoping choice. The item text is not a decision that narrows the generic clause, which governs. No Not yet met line or item tracks the gap. The workaround is to exclude the address from the pool by hand. Whether another cluster's MetalLB pool counts as "another declared object" is ambiguous and is not claimed.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a CephCluster case to `addressClaims`, or a cephcluster-owned claims helper as `substrate.AddressClaims` does, claiming each declared service's `virtual_ip`. The ingress and NFS values carry a prefix and the management gateway value is bare; the `claim()` closure at [endpoint_ownership.go:21-29](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/endpoint_ownership.go) already reduces a prefixed value to its address. Exit: a test in which a CephCluster ingress declares `virtual_ip` 198.51.100.85/24 and a metallb pool covers it expects `api.invariant` at `.pools[0].addresses[0]` with a message naming `CephCluster/<name>`; a matching endpoint-collision test.

#### ADA-10

**Low, defect.** acm hub.nodeSelector keys and values are not validated as Kubernetes labels.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:554](../../specs/api/addons.md): the row for `hub.nodeSelector` (map of string to string, optional) whose rule reads "Label keys and values for the hub's components." The schema types the field as `stringsMap()` ([api/v1alpha1/addons_hub.go:59](../../api/v1alpha1/addons_hub.go)), an open mapping of free text ([schema.go:88](../../api/v1alpha1/schema.go)). `admitACM` checks only the single-node `availabilityConfig` ([packages/acm.go:24-29](../../internal/addons/packages/acm.go)), and `renderACM` passes `hub` unchanged into the MultiClusterHub. By contrast, namespace labels are validated with `api.ValidLexical("kubernetes-label-key")` and `("kubernetes-label-value")` ([admission.go:158-160](../../internal/addons/admission.go)), and MetalLB selectors in [pool_allocation.go:45](../../internal/addons/packages/pool_allocation.go). The only nodeSelector test uses a valid key ([hub_test.go:38](../../internal/addons/packages/hub_test.go)).

**Impact.** A typo in a nodeSelector key or a value over 63 bytes passes `validate` and `plan`. The hub's component Deployments are then likely to fail pod-spec validation or never schedule, so the failure shows far from the authored field instead of at `$.spec.packages.acm.hub.nodeSelector`. This consequence is inferred from Kubernetes behavior and was not seen in a run.

**Counterevidence.** The spec names no diagnostic or fault row for this field, which is why the verifiers split between defect and gap; the requirement is read from the Rule column and from the parallel namespace-label rule at [specs/api/addons.md:110](../../specs/api/addons.md). Tolerations are constrained to the listed enumerations by the schema. There is no data, host or secret consequence, and the operator can correct the field and re-apply.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In `admitACM`, refuse each `hub.nodeSelector` key or value that fails the kubernetes-label lexical, with `api.value` at `.hub.nodeSelector` (the same convention as `.hub.availabilityConfig`) and the remedy "use valid Kubernetes label keys and values". Add the fault row to the acm table at [specs/api/addons.md:557-559](../../specs/api/addons.md). Exit: a hub_test.go case with `nodeSelector {"bad key!": "x"}` expects the issue.

#### ADA-11

**Low, test-gap.** No test asserts the field or remedy of add-on step-content refusals, and an escaping step path is tested only through ValidatePartial.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:375](../../specs/api/addons.md): "Each step-content refusal carries a remedy."; [lines 262-266](../../specs/api/addons.md) list the refusals (no `source.git`, no reserved connection variable, a contained content path). `Validate` forwards step content to customplaybooks ([admission.go:173-181](../../internal/addons/admission.go)), and the remedy is chosen by a field-suffix switch ([customplaybooks/validation.go:352-374](../../internal/desiredstate/customplaybooks/validation.go), `.steps[` test at 357, `.source.git` at 359, `extraVars` at 361, default at 365, and a `.source.path` remedy at 363-364). `TestAddonSemanticFailures` checks only `len(issues) == 0` for the Git source and connection-variable cases ([admission_test.go:51-85](../../internal/addons/admission_test.go)). The `../escape.yaml` step runs only through `ValidatePartial`, which checks the `$.spec` prefix and not the remedy ([admission_test.go:498-513](../../internal/addons/admission_test.go)). A grep of test files for the three remedy strings finds nothing. The customplaybooks tests use the field `spec`, so the `.steps[` branch never runs there.

**Impact.** A change to the customplaybooks issue builder could drop the remedy or misplace the field on step refusals, and no gate would fail.

**Counterevidence.** Behavior is correct at HEAD. One step refusal does have a remedy assertion, the step requirement Secret case at [admission_test.go:291 and 305](../../internal/addons/admission_test.go), but it is a requires check, not step content.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Extend `TestAddonSemanticFailures` or add a table test through `Validate` asserting code, field (`$.spec.steps[0].source.git`, `.extraVars`, `.playbook`) and a non-empty remedy for git, a reserved variable and a `../` playbook path. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/addons/ -run TestAddonSemanticFailures` passes with the new assertions.

#### ADA-12

**Low, drift.** A foreign csvSucceeded readiness check is refused one level below the check's indexed field.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/addons.md:254-258](../../specs/api/addons.md): "A `csvSucceeded` check of an OLM add-on names its own `namespace.name` and effective `subscription.name`. Each fault is refused at the check's indexed field with `api.invariant`." The Secret-check fault uses the indexed field, `at := indexed(field, i)` ([admission_olm.go:224-226](../../internal/addons/admission_olm.go)), but the csvSucceeded identity fault uses `at+".csvSucceeded"` (line 230). Tests pin the deeper field: `cr + ".gate[1].csvSucceeded"` at [admission_test.go:274](../../internal/addons/admission_test.go) and `"spec.readiness.checks[0].csvSucceeded"` at [lines 282-287](../../internal/addons/admission_test.go). The same function serves gates and readiness checks, so both are affected.

**Impact.** An operator or tool that matches on `$.spec.readiness.checks[<i>]` misses the diagnostic. The refusal still fires with the right code and a usable remedy, and the deeper path points inside the right check.

**Counterevidence.** No D, X or B record sets `.csvSucceeded` as the intended field (searched in specs/milestones). The tests pin the deeper path deliberately, which makes the spec sentence the likelier stale side. A malformed check reported at `at` with `api.value` ([admission_olm.go:235](../../internal/addons/admission_olm.go), test line 288) is a value fault rather than one of the two identity faults and is outside this clause.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either report the fault at the check's indexed field and update admission_test.go:274, 282 and 285, or change the spec sentence to say the fault is reported at the check's `csvSucceeded` member. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/addons/ -run Admission` passes with the chosen field, or the spec line names `.csvSucceeded`.

#### Observations

- Message style is enforced centrally: `addonIssue` lowercases the first letter and strips the final period for every add-on diagnostic ([admission.go:294-303](../../internal/addons/admission.go)).
- Diagnostic indexes after normalization sorting (addonConfigs, inputs, pools) are mapped back to authored positions by the compiler's generic `recordReordering` ([phases.go:253](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go)).
- Every MetalLB pool diagnostic in the spec table has a code path in pools.go or pool_allocation.go and a matching test string.
- Executable-shape admission faults (reserved namespaces, label prefixes, API groups, Secret kind, CRD gate binding, priority, pollInterval, name length) all have code in admission_olm.go and admission.go.
- Registry construction proves every provided token has a reader or is in `DefinedCapabilityTokens` ([packages.go:171-214](../../internal/addons/packages.go)), tested in instances_test.go:139-195.
- Environment kind defaults cannot select a package: `MembersSelect` on `spec.packages` is honored in compilation/defaults.go:58.
- Retired OLM fields (displayName, publisher, grpcPodConfig, installPlanApproval, bare customResources apiVersion and kind) are in [retired.go:57-62](../../api/v1alpha1/retired.go).
- Step validation reuses customplaybooks content rules with `allowGit=false`, and the issue builder lowercases the message and attaches a step-specific remedy whenever the field contains `.steps[`.
- Authored-identity sharing checks treat every built-in package as earlier than any authored add-on, so a clash is always reported on the authored add-on.
- `addressClaims` is shared by endpoint collision checks and the MetalLB held-address facts, so one added holder kind fixes both (ADA-09).
- The authored add-on gate binding, descriptor digest and plan refusal rows are each implemented and pinned by tests at both the addons and instance package levels.
- Ordering diagnostics follow the spec's precedence: a binding cycle suppresses the authored member cycle, and capability-only cycles are told apart from cycles that afterRefs closes.
- Critic notes: after round 1 the Steps, metallb execution and fdf consumer clauses were examined thinly; after round 2 the plan- and execution-side clauses (gate scope augmentation, descriptor freezing, KubeVirt-hosted namespace refusal) were marked met without tests that pin them, and the custom-resource label prefix check covers only the exact `bootwright.io/` prefix while the namespace-label check also covers subdomains. The remaining spot checks (API group list, reserved namespaces, priority and pollInterval bounds, Secret checks, pool and allocation bounds, package timeouts, last-package message) matched the spec.

#### Limits

The step-content validation (customplaybooks.ValidateContent) and the execution-side clauses (MetalLB allocator, CSV approval, gate deadline behavior, immutability of pools) were read only as far as their entry points, because other lanes own them. Three validate probes were run on scratch copies of examples/add-ons/lab-compact-df and one go test; a further probe test for ADA-03 and ADA-07 was run by the reproducing verifiers and removed. The readiness.timeout and pollInterval duplicates (ADA-02) come from reading the code and were not probed. The claim that a typed invalid nodeSelector fails at pod level (ADA-10) is inferred and was not checked against Kubernetes or the MultiClusterHub CRD. Whether "no other pool" includes other clusters' MetalLB pools on a shared segment is ambiguous in the spec and was not reported. The gitlab and certmgr schemas were not checked against code because those packages do not exist (B93, B767). The cluster-side evaluation of the gate statusPhase checks was not read, so the claim that an attempt fails at its deadline was not verified from source.

### Group: Command line

### CLI: Command tree, unavailable commands, parsing and input conventions, confirmation, local privilege, context and setup behavior, controller declaration, validation, preflight and rendering; the global flags and the command and flag catalog

Lane `cli-parsing`. Spec range: `specs/cli.md` lines 1-557; `specs/cli/commands.md` lines 1-507. Register: 488 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 15; confirmed: 13; tracked: 0; refuted: 2.

#### Assessment

**Assessment.** The command catalog, the parsing rules and the flag-relationship checks are sound. The command and flag tables of [specs/cli/commands.md](../../specs/cli/commands.md) match the catalog in `internal/cli` command for command and flag for flag, with no entry on one side only. Exact-name resolution, local-flag non-inheritance, the payload stop, the `--` rule, the raw bounds (1024 arguments, 16384 bytes per argument, 1048576 in total), occurrence-local empty-value rejection, byte-wise confirmation reading with a 64-byte ceiling, and the two `Not yet met` lines at [commands.md:133](../../specs/cli/commands.md) and [commands.md:198](../../specs/cli/commands.md) agree with the code at the baseline. Thirteen discrepancies are confirmed: one High, three Medium and nine Low. They cluster in two places. The first is the privilege boundary: `render` is classed as a privileged command whose output side runs as root (CLI-01), bare `render` and `preflight container-cluster` with `--ssh-*` elevate before a help or usage outcome (CLI-02, CLI-03), and the sudo-entry environment guard runs ahead of the no-effect contracts of help, version, completion and raw bounds (CLI-04). The second is spec text that disagrees with itself or with the owning section: confirmation codes, the standard-input list, the trust command and local controller, the `--yes` condition for structured trust, the SSH flag list, and the sudo refresh and executable-path details. The audit of this lane is bounded by its ledger: the sudo supervision internals in `internal/controller/privilege` were checked mostly by constants and remedy strings, and effective-origin and schema generation were only partly traced. No discrepancy in this lane was already tracked.

#### CLI-01

**High, unsafe.** render publishes its output as root and holds --sensitive's ownership check to root instead of the invoking account. Re-verified independently with probe tests in a worktree: both render forms classify RequiresRoot and the publisher's UID is never injected in production wiring; the root write is bounded to directory creation and replacing a regular effective-state.yaml, and a direct root login is unaffected.

All three verification lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** `render` is registered through `available(...)` at [commands_nativeartifacts.go:11](../../internal/cli/commands_nativeartifacts.go), and `available` sets `privileged` to true at [catalog.go:20-23](../../internal/cli/catalog.go). [invocation.go:50-61](../../internal/cli/invocation.go) returns early only for help, a validation failure, a non-privileged path, explicit-input `validate` and `controller install --dry-run` or `--download-only`; every other privileged path, context-free `render --input-dir` included, reaches `classification.RequiresRoot ... = true`, so a non-root invocation re-executes as UID 0. The publisher is wired with no invoking-account identity at [wiring.go:175](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring.go), `Files: renderlocal.Files{}`. In [files.go:47-61](../../internal/nativeartifacts/renderlocal/files.go), `os.MkdirAll(directory, directoryMode)` and the file creation run with the elevated child's credentials. In [files.go:129-139](../../internal/nativeartifacts/renderlocal/files.go) the ownership check reads `uid := os.Geteuid` and refuses with "is not owned by this account" when the directory owner differs from that. The spec at [cli.md:500-504](../../specs/cli.md) requires that with `--sensitive` "the output directory must be owned by the invoking account and not be group- or other-writable unless sticky". [cli.md:394-398](../../specs/cli.md) says root identity "governs only root-owned runtime storage and the Bootwright executable". The sibling clause at [cli.md:969-972](../../specs/cli.md) states that what `diff --output-dir` creates is written "with the invoking account's credentials as every operator-named path is". The only credential-switching helper is `comparisonlocal` for `diff` ([service.go:131-142](../../internal/nativeartifacts/comparisonlocal/service.go), [helper.go:99](../../internal/nativeartifacts/comparisonlocal/helper.go), served from [main.go:20](../../cmd/bootwright/main.go)). A search for `Setfsuid`, `Setresuid`, `Setuid` and `Credential` in `internal` and `cmd` outside tests finds only that helper.

**Impact.** The ownership check is inverted under elevation. A root-owned directory passes `--sensitive` and the operator's own 0700 directory is refused as not owned by this account. A directory that `render` creates is owned by root with mode 0700 and holds a 0600 file that the invoking account cannot read. Every `render`, context-free included, can create directories and replace a regular `effective-state.yaml` as root at any path the invoking account names, including paths it cannot write itself. Under a sudoers rule that permits only Bootwright, that is a root write the account does not otherwise hold.

**Counterevidence.** Input is read under the invoking account ([wiring_desiredstate.go:85-90](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_desiredstate.go)), so only the output side is affected. The file name is fixed, the content is effective state with no secret value, and an existing link or non-regular target is refused ([files.go:84-88](../../internal/nativeartifacts/renderlocal/files.go)). A direct root launch behaves correctly. The same `renderlocal.Files{}` pattern at [wiring.go:177](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring.go) for `diff` runs inside the credential-dropped helper and is correct. The `--sensitive` refusal matters only for context-backed `render`, because context-free `render` conflicts with `--sensitive`. The unit tests inject a UID ([files_test.go:177-185](../../internal/nativeartifacts/renderlocal/files_test.go)), so they pass without covering the production wiring. The output-side rule for `render` is implied by [cli.md:503](../../specs/cli.md) and by the `diff` clause, not stated in the `render` section. No milestone item, decision or `Not yet met` line records it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Write `render`'s output through the invoking-account helper path, as `diff --output-dir` does through `comparisonlocal`, or inject the invoking account's UID into `renderlocal.Files` and create and publish through a descriptor opened under that account. Whether context-free `render` should elevate at all is a separate design choice. The spec also needs to say who owns a directory that `render` creates. Exit: a `cmd/bootwright` test that composes `render` with an elevated child and a non-root invoking account shows that a user-owned 0700 directory is accepted with `--sensitive`, a root-owned one is refused, and the created file is owned by the invoking account; add a `ClassifyInvocation` case for `render --input-dir` that records the chosen class.

#### CLI-02

**Medium, defect.** Bare `render`, which only prints help, is classified as requiring root and elevates through sudo.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:278-280](../../specs/cli.md) lists help, completion, version, invalid invocations and unavailable commands among those that "never elevate". [cli.md:482-485](../../specs/cli.md) says bare `render` "prints render help and succeeds" and "performs no command work", and [cli.md:53](../../specs/cli.md) places that special case at precedence step 5. [cli.md:286](../../specs/cli.md) limits elevation to "Available commands requiring context state". `render` is privileged through [catalog.go:20-23](../../internal/cli/catalog.go). `validateRenderDirectories` returns an empty string when neither path flag is set ([validation.go:299-315](../../internal/cli/validation.go)), so [invocation.go:50-61](../../internal/cli/invocation.go) falls through to `RequiresRoot = true`. The bare-render help branch is in `Runner.run` at [runner.go:200-205](../../internal/cli/runner.go), which runs only after the privilege boundary at [run.go:57-83](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go) has acted on the classification. The classification table in [invocation_test.go:12-39](../../internal/cli/invocation_test.go) has no bare-`render` row.

**Impact.** Asking for `render`'s help prompts for a sudo password. In a JSON, YAML or non-interactive invocation without cached sudo it fails with `runtime.privilege` instead of printing help.

**Counterevidence.** A root invocation prints help correctly, and `render --help` takes the explicit-help branch and does not elevate. A temporary probe of `ClassifyInvocation` returned `RequiresRoot=true` for `render` and for `render --output json`, and false for `render --help`; the probe file was deleted afterwards. The requirement is derived from [cli.md:482-485](../../specs/cli.md), [cli.md:53](../../specs/cli.md) and [cli.md:286](../../specs/cli.md) together, since no clause names bare `render` in the never-elevate list. Whether `render --input-dir` or `--output-dir` should elevate is a separate question that [report-final.md:452-454](../002-addons/report-final.md) marks unexamined.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In `ClassifyInvocation`, return without `RequiresRoot` when the path is `render` and neither `--input-dir` nor `--output-dir` is set, and share that condition with [runner.go:200](../../internal/cli/runner.go) instead of duplicating it. Exit: `TestPrivilegeClassificationHasNoInformationOrInvalidEffects` gains `{render}` and `{render, --output, json}` rows that expect no elevation.

#### CLI-03

**Medium, defect.** preflight container-cluster advertises and accepts every --ssh-* flag but its use case always refuses them, after elevation.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [commands.md:12-13](../../specs/cli/commands.md) lists "every `preflight` check but `preflight controller` and `preflight infra`" among the commands that accept `--ssh-*`, while [commands.md:8-9](../../specs/cli/commands.md) limits those flags to "the commands whose use case reads them", [cli.md:15-17](../../specs/cli.md) says a command "never accepts one only to ignore it", and the command's own row at [commands.md:119](../../specs/cli/commands.md) lists only `--clusters` and `--dry-run`. The owning clauses for the OpenShiftCluster checks say the opposite of the list: [openshift-clusters.md:1073](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md) and [output.md:376-378](../../specs/cli/output.md). The scope table at [inherited_scope.go:16-18](../../internal/cli/inherited_scope.go) gives `preflight container-cluster` all four flags (line 17). The dispatch passes `values.ssh()` at [commands_containercluster.go:48-55](../../internal/cli/commands_containercluster.go). The use case refuses any value in [service.go:36-38](../../internal/containercluster/preflight/service.go) with `cli.usage` and "container-cluster preflight checks the controller and accepts no SSH or trust-on-first-use options", and `Borrowed()` is true when any of the four fields is set ([ssh.go:12-13](../../internal/machine/ssh.go)). The refusal is pinned by `TestControllerPreflightRefusesUnusedRemoteOptions` ([service_test.go:184-191](../../internal/containercluster/preflight/service_test.go)). The command is built through `available()` ([catalog.go:20-21](../../internal/cli/catalog.go)), so [invocation.go:50-61](../../internal/cli/invocation.go) sets `RequiresRoot` and [run.go:82-83](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go) elevates before the service runs.

**Reproduction.** A temporary probe showed `ClassifyInvocation` returning `RequiresRoot=true` for `preflight container-cluster --ssh-user x --ssh-ask-sudo-password`, false for `preflight infra --ssh-user x`, and `preflight container-cluster --help --detail full` printing an "SSH overrides" section with `--ssh-ask-sudo-password`, `--ssh-id-file`, `--ssh-user` and `--ssh-user-for-provisioned`. The probe file was deleted afterwards.

**Impact.** Help and completion offer four flags that always fail, and the usage refusal arrives after the elevation step, against [cli.md:278-280](../../specs/cli.md) ("invalid invocations ... never elevate").

**Counterevidence.** The refusal is explicit and fires before any context or host access, so nothing unsafe happens. `preflight clusters` legitimately forwards SSH options to its CephCluster part ([output.md:373-378](../../specs/cli/output.md)). The `--trust-on-first-use` half of the service refusal is unreachable from the CLI, because the command declares no such flag. The spec contradicts itself: the SSH-accepting list at commands.md:12-13 is the stale half. The stale list is repeated in the delivered record [delivered.md:9278](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md).

**Correction and exit evidence.** Remove `preflight container-cluster` from `sshFlagsByCommand` so the flags are refused at resolution without elevation, stop dispatching `values.ssh()` for it, and amend commands.md:12-13 to exclude it as it already excludes `preflight infra`. Keep `preflight clusters` as is. Exit: `TestACommandRefusesAnInheritedFlagItDoesNotRead` and [inherited_scope_test.go:49-60](../../internal/cli/inherited_scope_test.go) cover `preflight container-cluster --ssh-user` refused as "flag is not accepted by this command" with no service call, and the help goldens omit the SSH overrides for it. The existing scope test asserts today's behavior and moves with the fix. `preflight add-ons` shares `allSSHFlags` at inherited_scope.go:18 and was not examined here.

#### CLI-04

**Medium, drift.** The sudo-entry environment guard runs before raw bounds and on help, version and completion, contradicting their no-effect contracts.

All three lenses agreed; the specification pages conflict and the code follows the security owner.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:46-49](../../specs/cli.md) puts raw bounds first in the precedence list for every invocation. [cli.md:105-110](../../specs/cli.md) says a raw-bound violation "always emits one source-free `cli.usage` diagnostic" and exits 2 without ambient-configuration or filesystem I/O. [commands.md:281](../../specs/cli/commands.md) says `version` "performs no environment lookup, filesystem access", and [commands.md:289-290](../../specs/cli/commands.md) gives completion no environment access. Against these, [security.md:449-453](../../specs/security.md) says every root invocation whose parent is the qualified sudo "refuses `runtime.privilege` before it acts on any variable outside what sudo sets", with the only stated limit at [security.md:465-467](../../specs/security.md). In [run.go:65-69](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go), `if b.euid() == 0 && b.sudoEnviron != nil { if refusal := b.sudoEnviron(); refusal != nil { return refuseAtBoundary(...` runs with no command classification gate, before `runServices` and so before the raw bounds in `runner.go`. `ConfirmSudoEnvironment` ([process_linux_amd64.go:195-229](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go)) stats `/proc/<ppid>/exe` through `sudoParent` ([account_linux_amd64.go:45-54](../../internal/controller/privilege/account_linux_amd64.go)) and reads the whole environment. The test at [session_refusal_test.go:111-127](../../cmd/bootwright/session_refusal_test.go) states the intent ("whether or not its command needs root") and expects `{"version"}` to refuse with exit 1.

**Reproduction.** `./scripts/go test ./cmd/bootwright/ -run TestASudoStartedRootInvocationRefusesAForeignVariableFirst` passes at the baseline, which confirms the behavior is intentional and pinned. The test covers `version`; help, completion and over-bound vectors share the same code path but have no row.

**Impact.** On a host whose sudoers `env_keep` passes ordinary variables such as `DISPLAY` or `LS_COLORS`, `sudo bootwright version`, `sudo bootwright --help` and `sudo bootwright completion bash` fail with `runtime.privilege` and exit 1. An over-bound argument vector under sudo reports `runtime.privilege` with exit 1 instead of `cli.usage` with exit 2. The CLI pages promise effect-free handling that the security page overrides without a stated exception.

**Counterevidence.** The behavior is deliberate and tested. The guard does nothing unless sudo started the invocation, so a root login shell is unaffected. The guard's `/proc` stat and environment read are boundary work, not the command's own work, and [cli.md:278-279](../../specs/cli.md) ("never elevate") is not violated. The only delivery records are X232, B977 and D212 ([delivered.md:10108](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md), [backlog.md:6413](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)), which add `COLORTERM` to the allowlist and do not address ordering.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Decide which page wins. The likelier remedy is spec text: state in the [cli.md](../../specs/cli.md) precedence list and in the version and completion clauses of commands.md that the sudo-entry guard of [security.md](../../specs/security.md) runs at the process boundary before step 1, with `runtime.privilege` and exit 1. The alternative is to run the guard only for invocations that `ClassifyInvocation` admits as acting, which weakens the "every root invocation" text and changes the test. Exit: either the spec text, or a boundary test under euid 0 with a foreign variable showing that over-bound arguments give `cli.usage` exit 2 and that version and help succeed.

#### CLI-05

**Low, defect.** Root human help omits the public `schema` command.

All three lenses agreed; the spec basis is an inference.

**Evidence.** The human root listing builds its rows from a fixed group list at [help.go:33-38](../../internal/cli/help.go): `{"Start", "context controller validate preflight"}` through `{"Tools", "version completion help"}`. `schema` is in none of the groups, and the Tools section of [help-root.golden](../../internal/cli/testdata/help-root.golden) holds only version, completion and help. `schema` is a visible catalog command ([commands_cli.go:6-7](../../internal/cli/commands_cli.go)) and a public one ([commands.md:163](../../specs/cli/commands.md)).

**Reproduction.** `./bin/bootwright --help | grep -c schema` prints 0, while `./bin/bootwright --help --output json` contains `"name":"schema"`. The binary was not rebuilt, so the probe assumes it matches the baseline; the code and the golden agree with it.

**Impact.** Operators reading root help cannot discover `bootwright schema`, and the human and structured root help disagree.

**Counterevidence.** `bootwright help schema`, completion and JSON help expose it. [cli.md:29-30](../../specs/cli.md) makes the catalog the sole list of command paths, and [commands.md:207-213](../../specs/cli/commands.md) discusses the root listing, but no clause says in words that the human root listing names every public command. `TestHelpGolden` pins the omission instead of catching it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add `schema` to the Tools group, for example `version schema completion help`, regenerate `help-root.golden`, and consider deriving the root rows from the catalog. Add one sentence to the Help content section of commands.md that the root listing names every non-hidden root child. Exit: `TestHelpGolden` with an updated golden and a test that every root child appears in the human root listing.

#### CLI-06

**Low, defect.** version accepts any letter case for the source state, where the spec requires exactly `clean` or `modified`.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [commands.md:270-276](../../specs/cli/commands.md) allows one normalization of composition-root values, "Surrounding whitespace is removed", renders the commit "in lowercase", and says "The source state is exactly `clean` or `modified`; any other value, including an absent one, renders as `unknown`." [version.go:23-26](../../internal/cli/version.go) computes `source := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(info.Source))` and then maps anything but `clean` or `modified` to `unknown`, so `Clean` or `MODIFIED` render as a definite state.

**Impact.** A mis-stamped build reports a definite source state instead of `unknown`. The build identity inaccuracy is minor.

**Counterevidence.** The fallback `sourceState` ([run.go:255-262](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go)) produces only lowercase values, so only a malformed `-ldflags` value is affected. The lenient behavior is pinned: [version_test.go:21](../../internal/cli/version_test.go) expects `" CLEAN "` to render `clean` and [version_test.go:46](../../internal/cli/version_test.go) expects `" MODIFIED "` to render `modified`. [run.go:193](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go) also compares with `strings.EqualFold(..., "modified")`. The spec clause and the code line came in the same commit, 77d499f2f, so which side was intended is open and the finding could instead be drift.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Drop `strings.ToLower` and keep `TrimSpace`; align [run.go:193](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go) with an exact comparison or record the leniency as deliberate. Exit: the two test cases above flip to expect `unknown`, with a `version` test that `Clean` renders `unknown`.

#### CLI-07

**Low, doc-stale.** The ordinary-confirmation code list omits controller rebind's controller.identity.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:251-254](../../specs/cli.md) closes the list of codes under which a confirming command refuses: `controller.install`, `controller.uninstall`, `media.store`, `machine.power`, `lifecycle.state`, `trust.identity`, `context.state` or `secret.store.conflict`. [cli.md:245-247](../../specs/cli.md) says only `controller install`, `controller uninstall` and `media` act on the host and name no context. [confirmation.go:110-112](../../internal/cli/confirmation.go) gives `controller rebind` its own confirmation: `case "controller rebind": return confirmation{code: "controller.identity", label: "rebind", ...`, whose prompt names the shown object and no context. The command is specified at [commands.md:152](../../specs/cli/commands.md) ("after a confirmation naming the recorded and the new identity") and added by D184 ([backlog.md:5278](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)).

**Impact.** Automation keyed on the documented codes misses the refusal code of `controller rebind`, and the spec under-describes a shipped confirmation.

**Counterevidence.** `controller.identity` is a documented diagnostic code at [output.md:1044](../../specs/cli/output.md), and the code behavior is sensible. A confirmation test exists ([confirmation_test.go:385](../../internal/cli/confirmation_test.go)) but does not compare codes against the spec list. No milestone item tracks the omission.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add `controller.identity` (`controller rebind`) to the list at cli.md:251-254, and name `controller rebind` among the host-level confirmations at cli.md:245-247. Exit: spec text updated, optionally with a test that enumerates the confirmation codes against the spec list.

#### CLI-08

**Low, doc-stale.** The closed list of standard-input readers omits media add --from-url-file - and the cluster sessions.

All three lenses agreed on the media half; the cluster-session half was dropped.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:228-231](../../specs/cli.md) says "Standard input is read only for an ordinary confirmation, the host-key confirmation and the session of `machine rsh` and `machine exec`, an explicitly requested sudo-password prompt, `secret set --password-stdin`, or `secret set --value-stdin`." [commands.md:464-475](../../specs/cli/commands.md) says `--from-url-file` reads the URL "from standard input for `-`", with a one-line limit of 16 KiB, a refusal under a logging sudo policy and a `--yes` requirement. The code reads stdin there: [invocation.go:63](../../internal/cli/invocation.go) sets `classification.URLStdin = path == "media add" && stringValue(command.Flags(), "from-url-file") == "-"`, [run.go:51](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go) and [run.go:113](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go) act on it, [wiring_managedos.go:44](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_managedos.go) and [wiring_managedos.go:73-79](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_managedos.go) bind the reader, and [service.go:151](../../internal/managedos/media/service.go) says "`--from-url-file - reads the URL from standard input`". The reader came from D183 and Q99 ([backlog.md:3353](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)).

**Impact.** A reader who treats cli.md as the owner of standard-input acquisition misses a credential-bearing stdin read.

**Counterevidence.** commands.md specifies the media stdin behavior fully. The cluster `rsh` and `exec` sessions are covered by delegation: [cli.md:1269-1279](../../specs/cli.md) opens them "exactly as `machine rsh` and `machine exec` do", and [cli.md:1245](../../specs/cli.md) and [cli.md:1328](../../specs/cli.md) say a session of several takes no standard input. They are not a missing reader. No item tracks the omission.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add `media add --from-url-file -` to the list at cli.md:228-231 with a link to commands.md:464-475; naming the cluster sessions is optional clarity. Exit: spec text updated.

#### CLI-09

**Low, drift.** cli.md says the trust command refuses the local-access controller; machine trust skips it, and --replace refuses with no remedy.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:458-462](../../specs/cli.md) says the SSH session and trust commands refuse the local-access controller "with an actionable diagnostic naming direct execution on that host". Sessions do: [resolve.go:36-38](../../internal/machine/access/resolve.go) fails `access.unavailable` with the remedy "run the command directly on" the object. `machine trust` instead classifies it as a skip: [target.go:100-103](../../internal/machine/target.go) returns `trust.ExemptReachedLocally`, and [selection.go:52-58](../../internal/trust/enrollment/selection.go) turns that into a `skip` row. That matches the owning Host-key trust section, [cli.md:1467-1474](../../specs/cli.md): `skip`, with its reason, "for every other Machine, which it never contacts". `--replace` on such a Machine refuses at [selection.go:74-76](../../internal/trust/enrollment/selection.go) with `failure("access.unavailable", name+" does not use context-managed trust: "+selection[index].skip, "")`, whose remedy is empty.

**Impact.** The two spec sections disagree, and an operator who names the controller in `--replace` gets a refusal with no remedy.

**Counterevidence.** Nothing is contacted and no host-key operation is fabricated, so the safety intent holds. The empty remedy applies to every ineligible Machine, not only the controller (installed Machines, Machines with a `knownHostsRef` and Machines with no SSH access). The matching `--expect` refusal at [service.go:212](../../internal/trust/enrollment/service.go) carries the remedy "drop it from --expect". The spec requires no remedy text for the `--replace` refusal today. Tests assert the code only ([service_test.go:503](../../internal/trust/enrollment/service_test.go)) and the removal row ([service_test.go:691-701](../../internal/trust/enrollment/service_test.go)).

**Correction and exit evidence.** Narrow cli.md:458-462 to say that sessions refuse the local-access controller while `machine trust` reports it as skipped with its reason. Give the `--replace` refusal a per-reason remedy: for the controller, run the command directly on that host; for the others, drop the name from `--replace`. Exit: spec text aligned, and a trust test asserting the `--replace` refusal's remediation.

#### CLI-11

**Low, defect.** The refusal for an executable path the invoking account cannot search names the path but not the account.

All three lenses agreed; the strict reading of "naming" is the basis.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:403-406](../../specs/cli.md) requires that an invoking account that cannot search a directory on the executable path "refuses `runtime.privilege` naming the path and that account, with the remedy of a local copy both that account and root can read". `unreadableExecutable(path)` at [process_linux_amd64.go:119-123](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go) takes only the path and says "the invoking account cannot resolve the Bootwright executable at "+path+" (permission denied)". Both callers at [process_linux_amd64.go:70-80](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go) pass only a path; the second passes the symlink-resolved path.

**Impact.** On a root-squashed or restricted mount, the operator has to work out which account lacks search permission. The remedy is correct.

**Counterevidence.** The path and the remedy text match the spec. The message does say "the invoking account", so a loose reading of "naming" could accept the role. The sibling clause at [cli.md:411-412](../../specs/cli.md), which "names the file or directory and its owner", supports the strict reading. `TestAnUnreadableExecutablePathNamesTheLocalCopyRemedy` ([process_linux_amd64_test.go:436-465](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64_test.go)) asserts only the prefix, the path and the remedy, so it passes without an account name.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Pass the invoking account's name, or its UID when no name resolves, into `unreadableExecutable` and include it in the message; the supervisor can obtain it from the invoking-account capture it already makes. Otherwise clarify the spec word. Exit: a unit test in `internal/controller/privilege` that asserts the message contains the account name.

#### CLI-12

**Low, drift.** A positive sudo timestamp_timeout that halves to less than 1 ms gets no refresh, but the spec says every unambiguous positive timeout refreshes at half its duration.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:365-367](../../specs/cli.md) says "An unambiguous positive effective timeout refreshes at half its duration, including fractional minutes. Zero and negative timeouts need no expiry refresh." In [sudo.go:278-283](../../internal/controller/privilege/sudo.go), `interval := time.Duration(minutes * float64(time.Minute) / 2)` is followed by "Sub-millisecond policies cannot support a bounded external-process loop." and `if interval < time.Millisecond { return 0 }`. The refresh goroutine returns at once when the interval is zero ([sudo.go:171](../../internal/controller/privilege/sudo.go)). A positive timeout below about 0.0000333 minutes therefore gets no refresh.

**Impact.** Almost none. A policy that short has expired before any refresh process could run, and sudo remains the authority. The spec and the code disagree on a stated number rule.

**Counterevidence.** The guard is intentional and commented. A loop faster than once per millisecond would be unbounded process churn. `TestRefreshTimeoutPolicy` ([sudo_test.go:164-190](../../internal/controller/privilege/sudo_test.go)) covers positive, zero, negative and fractional (0.01 gives 300 ms) policies but no sub-millisecond one. No item or knowledge page records the guard.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add one clause to cli.md:365-367 that a positive timeout whose half is under 1 ms gets no refresh, like zero. Clamping the interval to 1 ms is the weaker alternative, since it would start a process loop for an already expired timestamp. Exit: a `sudo_test.go` case pinning `refreshInterval` for `timestamp_timeout=0.00001` and the matching spec sentence.

#### CLI-13

**Low, doc-stale.** Structured machine trust without --yes or --dry-run is refused even when it has no pending trust-store write.

The reproduce lens read the finding as a code defect, the spec and refute lenses as stale spec wording; an arbitration settled it as doc-stale.

**Evidence.** [commands.md:457-461](../../specs/cli/commands.md) says "A `machine trust` invocation selecting JSON or YAML with pending trust-store writes requires `--yes`; without it the invocation must use `--dry-run` or fails without writing." The owning Host-key trust section is unconditional: [cli.md:1514-1516](../../specs/cli.md) says "Under `--yes` or `--dry-run`, and in either structured format, which requires one of them, nothing precedes the result", [cli.md:1523-1524](../../specs/cli.md) says "Under `--yes`, and so in either structured format", and [security.md:675](../../specs/security.md) says "Under `--yes` or a structured format". The code, reached from the `machine trust` case at [validation.go:250-251](../../internal/cli/validation.go), is at [validation.go:256-258](../../internal/cli/validation.go): `if selectedJSON(command) && !boolValue(flags, "yes") && !boolValue(flags, "dry-run") { return structuredLabel(command) + " trust changes require --yes or --dry-run" }`. The validation table row `{"machine trust --output json", false}` at [validation_test.go:28](../../internal/cli/validation_test.go) holds the refusal, but no test asserts its text.

**Impact.** A scripted `machine trust -o json` over Machines that are all already trusted fails with `cli.usage` and exit 2, and the catalog wording suggests it would succeed. The workaround is `--dry-run`.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fails safe and writes nothing. Pending writes are known only after observation, so a usage-time check cannot test that condition; the unconditional rule is the only form the check can take. D183 and Q97 cover `--expect` only, and no item tracks the wording.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Drop "with pending trust-store writes" from commands.md:457-458 so the catalog matches cli.md. No code change is warranted. Exit: spec text aligned.

#### CLI-14

**Low, defect.** render effective --origins names leaves by effective list positions, not the authored positions the spec requires.

All three lenses agreed.

**Evidence.** [cli.md:531-532](../../specs/cli.md) says "A leaf is a scalar, an empty map or an empty list, named by its field path with authored list positions." The general rule at [api.md:176](../../specs/api.md) is that in a diagnostic path "a list index is the authored position in the document, even for a list the schema later sorts". `fieldOrigins` walks the effective spec, `r.object.Spec()`, and writes the effective path into the result ([origins.go:20-39](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/origins.go)): `walk(item, path+"["+strconv.Itoa(index)+"]")` at line 31, then `FieldOrigin{Field: path, Origin: r.originOf(path)}` at line 34. `originOf` ([origins.go:41-51](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/origins.go)) calls `r.sourceField(path)` at line 42 only to look up the origin. When a normalizer moves a list element, `recordReordering` records `moved[to] = from` ([provenance.go:51-121](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/provenance.go), the assignment at line 111), and `sourceField` maps an effective path back to its authored one ([provenance.go:123-139](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/provenance.go)); [phases.go:253](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/phases.go) calls `recordReordering`. Diagnostics already report the authored position: [diagnostics.go:164](../../internal/desiredstate/compilation/diagnostics.go) sets `item.Field = record.sourceField(issue.Field)`. The case is reachable on a qualified path: CephCluster normalization sorts `serviceBindings` by `serviceRef` and each binding's `secrets` by `path` ([normalization.go:130-139](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/normalization.go)), and both lists carry a name key ([storage_native.go:15-17](../../api/v1alpha1/storage_native.go)), so the move is recorded.

**Impact.** When `serviceBindings` are authored out of `serviceRef` order, `render effective --origins` reports their leaves at the sorted positions, so an operator who looks up a reported field in the authored document finds a different element. The origin value of each leaf is still classified correctly, since the lookup uses the authored path, and the origins output disagrees with diagnostics on list numbering.

**Counterevidence.** With no reordering the two numberings agree. `TestRenderEffectiveOriginsMarkEachLeaf` in [render_origins_linux_amd64_test.go:15-54](../../cmd/bootwright/render_origins_linux_amd64_test.go) uses no reordered list, so no test pins either reading. Derived elements have no authored position, and the spec gives no rule for naming them. The delivered record of the feature ([delivered.md:9045-9053](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)) repeats the authored-position rule with no qualifier, and no item, decision or `Not yet met` line tracks the discrepancy.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Report `r.sourceField(path)` as the field when the leaf has an authored position, and fall back to the effective path for a derived element; state that fallback in the spec. The alternative, rewording the spec to effective positions, would also have to reconcile [api.md:176](../../specs/api.md). Exit: extend `TestRenderEffectiveOriginsMarkEachLeaf` with a CephCluster whose `serviceBindings` are authored out of order and assert that each reported index is the authored one.

#### Observations

- The catalog in `internal/cli/catalog.go` and `commands_*.go` matches every row of the commands.md tables in command paths, local flags, requiredness and repeatability. No flag or command exists on one side only.
- Parsing (`resolveInvocation` and `tokenFlag`) implements exact-name resolution, local-flag non-inheritance, payload stop, the `--` rule and syntactic `--output` selection on failures, as specified.
- Occurrence-local empty rejection is built into `scalarValue.hasEmptyOccurrence` (flags.go), with the exceptions context, sha256, clusters, replace and `machine trust --name`.
- Context-independent inherited-flag checks (DNS-label `--context`, trimmed `--ssh-user` grammar, `--ssh-user-for-provisioned`, `--ssh-ask-sudo-password` versus structured output, sessions requiring text) run before availability and privilege.
- The raw-bound check applies count first, then per-argument length, then the aggregate, with inclusive maxima, and never echoes an argument.
- All tests named by the in-range spec text exist at the baseline.
- Confirmation reads byte by byte with a 64-byte ceiling including LF, accepts only `y` or `yes`, and its remedy repeats the invocation with `--context`, placeholders for undisclosed flags and a bound data-loss digest placeholder.
- `diff --output-dir` and `--tool` use an invoking-account helper (`comparisonlocal`); `render` does not, which is why its output side diverges (CLI-01).
- The supervisor's start-line filter carries out the held-line rules exactly: 16 lines of at most 4096 bytes, withheld in structured mode, held in human noninteractive mode and passed in interactive mode, with boundary tests ([elevation_test.go:617-649](../../internal/controller/privilege/elevation_test.go)).
- Escalation ignores SIGHUP after the first cancellation, and `runRelayed` kills sudo only on the escalation channel, which matches [cli.md:349-352](../../specs/cli.md).
- The refresh warning is suppressed in structured output through `Quiet: invocation.JSON`, which covers YAML as well.
- Media URL standard input reuses the secret input-logging refusal through `privilege.MediaURLInput` ([run.go:113-115](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go)).
- The redirect refusal names the target without its query, which is stricter than the spec and protects signed URLs.
- The JSON Schema export marks nothing required at the top level of a spec and nothing inside kind defaults, which follows the partial-spec rule.
- Invoking-account reads (input directories, secret files, media sources, `--ssh-id-file`) all go through `invokerfs.Opener`, wired once in [wiring.go:108](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring.go). Selection files use a separate helper that runs as the account.
- The background-terminal read in [stdin_linux_amd64.go:196-213](../../cmd/bootwright/stdin_linux_amd64.go) deliberately raises SIGTTIN so job control can hand the terminal over, and has a test.
- Preflight remote reads bind no Confirmer or Terminal in `machineaccess.Options`, so a live preflight cannot enroll a host key.
- The sudo refresh loop is sequential within one goroutine and the supervisor waits for it before returning, so refresh processes cannot overlap or outlive the child.
- The trust confirmation prompt names only the context; the Machines it acts on appear only in the plan printed before it.
- `cluster oc` and `cluster kubectl` are non-available catalog entries ([catalog.go:219-227](../../internal/cli/catalog.go)), so they take the unavailable path without privilege.

#### Limits

The sudo supervision internals in `internal/controller/privilege` (relay, held-line release, signal escalation, refresh scheduling, getent parsing) were checked only by their constants and remedy strings, not by tracing the code paths, and that package is outside the lane's listed code owners. Effective-origin and schema-export generation were checked in later rounds but not exhaustively. Compilation's discovery and path deduplication were not traced. Effects cells owned by other lanes (lifecycle, secrets, media, trust, controller) were matched for flag shape only. No test was added; the read-only probes were `bin/bootwright --help`, `version` and `preflight container-cluster --help`, one existing boundary test run, and temporary classification probes that were deleted. The `render` findings (CLI-01, CLI-02) rest on static reading plus a classification probe, because reproducing elevation needs sudo, which the rules forbid. `bin/bootwright` was not rebuilt, so its probes assume it matches the baseline. Reaping of refresh processes on cancellation and the ordering of concurrent results by frozen plan order ([cli.md:1-12](../../specs/cli.md)) are unproven by any run and belong to the lifecycle and output lanes. Not walked end to end in the last round: the secret and context publication paths of `contextfs` (a pre-existing symlink at a record name), the context delete orphan-inventory ordering before its prompt, and the elevated child's descriptor handoff through `invokerfs` `ServeHelper`.

#### Refuted candidates

- CLI-10, `cluster oc` and `cluster kubectl` unavailable outside the stub wiring held by `TestUnavailableCommandsMatchTheStubWiring`: the test holds the three-command list of its own section ([commands.md:133-137](../../specs/cli/commands.md)); the pair has its own `Not yet met` line at [commands.md:198](../../specs/cli/commands.md) tracked as B101, and the sentinel is pinned by `TestCompositionWiresEveryApplicationCommand` and the access package's unavailable test.
- CLI-15, completion, version and help read `NO_COLOR` and `TERM` before dispatch: the specs assign terminal, no-color and dumb-terminal facts to the composition root ([output.md:95-96](../../specs/cli/output.md), [commands.md:28](../../specs/cli/commands.md)), and the no-environment clauses govern the command's own derivation, not the composition root's presentation facts, and no completion or version output depends on these values.

### CLJ: Lifecycle behavior (stage selection, receipts, observation and exit status), desired and realized state comparison, resource inspection and explicit access (administrator export, machine SSH sessions, cluster sessions, storage dashboard, client keyring export, host-key trust, machine power)

Lane `cli-journeys`. Spec range: `specs/cli.md` lines 558-1648. Register: 472 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 7; confirmed: 6; tracked: 0; refuted: 1.

#### Assessment

Assessment. The lane covers specs/cli.md lines 558-1648. The behavior the ledger examined is largely sound: stage selection, the receipt format and next-step derivation, the authorization order (present, authorize, confirm, execute), the diff header and summary strings, the `--tool` and `--output-dir` file-system rules, the machine SSH session refusals and exit mapping, the several-Machine session rules, host-key trust enrollment, the storage dashboard and keyring export, and the machine power batch rules all matched the code, and goldens or dedicated tests pin most of them. No finding reaches High or Blocking. The six confirmed findings are all Low and cluster in two places: output wording and spec text that disagree with intentional code (CLJ-02, CLJ-03, CLJ-04, CLJ-07), and the proof behind clauses that are met in behavior but guarded loosely (CLJ-01 on the order of a credential read, CLJ-05 on the status parity sweep). The two Not yet met lines in the range (B544, B545) still match the code. The ledger leaves some sections lightly examined or not traced at the adapter boundary; the Coverage ledger and Limits below bound what this report claims.

#### Confirmed findings

| ID | Severity | Kind | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CLJ-01](#clj-01) | Low | defect | Machine and cluster session refusals at host-key proof and crypto-policy admission run after the session's private key has been decrypted |

| [CLJ-05](#clj-05) | Low | test-gap | The status parity sweep never derives a destroy over a completed apply and has no lost-binding or no-execution-definition row, though the spec cites it as proving the cases |
