#### ARC-01

**Medium, defect.** General-flow packages read the CephCluster's spec.management field path, and the architecture test explicitly does not look for field paths.

T detect field paths.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:77-79](../../specs/architecture.md) says "An architecture test refuses a substrate arm, an implementation identity or a Ceph field path or host layout in `internal/reconciliation`, `internal/desiredstate`, `internal/environment` and `internal/cli`."
[specs/architecture.md:60](../../specs/architecture.md) names the Storage family's current implementation as "the `CephCluster` kind, managed or external by `spec.management`". [specs/architecture.md:1162-1165](../../specs/architecture.md) and [specs/ceph.md:69](../../specs/ceph.md) confirm that `management` is the selector the Ceph implementation claims objects by.
[specs/architecture.md:1159-1160](../../specs/architecture.md) adds that application and domain policy never branch on concrete implementation identity. [specs/architecture.md:65-72](../../specs/architecture.md) has composition bind kind facts into Environment through published ports such as `StorageEvidence`.
Three general-flow sites read the field directly on storage objects.
- [internal/environment/access/service.go:103](../../internal/environment/access/service.go) reads `storage.Spec().Get("management").Text()` and refuses unless it is `managed`.
- [internal/environment/inspection/service.go:208-211](../../internal/environment/inspection/service.go) has `func external`, which reads `cluster.Spec().Get("management").Text()` and compares it with `ManagementManaged`.
- [internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/status_resources.go:24](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/status_resources.go) reads the same field in `storageSummaries`.

`implementationLiterals` in [test/architecture/family_neutral_test.go:53-77](../../test/architecture/family_neutral_test.go) matches only arm values, identity values, `"ceph"` and `"/ceph/"`. Its comment says "Field paths carry no family marker, so familyKindNames catches a family's kinds instead." TestGeneralFlowNamesNoImplementation therefore passes over all three reads.

**Impact.** Environment access, environment inspection and lifecycle status decide whether storage is external or managed from a Ceph field. They do not ask a port that the Storage family publishes. A second storage implementation, or a renamed selector, would need edits to the general flow, and the guard the spec cites would still pass.

**Counterevidence.** The storage family has one kind today, so behavior is correct; a second kind would read an empty value and be treated as managed. The family-kind and implementation-literal parts of the check work. `management` is also a field shared with infrastructure-service kinds ([specs/api/infrastructure-services.md:33](../../specs/api/infrastructure-services.md)), which weakens the label "Ceph field". The read at `internal/environment/selection.go:371` is on those service kinds and is not counted. Two more reads fall outside the four named packages: [cmd/bootwright/wiring_inspection.go:129](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_inspection.go) is composition and is allowed, and [internal/containercluster/access/service.go:101](../../internal/containercluster/access/service.go) is in the container-cluster context. The test comment shows that the narrower check is intentional. No item tracks this. Audit 001 F18-04 covered field paths in the general flow and was closed through B810 and X169 without removing these reads, so that closure record needs a cross-check.

**Correction and exit evidence.** There are two valid corrections. One: have the Storage domain publish a management predicate that composition binds, call it at the three sites, and extend `implementationLiterals` to refuse the Ceph field names the general flow must not read. Two, the cheaper one: narrow [specs/architecture.md:77-79](../../specs/architecture.md) to the kinds, arms, identities and literals the test checks, and say where the management decision is allowed to live. Exit for the first: `./scripts/go test ./test/architecture/ -run TestGeneralFlowNamesNoImplementation` fails on a seeded `Spec().Get("management")` in `internal/environment` and passes once the three sites use the accessor. Exit for the second: `make docs-check` after the spec edit.

#### ARC-02

**Low, defect.** Clock reads sit outside the effect boundary: the CLI and two application services read the system clock and timers directly.

Clock reads sit outside the effect boundary. The CLI builds its own wall clock and timers, and three application services fall back to `time.Now` because composition passes them no clock.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:374-375](../../specs/architecture.md) says "The composition root injects terminal, environment and timing facts; the CLI never discovers them." [specs/architecture.md:388-390](../../specs/architecture.md) says "Filesystem, process, persistence, network, clock, randomness, and remote access occur only in injected adapters."
- CLI: [internal/cli/progress.go:50-55](../../internal/cli/progress.go) defines `systemProgressClock()` with `now: time.Now` and `time.AfterFunc(delay, fire).Stop`. [internal/cli/output_controller.go:33](../../internal/cli/output_controller.go) and [internal/cli/output_reconciliation.go:69](../../internal/cli/output_reconciliation.go) call it, and their constructors take no clock. The comment at [internal/cli/progress.go:38-39](../../internal/cli/progress.go) says "Composition injects the wall clock", which the code contradicts.
- Prerequisites: [internal/controller/prerequisites/service.go:243-249](../../internal/controller/prerequisites/service.go) falls back to `time.Now` when `Options.Now` ([service.go:24](../../internal/controller/prerequisites/service.go)) is nil. [cmd/bootwright/wiring_controller.go:103-110](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_controller.go) passes no `Now`.
- Machine access: [internal/machine/access/service.go:157-163](../../internal/machine/access/service.go) falls back to `time.Now` when `Options.Clock` ([service.go:31](../../internal/machine/access/service.go)) is nil. No clock is passed at [cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go:68-72](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go) or at [cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go:56](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go) and [:73](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go).
- Secret material: [internal/secrets/material/service.go:50](../../internal/secrets/material/service.go) defaults to `clock: time.Now` in its constructor. [specs/secrets.md:223](../../specs/secrets.md) requires an injected UTC-second clock for certificate validity.

`effectImport` in [test/architecture/boundaries_test.go:617-619](../../test/architecture/boundaries_test.go) lists `os`, `net`, `golang.org/x/sys`, `syscall`, `crypto/rand` and `unsafe`, but not `time`.

**Impact.** Progress timing and recorded timestamps cannot be replaced or held deterministic from composition. Any application package can start reading the clock and no fitness check fails. No safety, durability or secret consequence follows, which is why the severity is Low.

**Counterevidence.** Trust enrollment receives `Clock: time.Now` from [cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go:130](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go), though [internal/trust/enrollment/service.go:336](../../internal/trust/enrollment/service.go) keeps the same fallback. A `systemClock` adapter already exists at [cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go:98](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go). Domain roots read no clock. The spec does not claim that the effect-boundary test covers `time`, so the missing check is unenforced, not a broken enforcement claim.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Inject the progress clock from `cmd/bootwright` into the CLI presenters. Pass `Now` and `Clock` into `prerequisites.Options`, into all three `machineaccess.Options` sites and into secret material. Then remove the fallbacks and fix the comment at `progress.go:38-39`. Add `time.Now`, `time.Since`, `time.AfterFunc`, `time.NewTimer` and `time.Sleep` to the effect boundary as member grants held by the adapters that need them. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./test/architecture/ -run 'TestAdmissionEffectBoundary|TestEveryEffectClauseRefusesWhatItGuards'`, with a fixture in TestEveryEffectClauseRefusesWhatItGuards proving that a `time.Now` reference in an application package is refused.

#### ARC-03

**Low, drift.** Adapter-to-adapter wiring beyond the one named exception: invokerfs is injected into four other adapters through ports those adapters own.

Composition binds the `workspace/invokerfs` opener into four other adapters. The Named exceptions list says it is exhaustive and does not name this binding.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:107-110](../../specs/architecture.md) says "An adapter never calls another adapter to bypass that service. The named exceptions are the only departures from these rules." [specs/architecture.md:147-155](../../specs/architecture.md) adds "Each is deliberate and bounded; another like it is a defect." The one adapter-to-adapter case it names is `stagelocal`, injected into `controller/ansiblelocal` and `reconciliation/ansiblerunner` through a Controller-owned contract.
[cmd/bootwright/wiring_account.go:80-86](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_account.go) builds the `invokerfs.Opener`, and `openerFiles` at [wiring_account.go:105-112](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_account.go) binds it to the composition-root interface `operatorFiles` ([cmd/bootwright/wiring.go:55-59](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring.go)). Four wrappers then hand it to receiving adapters through ports those adapters own.
- `inputFiles` in [cmd/bootwright/wiring_desiredstate.go:85-98](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_desiredstate.go) builds `inputfs.Reader{Files: inputFiles{files: files}}`. The port is [internal/desiredstate/inputfs/reader.go:17-23](../../internal/desiredstate/inputfs/reader.go).
- `mediaFiles` in [cmd/bootwright/wiring_managedos.go:38-56](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_managedos.go) feeds `medialocal.New(mediaRoute(route), sources)`. The port is [internal/managedos/medialocal/acquirer.go:30-35](../../internal/managedos/medialocal/acquirer.go).
- `sshFiles` in [cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go:109-124](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go) returns `sshlocal.Files`. The port is [internal/machine/sshlocal/launcher_linux_amd64.go:43-48](../../internal/machine/sshlocal/launcher_linux_amd64.go).
- `secretFiles` in [cmd/bootwright/wiring_secrets.go:26](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_secrets.go) and [:57](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_secrets.go) feeds `material.New(... Files: secretFiles(deps.Files) ...)`. The port is [internal/secrets/material/contracts.go:22-25](../../internal/secrets/material/contracts.go).

The effect-grant comments describe this as intended: "An offered key arrives as a descriptor from the invoking account's opener" ([test/architecture/boundaries_test.go:518-522](../../test/architecture/boundaries_test.go)) and "Media acquisition receives an operator-named file as a descriptor" ([boundaries_test.go:530-533](../../test/architecture/boundaries_test.go)).

**Impact.** The exception list no longer states the actual dependency graph. A reviewer applying "another like it is a defect" would either reject intended wiring or stop trusting the list. The edges also cross contexts (Workspace into Desired State, Secrets, Managed OS and Machine), unlike the one listed exception, which stays within Controller.

**Counterevidence.** No adapter imports another; TestPackageDependencyDirection holds that. The binding is described in prose at [specs/architecture.md:517-532](../../specs/architecture.md), which says composition "binds `workspace/invokerfs` to the same lazily verified account for operator-named paths", and that each receiving adapter keeps its own type, ownership and stability proofs. Passing a descriptor bypasses no application service, so the line-109 rule is arguably not engaged. Only the exhaustive list is stale.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a Named exceptions bullet for the invoking-account opener that names `inputfs`, `secrets/material`, `medialocal` and `sshlocal` and links to the Workspace section. Alternatively, reword [specs/architecture.md:109-110](../../specs/architecture.md) so that passing a descriptor through the receiving adapter's own port is not a departure. Moving the port into a Workspace-owned contract is possible but larger than the gap warrants. Exit: `make docs-check`, with the bullet checked against `grep -n 'FileSession\|Files:' cmd/bootwright/wiring_*.go`.

#### ARC-04

**Low, drift.** "No Ansible role installs a host package" contradicts substrate_libvirt_host, which dnf-installs the hypervisor closure on an SSH provider host as substrates.md specifies.

Architecture.md says without qualification that no Ansible role installs a host package. The libvirt host role installs the hypervisor closure with dnf on a provisioned provider host, which substrates.md specifies.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:734-738](../../specs/architecture.md) says Go "installs host packages by running the host's own dnf (`internal/controller/hostdnf` ...), for setup and for a context's controller stage alike; no Ansible role installs a host package." The framing at [specs/architecture.md:722-723](../../specs/architecture.md) is "Go owns the controller's own dependencies".
[specs/substrates.md:136-140](../../specs/substrates.md) says "On an SSH host this block installs the named packages with the host's native package manager ... versions are not pinned".
[ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml:31-43](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml) runs `/usr/bin/dnf --assumeyes --setopt=install_weak_deps=False install` once per package, when the host is provisioned and no hypervisor was observed. It is the only dnf command in any role. [tests/unit/test_role_boundaries.py:85](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_role_boundaries.py) allowlists `/usr/bin/dnf` in the exact executable set, so the install is deliberate and pinned by a test.

**Impact.** A reader applying the architecture rule would treat specified substrate behavior as a violation, or would assume that an unpinned remote package install cannot happen. The boundary is stated wrongly for managed remote hosts.

**Counterevidence.** Read in context, the sentence is about the controller host, and the controller-hosted branch at [apply.yml:45-55](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_host/tasks/apply.yml) refuses and points to `bootwright apply --stage controller` rather than installing. The code matches the owning section, so this is a contradiction between specs, not a code defect. Audit 001 endorsed the unqualified sentence ([audits/001-spec/report-final.md:1339](../001-spec/report-final.md)), so that review missed it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Narrow [specs/architecture.md:738](../../specs/architecture.md) to "no Ansible role installs a package on the controller host". Link to the substrates.md provider host realization section for the one managed-host exception instead of restating it. Exit: `make docs-check`, and `grep -rn 'no Ansible role installs' specs` shows the qualified wording.

#### ARC-05

**Low, drift.** Composition root holds preflight decision logic over the SSH client, and the sshlocal exception does not admit preflight or capacity probes.

`cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go` translates the results of preflight and capacity remote commands, and it calls the SSH client's host-key observation itself. Neither the Composition translation exception nor the `sshlocal` exception names this.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:354-356](../../specs/architecture.md) says wiring "performs no context discovery, application work, domain decision, or presentation." [specs/architecture.md:164-169](../../specs/architecture.md) describes `machine/sshlocal` as the pinned SSH client "an explicit session and a host-key observation cross", "bound only to `machine/access` and `trust/enrollment`" ([:166-168](../../specs/architecture.md)). The Composition translation exception at [specs/architecture.md:170-179](../../specs/architecture.md) names its members exactly and lists no preflight member.
`preflightReads` at [cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go:84-117](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go) runs `machineaccess` Exec and maps the result.
- The untrusted-identity branch is at [:92-102](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go). When `request.ObserveUntrusted` is set, it calls `launcher.Observe(ctx, request.Address, request.Port)` on the `sshlocal` client at [:97](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go).
- Exit 255 (`sshTransportExit`, [:119](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go)) maps to `preflight.ErrUnreached` at [:103-106](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go). Other non-zero exits map to `preflight.ExitStatus`. On overflow the capture is cleared.
- `remoteCommands.Run` at [:46-69](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go) builds its own `sshlocal` client for the capacity probes used by `remoteCapacity` ([:40-42](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go)). It only returns the exit code and clears on overflow or a non-zero exit.

**Impact.** The spec's account of where Go reaches managed hosts over SSH omits preflight and capacity probes. A host-key observation crosses `sshlocal` outside the two packages the exception binds it to. No operator-visible or safety consequence follows: the trust proof still runs in `machine/access` Exec.

**Counterevidence.** The wiring does not decide check outcomes. It translates Exec results into the port vocabulary of `storage/preflight` (`ErrUnreached` and `UntrustedKey` at [internal/storage/preflight/contracts.go:35](../../internal/storage/preflight/contracts.go) and [:74](../../internal/storage/preflight/contracts.go)), and [internal/storage/preflight/guests.go:53-105](../../internal/storage/preflight/guests.go) classifies the checks. This is the kind of decoding the Composition translation exception describes. The application-side mapping is tested in [internal/storage/preflight/tiebreaker_test.go:261](../../internal/storage/preflight/tiebreaker_test.go) and [guests_test.go:88-91](../../internal/storage/preflight/guests_test.go). `preflightReads` itself is tested in [cmd/bootwright/preflight_fleet_linux_amd64_test.go:52](../../cmd/bootwright/preflight_fleet_linux_amd64_test.go) (the exit-255 refused fleet key), [:92](../../cmd/bootwright/preflight_fleet_linux_amd64_test.go) and [:137](../../cmd/bootwright/preflight_fleet_linux_amd64_test.go) (a non-zero exit status). The observe-untrusted branch and the overflow clearing are not tested at composition. [specs/cli/output.md:345-346](../../specs/cli/output.md) ("Installed guest probes use established verified Machine access") is consistent with this path. [specs/milestones/m2.md:2613](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) names the file as the operator session path, so the code is intentional.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either add `preflightReads` and `remoteCommands` to the Composition translation exception and admit the preflight untrusted-key observation in the `sshlocal` exception, or move the `Observe` call behind `machine/access`. Exit: `make docs-check` for the spec edit. A composition test covers the observe-untrusted fingerprint branch and the overflow clearing, run with `./scripts/go test ./cmd/bootwright/ -run TestStoragePreflight`.

#### ARC-06

**Low, drift.** Composition translation also decodes KubeVirt-proved identity through kubevirt.PinnedIdentity, which the named exception does not list.

The Composition translation exception names only `baremetal.PinnedIdentity`. Composition also decodes identity that `substrate/kubevirt` proved, through `kubevirt.PinnedIdentity`.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:175-177](../../specs/architecture.md) says "`machineIdentities`, for a power operation, and `provedIdentities`, for an installation's attempt, decode through `baremetal.PinnedIdentity` the hardware identity `substrate/baremetal` proved." [specs/architecture.md:149](../../specs/architecture.md) says "another like it is a defect".
`pinnedIdentity` at [cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go:241-246](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go) tries `baremetal.PinnedIdentity` and, when that finds nothing without an error, returns `kubevirt.PinnedIdentity(name, published)`. Both `machineIdentities.ProvedIdentity` ([:238](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go)) and `provedIdentities.PinnedIdentity` ([:262](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go)) call it. [internal/substrate/kubevirt/pin.go:10-29](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/pin.go) decodes the kube-system UID as UUID and the VirtualMachine UID as Serial. Commit 5bce25aef ("fix(substrate): pin every KubeVirt port entry point to its recorded cluster and VM") added the fallback. The comment on `provedIdentities` at [wiring_machine.go:249-253](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go) still speaks only of the bare-metal capability.

**Impact.** The exception list is incomplete. Read literally, it flags intended KubeVirt pinning as a defect.

**Counterevidence.** The fallback is intentional, and the decode goes through the owning package's own exported function, which is the purpose of the exception. No fitness test enforces the list. `provedIdentities` keeps only blocks whose kind is `baremetal.Kind` ([wiring_machine.go:255-262](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go)). `kubevirt.MachineKind` is also `"Machine"` ([internal/substrate/kubevirt/catalog.go:25](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/catalog.go)), so the filter passes KubeVirt blocks. Whether the installation path actually reaches the fallback depends on the published evidence and was not traced. The power path reaches it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Name `kubevirt.PinnedIdentity` and `substrate/kubevirt` in [specs/architecture.md:175-177](../../specs/architecture.md), and say that `pinnedIdentity` tries bare metal first and then KubeVirt. Update the comment at `wiring_machine.go:249-253`. Exit: `make docs-check`.

#### ARC-07

**Low, defect.** The adapter protocol decoder admits a controller "native" phase that the phase table does not define and no runner accepts.

The single protocol decoder admits a controller `native` phase. The phase table does not define it, no adapter emits it, and the controller judge refuses it.

**Evidence.** The phase table at [specs/architecture.md:937-946](../../specs/architecture.md) lists `loaded`, `prepared`, `continue`, `completed` and `refused` for the controller runner. [specs/architecture.md:991-996](../../specs/architecture.md) says the one decoder refuses "a phase its runner does not admit". [specs/architecture.md:998-1000](../../specs/architecture.md) counts the controller bound as "`loaded`, `prepared`, `completed` or `refused`, and a `continue` per tool".
[internal/adapterprotocol/record.go:101-102](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record.go) calls `phases` "the one table of which runner admits which phase", and [record.go:106](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record.go) has `"native": {members: []string{"phase"}, admitted: Controller}`.
Tests pin the row. [record_test.go:125](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record_test.go) and [:141](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record_test.go) accept it for Controller. [:105](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record_test.go) refuses it for Lifecycle. TestReadEndsOnTheConsumersShapeRefusal ([:248-251](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record_test.go)) and TestDecodeAcceptsWhatThePluginsEmit ([:273](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record_test.go)) also use it.
[plugins/action/controller_protocol.py:80-93](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/controller_protocol.py) emits only `loaded`, `continue`, `prepared` and `completed`. The controller judge's switch at [internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go:212](../../internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go) has no `native` case, and `default: valid = false` at [:262-263](../../internal/controller/ansiblelocal/runner_linux_amd64.go) treats it as a breach. The row arrived with the single-protocol refactor, c4c335609.

**Impact.** The decoder's vocabulary and the spec disagree, so the one decoder no longer states the contract on its own. TestDecodeAcceptsWhatThePluginsEmit claims a record that no plugin emits. No run outcome changes, because the judge refuses the phase.

**Counterevidence.** The judge's refusal makes the run outcome match the spec. No delivered record or decision introduces the phase, so this is a leftover row rather than spec drift.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Remove the `native` row from [record.go:106](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record.go). Move the cases at `record_test.go:105`, `:125`, `:141` and `:273` to the Controller refusal list, and give the shape-refusal test at `:248-251` another record. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/adapterprotocol/ -run 'TestDecodeAdmitsEachRunnersPhasesOnly|TestDecodeAcceptsWhatThePluginsEmit|TestReadEndsOnTheConsumersShapeRefusal'`, with `native` among the Controller refusals.

#### ARC-08

**Low, defect.** Command-service file convention (requests.go holds the CLI's request and result types) is not enforced, and several services place them elsewhere.

The package table puts a command service's request and result types in `requests.go`. At least eight CLI-facing services declare them elsewhere, and no check holds the convention.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:300](../../specs/architecture.md) says "`requests.go` the request and result types the CLI consumes". Finding code step 3 ([specs/architecture.md:406-409](../../specs/architecture.md)) says "`requests.go` is what the CLI sees".
- [internal/addons/catalog/service.go:18-28](../../internal/addons/catalog/service.go) declares `ListRequest`, `ListResult`, `DescribeRequest` and `DescribeResult`, and the package has no `requests.go`.
- [internal/environment/preflight/contracts.go:15](../../internal/environment/preflight/contracts.go) and [:20](../../internal/environment/preflight/contracts.go) declare `InfrastructurePreflightRequest` and `AllPreflightRequest`.
- [internal/nativeartifacts/rendering/contracts.go:12](../../internal/nativeartifacts/rendering/contracts.go) and [:19](../../internal/nativeartifacts/rendering/contracts.go) declare `RenderRequest` and `Result`.
- [internal/containercluster/preflight/contracts.go:19](../../internal/containercluster/preflight/contracts.go) declares `PreflightRequest`.
- [internal/storage/preflight/service.go:27](../../internal/storage/preflight/service.go) declares `PreflightRequest`. `CommandRequest` at [contracts.go:56](../../internal/storage/preflight/contracts.go) may be an adapter request rather than a CLI one.
- [internal/environment/clusterpreflight/contracts.go:11](../../internal/environment/clusterpreflight/contracts.go) declares `PreflightRequest`.
- [internal/environment/inspection/service.go:34-38](../../internal/environment/inspection/service.go) declares `ListClustersRequest` and `ClusterInfoRequest`. `KeyringRequest` and `KeyringResult` are in [keyring.go:15-21](../../internal/environment/inspection/keyring.go), and two result types are in [result.go:43](../../internal/environment/inspection/result.go) and [:137](../../internal/environment/inspection/result.go).
- [internal/containercluster/access/service.go:29](../../internal/containercluster/access/service.go) and [:42](../../internal/containercluster/access/service.go) declare `OCRequest` and `KubectlRequest`, while the package's `requests.go` holds only the kubeconfig types.

Twelve of the 25 packages that declare `Service` in `service.go` have no `requests.go`. TestServicePackagesFollowTheFileConvention ([test/architecture/layout_test.go:69-107](../../test/architecture/layout_test.go)) checks only where `Service` and exported interfaces are declared.

**Impact.** A reader following the Finding code path misses request types. There is also a test consequence: TestEveryRequestFieldIsRead scans only types declared in a file named `requests.go` ([test/architecture/requests_test.go:153](../../test/architecture/requests_test.go); see [:20-36](../../test/architecture/requests_test.go) and [:133-160](../../test/architecture/requests_test.go)). Request types placed elsewhere therefore escape the unread-field refusal, the CLI contract against accepted but ignored flags. No unread field has been shown to exist.

**Counterevidence.** Each of these packages keeps its interfaces in `contracts.go` and `Service` in `service.go`. `addons/catalog` is a working service, not a stub, so the "service.go alone" stub shape does not excuse it. Several packages hold only a few trivial types.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Move the request and result types into `requests.go`, and decide where type aliases such as `Report` in the two preflight packages belong. Extend TestServicePackagesFollowTheFileConvention to refuse an exported request or result type outside `requests.go` in a command service, or widen the `requests_test.go` scan to every file. The alternative is to soften the spec to apply only where a package has several such types. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./test/architecture/ -run 'TestServicePackagesFollowTheFileConvention|TestEveryRequestFieldIsRead'` fails on a seeded request type in `service.go`.

#### ARC-09

**Low, test-gap.** "Context root: no ports" is only checked for function types; managedos declares an exported interface port and reads through it.

The spec says a context root holds no ports and no I/O. The guard checks exported function types only, and the domain root `internal/managedos` declares an exported interface it reads image bytes through.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:297](../../specs/architecture.md) describes a context root as "Pure domain values, invariants and derivations ... No ports and no I/O."
[internal/managedos/treeinfo.go:20-22](../../internal/managedos/treeinfo.go) declares `type MediaBytes interface { ReadAt([]byte, int64) (int, error) }`. `ReadMediaRelease(image MediaBytes, size int64)` at [treeinfo.go:24](../../internal/managedos/treeinfo.go) and the reader at [:44-57](../../internal/managedos/treeinfo.go) read through it. The only caller, [internal/managedos/media/service.go:114](../../internal/managedos/media/service.go), passes the staged media file, whose `ReadAt` is implemented by the adapter at [internal/workspace/contextfs/media_linux_amd64.go:905](../../internal/workspace/contextfs/media_linux_amd64.go).
TestDomainRootsDeclareNoFunctionTypedPorts ([test/architecture/domain_ports_test.go:24-46](../../test/architecture/domain_ports_test.go), allowlist at [:15-19](../../test/architecture/domain_ports_test.go)) collects function types only. Its fixture at [:70-76](../../test/architecture/domain_ports_test.go) expects an interface to be ignored. The exported-interface check in [test/architecture/layout_test.go:87-89](../../test/architecture/layout_test.go) skips every package that is neither an application package nor a listed contracts package, so no guard looks at exported interfaces in domain roots.

**Impact.** A domain root can add an interface-typed port and the fitness suite does not notice, which weakens the rule the spec relies on. `MediaBytes` is the only exported interface in a domain-role package today.

**Counterevidence.** `MediaBytes` has exactly the shape of `io.ReaderAt`, and the parsing it feeds is deterministic, so it can be read as a value contract rather than a port. Excluding interfaces from the guard is deliberate. The spec names no test for this clause. The gap stands even if `MediaBytes` is accepted.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Replace `MediaBytes` with `io.ReaderAt`; `*os.File` and `bytes.Reader` already satisfy it. Then extend the domain-port guard to exported interfaces in domain roots, with an exact allowance that only shrinks. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./test/architecture/ -run TestDomainRootsDeclareNoFunctionTypedPorts`, with a fixture proving that an exported interface in a domain root is refused.

#### ARC-10

**Low, test-gap.** The ban on package-global mutable state has no fitness check; an exported mutable slice backs the sudo environment allowlist.

The spec forbids package-global mutable configuration and registries apart from the schema registry, and no fitness check looks at package-level variables. An exported, writable slice serves as the allowlist of environment names that cross sudo.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:390-392](../../specs/architecture.md) says "Package-global mutable flags, streams, registries, clocks, configuration, and service instances are forbidden, apart from the schema registry". The schema-registry exception is at [specs/architecture.md:180-182](../../specs/architecture.md).
[internal/controller/route.go:17](../../internal/controller/route.go) declares `var ProxyEnvironmentNames = []string{"HTTPS_PROXY", "HTTP_PROXY", "NO_PROXY"}`. It is read at [internal/controller/privilege/sudo.go:199](../../internal/controller/privilege/sudo.go) (`!slices.Contains(controller.ProxyEnvironmentNames, name)`), at [internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go:241](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go) and at [route.go:140](../../internal/controller/route.go).
The test/architecture walkers that visit package-level declarations serve other purposes: tracing diagnostic codes, resolving doc references, and reading constants. None refuses a mutable package variable.

**Impact.** Any package could append to `ProxyEnvironmentNames` and widen what crosses the privilege boundary, and no fitness check would object.

**Counterevidence.** Nothing writes the slice today. The spec's list of what the fitness packages enforce ([specs/architecture.md:397-400](../../specs/architecture.md)) does not include this ban, so the gap is an unenforced rule, not a broken enforcement claim. The `sync.OnceValue` caches at [internal/environment/selection.go:420](../../internal/environment/selection.go) and [api/v1alpha1/schema.go:144](../../api/v1alpha1/schema.go) are derived once from the immutable schema registry. They are lazy constants, not violations. The many unexported package-level tables (for example `sudoVariables` at [internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go:231](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go) and `phases` at [internal/adapterprotocol/record.go:102](../../internal/adapterprotocol/record.go)) are read-only lookup tables. It is not clear that the clause covers them.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Make `ProxyEnvironmentNames` an accessor that returns a fresh slice. Add a fitness check that refuses an exported package-level variable of slice, map or func type outside the schema registry, with an exact allowance that only shrinks. Among the variables found, that check would flag only `ProxyEnvironmentNames`. Exit: a new test in test/architecture refuses a seeded `var Exported = []string{}` in an internal package and passes on the tree.

#### ARC-11

**Low, drift.** KubeVirt arm identities added after the naming rule do not read `<domain>`-`<implementation>`-`<capability>`-`v<N>`, and no test holds the pattern.

The recipe for a new implementation requires identities to read `<domain>-<implementation>-<capability>-v<N>`. The KubeVirt identities were added two days after that rule and use the older libvirt shape. The KubeVirt decision record and substrates.md name those identities as written, and no test holds the pattern.

**Evidence.** [specs/architecture.md:455-460](../../specs/architecture.md) puts the implementation identity "in `catalog.go`" and says "A new identity reads `<domain>-<implementation>-<capability>-v<N>`." The rule entered the spec in 7a63488a2 (2026-10-26).
[internal/substrate/kubevirt/catalog.go:16-17](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/catalog.go) declares `HostImplementation = "substrate-host-kubevirt-v1"` and `MachineImplementation = "machine-kubevirt-v1"`. They first appear in 016e31b89 and 225e02db2 (2026-10-28). The host identity orders domain, capability, implementation, which mirrors [internal/substrate/libvirt/catalog.go:16-17](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/catalog.go).
D197 names `substrate-host-kubevirt-v1` on purpose ([specs/milestones/backlog.md:5620](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)), and [specs/substrates.md:24-26](../../specs/substrates.md) names the identities as written.
Most identities follow the same order, so the tree does not use the pattern: `os-install-anaconda-v1`, `dns-server-dnsmasq-v1`, `machine-power-v4`. [internal/storage/ceph/export.go:20](../../internal/storage/ceph/export.go) declares `ceph-export-v1` with no storage domain, and [internal/controller/clients/requests.go:20](../../internal/controller/clients/requests.go) declares `controller-prerequisites` with no version.
Several identities sit outside `catalog.go`, for example [internal/storage/ceph/host.go:20](../../internal/storage/ceph/host.go) (`storage-ceph-host-v1`, which follows the pattern) and [internal/managedos/installation/firewall_request.go:23](../../internal/managedos/installation/firewall_request.go).
[test/architecture/implementation_identity_test.go:18-52](../../test/architecture/implementation_identity_test.go) holds the allowlists, and the identity collection at [:60-80](../../test/architecture/implementation_identity_test.go) checks where identities are used, not how they are named.

**Impact.** No operational effect. Readers cannot predict an identity from its parts, and the specs disagree with each other about the newest substrate arm. Identities are frozen into plans, so renaming one later needs a version move.

**Counterevidence.** The rule binds only "a new identity". The pattern is ambiguous for substrate-family names, and `machine` can be read as the domain of `machine-kubevirt-v1`. The KubeVirt shape keeps symmetry with its libvirt and bare-metal siblings. [specs/architecture.md:301](../../specs/architecture.md) requires `catalog.go` only for packages that have identities, so the location claim applies to the recipe's package, not to capabilities inside existing packages. No spec clause requires a naming test.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either state in the recipe that identities predating the rule, and new members of a family whose siblings already use another shape, keep that shape, and list those families; or add an architecture test that holds every identity bound in `buildCapabilitiesWith` to the pattern with an exact allowance that only shrinks. Note the unversioned `controller-prerequisites` separately. Exit: `make docs-check` for the spec route, or a test in test/architecture that fails on an identity outside the pattern and the allowance.

#### Observations

- Every test the spec names exists at f8b15669f: 30 Go tests across test/architecture, cmd/bootwright, internal/cli and ansible, plus the named collection tests.
- `packageRoles` classifies every production package, and TestPackageDependencyDirection keeps `applicationDependencies` exact in both directions, so a stale edge fails.
- The effect boundary uses exact grants. A grant a package no longer needs fails, and each clause has a refusing fixture (TestEveryEffectClauseRefusesWhatItGuards).
- The bounds in internal/adapterprotocol/record.go:63-77 and the runner deadline and drain constants match the spec numbers.
- The implementation-identity, family-kind, long-function and contract-deviation allowlists are all empty.
- The produced-material custody rule is enforced in one function, `lifecycle.capture`, which clears the material on every path.
- The adapter runner core has one session state machine that encodes the post-exit judgment and the EPIPE split. StopOnBreach is the only difference between the lifecycle and controller runners.
- Version specialization has a single Python registry whose tests prove seam exclusivity over all fact assignments.
- nativeError is gated three times (Python capability flag, Go decoder, runner per-request gate). Credentials are redacted twice on the Python side. Only five protocol plugins opt in, because the Ceph host and core share one plugin.
- The read-only observe allowlist is keyed on `operationPlaybook` entries ending in `/observe`. Read-shaped ports such as `machine/power_read.yml` are held only by their own unit tests.
- Implementation identities do not follow the naming pattern uniformly. The spec applies it only to new identities, and no test enforces it (ARC-11).

#### Limits

The whole of specs/architecture.md was read. The work was reading only: no Go test, vet or ansible-check run was made, and the verdicts rest on the sources and tests plus one PyYAML scan of the argument specs. The first round checked the runtime semantics of the adapter protocol, the lifecycle ports, version-specialization exclusivity and the make quick and make focus selection only at the level of constants and test existence. The second and third rounds traced the targeted clauses in code; the ledger rows prefixed Round 2 and Round 3 record them. Some points remain untraced. They are the text of the lifecycle.unsupported message beyond its test, whether every local service effect takes host reservations, the registration-time authorization check for consumed removals, whether root only sends back helper-issued descriptors in invokerfs, and the lane-verdict and collection-narrowing rules in scripts/tools/focus.py. The e2e renderer behavior and the private-material clause were not examined, and private fixtures were excluded by rule. Prose rules on comments and naming are reviewer judgments and were left unverifiable. Controller-host protection and deeper engine semantics overlap the state-reconciliation, controller and tooling lanes.

#### Refuted candidates

- ARC-12, "The generic policy bucket ban has no fitness check by name": refuted because [specs/architecture.md:34-37](../../specs/architecture.md) forbids those buckets only "when they lack one semantic owner". The required declared-ownership check (every package must have a `packageRoles` entry, [test/architecture/boundaries_test.go:286](../../test/architecture/boundaries_test.go)) already covers that condition. [specs/architecture.md:1244-1245](../../specs/architecture.md) leaves semantic ownership to reviewers, and no bucket package exists. A name denylist would be an optional hardening, not a missing required check.

### SEC: Trust model and input bounds, sensitive material, filesystem and artifact safety, process boundary, local context privilege, network and remote systems and privilege, cryptography and supply chain, logs and diagnostics, custom code, stateful mutation, required security proof

Lane `security`. Spec range: `specs/security.md` lines 1-871. Register: 364 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 7; confirmed: 7; tracked: 0; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

The security lane is largely sound. The privilege boundary, the runner's handling of confidential material, the process-boundary lock protocol, private publication of files, the SSH client options and the proof register all match `specs/security.md` where they were read, and every one of the 210 test names the spec cites exists as a test definition. The discrepancies cluster in three places. First, the same rule is implemented several times and the copies disagree: the root-owned executable qualifier exists for sudo, rpm, dnf and the NSS getent but not for the preflight getent, firewall-cmd and the SSH client (SEC-01), and the three SSH crypto-policy parsers disagree on the `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` line that every FIPS back end carries (SEC-07, the only High finding). Second, three general clauses of the network and logs sections have no code behind them: redirect and connection-target authorization for wheel fetches (SEC-06) and the internal-error boundary with a correlation identity (SEC-02). Third, the proof register and the Not yet met lines have drifted from delivery state (SEC-03, SEC-05), and one proxy-spelling rule is met only by accident (SEC-04). No Blocking finding was confirmed, and no confirmed finding is already tracked by a Not yet met line. The assessment is bounded by the ledger: the filesystem handle-based opens, the Listener ACLs beyond the managed proxy and chrony defaults, custom code and stateful mutation (owned by other lanes) were examined thinly or not at all.

#### Confirmed findings

| ID | Severity | Kind | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [SEC-01](#sec-01) | Medium | defect | Root-run exec sites for getent, firewall-cmd and the SSH client skip the root-ownership qualification; two also inherit the invoker's working directory |
| [SEC-02](#sec-02) | Medium | gap | No internal-error boundary: a Go panic prints a full goroutine stack, and no correlation identity exists |
| [SEC-03](#sec-03) | Low | doc-stale | The B721 Not yet met line is stale: the image build already receives the controller Machine's proxy route |
| [SEC-04](#sec-04) | Low | defect | The image-build route sets only upper-case proxy variables, against the rule that both spellings carry the same value |
| [SEC-05](#sec-05) | Low | doc-stale | Required-security-proof Gap cells name delivered items, and the Ceph consumer row says "none yet" although B86 and B760 are in-tree with tests |
| [SEC-06](#sec-06) | Medium | gap | Wheel fetch redirects are not revalidated for destination or private-address policy, and no Go dialer checks the resolved connection target |
| [SEC-07](#sec-07) | High | defect | The controller-side SSH policy parser refuses the generated `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` back end line that the tunnel parser admits |

#### SEC-01

**Medium, defect.** Root-run exec sites for /usr/bin/getent, /usr/bin/firewall-cmd and the SSH client skip the root-ownership qualification the attacker model requires; two of them also inherit the invoker's working directory.

**Evidence.** [security.md:55-60](../../specs/security.md) says "Every file the controller executes or loads ... is therefore admitted only when it and every directory above it are owned by root ... and writable by neither group nor others". [security.md:242-247](../../specs/security.md) requires "a pinned, verified executable" and "a fixed safe working directory", and [security.md:666-667](../../specs/security.md) requires that the SSH client's "identity is verified before launch". Three Go sites run a fixed absolute executable without that proof. [resolver.go:26-28](../../internal/containercluster/preflightlocal/resolver.go) runs `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "/usr/bin/getent", argv[1:]...)` and sets Env and WaitDelay only. [native.go:24-26](../../internal/controller/firewalllocal/native.go) runs `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "/usr/bin/firewall-cmd", args...)` with no Dir and no ownership check. The SSH launcher's `executable()` ([launcher_linux_amd64.go:395-409](../../internal/machine/sshlocal/launcher_linux_amd64.go)) does `os.Stat(client)` and tests `!info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Mode().Perm()&0o111 == 0` at line 405, with no owner check, no parent-directory walk and no symlink resolution. For contrast, `qualifiedSystemExecutable` ([account_linux_amd64.go:90-120](../../internal/controller/privilege/account_linux_amd64.go)) proves Uid 0 and no 0022 bit on the file and on every parent; the NSS getent uses it and refuses with "the system getent is not a root-owned system executable" ([nss_linux_amd64.go:30-32](../../internal/controller/privilege/nss_linux_amd64.go)); hostdnf carries its own copy ([packages_linux_amd64.go:452-454](../../internal/controller/hostdnf/packages_linux_amd64.go)).

All three sites run in the elevated child. Every available command is marked privileged ([catalog.go:21](../../internal/cli/catalog.go)), and `ClassifyInvocation` sets RequiresRoot for them ([invocation.go:61](../../internal/cli/invocation.go)). The firewall Inspector is bound at [wiring_controller.go:48](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_controller.go), the resolver at [wiring_preflight.go:131](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go), and the SSH launcher at [wiring_machine.go:63](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_machine.go). The elevated `ProcessExecutor` sets no Dir on its sudo child ([process_linux_amd64.go:290-309](../../internal/controller/privilege/process_linux_amd64.go)), so the getent and firewall-cmd processes start in the invoker's directory. The SSH launcher does pin Dir "/" ([launcher_linux_amd64.go:106](../../internal/machine/sshlocal/launcher_linux_amd64.go), 149 and 223), so the working-directory half applies only to the first two sites. The decision [D152](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md) restates the rule at backlog.md:4245: "Root ownership with no group or other write stays on every executed or loaded path".

**Impact.** On a host where one of these binaries, or a directory above it, is group- or other-writable or not owned by root, the elevated invocation runs it as root without refusing, which breaks the stated trust boundary. getent and firewall-cmd also start in whatever directory the operator invoked from. [cli.md:378](../../specs/cli.md) binds only the NSS getent of the account capture, which is already met; it is not the owning clause for the resolver, whose clauses are security.md:55-60 and 242-247. For the SSH client, "verified" at security.md:667 is not defined as an ownership proof, so that part of the finding rests on a weaker clause. No milestone item, Not yet met line or audit record tracks any of the three sites.

**Counterevidence.** On a standard Fedora or RHEL host these paths are root-owned with 0755 parents, so an unprivileged attacker needs a prior misconfiguration. The environment of each site is minimal (PATH and LC_ALL only). The architecture effect grants ([boundaries_test.go:486-487](../../test/architecture/boundaries_test.go) and 522) list these packages as holding os/exec, so the set of sites is known, but nothing checks ownership.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Route all three through one shared root-owned-executable qualifier (the privilege package's `qualifiedSystemExecutable`, exported or moved to a shared host package), called from the resolver, the firewall command and `Launcher.executable()` (the single fix point for the three SSH command sites at lines 83, 117 and 193). Refuse with a typed diagnostic naming the file, and set Dir "/" on the getent and firewall-cmd commands. Exit: unit tests modeled on the NSS getent qualification tests, where a getent, firewall-cmd or SSH client that is group-writable, owned by another UID, or below such a directory refuses before any process starts; a test asserts `Dir == "/"` on each of the two commands.

#### SEC-02

**Medium, gap.** No internal-error boundary: a Go panic prints a full goroutine stack, and no correlation identity exists.

**Evidence.** [security.md:787-790](../../specs/security.md) says "An internal error exposes a correlation identity and safe summary, not a stack, memory dump, request body, or provider response". [main.go:13-24](../../cmd/bootwright/main.go) calls the three helper servers and then `os.Exit(runInteractive(context.Background(), os.Args[1:], os.Stdout, os.Stderr))` with no deferred recover; `runInteractive` ([run.go:27-29](../../cmd/bootwright/run.go)) only delegates. A grep of cmd/ and internal/ for `recover()`, `SetTraceback`, `GOTRACEBACK` and `SetCrashOutput` finds one test-local recover ([secrets_linux_amd64_test.go:182](../../internal/workspace/contextfs/secrets_linux_amd64_test.go)). The word "correlation" appears in code only in a controller identity comment ([identity.go:74](../../internal/controller/identity.go)) and in specs only at security.md:790. A typed `runtime.internal` diagnostic does exist ([output.md:1021](../../specs/cli/output.md), [cli.md:326](../../specs/cli.md), [remediation.go:41](../../internal/diagnostics/remediation.go), [runner.go:161](../../internal/cli/runner.go), [output_secrets.go:283](../../internal/cli/output_secrets.go)), with fixed safe summaries, but none carries a correlation identity and none covers a panic.

**Impact.** A runtime panic anywhere in a root invocation, including inside secret handling, reaches the operator's terminal, scrollback, CI logs or crash reports as Go's default goroutine traceback. Nothing ties the failure to a private log. Panics in goroutines and in the helper entry points ([main.go:14-22](../../cmd/bootwright/main.go)) are equally uncovered. The link to the crash-report sink at [security.md:117-120](../../specs/security.md) is weak, since that clause prohibits secret values and a Go traceback prints argument words as hex, not string contents.

**Counterevidence.** Panics are not observed on normal paths, and no secret disclosure is demonstrated. Nothing in milestones or backlog tracks the clause; the panic mentions at backlog.md:505, 799 and 1068 concern tests. The fix must be checked against the log-redaction rules, because [security.md:787-788](../../specs/security.md) lets a diagnostic identify a "private log reference", which could serve as the correlation identity.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add one recover boundary in `runInteractive` and in the helper entry points that renders the typed `runtime.internal` diagnostic with a random correlation identity and a fixed safe summary, writes the stack only to a private operation log if one exists, and exits non-zero. Specify the rendering in the diagnostic table of [output.md](../../specs/cli/output.md). Exit: a cmd/bootwright test that injects a panicking service and asserts stderr holds only the typed diagnostic and a correlation identity, with no "goroutine" or "panic:" text.

#### SEC-03

**Low, doc-stale.** The B721 Not yet met line is stale: the image build already receives the controller Machine's proxy route.

Tracked as B721 (the item itself stays open for operator acceptance; the Not yet met line is what is stale).

**Evidence.** [security.md:427-428](../../specs/security.md) reads "Not yet met: the image build runs direct; tracked as B721". The code now passes the route. [selection.go:371-387](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go) takes the controller Machine's egress through `managedservice.EgressFor(catalog, host)` and freezes `buildEgress = {"HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "NO_PROXY"}` into `request.BuildEgress` ([requests.go:153](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/requests.go)). The media role combines it into `containercluster_media_agent_environment` ([defaults/main.yml:33-35](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/containercluster_media_agent/defaults/main.yml)), and [build.yml:139](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/containercluster_media_agent/tasks/build.yml) (the `agent create cluster-manifests` task, which runs only when diskEncryption is defined) and build.yml:197 (the `agent create image` task, where the release payload is fetched) both use it as `environment:`. [proxy_test.go:64-74](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/proxy_test.go) pins the projection. The milestone record says "In-tree delivery, 2026-10-23: implementation and host-independent probes are delivered" ([m3.md:1185-1187](../../specs/milestones/m3.md)), the status row says "awaiting operator acceptance, X123" ([m3.md:489](../../specs/milestones/m3.md)), and [delivered.md:9712-9716](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) records X123.

**Impact.** Readers and later audits treat the proxy route of the image build as absent and may plan duplicate work. The unmet-clause register misstates delivery state.

**Counterevidence.** Operator acceptance of B721 is open, so the item rightly stays unclosed. Only the claim that the build "runs direct" is wrong.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Remove the Not yet met line. It cannot be reworded to point at acceptance, because a Not yet met line states what code does not do and never holds acceptance state ([SKILL.md:31-33](../../.agents/skills/milestones-and-knowledge/SKILL.md)); acceptance stays on [m3.md#b721](../../specs/milestones/m3.md). Exit: `make docs-check` passes and security.md no longer says the image build runs direct.

#### SEC-04

**Low, defect.** The image-build route sets only upper-case proxy variables, against the rule that both spellings carry the same value.

**Evidence.** [security.md:250-253](../../specs/security.md) says "An adapter that hands such a route to a native tool through its environment sets the upper- and lower-case spelling of each proxy variable to the same value, so a spelling the request did not set cannot supply a route of its own". [security.md:421-425](../../specs/security.md) gives the image build its route "under the same rule", and names the upper-case trio as the request keys. [selection.go:384](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go) builds only `{"HTTP_PROXY": ..., "HTTPS_PROXY": ..., "NO_PROXY": ...}`, the golden [media-request-build-proxy.golden:71-75](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/testdata/media-request-build-proxy.golden) shows the same three, and the role passes the map through unchanged ([defaults/main.yml:33-35](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/containercluster_media_agent/defaults/main.yml), [build.yml:139](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/containercluster_media_agent/tasks/build.yml) and 197). The Ceph pull broker sets both spellings ([ceph_pull_broker.py:591](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_pull_broker.py)) and validates them as a pair ([ceph_native.py:412-418](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native.py)).

**Impact.** Nothing today. The adapter's environment is rebuilt from a fixed list with no proxy variable ([process_linux_amd64.go:104-110](../../internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go)) and the inventory runs the controller locally ([runner.go:47](../../internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/runner.go) and 95), so no ambient lower-case variable reaches the installer. The rule holds by that accident, not by construction. One concrete latent edge: when NoProxy is empty the map sets `NO_PROXY=""`, Go's environment lookup skips an empty value and would fall through to an ambient `no_proxy`, which is the case the Ceph broker guards by also setting `no_proxy` to an empty string.

**Counterevidence.** The fixed adapter environment and Go's preference for upper-case names make the gap inert. The kind could equally be read as drift, since the spec names only the upper-case trio for this route. The existing tests check only the upper-case keys ([proxy_test.go:64-74](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/proxy_test.go), [test_install_features.py:8-21](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_install_features.py)), so a test gap goes with the defect. The spec section is also stale on the build route (SEC-03).

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` and `no_proxy` with the same values to `buildEgress` (or in the role defaults), and align security.md:421-425 and [B721](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) with the general rule; alternatively state that the upper-case trio is a deliberate exception. Exit: the agentinstall projection golden shows all six variables, and a media-role test checks both spellings.

#### SEC-05

**Low, doc-stale.** Required-security-proof Gap cells name delivered items, and the Ceph consumer row says 'none yet' although B86 and B760 are in-tree with tests.

B86 and B760 are named in the register and track the Ceph export work, not the register's staleness; the B17, B23 and B751 cells have no tracking.

**Evidence.** [security.md:850-852](../../specs/security.md) says "Each invariant names the tests that guard it and, where proof is known to be missing, the backlog item that adds it". Row 864 (time, retry, concurrency) ends `| B17, B23 |`, but B23 is delivered ([delivered.md:9735-9741](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md), "Real pinned-Ansible tests prove killed-supervisor cleanup and normal completion") and B17 is recorded delivered in the B265 record ([delivered.md:2748-2751](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md), "The work area moved under a root-only 0700 parent ... (B17, D98)"), with its remainder B303 also delivered ([delivered.md:4150-4155](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)). There is no standalone B17 heading. Row 870 links `B751` to `delivered.md#b751`, which exists at [delivered.md:8226](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md); B753 is still open ([m4.md:718](../../specs/milestones/m4.md)). Row 871 ([security.md:871](../../specs/security.md)) reads `none yet | B86, B760`, while [m4.md:1057](../../specs/milestones/m4.md) and [m4.md:1162](../../specs/milestones/m4.md) say "in-tree implementation complete; awaiting operator acceptance on B761", and tests exist: `test_rgw_lost_reply_recaptures_one_pair_without_key_arguments` ([test_ceph_export_native.py:298](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_export_native.py)), `test_failed_rgw_create_retains_no_rgw_material` (line 334) and `TestExportEvidenceGolden` ([export_test.go:102](../../internal/storage/ceph/export_test.go)).

**Impact.** The proof register misstates which safety invariants lack proof. The Ceph consumer secrecy invariant names no guard test, so a reviewer cannot tell whether its never-a-record, never-evidence and never-a-log clauses are proved. The existing tests cover parts of it (no key arguments, no retained material, evidence golden); no one checked that they cover every clause, including the log, diagnostic, gateway private key and no-adoption clauses.

**Counterevidence.** All 210 test names the table cites exist. B86 and B760 await operator acceptance, so naming them in the Gap cell is defensible; the stale part of row 871 is the "none yet" guarding-tests cell. The test at [test_ceph_export_native.py:69](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_export_native.py) asserts only that five keys are retained and is not a secrecy proof by itself.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Set the Gap cell of row 864 to "none" (B303, the successor of B17, is delivered too). Drop B751 from row 870 and keep B753. In row 871, list the export worker and evidence tests that prove the invariant and keep B86 and B760 only for clauses still unproved. Exit: `make docs-check` passes and every Gap cell names only open items.

#### SEC-06

**Medium, gap.** Controller wheel and tool fetch redirects are not revalidated for destination or private-address policy, and no Go dialer checks the resolved connection target.

**Evidence.** [security.md:487-489](../../specs/security.md) says "Redirects are disabled unless the port contract allows them; every permitted hop is revalidated for scheme, destination, credentials, and private-address policy", and [security.md:506-508](../../specs/security.md) says "DNS resolution and every connection target are checked against the same authorization so rebinding or alternate-address retries cannot expand scope". The wheel client's `approvedURL` ([fetch.go:274-277](../../internal/controller/venvlocal/fetch.go)) accepts any URL with an https scheme, no userinfo and a non-empty host on port 443, and its `CheckRedirect` ([fetch.go:298-306](../../internal/controller/venvlocal/fetch.go)) applies only `len(previous) >= maxRedirect || !approvedURL(request.URL)`, with no comparison against the lock host or mirror host. A mirror is any HTTPS host named by `mirror.Location` ([fetch.go:147-148](../../internal/controller/venvlocal/fetch.go)). Both transports use a plain `net.Dialer` `DialContext` ([fetch.go:293](../../internal/controller/venvlocal/fetch.go), [acquisition.go:35](../../internal/controller/bundlelocal/acquisition.go)). A grep for `Control:`, `IsPrivate` and dial-time address checks in non-test Go finds none; `IsLoopback` appears only in classifiers at [sshhost.go:76](../../internal/machine/sshhost.go) and [check.go:52](../../internal/controller/firewall/check.go). The phrase "private-address policy" appears in the specs only at security.md:489, and no spec defines it. The tool-metadata client is host-allowlisted ([tools_transport.go:25-34](../../internal/controller/bundlelocal/tools_transport.go), through the approver passed at [acquisition.go:33-48](../../internal/controller/bundlelocal/acquisition.go)), and media acquisition refuses every redirect, so only the wheel client lacks a destination check. No venvlocal test covers a cross-host redirect.

**Impact.** A wheel redirect from the lock's host or an operator mirror can send the controller's root setup to any HTTPS host on port 443, internal or private addresses included. That host lies outside the destinations the operator guide tells the operator to allow, which [destinations_docs_test.go:17-23](../../internal/controller/bundlelocal/destinations_docs_test.go) builds from the lock URLs and the collection's redirect hosts only. The scope guarantee of the general clause is not met, and the spec names a policy that does not exist.

**Counterevidence.** The wheel port's own contract allows what the code does: [controller.md:141](../../specs/controller.md) says "over HTTPS with bounded redirects" and [controller.md:766-767](../../specs/controller.md) says "HTTPS-only redirects and a bounded chain". The code meets those lines, so the conflict is between the port contract and the general clause, and the remedy may be a spec edit. Each wheel is verified for size and SHA-256 before use, TLS is verified against system roots, userinfo and non-443 ports are refused, and the chain is bounded at five, so no unverified byte is used. The gap is scope and SSRF reach, not integrity. Restricting hops to the lock's hosts could break legitimate publisher CDN redirects unless an allowlist is added, and a private-address refusal would have to admit an operator-named mirror or route. No item, Not yet met line or audit record tracks it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either restrict wheel redirect hops to the lock's own hosts or the admitted mirror host, as `toolMetadataOrigin` does for metadata, and define the private-address policy in security.md (for example a dial `Control` hook that refuses loopback, link-local and private targets for publisher fetches unless the admitted route or mirror names them); or narrow security.md and controller.md to what the code guarantees (HTTPS-only, port 443, no userinfo, bounded chain, digest-verified bytes). Exit: a venvlocal test where a wheel URL redirects to another HTTPS host and the fetch refuses, plus a spec edit naming the policy and the test that guards it.

#### SEC-07

**High, defect.** Controller-side SSH policy parser refuses the generated 'GSSAPIKeyExchange no' backend line that the tunnel parser admits, so Ceph controller sessions and placement checks fail ssh-policy-unavailable on such a host. Re-verified independently by feeding the shipped DEFAULT and FIPS back ends to the three parsers: only the controller parser refuses FIPS; the managed-OS, firewall and bare-metal tasks fail only when their placement host runs FIPS, and no accepted run has driven Ceph from a FIPS controller.

**Evidence.** [security.md:595-597](../../specs/security.md) requires the Ceph host, cluster and SMB controller sessions to take "the controller's crypto-policy back end, reduced to its crypto directives", and [security.md:689-693](../../specs/security.md) requires the direct session to carry "only allowlisted cryptographic directives from the host crypto-policy backend ... so site and FIPS policy is retained". "Reduced" means non-crypto lines are dropped, and the Go parser does that: [policy.go:79-84](../../internal/machine/sshlocal/policy.go) keeps `cryptographicDirectives` and refuses only `unsafeDirectives`. The Python controller parser instead refuses. [ssh_key_policy.py:72-73](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ssh_key_policy.py) reads `if match is None or match.group(1).lower() not in DIRECTIVES: raise PolicyError("... has unsupported syntax or a non-crypto directive")` with reason `ssh-policy-unavailable`; `DIRECTIVES` ([ssh_key_policy.py:22-27](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ssh_key_policy.py)) has no `gssapikeyexchange`; [ceph_ssh_policy.py:27-33](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_ssh_policy.py) maps the error to `PolicyRefusal(UNAVAILABLE)`. Only the tunnel parser admits the line ([ceph_tunnel.py:83-84](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_tunnel.py), `match.group(1).lower() == "gssapikeyexchange" and match.group(2).lower() == "no"`), as repaired by X254 and B1011 ([backlog.md:6498-6503](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)). A reproduction through `ssh_key_policy.configuration('Ciphers aes128-ctr\nGSSAPIKeyExchange no\n')` raised: "the placement host SSH crypto policy has unsupported syntax or a non-crypto directive", reason `ssh-policy-unavailable`.

The trigger is real on a controller. The host's crypto-policies generator (`/usr/share/crypto-policies/python/policygenerators/openssh.py:183-186`) writes `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` whenever a policy admits no GSS key exchange, and the shipped FIPS back end (`/usr/share/crypto-policies/FIPS/openssh.txt:3`) contains exactly that line. The knowledge page records the same line in a RHEL-generated back end and says "Keep this disabling line; do not drop policy lines" ([ibm-ceph-native-ssh.md:158-175](../../.agents/knowledge/ibm-ceph-native-ssh.md)), and at lines 180-182 states that the controller's independent parser "is not part of this image-policy failure", so the controller parser was left out of the repair. No test in [test_ssh_key_policy.py](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ssh_key_policy.py) or [test_ceph_ssh_policy.py](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_ssh_policy.py) uses a GSSAPIKeyExchange line; [test_ceph_tunnel.py:151-165](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_tunnel.py) covers only the tunnel.

**Impact.** On a FIPS controller or placement host, every consumer of `ssh_key_policy` refuses `ssh-policy-unavailable` before contacting any host although the policy is present and evaluable. The consumers are the Ceph host, cluster and SMB controller sessions, the placement-host key checks, the physical-erase controller ([physical_erase_controller.py:158](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/physical_erase_controller.py)) and the `ssh_key_policy` module task in the managedos_install_anaconda role (guest, reachable, register, update_session and apply task files), the managedos_host_firewall role (session.yml:14) and the substrate_baremetal_machine role (identity_read.yml:11). A FIPS controller is a qualified case, and [security.md:78](../../specs/security.md) says Bootwright follows the host's crypto-policy and FIPS mode. The refusal fails closed and has no security consequence, but it names a policy that cannot be read when it can, and it breaks a specified function. The accepted FIPS controller runs (X302) used a non-FIPS placement host, which explains why the defect did not show.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fails closed: no weaker policy is used and nothing is contacted. The spec's GSSAPI admission at [security.md:602-606](../../specs/security.md) names only the tunnel parser, and the spec does not state whether a non-crypto line in the controller back end is dropped or refused, so the repair also needs a spec sentence. The Go parser drops every unlisted non-unsafe directive, not this line specifically. No item, Not yet met line or decision tracks the controller parser.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Admit the fixed `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` form, case-insensitively and with every other value refused, in `ssh_key_policy.configuration`, or drop non-crypto, non-unsafe lines as `policy.go` does. State the shared reduction rule once in security.md:595-606 and 689-693 so the three parsers are specified alike. Exit: a parametrized test in test_ssh_key_policy.py where a back end holding `GSSAPIKeyExchange no` plus algorithm lines is accepted and `GSSAPIKeyExchange yes` refuses; a matching case in `internal/machine/sshlocal/policy_test.go`; a ceph_ssh_policy test showing `evaluate_controller_policy` does not raise UNAVAILABLE for that back end.

#### Observations

- Every one of the 210 test names cited in specs/security.md has a definition in the tree.
- The runner's frozen-request encoding marks every string as `__ansible_unsafe` and refuses ansible-core reserved keys at plan time and at execution; the template refusal names a field path and never the value.
- The privilege boundary is thorough: re-execution path pinning, a sticky-directory exemption limited to root-owned sticky directories, SUDO_COMMAND first-word identity, foreign-variable refusal with unprintable-name masking, and session-variable unsetting with refusal on failure.
- SSH clients across the Go runner inventory, guest sessions and the cephadm tunnel carry ServerAliveInterval=15 and CountMax=3, no agent, no ControlMaster and strict host keys; ansible.cfg pins ControlPath=none and pipelining on both connection sections.
- test/architecture/boundaries_test.go enumerates every package allowed os/exec, so the unqualified exec sites in SEC-01 are a closed, known set.
- B334 and B99 Not yet met lines still match the code.
- The management-controller refusal rule is proved structurally: the collection test runs every controller task's following refusal under a refused and an answered result and asserts printability, bounds and the absence of the account given.
- The job sweep follows the spec's lock protocol exactly.
- The managed proxy's squid ACL also denies loopback and link-local destinations, which is stronger than the listener table states.
- Tool-metadata redirects are host-allowlisted and media redirects always refuse; only the wheel client admits any HTTPS redirect host.
- Every KubeVirt connection, including the lend and the virtctl upload, goes through one kubeconfig acceptance before its first request.
- The assisted-service token stays inside `containercluster_install_inspect`, is sent only to a declared node address, and follows no redirect or proxy.
- Host-key trust under `--yes` refuses any add or replace whose fingerprint was not named.
- Controller-run cancellation spares an authorized tree, closes the channels and does not kill the group, as security.md:311-315 requires.
- The `*_port_refusal` facts in the substrate_baremetal_machine and substrate_libvirt_machine port tasks are set but never read; consumers use `port_result.msg`. This is dead code, not a defect.

#### Limits

The lane is too large to cover every clause in one pass. Clauses not traced into code: the sweep's lock-ordering details beyond the constants and the named tests; contextfs, selectionfs and invokerfs handle-based file safety; the full disposal-proof chain of context deletion; BMC CA trust; the Squid, chrony and artifact listener ACLs beyond the defaults; target-tool publisher metadata; the custom-code and stateful-mutation sections (owned by other lanes); and the Python no_log, private_file and transfer-scanning tests, which were confirmed to exist by name but not read in full. The first round ran no Go or ansible-check test probes, and every judgment comes from reading source at commit f8b15669f; the later rounds were limited to targeted clauses and one in-process Python reproduction for SEC-07. The SEC-07 finding rests on reading the code and on the crypto-policies files of the audit host, not on a capture of the back end of a qualified controller. The Redfish refusal rule was spot-checked on one arm and one consumer, not all roles. The venvlocal cache verification and the firewall-admission clauses were not re-traced.

#### Refuted candidates

No candidate was refuted. All seven candidates across three rounds were confirmed, and one (SEC-07) was settled by arbitration, which raised its severity from Medium to High.

### Group: Controller, contexts and secrets

### CTH: Supported hosts, the runtime lock, the controller runtime, host packages, the setup flow, the uninstall flow; the controller record format

Lane `controller-host`. Spec range: `specs/controller.md` lines 1-467; `specs/contexts/controller-record.md` lines 1-314. Register: 338 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 13; confirmed: 13; tracked: 0; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

Spec ranges: [specs/controller.md](../../specs/controller.md) lines 1-467 and [specs/contexts/controller-record.md](../../specs/contexts/controller-record.md) lines 1-314. Finding code `CTH`. Baseline f8b15669f.

#### Assessment

The lane is sound where a mistake would be destructive. Uninstall resolves paths with `openat2` and `RESOLVE_BENEATH`, no links and no mounts, so a bind mount is refused before any effect. Trees are renamed aside under held locks, package removal fails closed (an erase test, conservative preview matching, a re-check after confirmation, a refusal over a truncated preview), and no state is removed after a package failure. The runtime build follows the specified steps, the launch guard holds the shared lock for the whole block, and the record decoder enforces the closed schema, the ordering and every stated bound. The two Not yet met lines in the range, [B559](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md#b559) and [B561](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md#b561), still match the code.

The thirteen confirmed discrepancies cluster in four places. Receipt provenance is the weakest durability point: a later setup rewrites the whole receipt and loses or relabels what an earlier install added (CTH-01), and a setup resumed after an interrupted install attributes the earlier packages to nobody (CTH-02). Both errors are conservative, since no package that was present before Bootwright is removed, but uninstall then fails to return the host to its pre-install state and states a wrong reason. The dnf adapter departs from the spec text in three narrow ways (CTH-07, CTH-10, CTH-13). Four spec sentences are stale against intentional code (CTH-08, CTH-09, CTH-11, CTH-12). The remaining three are edge cases in the record and runtime paths: run-number exhaustion, an unsafe `.lock`, and the order of the version check against the closed decode (CTH-03, CTH-05, CTH-06), plus a glibc check that runs after the install on a host with no interpreter (CTH-04). No finding is Blocking or High after verification, and none is tracked. Coverage is bounded by the ledger below: no tests were run, and several record-publication and presenter paths were read only partly.
