| Round 3: Opt-in physical logical overwrite | 2461-2464, 2490-2491, 2518-2552 | 14 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Custody root and foreign-custody check, frozen original attempt, host key reuse, Redfish phase deadlines within 2 h, serial resolution, `O_EXCL / O_DIRECT` opens, restricted RAM sshd. Claim retention on deadline exhaustion was not traced into `claims.go`. |
| Round 3: Physical disk safety | 2435-2440 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Kickstart `%pre` is generated in Go; every target is proved first, then holders released, then writes; intervals must equal `MetadataClearRegions(size)`. |
| Round 3: Controller-host protection | 2634-2637 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Requests naming the controller Machine are refused; the host UUID and MAC refusal is armed for physical targets; an unpinned physical target requires declared MACs. The MAC predicate is RCS-01. |
| Round 3: Mutation safety | 2294-2305 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | The libvirt destroy refuses an unanswered hypervisor and a foreign domain; KubeVirt treats only a 404 as absence; Ceph removal evidence goes through `EvaluateEvidence`. |
| Round 3: Confirmation and authorization | 2682-2683 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | An enabled CustomPlaybook refuses `lifecycle.unsupported`; no token admits it (`journey_test.go:2021-2023`). |

#### Observations

- The physical erase worker is a close match to the spec: diskseq-bound identity on every 4 MiB chunk, a 1 s paced system proof and usage scan, first refusal stops all threads, and device-mapper release limited to declared slaves.
- The 896 GiB logical-overwrite bound is enforced in three places, as the spec requires: `internal/machine/erase_admission.go:60`, `internal/managedos/installation/erase_request.go:114` and `physical_erase_worker.py` `validate_request`.
- Rebind admission runs after token authorization and before confirmation (`execution.go:91-96`), and tests prove that a refusal issues no binding and asks no confirmation.
- The fresh-removal controller-host proof runs at decision, in the shared re-proof before presentation, and under the exclusive lock, each tested in `fresh_destroy_host_test.go`.
- Controller-host protection for apply and destroy rests on two facts: admission makes the controller `os.provided`, and every physical change requires a power-off proof that a running controller can never give. Power requests refuse the controller Machine by name and pass the host's UUID and MACs to the role.
- The receipt is recorded in the lifecycle attempt before the shutdown acknowledgement (`destroy.yml:57-69` runs `physical_erase_protocol` phase `prepared`, emitted with `acknowledge=True`). A partial receipt is live only while `bootwright-erase.service` is active; a stopped worker refuses at once with `worker-failed`.
- `finish()` follows the specified order: withdrawn publication check, publication directory fsync, `finalizing.json`, key and boot file removal, custody directory fsync, then `completed.json`. Custody is keyed by the immutable apply operation, and the finalizing marker prevents key regeneration on an interrupted cleanup.
- The RAM erase sshd uses ForceCommand plus restricted authorized keys, and `serve()` dispatches only receipt and ack. Every erase-owned Redfish phase has a total deadline. The install-time clear `%pre` proves all targets before releasing holders or writing any disk.
- The pre-stop and online removal phases are enforced in the scheduler and covered by `prestop_removal_test.go` and `online_removal_test.go`.
- The digest, duplicate and empty-token refusals and the stale-digest remedy naming `bootwright plan` match the spec text.
- Rebind bindings that a continuation issued and then abandoned are collected by the next fresh transition's held-binding sweep, not at once. The spec states no timing for that case.
- The audit 001 follow-up record F10-05 describes the erase worker's MAC set as equality only; it did not check the host-interface exception (RCS-01).
- A wording tension exists between [state-reconciliation.md:2708-2709](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md) (a verb that settles or finalizes takes no rebind) and [state-reconciliation.md:57-64](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md) (a token on a settling verb "authorizes nothing and refuses nothing"). It is recorded under the refuted candidate below.

#### Limits

No probe test was run in this lane; every judgement comes from reading code, test names and test bodies at f8b15669f, apart from one render probe of a physical agent node that supports RCS-02. These parts were not read line by line: the online and pre-stop removal phase ordering in the first pass (read in later rounds), the Ceph physical retirement proofs under `internal/storage/ceph/physical*.go`, and the kickstart RAM-image directives. The register clauses on leases, plan views and lost-reply adoption belong to other lanes and were only located. The durability of the one-mutator lease was not verified because the workspace lock implementation was not opened. Claim retention after an erase deadline exhaustion was not traced into `claims.go`, the `--unregistered` pre-stop path was not followed end to end, and Ceph frozen host-key reuse under a context rename was checked only through the incarnation derivation. Real-hardware qualification clauses cannot be verified from source.

#### Refuted candidates

- RCS-03, "A settled, finalized or unclaimed apply or destroy silently accepts `--authorize data-loss`, `rebind=<secret>` and `--unregistered`": refuted on the spec reading. [state-reconciliation.md:57-64](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md) says a verb that settles "requires no authorization and no confirmation" and "a token it is given authorizes nothing and refuses nothing", [state-reconciliation.md:140-153](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md) gives an unclaimed or settling destroy the same treatment, and [state-reconciliation.md:2678-2681](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md) has finalization consume no token. The code follows that: the unclaimed and noop branches at `execution.go:59-67` return before `splitRebinds`, `authorized` and `admitRebinds`, and `settle.go:9-12` states the rule. No effect runs and nothing is pre-authorized; a finalize that leads to an executable plan still validates its tokens. Two of the three readings judged the missing diagnostic a Low gap against the rebind sentence at [state-reconciliation.md:2708-2709](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md); the residue is the wording tension in Observations.

### Group: Infrastructure services and substrates

### INF: Infrastructure services: selection and refusal, placement arms and credentials, host reservations, managed artifact serving, managed network services, adapter boundary; the InfrastructureService API kinds

Lane `infra-services`. Spec range: `specs/infrastructure-services.md` lines 1-700; `specs/api/infrastructure-services.md` lines 1-289. Register: 453 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 9; confirmed: 6; tracked: 2; refuted: 1.

#### Assessment

**Assessment.** The lane is sound where it is safety-critical. The refusal table, the placement and reservation refusals, the admission rules for the six API kinds, the serving-certificate proof, the SSH host-key pinning of the adapter runner, the foreign-listener and unassigned-address preflights, and the Go and Python evidence shapes agree with the specifications in the clauses the ledger examined, and every test anchor the specifications name exists. No finding reaches Blocking or High: nothing in the lane destroys data, bypasses a required refusal, exposes secret material or leaves impossible durable state. The six confirmed findings are three Medium defects and three Low items. The Medium defects cluster in the readiness proofs and listener behaviour of the managed services at the Ansible boundary: outcome classification of an unanswered or mismatched listener (INF-01), the TCP leg of the DNS readiness proof (INF-05), and the address family of the sockets that chrony opens (INF-07). The Low items are a role guard that binds only part of the content-root form (INF-06) and two sentences in the specifications that overstate or miscount (INF-04, INF-09). Two further discrepancies, the artifact server's blindness to a stale start (INF-02) and the single-family wildcard bind (INF-08), are already tracked as B248 and B412 and still match the code. The assessment is bounded by the ledger below: host reservations, consumer publication and private publication were examined partly through test anchors, and the daemon-level socket behaviour of chrony, dnsmasq, squid and nginx was read from source and documented defaults, not observed.

#### Confirmed findings

| ID | Severity | Kind | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [INF-01](#inf-01) | Medium | defect | Readiness outcome classification is inverted: an unanswered listener fails the attempt, while a certificate mismatch is recorded unknown |
| [INF-04](#inf-04) | Low | doc-stale | "Two consumers use it" introduces three consumers of private publication |
| [INF-05](#inf-05) | Medium | defect | Managed DNS readiness proves TCP with one A query for records[0] only, so an IPv6-only first record never completes and TCP proves no declared address |
| [INF-06](#inf-06) | Low | defect | Service content-root asserts never bind the kind and name components to the request, so the "exactly context/kind/name" rule is only partly enforced |
| [INF-07](#inf-07) | Medium | defect | A managed NTPServer bound to one address also opens an unreserved wildcard server socket of the other address family |
| [INF-09](#inf-09) | Low | drift | The controller-arm clause says every missing, contradictory or stale binding names `controller install`, but the owning contexts specification and the code give other remedies |

#### INF-01

**Medium, defect.** Readiness outcome classification is inverted: an unanswered listener fails the attempt, while a certificate mismatch is recorded unknown.

**Evidence.** The specification makes the outcomes distinct. [infrastructure-services.md:410-413](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) reads "A certificate mismatch or a refused connection after the service reports started is a definite failure. A socket that never answers within the bounded readiness window is unknown, not failure." The network-services readiness clause repeats the second sentence at [infrastructure-services.md:676-678](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md). The artifact server role asserts the opposite for every unproved listener: [apply.yml:297-304](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_artifact_server_nginx/tasks/apply.yml) is "Refuse an unproved listener" with `that: infra_artifact_server_nginx_after.unproved | length == 0`, and [apply.yml:258-265](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/tasks/apply.yml) does the same for an address. [artifact_server_inspect.py:127-143](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/artifact_server_inspect.py) collects every probe failure, a timeout included, into `unproved`. A failed assert exits non-zero, which the adapter protocol reports as a failed exit ([process_linux_amd64.go:286-287](../../internal/adapterprotocol/process_linux_amd64.go)), the runner turns into a `lifecycle.state` failure "the adapter operation did not complete" ([process_linux_amd64.go:457-458](../../internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go)), and [invocation.go:282-293](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/invocation.go) maps to `OutcomeFailed` for any code other than `lifecycle.unknown`. A certificate mismatch is not unproved: the probe uses `CERT_NONE` and returns the presented fingerprint, the role publishes completion, and [capability.go:156-175](../../internal/infrastructureservices/artifactserver/capability.go) runs `ValidatePresence`, which refuses "presented a different certificate than the operation bound" ([evidence.go:145-147](../../internal/infrastructureservices/artifactserver/evidence.go)) and returns `unknown, err`.

**Impact.** Severity Medium, kind defect. An operator whose listener is slow to come up sees the block and operation recorded failed with a failure remedy, where the specification promises unknown. A server presenting the wrong certificate is recorded unknown and goes to read-only resolution, not shown as the definite failure it is. The refused-connection case is classified correctly, since it is also unproved and fails the role, so only the timeout and the mismatch are inverted. The mismatch half applies to the artifact server only, because the managed-service probes involve no certificate; the timeout half applies to both roles. The managed-service Go side was not opened, so that half is confirmed at the role level.

**Counterevidence.** Both outcomes still lead to a retry: a failed block retries, and an unknown block resolves to partial and then retries. No effect is skipped and no false success occurs. The Python helper names a timeout `TimeoutError` as the specification asks. [state-reconciliation.md:627-640](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md) maps a typed adapter failure to block failed, so it explains the failed result and does not set the readiness rule. No milestone item or Not yet met line tracks this.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Have the inspect modules sort the last cause into timeout, refused or mismatch. Publish a timeout through the protocol as an unknown or unproved outcome rather than a failed assert, and turn a fingerprint mismatch or a refused connection into a named definite failure, before completion is published. Alternatively amend the specification to the current classification and cite a decision. Exit: a Go capability test in which a timed-out listener yields `OutcomeUnknown` and a mismatched fingerprint yields `OutcomeFailed`, plus a role unit test for the unproved branch.

#### INF-04

**Low, doc-stale.** "Two consumers use it" introduces three consumers of private publication.

**Evidence.** [infrastructure-services.md:566](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) opens the private consumer publication section with "Two consumers use it." and lists three: the physical installation, the encrypting managed-OS installation and the container cluster's agent boot image ([infrastructure-services.md:566-578](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md)). The code has all three. The container cluster publishes under the reserved root `<content root>/public/private/<consumer>/<object>` ([containercluster_media_token.py:27](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/containercluster_media_token.py)), and the managed-OS role fetches its recovery passphrase through the private listener ([private_recovery.yml:28-40](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/managedos_install_anaconda/tasks/private_recovery.yml)). The physical and encrypting managed-OS installations share that role.

**Impact.** Severity Low, kind doc-stale. A reader is misled about how many consumers the confidentiality rules must hold for. The decisive evidence is the specification text alone.

**Counterevidence.** The sentences that follow are complete and correct, and no behaviour differs.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Change "Two consumers use it" to "Three consumers use it", or drop the count. Exit: `make docs-check` after the edit.

#### INF-05

**Medium, defect.** Managed DNS readiness proves TCP with one A query for records[0] only, so an IPv6-only first record never completes and TCP proves no declared address.

**Evidence.** [infrastructure-services.md:672-673](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) requires that "a resolver answers every declared address of every one of its records over UDP, and over TCP as well". `probe_dns` checks every (name, type) pair over UDP ([infra_service.py:245-251](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py)). Its TCP leg ([infra_service.py:252-259](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py)) sends one query, `payload = dns_query(records[0]["name"])`, whose record type defaults to 1, type A ([infra_service.py:169-179](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py)). It reads with one `recv(2)` and one `recv(min(length, 512))` and requires only `streamed >= 1`; `dns_answers` returns the header count and compares no address. Records are sorted by name ([requests.go:187-197](../../internal/infrastructureservices/managedservice/requests.go)) and a Machine whose addresses are all IPv6 is kept ([requests.go:123-143](../../internal/infrastructureservices/managedservice/requests.go)); `dns_expected` maps an IPv6 address to AAAA ([infra_service.py:218-226](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py)). The unit fixture begins with an IPv4-only record and its fake stream replies with a fixed A answer to any query ([test_infra_service.py:215-242](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_infra_service.py)).

**Impact.** Severity Medium, kind defect. When the alphabetically first record has only IPv6 addresses, the A query returns NODATA, readiness fails every time even though the resolver is correct, and the DNSServer apply cannot complete. On every other graph, TCP serving is proved by a non-empty answer for one name, so a resolver that serves TCP wrongly for every other record still passes. The case needs an IPv6-only Machine or cluster endpoint that sorts first. The truncation of a reply above 512 bytes does not fail the check, because only the header count is read, and is a robustness point only.

**Counterevidence.** UDP checks every declared address of every record. Dual-stack and IPv4-only first records work. The specification is somewhat open on whether the per-address comparison must also run over TCP; the unambiguous failure is the IPv6-only first record. No milestone item tracks it; B1067 covers the UDP leg only.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Over TCP, query each (name, type) pair that `dns_expected` yields, or at least query the first record with the type its own addresses carry. Read the full length-prefixed reply and compare addresses as the UDP leg does. Exit: a unit test in `test_infra_service.py` where the first record is AAAA-only and the TCP stream answers AAAA proves readiness, and one where TCP omits a declared address fails. Repro: `./scripts/ansible-check --suite units ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_infra_service.py | cat` after adding a fixture whose first entry is IPv6-only.

#### INF-06

**Low, defect.** Service content-root asserts never bind the `<kind>` and `<name>` components to the request, so the 'exactly `<context>`/`<kind>`/`<name>`' rule is only partly enforced.

**Evidence.** [infrastructure-services.md:358-363](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) has apply and destroy refuse "a content root that is not exactly `/var/lib/bootwright-services/<context>/<kind>/<name>` in normal form", and [infrastructure-services.md:613-614](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) repeats the rule for managed services. The first asserts of [destroy.yml:2-17](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/tasks/destroy.yml) and [apply.yml:2-19](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/tasks/apply.yml), and of [destroy.yml:6-13](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_artifact_server_nginx/tasks/destroy.yml) and the artifact apply, check the prefix, seven components, no empty, `.` or `..` component, and that `contentRoot | dirname | dirname` equals the prefix plus `identity.context`. None compares the kind component to the request kind or the name component to the service. The Go decoders do not re-derive the root ([requests.go:69-71](../../internal/infrastructureservices/artifactserver/requests.go)), and the planted cases list only `.`, `..`, empty, trailing, extra-depth and nested-context roots ([test_service_destroy_safety.py:37-70](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_service_destroy_safety.py)).

**Impact.** Severity Low, kind defect. A frozen request whose root names a sibling service of the same context, for example `/var/lib/bootwright-services/lab/artifact-server/other` in a DNS request, passes the assert, and the destroy removes that tree recursively. Reaching it needs a Go derivation bug or an altered frozen request, so the protection is defense in depth that the specification wording claims and the code gives only for the context. The request kind is the API kind (DNSServer, NTPServer, Proxy), so an added assert must map it to dns, ntp or proxy first, and the argument specification declares `identity` only as a dict, so the name field must be confirmed before the guard is written.

**Counterevidence.** The root is derived in Go (`ContentRoot`, [capability.go:176](../../internal/infrastructureservices/managedservice/capability.go) and [publication.go:85-86](../../internal/infrastructureservices/artifactserver/publication.go)), digest-bound and proved canonical on decode, and the context check confines a mistake to one context. The enumerated conditions at lines 360-363 may be the intended full definition of "normal form", in which case the repair is a wording change. [delivered.md:3549-3555](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) (B435) records only the enumerated conditions. B461 tracks the Go decoders' clean-root check, a related but different gap.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add asserts that the kind component equals the kind slug and the name component equals the service name, in all four entry points, or state in the specification that the enumerated conditions are the whole rule. Exit: `test_a_content_root_not_in_normal_form_refuses_before_any_removal` gains wrong-kind and wrong-name roots, and they refuse.

#### INF-07

**Medium, defect.** A managed NTPServer bound to one address also opens an unreserved wildcard server socket of the other address family.

**Evidence.** [infrastructure-services.md:582-584](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) has each kind run "serving one declared port on its declared bind address", and [infrastructure-services.md:130](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) defines `socket:<address>:<port>` as one effective listening socket. [chrony.conf.j2:7](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/templates/chrony.conf.j2) writes a single `bindaddress`, and [chrony.conf.j2:11-13](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/templates/chrony.conf.j2) writes one `allow` per client. `Clients()` always seeds `127.0.0.1/32` and `::1/128` ([requests.go:98-100](../../internal/infrastructureservices/managedservice/requests.go)), so both families are allowed. The container runs `Exec=-d -x -f /etc/chrony/chrony.conf` with no `-4` or `-6` ([chrony.container.j2:17](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/templates/chrony.container.j2)). chrony keeps one `bindaddress` per family, so, from its documented behaviour and source, it also opens the server socket of the other family on that family's wildcard. The foreign-listener preflight is conservative: `overlaps` returns true when the local socket is the IPv6 wildcard ([host_sockets.py:86-102](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/host_sockets.py)), and `foreign` skips the check only when the service's own unit is active or its container is present ([infra_service.py:131-142](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py)).

**Impact.** Severity Medium, kind defect, confidence medium. A second managed NTPServer on the same host with a different, non-wildcard bind address passes the reservation comparison, then its foreign-listener preflight finds the first chronyd's `[::]:123` or `0.0.0.0:123` socket and refuses with `lifecycle.state`, naming as foreign a listener that is a Bootwright service. The refusal applies to a second service that is not yet running; a service's own re-apply is not refused. The time service also answers allowed clients on every address of the other family. The reservation's socket key does not describe that socket.

**Counterevidence.** The allow list still limits who gets an answer, and readiness of the declared address is unaffected. The per-family socket behaviour was not observed: chronyd could not be run unprivileged in this audit (it exits with "Not superuser"). [managed-network-service-runtime.md:66-69](../../.agents/knowledge/managed-network-service-runtime.md) concerns the stock host chronyd, so it supports the claim by analogy only. No item or Not yet met line tracks this.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Restrict chronyd to the bind family with `-4` for an IPv4 bind and `-6` for an IPv6 bind in `chrony.container.j2`, or write the other family's `bindaddress` as that family's loopback; keep the wildcard case as it is. Exit: a template golden in `tests/unit/test_role_templates.py` showing the family flag for both binds, and a live `ss -ulpn` check that one IPv4-bound managed NTPServer holds only `<addr>:123`.

#### INF-09

**Low, drift.** The controller-arm clause says every missing, contradictory or stale binding names controller install, but the owning contexts spec and the code give other remedies.

**Evidence.** [infrastructure-services.md:71-75](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) reads "A missing, contradictory or stale binding refuses before effects and names `controller install`." The code names it only for missing setup or runtime: `Bind` returns `completeSetup`, "run bootwright controller install, then repeat the command", when `!t.controller.Prepared` ([reconciliation_linux_amd64.go:525-526](../../internal/workspace/contextfs/reconciliation_linux_amd64.go); constant at [controller_linux_amd64.go:29](../../internal/workspace/contextfs/controller_linux_amd64.go); the lifecycle check at [register_run.go:232-241](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/register_run.go)). A changed host returns `controller.HostMismatchRemedy`, which names the original host, `bootwright controller rebind` and `context delete --name <name> --purge --allow-orphans` ([identity.go:114-121](../../internal/controller/identity.go)). A binding to another Machine returns "restore the bound controller Machine input, or create a context on this host" ([reconciliation_linux_amd64.go:543-549](../../internal/workspace/contextfs/reconciliation_linux_amd64.go)). [contexts.md:91-103](../../specs/contexts.md) owns these exits.

**Impact.** Severity Low, kind drift between a cross-reference sentence and its owning specification; the code follows the owner, so no runtime behaviour is wrong. A reader following the infrastructure-services page would expect `controller install` to cure a contradictory binding, which it does not. A missing or unattributable runtime bundle does name the command, so the stale-runtime reading is met.

**Counterevidence.** The code matches [contexts.md:97-106](../../specs/contexts.md). Only the sentence in the non-owning section is too broad. No item tracks it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Narrow the sentence: a missing setup or runtime names `controller install`; contradictory or changed-host evidence refuses with the exits the contexts specification names, linked and not restated. Exit: `make docs-check` after the edit.

#### INF-02

**Medium, defect, tracked.** An artifact server's presence never compares its container start with the files it runs from, so an interrupted apply can resolve completed on stale configuration. The discrepancy holds at the baseline and is recorded as open work under B248.

**Evidence.** Spec 425-426: "An apply stopped between publishing a file and restarting the service is therefore completed by its next attempt." Spec 399: "tls.minVersion selects the exact protocol floor the server enforces." artifact_server.py observe() returns only unit, unitDigest, container, containerPresent and contentRoot, with no start time. artifact_server_protocol.py:50: "postcondition": observation.get("unit") == "active" and bool(observation.get("contentRoot")). The artifact Evidence struct has no start field. The managed network services do check it: evidence.go:66 `if !evidence.StartedAfterFiles { return Refusal(... "started before a file it runs from was last published") }`, fed by infra_service.py:125 `started_after(runner, request["unit"], [unit_path] + list(runs_from))`. Spec: `specs/infrastructure-services.md:399`, `specs/infrastructure-services.md:418-426`, `specs/infrastructure-services.md:450-456`, `specs/infrastructure-services.md:680-689`. Code: `internal/infrastructureservices/artifactserver/evidence.go:12-21`, `internal/infrastructureservices/artifactserver/evidence.go:99-152`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/artifact_server.py:149-159`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/artifact_server_protocol.py:50`, `internal/infrastructureservices/managedservice/evidence.go:66-68`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py:125`.

**Impact.** After an interrupted apply that changed only the server configuration, such as the TLS floor, continuing the operation records the block completed while nginx still enforces the earlier configuration. The plan reports success for a protocol floor the server does not enforce.

**Counterevidence.** A changed certificate is caught by the fingerprint comparison, a changed listener port by the probes, and a changed image by the image comparison. Only differences in configuration or unit that leave the listeners and the certificate unchanged slip through, so the path is narrow. The managed network services already implement the rule.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Carry the same startedAfterFiles observation into the artifact server's inspect, protocol and Evidence (nginx.conf, the unit and the TLS material), require it in ValidatePresence, and read its absence as partial, as managedservice does. Exit: An artifactserver evidence test in which presence with startedAfterFiles false is refused and observed as EffectPartial, and a protocol unit test for the field.

#### INF-08

**Medium, defect, tracked.** A wildcard bind serves one address family while readiness probes endpoint addresses of both, and the derived wildcard is always IPv4. The discrepancy holds at the baseline and is recorded as open work under B412.

**Evidence.** The API spec says the service "binds the wildcard `0.0.0.0`" when "its endpoints name several addresses", that a wildcard "binds every address", and that a wildcard bind is proved "through its endpoint addresses". Spec 666: "Completion requires a positive answer on every address the service serves: ... every declared endpoint address when the bind address is a wildcard." derivedBind returns "0.0.0.0" whenever `bound != "" && bound != address.String()`. validateWildcardProbes only requires an endpoint to exist and never compares families. dnsmasq.conf.j2 writes `listen-address={{ ...bindAddress }}` and `bind-interfaces`. probe_targets returns `sorted({endpoint["address"] for endpoint in request.get("endpoints", [])})` for a wildcard. Spec: `specs/api/infrastructure-services.md:87-92`, `specs/api/infrastructure-services.md:108-112`, `specs/infrastructure-services.md:130`, `specs/infrastructure-services.md:666-667`. Code: `internal/infrastructureservices/admission.go:41-55`, `internal/infrastructureservices/admission.go:241-264`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/templates/dnsmasq.conf.j2:11-13`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_managed_service/templates/squid.conf.j2:11`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/infra_artifact_server_nginx/templates/nginx.conf.j2:27`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/infra_service.py:144-148`.

**Impact.** A managed DNSServer, Proxy or ArtifactServer with two IPv6 endpoints and no authored bindAddress derives 0.0.0.0 and never answers on its IPv6 endpoints. Every apply ends unproved, then partial, with no diagnostic that names the family mismatch. An authored `::` with an IPv4 endpoint fails the same way for dnsmasq and nginx.

**Counterevidence.** chrony serves both families (see the separate finding), so an NTPServer is not affected. An operator can author bindAddress `::` when all endpoints are IPv6. Clusters are single-family by contract (B738 parked), but nothing parks dual-family service endpoints. The single-family behaviour of these daemons' wildcard sockets is their documented default (dnsmasq and nginx set IPV6_V6ONLY) and has not been verified live in this lane.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Derive `::` when every endpoint IP is IPv6. Refuse at admission (api.invariant at $.spec.endpoints[i]) a wildcard bind whose IP endpoints include the other family for the single-family implementations, or render dual listeners (dnsmasq listen-address for both wildcards, nginx/squid `[::]:port ipv6only=off` or a second listen line). Exit: An admission test where two IPv6 endpoints derive `::` and mixed families refuse, plus a dnsmasq/nginx template golden for each wildcard family.

#### Observations

- Both refusal-table tests parse `specs/infrastructure-services.md` directly, so a drifted row text fails CI; they pass at the baseline.
- Every test anchor named in both specification ranges exists at the cited package (36 checked).
- The managed network services implement the start-after-files rule end to end; the artifact server does not (INF-02).
- Foreign-listener and unassigned-address proofs are bounded, complete and fail closed.
- B323 and B568 still match the code: absence evidence carries no socket probe, and names carry only the context name.
- Admission's `validatePlacementHost` also counts managed Registry and LoadBalancer placements that no capability realizes; harmless but broader than the arms.
- `nginx listen [::]:port` defaults to IPv6-only while reservations and the foreign-socket check treat `::` as covering IPv4; this is conservative.
- The adapter runner pins SSH tightly: a job-local config, a rewritten one-line known_hosts, and agent, jump and global known-hosts disabled.
- `DecodeRequest` names a stale frozen version and its remedy before any role runs, so the role's `no_log` assert is a backstop.
- The Go and Python evidence shapes match field for field for the managed service and the artifact server.
- `host_sockets.overlaps` treats an IPv6 wildcard as overlapping every IPv4 bind, which turns chrony's extra socket into a false foreign-listener refusal (INF-07).
- The managed proxy's status line is validated only in the Python probe; Go checks that the answer is non-empty.
- The managed-OS private token comes from `openssl rand`, not directly from the operating system source the specification names; the difference is negligible.

#### Limits

Cross-lane machinery was verified through test anchors, not line by line: known-hosts parsing, the context record bounds and release marks, the controller sshd key reader and the controller-arm host binding. Private publication mechanics owned by managed OS and container clusters were sampled; withdrawal, fetch-proof retries and the remote-fetcher channel were not re-traced. The address-family behaviour of chrony, dnsmasq, squid and nginx comes from documented defaults and source, because no daemon could be run under the no-effects rule, so INF-07 and INF-08 carry medium confidence on that point. dnsmasq PTR generation for repeated host-record lines cannot be verified from source. Only targeted Go tests in the artifact server and managed service packages were run; the Ansible unit suites were not. Whether the engine skips server removal after a consumer's removal fails was not checked, so the consumer-subtree clause is judged on plan ordering alone.

#### Refuted candidates

- **INF-03, the DNS server's container-cluster records are derived in managedservice, which imports internal/containercluster, so the DNS import fitness test proves less than the spec claims.** Refuted: the dnsserver package imports neither forbidden package and the test proves exactly that, composition binding is required only for the storage derivation, and cluster names come from the container-cluster facts registry, so a new cluster implementation edits no DNS code (audit 001 F18-10); the remaining point is structural placement with no runtime effect.

### SBV: Substrate selection and refusal, qualification, provider host realization, Machine realization and capacity admission, KubeVirt machine realization, vSphere machine realization

Lane `substrates-virtual`. Spec range: `specs/substrates.md` lines 1-645; `specs/substrates.md` lines 904-1185. Register: 420 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 14; confirmed: 13; tracked: 1; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

The lane covers `specs/substrates.md` lines 1-645 and 904-1185 at commit f8b15669f. The selection and refusal machinery is sound: every row of the refusal table matches the text the capabilities emit (the table test was run and passes), the KubeVirt bound constants reproduce the spec's numbers, the provider host apply orders its observations and refusals as the spec requires (re-observation after the daemons start, driver silence, foreign network and pool, route collisions, busy restart, all before any network definition), the firewall readiness barrier proves effective systemd properties, the bridge-use and `bmc:` release guards are proved at registration and again before each destroy attempt, the Unresolved reasons follow the spec's first-match order, and the KubeVirt provider proof, lend, pin and removal by UID agree with their clauses. The vSphere section is unrealized by design: 19 of its 20 clauses are unmet and are tracked by B99, and the arm refuses before registration. The discrepancies cluster in four places. The SSH placement arm is the first: the emulated BMC's shared `bmc:` key is never claimed there (SBV-11, Medium), and the substrates page still says the arm is coordinated by the context lease alone (SBV-12). The second is the libvirt host probe, which skips default routes in every table (SBV-01, Medium). The third is the KubeVirt arm's edges: attachment kind is not proved, the media insert re-reads the upload proxy, and the off-machine rule for media is worded more broadly than the delivered behavior (SBV-04, SBV-09, SBV-10). The fourth is completeness of the refusal table and of wording parity between diagnostics (SBV-02, SBV-05, SBV-06, SBV-14). Three records are stale (SBV-03, SBV-12, SBV-13). The assessment is bounded by the coverage ledger below: the provider host, Machine realization and KubeVirt sections were examined at roughly 74, 66 and 70 percent of their clauses, and the unexamined remainder sits mostly at the adapter boundary.

#### SBV-11

**Medium, defect.** An emulated BMC on an SSH-placed libvirt provider never claims its shared bmc: key, so a physical Machine of another context addressing that endpoint is never refused.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:500-506](../../specs/substrates.md) says "The block also claims, shared, the `bmc:` key of its BMC endpoint, the key a physical Machine that addresses that endpoint claims exclusively", and that "the registration that carries this Machine's installation refuses while another context holds it". [infrastructure-services.md:140](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) states the key class with no placement exception. In [capability.go:181-194](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/capability.go) the non-local placement arm appends the exclusive `substrate-machine` claim to `plan.SSHReservations` and then reaches `continue` (lines 184-189). Only after that line is the shared `Kind: "substrate-machine-bmc"` reservation built from `request.SharedReservationKeys()` ([requests.go:202-204](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/requests.go)) with `Shared: true`, so it is appended on the controller arm only. The host capability, by contrast, sends its shared `substrate-host-use` claim over SSH ([capability.go:75-85](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/capability.go)). [capability_test.go:96-103](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/capability_test.go) asserts `len(plan.Reservations) != 0` fails and `len(plan.SSHReservations) != 1` fails for an SSH-placed Machine, which pins the omission. The controller arm is covered by [shared_claims_test.go:62-72](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/shared_claims_test.go). [delivered.md:8788-8789](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) records the shared `bmc:` claim with no SSH exception.

**Impact.** On a provider host reached over SSH, another context that declares a physical Machine with that emulated BMC endpoint claims `bmc:<host>:<port>/<uuid>` exclusively, and nothing conflicts. Two contexts can then drive one virtual machine's power and media, which is what the key exists to prevent. The registration that carries this Machine's installation does not refuse, and the release-side guard of [substrates.md:502-504](../../specs/substrates.md), which refuses removal while another context holds the key exclusively, has nothing to compare on this arm.

**Counterevidence.** The path is narrow: an operator must point a bare-metal Machine at another context's emulated BMC on an SSH-hosted provider. The `bmc:` key names a network endpoint, so it needs no SSH qualification. [infrastructure-services.md:227-231](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) says every SSH claim, an emulated BMC's included, is published with its keys qualified as `ssh/<addr>:<port>/<key>`. A qualified `bmc:` key never meets a physical Machine's unqualified `bmc:` key, so publishing the claim through `SSHReservations` would not close the gap; the spec is in tension with itself on this key.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Append the shared `substrate-machine-bmc` reservation to `plan.Reservations`, unqualified, on the SSH arm as well, and amend [infrastructure-services.md:227-241](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) to say the `bmc:` key is published unqualified because it names an endpoint. Update the two assertions in capability_test.go. Exit: a test in `internal/substrate/libvirt` plans an SSH-placed Machine and asserts a shared reservation of kind `substrate-machine-bmc` carrying `bmc:<bindAddress>:<port>/<uuid>`, plus a conflict test against an exclusive holder of that key from another context and a removal refusal while that holder exists.

#### SBV-01

**Medium, defect.** Default routes in any table are dropped from the managed-network collision check, so a policy-routed full-tunnel default (strongSwan table 220) never refuses.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:191-193](../../specs/substrates.md) refuses a route "identical to the managed prefix, nested inside it or broader than it and on-link (no gateway)". [substrates.md:205-208](../../specs/substrates.md) adds "Such a route in any other table still refuses, because a policy rule, a strongSwan table 220 for one, can select that table before main and send the host's traffic for the prefix through the gateway". In `host_routes` ([substrate_libvirt.py:380-415](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py)) the line `if destination in ("", "default"): continue` (399-401) and the guard `if prefix.prefixlen:` (405) drop every default route and every explicit `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`, in every table, whatever the hops. The docstring at 384-385 says "A default route overlaps every prefix and collides with none, so it is left out." The unit fixtures at [test_substrate_libvirt.py:864-871](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_substrate_libvirt.py) and the comment at 887-891 pin the assumption, including an on-link IPv6 `{"dst": "default", "dev": "eth0"}`.

**Impact.** A default route is the broadest route there is, so the rule that refuses a broader on-link route, and a broader route through a gateway in a non-main table, is never applied to it. A host with a full-tunnel IPsec or VPN that puts `default via <gw>` in a table a policy rule consults before main, or an on-link `default dev tun0`, passes the check. The apply defines and starts the network and reports completion with no warning, and the controller cannot reach its guests.

**Counterevidence.** Leaving out a main-table default through a gateway is reasonable: read literally, [substrates.md:194-198](../../specs/substrates.md) would give every host with a default gateway a `substrate.shadowed-route` warning, so the spec is imprecise on that case. A /8 in table 220 does refuse ([test_substrate_libvirt.py:967-968](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_substrate_libvirt.py)). Whether strongSwan installs a default route in table 220 depends on its traffic selectors and was not observed on a live host. No record accepts the exclusion: [D188](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md) (backlog.md:5319-5330) and [X178](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) (delivered.md:9294-9310) name only broader gateway routes in main (warn) and on-link, other-table and nested routes (refuse). The earlier audit calls the exclusion "a stated owner choice (B843)" at [report-claude.md:385](../001-spec/follow-up/001/report-claude.md) and :629, which those records do not support.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Skip only a main-table default route whose every hop names a gateway. Treat a default route in any other table, or one with an on-link hop, as broader than every managed prefix, so it refuses. State in [substrates.md:188-212](../../specs/substrates.md) that the main-table default through a gateway is neither a collision nor a warning, and correct the earlier audit's attribution. Exit: unit tests in test_substrate_libvirt.py where `{"dst":"default","gateway":"192.0.2.1","dev":"eth0","table":"220"}` and `{"dst":"default","dev":"tun0"}` each yield one collision for managed 10.1.0.1/24, and a main-table default via a gateway yields none.

#### SBV-02

**Low, doc-stale.** The hosted-provider attachment refusal is a capability refusal with no refusal-table row and no test.

**Evidence.** [selection.go:28-36](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/selection.go) emits a refusal for an attachment of a `hostClusterRef` provider that names no `ClusterUserDefinedNetwork` among the host's `secondaryNetworks` (lines 33-34: "a KubeVirt provider hosted by ... attaches only to that cluster's secondary networks"). [substrates.md:939-941](../../specs/substrates.md) says planning refuses it and links the refusal table, but the table at [substrates.md:99-109](../../specs/substrates.md) has no row for it. [substrates.md:93-94](../../specs/substrates.md) says "`TestSubstrateRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported` holds its `Unsupported` to it". The test ([refusal_table_test.go:32-36 and 64-90](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/refusal_table_test.go)) iterates spec rows only, so its comment "a row added or removed on either side fails here" does not hold on the code side.

**Impact.** The exact reason and remedy of this refusal are specified nowhere. The link at 939-941 points to a row that does not exist.

**Counterevidence.** The behavior is tested: [nested_test.go:121-130](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/nested_test.go) asserts exactly one refusal whose reason contains "attachment storage names another network". Only the full reason and remedy are unpinned. The refusal fires before registration through the lifecycle collection at support.go:110, and every listed row matches its code.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a row for the hosted-attachment refusal to the table at substrates.md:99-109, with its exact reason and remedy, and a matching case in refusal_table_test.go. Make the test direction complete as described under [SBV-14](#sbv-14). Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/substrate/libvirt/ -run TestSubstrateRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported` passes with the row and fails when it is removed; `make docs-check`.

#### SBV-03

**Low, doc-stale.** The Not yet met line at substrates.md:65 claims the vSphere refusal is unmet, but the code refuses before registration.

Tracked as the stale line itself (specs/substrates.md:65).

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:65-66](../../specs/substrates.md) reads "Not yet met: a vSphere provider and its Machines refuse before registration; tracked as B99." [substrates.md:33-37](../../specs/substrates.md) states the refusal as current behavior, and the refusal table row for an unrealized substrate says the same. The code meets it: `Realized()` lists only baremetal, kubevirt and libvirt ([target.go:30](../../internal/substrate/target.go)); `Unrealizable` ([target.go:491-511](../../internal/substrate/target.go)) emits "this executable realizes no provider on the substrate it declares" for each unrealized provider and "its provider ... is on a substrate this executable does not realize" for each hosted Machine; [selection.go:21-25](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/selection.go) feeds them into `Unsupported`, which the lifecycle collects at [support.go:110-121](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/support.go). The cases "A provider on an unrealized substrate" and "A Machine on an unrealized substrate" in [refusal_table_test.go:47-50](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/refusal_table_test.go) hold them, and the test passes.

**Impact.** A reader concludes that vSphere objects may slip past registration. The record misstates delivery state.

**Counterevidence.** The realization gap is real and is recorded correctly at [substrates.md:1183-1184](../../specs/substrates.md): "Not yet met: nothing realizes a vSphere Machine; tracked as B99." B99 tracks realization, not the refusal.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Delete the Not yet met line at substrates.md:65-66 and keep line 1183 as the only one for the vSphere arm. Exit: `make docs-check`; `./scripts/go test ./internal/substrate/libvirt/ -run TestSubstrateRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported`.

#### SBV-04

**Low, gap.** KubeVirt attachments are never proved to be a Localnet CUDN or a bridge-type NAD, only to be one of the two kinds.

**Evidence.** The refusal row at [substrates.md:106](../../specs/substrates.md) says "a KubeVirt interface attaches to a Localnet ClusterUserDefinedNetwork or a bridge NetworkAttachmentDefinition", and [substrates.md:1063-1066](../../specs/substrates.md) says the machine attaches "for a `Localnet` ClusterUserDefinedNetwork the derived NetworkAttachmentDefinition ... and for a NetworkAttachmentDefinition of type `bridge` that object". `networkOf` ([selection.go:254-263](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/selection.go)) switches only on API group and kind; the same refusal wording sits at selection.go:52 and 233-235. The provider proof `network_present` ([kubevirt_machine.py:249-269](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py)) reads the NAD only for existence and, for a CUDN, only the `NetworkCreated` condition; the VM body hardcodes `{"bridge": {}}` ([kubevirt_machine.py:305-307](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py)). No code reads a CUDN topology or a NAD CNI type.

**Impact.** A provider whose attachment names a Layer2 or Layer3 CUDN or a non-bridge NAD passes the proof. The failure appears later as a VirtualMachineInstance that does not start or has no connectivity, not as a named refusal. Bootwright's own CUDN renderer always emits `Localnet` ([render.go:150](../../internal/containercluster/networking/render.go)), so the gap affects externally supplied objects on the `kubeconfigRef` path.

**Counterevidence.** The proof clause at [substrates.md:1003-1006](../../specs/substrates.md) lists exactly NAD existence and the CUDN's `NetworkCreated` condition, and the code meets that list; the requirement is implicit in the target text. KubeVirt's bridge binding works on many bridge-like attachments, so only some kinds fail (SR-IOV, Layer3). A CUDN that cannot be read passes the proof. [B741](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md) and [B909](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md) park other network kinds and do not track proving the kind.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either read the CUDN's `spec.network.topology` and the NAD's `spec.config` type in `network_present` and add both to the proof clause at substrates.md:1003-1006, or state that the arm trusts the operator for the kind. Exit: a unit test in test_kubevirt_machine.py where a NAD with config type `macvlan` and a Layer2 CUDN each add a proof failure naming the attachment.

#### SBV-05

**Low, defect.** The hosted-namespace label-conflict admission names only one of the two conflicting secondary networks.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:937-938](../../specs/substrates.md) says "admission refuses two such networks that give one key two values, naming both"; the same wording is in [backlog.md:5950-5951](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md). `HostedNamespaces` ([nested.go:48-56](../../internal/substrate/nested.go)) stores only the label value, and the conflict text at line 52 is `label %s is %q for one secondary network of %s and %q for %s`, which names the later network and calls the earlier one "one secondary network of `<cluster>`". `validateHostedProvider` passes it unchanged ([nested.go:101-106](../../internal/substrate/nested.go)). The test asserts only `label tier is "hub"` and `"edge" for edge` ([nested_test.go:50-64](../../internal/substrate/nested_test.go), line 54).

**Impact.** An operator facing the refusal must search every secondary network of the host to find the first one. A namespace with three or more disagreeing networks reports only the first pair (the guard at nested.go:51).

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fires and names the label, both values and the second network. "Both" can be read as both values, but "two such networks ... naming both" reads better as both networks.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Record the originating network per label value and name both networks in the message. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/substrate/ -run TestNetworksThatLabelOneNamespaceDifferentlyRefuseEveryProviderInIt` with assertions on both network names.

#### SBV-06

**Low, defect.** The managed-attachment admission message omits the readiness-unit key it budgets for.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:309-311](../../specs/substrates.md): "20 × 3 attachment keys plus two pool keys and one readiness-unit key use 63 of the 64 keys". The refusal table row ([substrates.md:108](../../specs/substrates.md)) and the capability refusal ([selection.go:32-36](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/selection.go), line 34) say "beside the two of its media pool and its firewall readiness unit". The admission message ([admission.go:463-470](../../internal/substrate/admission.go), line 467) says "three keys for each beside the two of its media pool, within the 64 keys one reservation holds", and the test pins that wording ([admission_directory_test.go:72](../../internal/substrate/admission_directory_test.go)). The comment at [naming.go:24-26](../../internal/substrate/naming.go) also omits the readiness-unit key.

**Impact.** Two diagnostics for one bound explain it differently, and the admission arithmetic (20 × 3 + 2 = 62) does not show why the bound is 20.

**Counterevidence.** [substrates.md:312-313](../../specs/substrates.md) requires admission to name only "the bound and spec.networkAttachments", which it does. The bound and remedy are identical in both messages.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Use the capability refusal's wording in `validateLibvirtHostFootprint`, correct the naming.go comment, and update the assertion in admission_directory_test.go. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/substrate/` with the admission directory test asserting the new message, and [reservation_bound_test.go:28](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/reservation_bound_test.go) unchanged.

#### SBV-08

**Low, defect.** libvirt machine apply proceeds without proving the hypervisor answered, so a silent lookup bypasses the foreign-domain refusal before disks are created and the domain is defined.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:448-451](../../specs/substrates.md) says a foreign same-name domain "refuses on apply and on destroy before any effect", and [substrates.md:589-591](../../specs/substrates.md) says that without a hypervisor answer "an empty domain proves nothing". [apply.yml:28-44](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/apply.yml) reads the domain once and asserts only `observation.domain | length == 0 or observation.owned`. It never reads `observation.answered`, yet the owned directory and disks are created at 56-77 and `virsh define` runs at 107-118. [destroy.yml:30-42](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_libvirt_machine/tasks/destroy.yml) carries the extra assertion on `observation.answered`, and [test_removal_never_forces.py:63](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_removal_never_forces.py) pins it for removal only. `domain_metadata` ([substrate_libvirt.py:511-516](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/substrate_libvirt.py)) returns an empty domain with `answered` undefined when `dumpxml` fails.

**Impact.** When the lookup fails for a reason other than "no such domain", the apply reads the domain as absent, creates the directory and disks in its reserved path and runs `virsh define`. A same-name domain that carries the frozen UUID but lacks this context's metadata could be overwritten, and a foreign domain with another UUID makes the define fail after disks exist, which is a partial effect the foreign refusal is meant to prevent.

**Counterevidence.** The effects are confined to this block's exclusively reserved path, `qemu-img` uses `creates:` so no file is overwritten, and a different-UUID domain makes `virsh define` fail. The completion form `presence()` ([substrate_libvirt_machine_protocol.py:100-104](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_libvirt_machine_protocol.py)) requires `owned`, so no false success results. A same-UUID domain without this context's metadata is mostly the B568 case, and the trigger needs a failed lookup together with a successful define. The spec names the answer requirement explicitly only for removal; the apply requirement follows from composing 448-451 with 589.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add the destroy's `observation.answered` assertion to apply.yml before "Create the owned disk directory", with a remedy naming the frozen URI. Exit: a role or unit test where `libvirt_domain_inspect` returns `answered=false` shows the apply failing before any `qemu-img` or `virsh define` task.

#### SBV-09

**Low, doc-stale.** KubeVirt media_eject and the final attach never re-prove the VirtualMachineInstance absent, and the spec contradicts itself about eject on a running machine.

Tracked as: D201 ([backlog.md:5845](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)) and B925 ([backlog.md:270](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)) record eject on a running instance as intended; the overbroad wording and the `attach()` window are untracked.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:1093-1094](../../specs/substrates.md) says "The machine must be off, by a positive `NotFound` of its VirtualMachineInstance, before any media write." The same section ([substrates.md:1112-1115](../../specs/substrates.md)) has `media_eject` leave the claim bound "until the instance next stops", and [openshift-clusters.md:222-228](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md) says release ejects "because the running instance still mounts it, and no node is restarted to release it". D201 clause (a) accepts that, and [release.yml:1-11](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/containercluster_install_agent/tasks/release.yml) dispatches `media_eject` on a node that is running the cluster. In code, only `upload_volume` refuses a running machine ([kubevirt_machine.py:685-687](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py)); `eject()` (659-680) and `attach()` (725-739) call `port_vm` and `media_of` and then patch, with no instance check. The dispatcher runs upload_volume, upload, wait and attach in sequence ([substrate_kubevirt_api.py:61-74](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_api.py)). The docstring of `eject()` at line 660 says "from the stopped VirtualMachine".

**Impact.** Eject on a running machine is required behavior, so line 1093's "any media write" is the stale text and the `eject()` docstring is misleading. A reviewer cannot tell from the spec which rule holds. A narrow check-then-act window remains in `attach()`: the VM template is patched after an upload of up to the upload bound without re-proving the instance absent.

**Counterevidence.** A template patch takes effect at the next start, the UID-tested patch keeps the write on the pinned VM, no Bootwright path starts the machine in that window, and the arm is unqualified (B87 and B731 unrun). Existing tests cover the refusal in `upload_volume` only ([test_kubevirt_machine.py:303 and 312](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_kubevirt_machine.py)). Restricting `eject()` would break the agent-installer release flow and contradict D201.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Narrow substrates.md:1093 to inserting media (the upload DataVolume and its attach), and correct the `eject()` docstring. Decide separately whether `attach()` re-proves the instance absent after the upload wait. Exit: `make docs-check`; if the re-check is added, a unit test where the VirtualMachineInstance exists at attach shows a `machine-running` refusal and no PATCH.

#### SBV-10

**Low, defect.** KubeVirt media_insert verifies against the upload proxy URL read at insert time, not the one the provider proof recorded.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:1098-1103](../../specs/substrates.md) has `media_insert` run `virtctl image-upload` "verifying the upload proxy the provider proof read against the ingress certificate authority", and [substrates.md:1008-1009](../../specs/substrates.md) says the proof's evidence records "the upload proxy". The proof records it ([kubevirt_machine.py:183-185](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py), [evidence.go:26](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/evidence.go)). `upload_trust()` ([kubevirt_machine.py:714-722](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/kubevirt_machine.py)) reads CDIConfig `status.uploadProxyURL` again and returns the live value. The port ([substrate_kubevirt_api.py:62-73](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/substrate_kubevirt_api.py), call at line 68) passes no recorded proxy, and the role task ([media_insert.yml:21-35](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/substrate_kubevirt_machine/tasks/media_insert.yml)) has no input for one.

**Impact.** If the upload proxy changes after the proof, the image goes to a destination the proof did not record, and the change is not reported.

**Counterevidence.** Both reads go through the verified, pinned API client (the `kube-system` UID pin holds) and the proxy is verified against the ingress CA, so trust stays anchored to the same cluster and the spec requires no refusal on a changed proxy. The CA bundle is also re-read, which the spec's "read through the verified API" permits. The finding is a literal-wording mismatch with no safety consequence.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either pass the proof's recorded `uploadProxy` to `media_insert` (touching the role task, its argument spec and the Go request) and refuse when the live value differs, or reword substrates.md:1098-1103 to say the proxy is read again through the verified API. Exit: a unit test where the CDIConfig proxy differs from the recorded one shows a refusal before `virtctl` runs, or `make docs-check` after the reword.

#### SBV-12

**Low, drift.** Substrates spec says the SSH placement arm is coordinated by the context lease alone, but SSH claims are published and conflict across contexts (Q96, D188).

Untracked. The publication was decided by D183 (Q96 answered a, delivered with B816, [backlog.md:543 and 3350](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)) and the host-key form by D188 (B844, [backlog.md:5319](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)).

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:71-75](../../specs/substrates.md): "The controller arm claims the host reservations below; the SSH arm is coordinated by the context lease alone, and its emulated BMC's socket is compared only with its own context's sockets on that host." The owning page says the opposite: [infrastructure-services.md:114-117](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) ("which an SSH host's blocks publish qualified by that host's declared address and port, and again by the SSH host key its Machine pins") and [infrastructure-services.md:227-254](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) ("Every claim placed over SSH is also published (Q96)"); [controller-record.md:110-117](../../specs/contexts/controller-record.md) agrees. `publishedSSHClaims` ([planning.go:206-243](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/planning.go)) qualifies every non-controller claim with `machine.SSHReservationQualifier(claim.Address, claim.Port)` (line 218) and publishes it (line 240), and `hostKeyedReservations` (245-264) adds the `sshkey/` form. The libvirt capability routes its non-local claims there ([capability.go:75-85](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/capability.go)). Doc comments in [contracts.go:555-559 and 566-569](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/contracts.go) say "which planning compares within this context alone" and "It is never published, because two contexts targeting one SSH host are not coordinated"; the comment at [capability_test.go:123-126](../../internal/infrastructureservices/managedservice/capability_test.go) says the same.

**Impact.** A reader of the substrates page expects two contexts to share one SSH libvirt host with no cross-context refusal. In fact a second context's provider or emulated BMC that reuses a bridge, pool, prefix or socket refuses with `controller.conflict`.

**Counterevidence.** The owning page and the code agree; only the substrates page and three comments are stale. Only the claim "its emulated BMC's socket is compared only with its own context's sockets" remains true for socket comparison within planning (`refuseOwnSocketConflicts`, planning.go:167), and claims on the controller host are published unqualified.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Rewrite substrates.md:71-75 to say that both arms claim the host reservations below, the SSH arm's published qualified by its SSH host and pinned host key as [host reservations](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) state, and link there. Correct the three comments. Exit: `make docs-check`, and a reread of substrates.md:68-80 against infrastructure-services.md:227-241. This page change interacts with [SBV-11](#sbv-11).

#### SBV-13

**Low, drift.** The capacity spec gives the remote domain listing the 64 KiB single-fact bound, but the code bounds it at about 8 MiB, and no test proves output past a bound makes the fact unknown.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:633-637](../../specs/substrates.md): "Each command has its own output bound: 64 KiB for a single fact, enough for both directories' bounded listings, and 16 MiB for the domain definitions." In [remote.go:22-31](../../internal/storage/preflightlocal/remote.go), `remoteFactBound = 64 << 10` and `remoteListingBound = remoteDomainDirectories * remoteEntryBound * (remotePathBound + 1)`, which is 2 × 1024 × 4097 = 8,396,800 bytes, passed to the `find` listing at line 146. The listing therefore has a third bound the spec does not name, and 64 KiB cannot hold a worst-case listing. Both lines trace to commit d483caa75 (2026-11-04). The fake runner errors past the bound ([remote_test.go:25-35](../../internal/storage/preflightlocal/remote_test.go), lines 32-33), but no case supplies such output, and no test sets `Capture.Overflow`, the branch at [wiring_preflight.go:50-68](../../cmd/bootwright/wiring_preflight.go) (line 61).

**Impact.** The documented bounds do not match the implementation. A reader expects a host with long domain paths to read unknown at 64 KiB, while the code admits up to about 8 MiB.

**Counterevidence.** Behavior stays bounded and fails closed: overflow becomes an error and the CPU fact reads unknown. Per-directory entry counts are capped and tested, and failing commands leaving one fact unknown are tested (`TestRemoteProbeFailureLeavesOnlyThatFactUnknown`). [B1099](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md) (backlog.md:3190-3203) touches the same listing but not its bound. There is no safety consequence.

**Correction and exit evidence.** State three bounds in the spec: 64 KiB for a single fact, the listing bound of two directories × 1024 entries × one bounded path each, and 16 MiB for the definitions. Add one remote_test case whose answer exceeds `remoteFactBound` for `nproc` and asserts CPU unknown. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/storage/preflightlocal/ -run TestRemote` passes with the case; `make docs-check`.

#### SBV-14

**Low, test-gap.** TestSubstrateRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported checks only table rows against its own case map, so a refusal Unsupported emits with no table row passes.

**Evidence.** [substrates.md:93-94](../../specs/substrates.md): "Each row is one refusal of the provider host lifecycle capability, and `TestSubstrateRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported` holds its `Unsupported` to it." The test ([refusal_table_test.go:32-87](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/refusal_table_test.go)) loops over spec rows (66-83), looks each up in a hand-written case map, filters the combined libvirt and KubeVirt `Unsupported` output to the row's object (77-78) and reports map entries that have no row (84-86). Nothing enumerates the reasons `Unsupported` can emit; they are inline literals at [libvirt/selection.go:21-43](../../internal/substrate/libvirt/selection.go), [kubevirt/selection.go:28-55](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/selection.go) and [kubevirt/capability.go:253-270](../../internal/substrate/kubevirt/capability.go). The doc comment (lines 32-36) says "a row added or removed on either side fails here".

**Impact.** A refusal added to a capability with no table row is not detected, which is how the hosted-attachment refusal of [SBV-02](#sbv-02) reached main without one. The spec's statement holds from table to code only.

**Counterevidence.** Every current table row is exercised against both libvirt and KubeVirt `Unsupported`, a second refusal on the same object in the same graph fails the comparison, and a row deleted from the spec or the map fails. The gap is the direction of checking, not a particular row.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Declare the refusal reasons in one list that the test compares with the table rows, or drive a graph set that triggers every `Unsupported` branch and assert each emitted reason matches a row. The first run will need the SBV-02 row. Exit: adding a refusal to `Unsupported` without a table row makes `./scripts/go test ./internal/substrate/libvirt/ -run TestSubstrateRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported` fail.

#### SBV-07

**Low, defect, tracked.** The vSphere arm fact says delivery fetch, where the spec says the vSphere realized target uses delivery push. The discrepancy holds at the baseline and is recorded as open work under B99.

**Evidence.** Spec 57-60: "Their realized target names no management controller: it names ... the delivery kind `push`". Code facts.go:26: `ArmVSphere: {delivery: DeliveryFetch, tools: []string{"govc"}, credential: account}`. The KubeVirt fact at 27 uses DeliveryPush. Spec: `specs/substrates.md:54-61`, `specs/substrates.md:1171-1173`. Code: `internal/substrate/facts.go:23-28`, `internal/substrate/target.go:171`, `internal/containercluster/agentinstall/pushed.go:17`.

**Impact.** No effect today, because vSphere objects refuse before registration. When B99 realizes the arm, consumers that branch on DeliveryOf (agentinstall pushed.go:17) would treat vSphere nodes as fetch-delivered unless the fact is corrected.

**Counterevidence.** The arm is unrealized, and MachineBoundsFor and the port dispatcher fail closed for vsphere.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Set ArmVSphere's delivery to DeliveryPush, or record in B99's definition that the fact changes with the realization. Exit: ./scripts/go test ./internal/substrate/ -run TestDeliveryOf (a new assertion that vsphere is push).
