#### Observations

- The refusal table is mechanically held to both capabilities' `Unsupported` by `TestOpenShiftClusterRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported`, which reads the spec file directly; it passes at the baseline.
- Refusal ordering matches the spec: endpoint-field rows are checked only after every other row (selection.go:57-66).
- Run-deadline arithmetic matches the spec numbers: 4 emulated nodes 3h56m, 28 emulated nodes 5h57m, 29 emulated nodes 6h18m, KubeVirt ceiling 8 nodes.
- Installer inputs are written by a filter that quotes every string and escapes code points above U+FFFF as `\U` escapes, as the spec requires (plugins/filter/to_installer_yaml.py).
- The insert token is `secrets.token_hex(32)` (256 bits); the sweep removes only directories holding the published inode and refuses anything else after removing what it can prove.
- Physical-node admission and continuation refusals are limited to the three private-delivery checks (physical.go), consistent with B67's in-tree delivery but not with spec lines 30-33 and 574-583 (OCI-01).
- Audit 001 (report-final.md:5482) already flagged the physical and virtual contradiction; no remediation item covers it.
- The Not yet met lines for B733 (vsphere: substrate.Realized excludes vsphere; projection refuses the platform) and B719 (only the Network manifest exists) still match the code.
- The budget derivation (requests.go:233-276, substrate ClusterBounds) and the resolve label, request timeout and ClusterVersion completion read (cluster_state.yml) were spot-checked against the spec and match.
- `restore()` also refuses when the kept copy is missing, a case the spec text does not name by that wording; the spec clause at line 837 covers it because a missing kept copy names no identity.
- B1088 is scoped to the managed-OS installation; container-cluster nodes off the server host already freeze `importCertificate` with certificate removal (selection.go:517-526), so lines 44 and 499 do not contradict each other.
- The kubeconfig identity parser is an allowlist that mirrors the installer's sigs.k8s.io/yaml output, with 33 parametrized rejected forms in test_containercluster_install_inspect.py:336-381.
- The install block resolves unknown, partial and no-effect in one function (install.go:271-292) with table tests for both the apply and the removal verbs.
- Wait diagnosis keeps the stall across an attempt the budget stopped through a separate fact (wait_attempt.yml:91-96), and tests prove host error first, then stall, then budget spent, then timeout.
- Custody withdrawal has one caller, the completed-removal transaction (reconciliation/lifecycle/produced.go:182-190), so a partial destroy keeps the access as the spec requires.

#### Limits

The Ansible install role was read in part: apply, prepare_boot, preboot_vips, boot, readiness, wait, wait_attempt, resolve and finish. These were not read: cluster_state, destroy, observe, release, port and node_release, the kubeconfig keep and identity code of containercluster_install_inspect.py beyond the registration read, and containercluster_media_layout and the publication module_utils. The KubeVirt and Redfish port internals belong to the substrate lane and were not traced. Neither were the contextfs incarnation formatting or the physical round margin value. One Go test invocation was run (the refusal table and physical delivery) and no Ansible unit suites. The sections from line 990 on (Node placement, Preflight, Post-installation network, Adapter boundary) are outside the assigned range and were not judged. A second pass examined only the targets named by a completeness review of the first and no other section; it ran no probes, and its judgments come from reading code and test sources without running the tests to confirm they pass at the baseline. The unit files test_containercluster_media_incarnation.py and test_containercluster_install_custody.py and the localkeyring produced tests were not opened, so those clauses rest on the implementation alone. The identity field in an equal-bytes custody capture belongs to the state-reconciliation and secrets lanes. The sweep after a node whose BMC read failed (destroy.yml:95-110 counts its media as an empty string and may retire its link) was judged lower-risk than a finding, since removing a link only lowers exposure, and was not followed further.

None. Six candidates were raised in the first round and all six were confirmed; the second round produced no candidates.

### OCN: Node placement, preflight, post-installation network configuration, the container-cluster adapter boundary; OpenShift provider coverage, feature matrix, acceptance profiles, qualification rules

Lane `openshift-nodes-coverage`. Spec range: `specs/openshift-clusters.md` lines 990-1147; `specs/openshift-coverage.md` lines 1-210. Register: 193 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 10; confirmed: 9; tracked: 0; refuted: 1.

#### Assessment

This lane covers [specs/openshift-clusters.md:990-1147](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md) and [specs/openshift-coverage.md:1-210](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md), audited at commit f8b15669f. The implementation is sound where it matters for safety. Node placement reads every declared node before it writes, refuses any conflicting label or taint value with nothing written, applies one uid-pinned JSON patch per node, reads the result back, and lets the Go side re-check completion as a set. Preflight resolution uses a fixed `getent` argument vector and the same wildcard-label derivation as the Ansible side. The secondary-network admission refuses, before rendering, the two inputs that the renderer's first-network-wins shortcut would mishandle. The adapter boundary composes substrate entry points by a fixed role name, refuses an off-controller placement for every verb, and keeps the pull secret out of the media values. No confirmed finding reaches Blocking or High. One is Medium: the observation diff reports taint drift on a correctly placed node whose authored taints are unsorted or repeated. The other eight are Low. Four are stale text in the coverage page (a Not yet met line, a matrix row, a mechanism sentence, inline delivery state), two are test gaps in the placement and network-condition paths, one is a patch-pinning defect narrower than its spec clause, and one is an undocumented pair of bridge options. The discrepancies cluster in the coverage page, which carries delivery state that has moved on, and in the observation projection. The findings are bounded by the ledger below: the KubeVirt and vSphere matrix rows, the physical BMC trust rows, the Left out items, half of the acceptance profiles and the lifecycle-engine settlement and retirement paths were examined only partly or not at all. No Python suite was run; the Python tests were read.

#### Confirmed findings

| ID | Severity | Kind | Title |

| [OCN-01](#ocn-01) | Medium | defect | `diff --observe` reports taint drift on a fully placed node whose authored taints are unsorted or repeated |
| [OCN-02](#ocn-02) | Low | doc-stale | Coverage Not yet met line still says clusters over 9 nodes and physical nodes refuse, though both are admitted |
| [OCN-03](#ocn-03) | Low | doc-stale | Trust bundle policy matrix row says API "none yet" and "Needs definition (Q13)" though the field ships and Q13 is answered |
| [OCN-04](#ocn-04) | Low | defect | Placement JSON patch pins only what it writes, and an absent label map is added unpinned |
| [OCN-05](#ocn-05) | Low | doc-stale | Feature matrix rows carry inline delivery and acceptance state and name `lab-sno-fips-controller`, which the profiles table does not list |
| [OCN-07](#ocn-07) | Low | test-gap | No test proves that a policy matching no node, or a network blocked by a foreign attachment definition, fails the block instead of waiting |
| [OCN-08](#ocn-08) | Low | test-gap | Placement's refusal for a declared node absent from the cluster has no test |
| [OCN-09](#ocn-09) | Low | drift | The secondary-network node policy sets OVS bridge options `stp: false` and `mcast-snooping-enable: true` that the spec never names |
| [OCN-10](#ocn-10) | Low | doc-stale | Coverage says every undelivered row refuses through the refusal table, but the arbiter, fencing and dual-stack rows refuse through schema or admission invariants |

#### OCN-01

**Medium, defect.** diff --observe reports taint drift on a fully placed node whose authored taints are unsorted or repeated.

**Evidence.** The owning clause says the observation projection "renders the observed `spec.nodes[].labels` and `spec.nodes[].taints`, so a label or taint removed or changed afterwards is reported" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1028-1034](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). The API page says "Desired-state compilation accepts and preserves repeated authored taints. A native projection deduplicates by `key` plus `effect`; explicitly authoring the standard infra taint is therefore a no-op rather than an error" ([specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:485-487](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md)). The placement rule is one taint per key and effect ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:996-999](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). The adapter sorts the observed taints with `taints.sort(key=lambda taint: (taint["key"], taint["effect"], taint["value"]))` ([containercluster_node_placement.py:90](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/containercluster_node_placement.py)). `nodeTaints` keeps "the first authored taint of each key and effect, sorted" ([selection.go:575-588](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go)). The projection emits `for _, taint := range seen.Taints` in that evidence order and filters only by authored key ([placement.go:75-91](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/placement.go)). The schema declares taints as a plain array with no name key ([openshift_clusters.go:59](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go)), so `canonical()` never sorts them ([projection.go:61-69](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/projection.go)). The overlay then falls through to `return observed` whenever the realized value differs from the effective value under the order-sensitive `Value.Equal` ([diff_overlay.go:111-145](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/diff_overlay.go)). The canonical-form rule orders only "a list the schema names by key" ([specs/state-reconciliation.md:2011-2014](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md)), and the observed-fields row speaks of "declared labels and taints a node lacks" ([specs/state-reconciliation.md:2239](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md)).

**Reproduction.** A temporary test in package `lifecycle` called `overlay(authored, authored, observed, api.Schema(api.OpenShiftCluster), false, false)`. Authored `[b.test/x, a.test/x]` against observed `[a.test/x, b.test/x]` printed `equal=false paths=[spec.nodes[n1].taints]`. Authored `[a, a]` against observed `[a]` printed the same. Authored and observed `[a, b]` in the same order printed `equal=true`. The test file was removed afterwards and the tree is clean.

**Impact.** Medium defect. An operator who authors two taints out of key-then-effect order, or repeats one (which the API page explicitly admits), gets a permanent difference from `bootwright diff --observe` on a correctly placed cluster. It cannot be cleared without re-authoring, and it hides real drift in the same field. The existing placement test authors a repeated taint ([placement_test.go:29](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/placement_test.go)) but never asserts that the diff is clean.

**Counterevidence.** Completion is not affected. `Unplaced` and `carries` compare as sets ([evidence.go:163-188](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/evidence.go)), so apply records the block done. Only the observation projection misreports. Authoring taints sorted and unique avoids it. The canonical-form rule does not state a comparison rule for unkeyed lists, so the spec intent comes from the two clauses above, not from a single sentence.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either project the taints in authored order, emitting for each authored taint the observed taint of that key and effect and keeping repeats, or compare taints in the overlay as a set keyed by key plus effect. A fix keyed by key and effect must still report an observed taint that shares an authored key but has a different effect, because [placement.go:81-83](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/placement.go) filters by key only and that drift is real. State the comparison rule for taints in [specs/state-reconciliation.md:2011-2014](../../specs/state-reconciliation.md). Exit: a `placement_test.go` case that authors taints unsorted and repeated, feeds `placedEvidence`, and asserts that the lifecycle diff reports no differing path for `spec.nodes[].taints`, plus one that asserts a different effect on a shared key is still reported.

#### OCN-02

**Low, doc-stale.** Coverage Not yet met line still says clusters over 9 nodes and physical nodes refuse, though both are admitted.

**Evidence.** The page says "Not yet met: a cluster of more than 9 nodes, a physical node and a multi-node vSphere cluster refuse; tracked as B714, B67 and B733" ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:70-72](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). The same page says a cluster's size "is bounded by its installation deadline alone" ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:65-68](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). The refusal table that owns these refusals has one size row, "more than 28 emulated `spec.nodes`" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:112-113](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)), and its lift list names only B723, B69, B733 and B748 ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:122-130](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). In code, `pastTheCeiling` refuses only when the derived deadline exceeds `lifecycle.MaxDeadline` ([selection.go:207-227](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go)). A physical target meets only `targetPrivateRefusal` ([selection.go:170-174](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go)), which refuses an HTTP BMC, unverified BMC TLS and unverified media TLS. `TestPhysicalRoundBudgetsAndMixedKinds` pins `largestCluster` at 32 for bare metal and 29 emulated nodes as the first size refused ([anysize_test.go:134](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/anysize_test.go), [anysize_test.go:138-141](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/anysize_test.go)). The milestone page records B67 and B714 as "In-tree delivery, 2026-10-23" ([m3.md:811-815](../../specs/milestones/m3.md), [m3.md:888-892](../../specs/milestones/m3.md)).

**Impact.** Low doc-stale. A reader of the coverage page believes clusters of 10 to 28 nodes and physical nodes refuse. That contradicts the refusal table and the page's own size rule.

**Counterevidence.** The multi-node vSphere refusal, "this executable installs no multi-node cluster on the declared platform" ([selection.go:138-143](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go)), is accurate under B733. B67 and B714 are not fully closed: the milestone page records operator evidence and acceptance as open. That is acceptance state, which belongs on the milestone page and not in a Not yet met line. A libvirt value of 28 follows from the refusal table and the test, not from a directly asserted `largestCluster` for libvirt.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Reduce the line to "Not yet met: a multi-node vSphere cluster refuses; tracked as [B733](../../specs/milestones/m3.md#b733)." Exit: `make docs-check` passes and the line names only B733.

#### OCN-03

**Low, doc-stale.** Trust bundle policy matrix row says API 'none yet' and 'Needs definition (Q13)' though the field ships and Q13 is answered.

**Evidence.** The matrix row reads "| Trust bundle policy | `additionalTrustBundlePolicy` | ... | none yet | [B195](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md#b195) | M3d | Needs definition (Q13) |" ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:112](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). The field ships: `field("additionalTrustBundlePolicy", enumeration("Always", "Proxyonly"))` ([openshift_clusters.go:42](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go)). The projection refuses it without bundles, "additionalTrustBundlePolicy requires additional trust bundles", and otherwise sets `config["additionalTrustBundlePolicy"]` ([projection.go:69-73](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/projection.go)). The API page documents it at [specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:98](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) and [specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:320](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md). Q13 is answered: "(a), implemented under D180 ... answered by D180" ([m3.md:142](../../specs/milestones/m3.md)). The delivered record states that admission twins and three projection goldens qualify the in-tree behavior and that it "does not claim live gateway trust" ([delivered.md:8608-8613](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)).

**Impact.** Low doc-stale. The coverage ledger reads a delivered typed field as undefined and absent, and disagrees with the API page it links.

**Counterevidence.** The item link to `delivered.md#b195` is correct. No example or e2e case sets the field, so no acceptance profile exercises it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Set the API column to `spec.install.additionalTrustBundlePolicy` and the Qualification column to "in-tree". Name no profile and make no live-trust claim. The neighbouring rows at [specs/openshift-coverage.md:110](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md) (Q16 "Needs definition", while [m3.md:443](../../specs/milestones/m3.md) says B723's definition closed) and [specs/openshift-coverage.md:101](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md) (arbiter "none yet") were not checked and deserve the same read. Exit: `make docs-check`; the row matches the schema field.

#### OCN-04

**Low, defect.** Placement JSON patch pins only what it writes, not the uid, label map and spec together, and an absent label map is added unpinned.

**Evidence.** The spec says each other node receives "one JSON patch ... that adds exactly its absent labels and taints, pinned by `test` operations on the uid, the whole label map and the whole spec it read, so nothing another manager owns is removed, taken over or replaced" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1013-1018](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)); the originating record repeats it ([backlog.md:5755-5756](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)). `patch_of` always emits the uid test (line 133). It emits the label-map test only inside `if labels:` and only when the read label map is not `None` (lines 134-139). When the read map is `None` it emits `add /metadata/labels` with the whole map and no test (lines 135-136). It emits the `/spec` test only inside `if taints:` (line 141) ([containercluster_node_placement.py:131-148](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/containercluster_node_placement.py)). The only pinning test uses `infra-0`, which adds both labels and taints ([test_containercluster_node_placement.py:115-123](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_containercluster_node_placement.py)).

**Impact.** Low defect. A label-only patch carries no `/spec` test and a taint-only patch carries no label-map test. Neither can remove anything another manager owns, because the patch does not write the part it leaves untested; the only lost guarantee is that a node changed since it was read fails the block. The null-label branch is the one real window: under RFC 6902 an `add` on an existing member replaces it, so a concurrent writer's labels would be replaced.

**Counterevidence.** A uid test is always present. Kubelet always registers nodes with labels, so the null branch is effectively unreachable on a qualified OpenShift path.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Emit the uid, `/metadata/labels` and `/spec` tests on every patch, testing `/metadata/labels` against null when the map is absent, which matches the spec's intent. The alternative is to narrow the clause to "the parts it writes". Exit: label-only, taint-only and null-label cases in `./scripts/ansible-check --suite units ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_containercluster_node_placement.py | cat`.

#### OCN-05

**Low, doc-stale.** Feature matrix rows cite the lab-sno-fips-controller acceptance and delivery state, but the profiles table has no such profile.

**Evidence.** The rows for B720, B722 and B726 write "(delivered)" as unlinked text and put acceptance state inline, "Accepted on one node (lab-sno-fips-controller)" ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:107](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md), [specs/openshift-coverage.md:109](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md), [specs/openshift-coverage.md:115-116](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). The page's own rule is "A row names its item beside it; the item's milestone page holds whether the row is delivered and its acceptance state" ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:142-143](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). Other delivered rows only link to the delivered record, for example B711 ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:95](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). The profiles table has no `lab-sno-fips-controller` row ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:147-163](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). The case exists as `e2e/lab-sno-fips-controller` and its acceptance is in the ledger ([docs/acceptance.md:159-160](../../docs/acceptance.md)) and in the delivered records for X294 ([delivered.md:11515-11525](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)) and X302 ([delivered.md:11733-11760](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)). X302 states that these rows "name other profiles" and that the owner accepted the run "in their place".

**Impact.** Low doc-stale. The rows repeat delivery and acceptance state that the delivered records own, and they lose their item links. The Qualification column therefore names a case that has no recorded node shape or budget on the page.

**Counterevidence.** The acceptance itself is recorded correctly elsewhere. The Qualification column also names things that are not profiles, such as `addons-sno` ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:117](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)), in-tree tests and drills, and the page does not say that every e2e case is a profile. The "(delivered)" wording appears in four rows in total.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Link B720 and B726 to the X302 record and B722 to the X294 record, and drop the inline "(delivered)" and "Accepted ..." text; naming the case in the Qualification column is allowed. Adding a profile row with node shape and budget is an alternative, not a requirement. A check that every name in the Qualification column appears in the profiles table would fail on unrelated rows and is not a suitable exit test. Exit: `make docs-check`; the three rows carry item links and no inline state.

#### OCN-07

**Low, test-gap.** No test proves that an NNCP matching no node, or a CUDN blocked by a foreign NetworkAttachmentDefinition, fails the network block instead of waiting.

**Evidence.** The spec says "A condition reporting `Degraded`, a policy matching no node and a foreign attachment definition each fail the block naming the object" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1113-1115](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). The owning mechanism is the condition check, where "a declared failure condition fails the check at once, naming the object, condition and reason" ([specs/add-ons.md:387](../../specs/add-ons.md)). Both cases depend on reason-filtered `failOn` entries: `{Type: "Ignored", Status: "True", Reason: "NoMatchingNode"}` and `{Type: "NetworkCreated", Status: "False", Reason: "SyncError"}` ([render.go:44-52](../../internal/containercluster/networking/render.go)). The model matches an entry when `(not failure.get("reason") or item.get("reason") == failure["reason"])` and returns `"failure condition " + native(item.get("reason", ""))` ([cluster_objects_model.py:175-182](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_model.py)). The engine raises `Refused(model.label(value) + " " + last)` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:158-178](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). The only direct condition test uses `{"type": "Degraded", "status": "True"}` with no reason ([test_cluster_objects.py:171-176](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py)). The program tests inject only `extra-csv`, `foreign` and `degraded` faults ([test_cluster_objects_programs.py:105-114](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects_programs.py)); `foreign` there is a foreign NNCP, NMState or MetalLB object, not a foreign attachment definition. The fixture `network.json` carries the `SyncError` entry, but only [adapter_fixture_test.go:21](../../internal/containercluster/networking/adapter_fixture_test.go) reads it, and that test compares the rendered program, not run-time evaluation. The knowledge page marks the NNCP condition facts as read from upstream main, not pinned to shipped operator builds ([ovn-localnet-secondary-networks.md:36-47](../../.agents/knowledge/ovn-localnet-secondary-networks.md)).

**Impact.** Low test-gap. If reason matching broke, or the operator used a different reason, a policy matching no node or a foreign attachment definition would wait out the check budget instead of failing at once. Nothing shows the code wrong today.

**Counterevidence.** The reason-matching code is short and reads correctly. The goldens and the fixture show the entries are rendered. The refusal text names the `ClusterUserDefinedNetwork` or policy object, which has the same name as the attachment definition, and the spec asks only for "naming the object". Carrying the condition's bounded native message, which names the conflicting attachment definition and its namespace, would be an improvement beyond the spec.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add engine unit tests: an `Available` check with `Ignored=True` and reason `NoMatchingNode` refuses, and one with `Ignored=True` and another reason does not; a `NetworkCreated=False` condition with reason `SyncError` refuses. Exit: `./scripts/ansible-check --suite units ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py | cat` with the reason-filtered cases passing.

#### OCN-08

**Low, test-gap.** Placement's refusal for a declared node absent from the cluster has no test.

**Evidence.** `place()` refuses with `node %s is not in the cluster, so no node was labelled or tainted` when a declared node is missing from the read, before any patch ([containercluster_node_placement.py:157-163](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/containercluster_node_placement.py)); the patch loop runs after every node is planned. The unit file has eleven tests, from `test_only_nodes_that_declare_a_placement_are_placed` to the malformed-request test ([test_containercluster_node_placement.py:94-203](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_containercluster_node_placement.py)). None declares a node that the read does not return, and a search for "not in the cluster" under the tests finds no hit. The spec says "The block first reads every declared node's uid, labels and spec" and that a conflict fails the block "writing nothing to any node" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1008-1012](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)), and that completion "also requires every declared node to carry its placement" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1020-1023](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)).

**Impact.** Low test-gap. The clause does not name the missing-node refusal; it follows from the read-everything-first rule and the completion rule. A regression that moved the check after the patch loop could label some nodes and then fail.

**Counterevidence.** The current code refuses correctly and before any write.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a unit test with two declared nodes where the read returns one, asserting `Refused` that names the missing node and zero patch calls; the fake cluster constructor at the top of the test file already supports it. Optionally add a sentence on the missing-node refusal to the spec. Exit: `./scripts/ansible-check --suite units ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_containercluster_node_placement.py | cat`.

#### OCN-09

**Low, drift.** Secondary-network NNCP sets OVS bridge options stp:false and mcast-snooping-enable:true that the spec never admits.

**Evidence.** The node policy names the bridge with one field: "holding an OVS bridge for each dedicated uplink (with `allow-extra-patch-ports: true`)" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1085-1089](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). The addressed-bridge paragraph adds "This is the shape OpenShift documents for `br-ex`; nothing else of the node's network changes" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1101](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). The renderer gives every dedicated-uplink bridge `field("options", mapping(field("stp", api.BoolValue(false)), field("mcast-snooping-enable", api.BoolValue(true))))`, with or without `hostAddresses: bridge` ([render.go:82](../../internal/containercluster/networking/render.go)). Both goldens pin it ([addressed-bridge.golden:69](../../internal/containercluster/networking/testdata/addressed-bridge.golden), line 164; [shared-uplink.golden:87](../../internal/containercluster/networking/testdata/shared-uplink.golden), line 145). A search of the specs, knowledge pages, audits and docs finds no mention of either option; they entered with commit 0fcdc3f50 and carry no recorded reason.

**Impact.** Low drift. Multicast snooping changes how multicast is forwarded on every Localnet secondary network, and the operator cannot learn that from the spec. The goldens show the choice is deliberate.

**Counterevidence.** The sentence "nothing else of the node's network changes" belongs to the addressed-bridge paragraph and concerns the node's other network objects, so it does not bar bridge options. The options probably copy the bridge shape OpenShift documents for `br-ex`, and `stp: false` is the OVS default. The effect on multicast is not shown by any run.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Name both options in the spec beside `allow-extra-patch-ports`, with the reason, or drop `mcast-snooping-enable` unless a run shows it is needed. A knowledge note on the OVN localnet page can hold any observed rationale. Exit: the spec text names the options, or the goldens no longer carry `mcast-snooping-enable`; `./scripts/go test ./internal/containercluster/networking/` passes (the golden tests are `TestNetworkRequestGolden`, `TestAddressedBridgeRequestGolden` and `TestAddressedBridgePolicyShape`).

#### OCN-10

**Low, doc-stale.** Coverage says every undelivered row refuses through the refusal table, but the arbiter, fencing and dual-stack rows refuse through schema or admission invariants that have no table row.

**Evidence.** The page says "A row not yet delivered refuses before any effect through the [refusal table](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md#refusal-table), never silently omitted" ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:10-12](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)). Among the matrix's undelivered feature rows, the refusal table holds OKD, disconnected and serving certificates, at lines 103, 105 and 106 of its 24 rows ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:95-120](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)). The topology rows for arbiter (B717), fencing (B737) and dual stack (B738) ([specs/openshift-coverage.md:60-62](../../specs/openshift-coverage.md)) refuse by other means. A node role is `enumeration("controlPlane", "worker", "infra")` and no arbiter or fencing field exists ([openshift_clusters.go:59](../../api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go)), so fencing fails strict decoding. The topology rule says a role "is never an arbiter and carries no fencing, so no rule lists it" ([topology.go:18-20](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/topology.go)) and refuses with "release %s accepts %s controlPlane nodes, not %d" ([topology.go:72-73](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/topology.go)). Dual stack meets "machine, cluster, service, node, and endpoint networks must use one address family" ([admission.go:663](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/admission.go)). The API page owns those two rules: [specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:378](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md) and [specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:497-503](../../specs/api/openshift-clusters.md).

**Impact.** Low doc-stale. All three rows refuse before any effect, so nothing is silently omitted. The sentence names the wrong mechanism, and a reader looking for the arbiter or dual-stack row in the refusal table will not find one.

**Counterevidence.** The safety property the sentence protects holds. I did not run the strict-decoding path for an authored `fencing` field; the conclusion rests on the record schema.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Reword the sentence to say that a row not yet delivered refuses before any effect, through the refusal table or an admission invariant, and link the topology and address-family rules in the API page. Exit: `make docs-check` passes with the reworded sentence.

#### Observations

- Node placement reads every node before any write, refuses any conflict with nothing written, applies uid-pinned JSON patches under `bootwright-cluster-install`, reads the placement back, and has Go re-check completion as a set ([evidence.go:163-219](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/evidence.go)).
- `diff --observe` outside an operation runs the install observe with no outputs and read-only ([placement_test.go:168-200](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/placement_test.go)), as the spec requires.
- Preflight uses `/usr/bin/getent ahosts` with a fixed argument vector and environment, and derives the wildcard label identically in Go ([endpoints.go:20-26](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/endpoints.go)) and Ansible (`resolve.yml:24-26`).
- Preflight capacity reuses `libvirt.CapacityAllocations`, `ReservesFromCatalog` and the same `Allocated` rule as `AdmitCapacity`, so the numbers match the apply gate per host.
- Secondary-network admission enforces consistent `hostAddresses` per bridge, addressed-uplink rules and route next-hop rules ([network_admission.go:74-212](../../internal/containercluster/openshift/network_admission.go)), which makes the renderer's first-network-per-bridge shortcut safe.
- The NNCP hostname selector and the agent-config hostname both use `spec.nodes[].name`.
- Both frozen-request decoders enforce placement as exactly `{local, Machine}` through one `onTheController` helper ([requests.go:297-335](../../internal/containercluster/agentinstall/requests.go)).
- Substrate port composition goes through one fixed role and an asserted allow-list of operations; no role or task name comes from the request.
- Size bound probe: libvirt 28, bare metal 32, KubeVirt 8, vSphere 512 (multi-node vSphere refused separately). The placement module's `MAX_NODES=128` is unreachable on admitted paths.
- No example or e2e case authors node labels or taints. B716 is exercised only through the infra role label of the lab-anysize infra node.
- The CUDN foreign-attachment-definition and NNCP `NoMatchingNode` condition facts rest on a knowledge page whose NNCP part is marked medium confidence.
- A scoped apply whose plan omits the DNSServer block would read the resolution check as pending even when DNS runs. That is what the spec says; it was not verified live.
- The acceptance rows for X294 and X302 depart from the qualification-rule fields (evidence archive, interruption drills) under owner exceptions recorded in [delivered.md:11733-11760](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) and D231.

#### Limits

The KubeVirt and vSphere matrix rows and the physical BMC trust rows were not traced into substrate code, which other lanes own. Settled-apply and retirement behavior, and the engine paths for partial realization, were not traced. The NNCP `Ignored/NoMatchingNode` mapping rests on a knowledge page of medium confidence and cannot be verified from source, and no live nmstate or OVN behavior was checked. No Ansible check suite was run; the Python tests were read, not executed. The acceptance runs' evidence archives are private and not in the repository. Only half of the acceptance profiles and two of the twelve Left out clauses were examined, and the budget arithmetic of the profiles was not recomputed. Whether the status source lists blocks outside a scoped operation's plan was not traced.

#### Refuted candidates

- Container-cluster preflight reports a resolver probe that timed out as failed with "answers: none", not unknown. Rejected: the owning clause says the resolution check "passes when every answer is the slot's effective address, and fails naming each answer otherwise" ([specs/openshift-clusters.md:1054-1058](../../specs/openshift-clusters.md)), the code does exactly that ([service.go:150-157](../../internal/containercluster/preflight/service.go)), and the unknown-on-incomplete-read rule in [specs/cli/output.md:349-351](../../specs/cli/output.md) governs storage host prerequisite probes. Readiness is never falsely proved. Reporting a timeout as unknown would be a betterment, not a correction.

### Group: Ceph storage

### CPL: Ceph ownership and supported inputs, selection and refusal, frozen release and trust (refusal table), plan and prerequisites (stretch services and front doors, cluster execution budget), stretch topology, bootstrap identity and continuation, named refusal outcomes

Lane `ceph-lifecycle`. Spec range: `specs/ceph.md` lines 1-1128. Register: 522 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 9; confirmed: 8; tracked: 1; refuted: 0.

#### Assessment

The lane covers specs/ceph.md lines 1-1128 against the Go in internal/storage/ceph and internal/storage/cephcluster, the Ceph adapters in the Ansible collection and the fitness tests that hold them together. The register held 522 clauses and every chunk was read. The implementation is sound where the spec is numeric or tabular: every deadline in the cluster execution budget and every fixed block deadline in the plan matches the code, the refusal table is read directly by TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported so a drifting reason or remedy fails the build, stretch admission and the five-stage activation journal follow the spec, and the adapter-side trust rules that were traced (anchor-only TLS contexts, the pull broker, the contained probe proofs, the positive-absence snapshot, pool-identity checks) hold. No finding is Blocking or High. The eight confirmed findings cluster in three places: the written refusal vocabulary, which is stale or incomplete against the codes the cluster and host blocks actually emit (CPL-02, CPL-05, CPL-07, CPL-08); planning refusals that the refusal table does not own or that its precedence wording does not match (CPL-03, CPL-06, CPL-07); and boundary tests that stop short of the edge or of one object kind (CPL-04, CPL-09). One further discrepancy, the undefined contract of the host time prerequisite, is tracked by a recorded constraint (CPL-01). The ledger bounds these conclusions: adapter-internal Python clauses in the frozen release and bootstrap sections were examined in part, and the unexamined remainder is named under Limits.

#### CPL-06

**Medium, gap.** A cephadm.addressRef or bootstrap.addressRef that differs from the fleet SSH address is admitted by the API, then refused at planning as 'not yet modeled'. No spec or item tracks this refusal.

**Evidence.** [specs/api/ceph.md:66](../../specs/api/ceph.md) defines `cephadm.addressRef` and `cephadm.bootstrap.addressRef` as "an address name on the Machine of every topology node, or of the bootstrap node", and [specs/api/ceph.md:324-327](../../specs/api/ceph.md) defaults the bootstrap address from `cephadm.addressRef`, else from the Machine's `access.ssh.addressRef`. [specs/api/ceph.md:455-456](../../specs/api/ceph.md) requires only that the MON address lie in the public CIDRs. No clause requires the address to equal the SSH address. Planning in [requests.go:462-487](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go) resolves the address and returns `failure("lifecycle.unsupported", ...)` whenever it differs from `ssh.Address`: "a separate bootstrap address is not yet modeled" for the bootstrap node (line 476) and "separate orchestration and fleet addresses are not yet modeled" for the other nodes (line 485). [provided_host.go:49-57](../../internal/storage/ceph/provided_host.go) repeats the second refusal for provided hosts, the tiebreaker among them. The refusal table at [specs/ceph.md:541-562](../../specs/ceph.md) has no row for it, no Not yet met line names it, and a search of specs, audits and the knowledge pages for the refusal's wording finds nothing. No Go test contains "not yet modeled".

**Impact.** A multi-NIC Machine whose management interface carries SSH and whose storage interface is named by `cephadm.addressRef` passes `validate` and refuses at request planning with a message the spec never promises. The refusal fires before any native effect, so no data or host is at risk, and the remedy text already names the workaround (use the same declared management address). The operator still cannot tell from the specification that this is a known limitation, and the refusal has no test, so it can regress silently. In-tree examples set `addressRef: ip`, which matches the SSH address, so they are unaffected.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal is early and carries a remedy. The rule at specs/api/ceph.md:455 is unaffected. The bootstrap branch at requests.go:463-478 additionally defaults the MON address to the SSH address when no `addressRef` is set, and the non-bootstrap branch runs only when `addressRef` is non-empty. The nearest record, B283, concerns SSH `addressRef` defaults and does not address this.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a Not yet met line under specs/ceph.md Ownership or Plan and prerequisites, tracked by a new M2 item, stating that orchestration and bootstrap addresses must equal the fleet SSH address until separate enrollment addresses are modeled, and amend [specs/api/ceph.md:66](../../specs/api/ceph.md) to match. Alternatively give the refusal a row in the refusal table and raise it from `Unsupported`; that requires moving the check out of the planning function. Exit: a Go test in internal/storage/ceph in which a cluster whose `cephadm.addressRef` and `cephadm.bootstrap.addressRef` resolve to non-SSH addresses refuses with the documented reason, covering the bootstrap, non-bootstrap and provided-host branches; `make docs-check` passes with the new line.

#### CPL-02

**Low, doc-stale.** The spec's list of the only refusals that leave a Ceph attempt failed misses cephx-policy, nvmeof-budget and stretch-intent, plus the api.value and lifecycle.state refusals.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:1116-1126](../../specs/ceph.md) says a named refusal ends the attempt with its entry's code and that "Only the entries coded `lifecycle.unsupported` (`unsupported-release`, `package-license`, `package-platform`, `dashboard-verify`, ...)" leave it failed, listing seventeen tokens. The code has more refusals that leave it failed. Three are coded `lifecycle.unsupported` and absent from the list: `cephx-policy` ([materials.go:369](../../internal/storage/ceph/materials.go)), `nvmeof-budget` ([materials.go:396](../../internal/storage/ceph/materials.go)) and `stretch-intent` ([stretch.go:148](../../internal/storage/ceph/stretch.go)). Two more fail the attempt under other codes: `fips-policy` is `lifecycle.state` ([materials.go:367](../../internal/storage/ceph/materials.go)) and `fips-not-enabled` is `api.value` ([provided_host.go:119-125](../../internal/storage/ceph/provided_host.go)); the host refusal map at [host.go:404](../../internal/storage/ceph/host.go) registers fips-policy, fips-not-enabled and stretch-intent. `AttemptOutcome` ([invocation.go:282-293](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/invocation.go)) returns `OutcomeUnknown` only for code `lifecycle.unknown` and `OutcomeFailed` for every other code. No test holds the spec's list to the code; a search for the section name under internal, test and cmd finds no file.

**Impact.** A reader of the spec concludes that api.value and lifecycle.state refusals do not fail the attempt, and misjudges how the next apply treats these refusals: a failed attempt is resolved from the refusal, while an unknown one is observed first. The effect is documentation only. The statement at [specs/ceph.md:111-112](../../specs/ceph.md) that a cephx-policy mismatch "retains ownership and reports its cause" is consistent with a failed attempt, so the consequence is mild. Many other `lifecycle.unsupported` failures arise at request or admission time rather than through the refusal maps (for example [requests.go:309-372](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go), [services.go:38-106](../../internal/storage/ceph/services.go) and [physical.go:53-85](../../internal/storage/ceph/physical.go)); they are not named tokens, which the corrected wording below covers.

**Counterevidence.** The codes look deliberate: each refusal is of frozen input or a deterministic precondition, and nothing here is unsafe. The spec's first sentence about `lifecycle.unknown` is correct.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Restate the rule as "every entry not coded `lifecycle.unknown` leaves the attempt failed", which covers the api.value and lifecycle.state entries and the request-time refusals, and drop or complete the closed list. No code change is needed. Exit: a test that parses the Named refusal outcomes list in specs/ceph.md, if one remains, and checks it equals the set of refusal tokens in `adapterRefusals`, `hostRefusals` and the SMB refusals whose code is `lifecycle.unsupported`; `make docs-check`.

#### CPL-03

**Low, defect.** The refusal table's row-precedence conditions ("that the previous row does not refuse") are not enforced against the replication-network row.

**Evidence.** Three rows of the refusal table tie themselves to the rows above. The auxiliary-image row at [specs/ceph.md:555](../../specs/ceph.md) applies "that the previous row does not refuse", and the previous row is the replication-network row at line 554. The SMB row at [line 556](../../specs/ceph.md) requires that "neither of the two previous rows refuses". The unneeded-image row at [line 557](../../specs/ceph.md) requires that "none of the three previous rows refuses". In [capability.go:318-327](../../internal/storage/ceph/capability.go) `replicationNetworkGap` sits in its own independent `if` (318-320). Only `unselectedAuxiliary`, `unselectedSMBImages` and `unneededAuxiliary` are chained with `else if` (321-327). None of the three image checks consults the replication result.

**Impact.** A graph with both a replication-network gap and an auxiliary service without its image gets two refusals per object (cluster, pool, client), where the table admits only the first. The operator sees an extra refusal row for the same object. Both refusals are correct on their own terms and the gating of effects does not change, so the consequence is output detail only. The SMB and unneeded-image rows have the same unenforced precedence against the replication row.

**Counterevidence.** The coordinates, host-budget and distribution checks at capability.go:307-317 are also standalone `if` statements, but the spec states no precedence among them, so they do not conflict. TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported ([refusal_table_test.go:35](../../internal/storage/ceph/refusal_table_test.go)) applies one edit per case and cannot see an overlap. The replication row's text has been present since b9a0c643b (2026-10-27); the precedence wording may have been meant for the image rows only, which would make the spec the side to correct. No decision record shows either intent.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either chain `replicationNetworkGap` into the image `else if` chain, or remove the replication row from the precedence wording of lines 555-557 and adjust the counts "two previous rows" and "three previous rows". Exit: a case in TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported, or a sibling test, with both `clusterCIDRs` outside every host and, in turn, a prometheus service without `images.prometheus`, a CephSMBResource without its images and an unneeded image, asserting exactly the refusals the table admits.

#### CPL-04

**Low, test-gap.** TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported never checks CephPlacementPolicy, which the spec says every row also refuses.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:544-547](../../specs/ceph.md) says TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported holds `Unsupported` to the table and that "The capability refuses the CephCluster and every CephPlacementPolicy, CephPool and CephClient whose `clusterRef` names it, each with the same row." The test's expectation map at [refusal_table_test.go:83](../../internal/storage/ceph/refusal_table_test.go) is `map[api.Kind]string{api.CephCluster: "example", api.CephPool: "volumes", api.CephClient: "consumer"}`; its catalog and doc comment (lines 30-34) also omit CephPlacementPolicy. The capability exists for the kind ([capability.go:33](../../internal/storage/ceph/capability.go), registered at cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go:277).

**Impact.** A regression in how `Unsupported` ([capability.go:296-305](../../internal/storage/ceph/capability.go)) resolves a policy's `clusterRef` would not be caught for any table row. The consequence is limited to refusal before operation registration for that kind.

**Counterevidence.** `Unsupported` is generic over the kind, so the policy most likely behaves like the pool. [cluster_budget_test.go:69-71](../../internal/storage/ceph/cluster_budget_test.go) already checks CephPlacementPolicy for the non-stretch host-budget row, so the gap is every other row.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a CephPlacementPolicy naming the pinned cluster to the test catalog and to the expectation map, and update the doc comment. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/storage/ceph/ -run TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported` passes with a policy entry for every row.

#### CPL-05

**Low, doc-stale.** The spec's .rgw.root create command passes the rule positionally and omits the confirmation, while the code (B1073) uses --rule and --yes-i-really-mean-it.

Related delivered record: B1073 ([delivered.md:11384](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md), [delivered.md:11405](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)), which delivered the code fix but not the spec text.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:728-729](../../specs/ceph.md), in the Pools bullet at lines 723-732, gives the command as `osd pool create .rgw.root 32 32 replicated <ruleName> --autoscale_mode on`. The code at [ceph_native_object.py:731-735](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_object.py) runs `"replicated", "--rule", self.request["stretch"]["rule"], "--autoscale_mode", "on", "--yes-i-really-mean-it"`. [ceph-stretch-native-facts.md:108-113](../../.agents/knowledge/ceph-stretch-native-facts.md) records why: the positional argument after the pool type is the erasure-code profile, so a replicated pool names its rule with `--rule`, and a name beginning with "." is created only when confirmed. The spec's ordering ("after its claim and before any radosgw-admin call") matches the code.

**Impact.** The spec states a native command that would create no pool, or a pool off the stretch rule, if followed by hand. The command is an internal Ansible-side detail, so no operator path is affected.

**Counterevidence.** The code is correct and the knowledge page records the fix. B1073 tracks the code fix; no item tracks the spec edit.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Edit the command to `osd pool create .rgw.root 32 32 replicated --rule <ruleName> --autoscale_mode on --yes-i-really-mean-it` and link the knowledge fact rather than restating its reason, or drop the literal command and state that the pool is created replicated on the stretch rule with the monitor's confirmation. Exit: `make docs-check` after the edit.

#### CPL-07

**Low, doc-stale.** The under-three-hosts refusal contradicts 'acceptance-profile sizes impose no additional restriction', has no refusal-table row or owner, and has no test.

Recorded by audit 001 at [report-final.md:5484](../../audits/001-spec/report-final.md); no open item or Not yet met line followed.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:483-485](../../specs/ceph.md) says native cluster size and role counts are the native tools' to judge and "acceptance-profile sizes impose no additional restriction", and [specs/ceph-coverage.md:153-155](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md) says the profiles do not restrict supported initial cluster sizes. The only mention of a lower bound is [specs/ceph.md:957](../../specs/ceph.md): "Fewer than three hosts keep their existing refusal." The refusal exists in `locateHosts` at [requests.go:493-495](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go): `if len(r.Hosts) < 3 || r.Bootstrap == "" { return failure("lifecycle.unsupported", "the core IBM profile requires at least three owned hosts and a bootstrap host", ...)`. The refusal table at specs/ceph.md:541-562 has no row for it, `Unsupported` ([capability.go:296-330](../../internal/storage/ceph/capability.go)) checks only the upper host bound, and a search for the reason text finds only requests.go:494: no spec owner and no test.

**Impact.** A one- or two-host managed declaration passes validation and refuses at request planning, with a reason that names an "IBM profile" the spec disclaims. The refusal precedes any native effect and is defensible as a product bound, so the defect is the missing owner, row and test and the sentence at line 483 that appears to deny the restriction. Line 957 does affirm that a refusal exists, so the text is an unowned assertion more than a flat contradiction. The refusal also fires when no bootstrap node is named, which its reason and remedy do not say.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal is a deliberate fail-closed choice. Audit 001 cited the sentence at its former location in specs/storage.md; it moved to specs/ceph.md:957 without gaining an owner.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Name the three-host floor and the bootstrap requirement in specs/ceph.md:483 as an intentional Bootwright bound with its reason, or add a refusal-table row and enforce it in `Unsupported`. Reword the reason so it does not rely on the "IBM profile". Exit: a test in internal/storage/ceph covering a two-host and a no-bootstrap CephCluster refusal with its reason and remedy; if a row is added, TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported covers it; `make docs-check`.

#### CPL-08

**Low, defect.** The cluster block's Go remedy map codes package-license and package-platform lifecycle.unknown, against the named-outcome list that makes them lifecycle.unsupported.

The finding has no operator-visible consequence today.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:1116-1126](../../specs/ceph.md) is not scoped to one block: it says a named refusal of a Ceph block ends the attempt with its entry's code and that "Only the entries coded `lifecycle.unsupported` (`unsupported-release`, `package-license`, `package-platform`, ...) leave it failed." The host block honors it ([host.go:466-468](../../internal/storage/ceph/host.go): `"package-license": failure("lifecycle.unsupported", ...)` and `"package-platform"`). The cluster block's `adapterRefusals` names both tokens in the generic loop at [materials.go:411-413](../../internal/storage/ceph/materials.go) and codes them `failure("lifecycle.unknown", "the Ceph adapter could not prove its "+reason+" boundary", ...)`. [CLUSTER_REASONS](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_core.py) admits both at lines 67-74, and `ceph_core.refusal` (lines 140-158) passes an admitted token through. The export block uses the same table.

**Impact.** If a cluster-block or export-block worker ever surfaced either token, the attempt would stay unknown instead of failed and the operator would get the generic remedy in place of the license or platform remedy. Today the entries are unreachable: the only emitters are [ceph_packages.py:29-41](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_packages.py), line 158 (package-platform) and line 178 (package-license), reached only through `Transport.packages` (ceph_core.py:715-719), whose sole caller is `host_step` (ceph_core.py:1654), itself called from the host module. The cluster module reports through CLUSTER_REASONS and runs no package worker. The two maps contradict each other and the spec for the same token.

**Counterevidence.** Reachability, as above. The other package tokens in the same loop (package-limit, package-timeout, package-artifact, package-drift) are not in the spec's unsupported list, so unknown is correct for them. No decision or delivered record accepts the cluster coding; [delivered.md:4650-4652](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) repeats the spec's list without scoping it.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Remove `package-license` and `package-platform` from CLUSTER_REASONS and from the loop at materials.go:411, or code them `lifecycle.unsupported` as `hostRefusals` does; the two must change together because TestEachCephBlockNamesExactlyTheRefusalsItsModuleMayPublish ([refusal_test.go:373-399](../../internal/storage/ceph/refusal_test.go)) holds the Go keys equal to the Python tuple. That test pins key-set equality and the presence of a remedy, not the code. Exit: extend it, or add a sibling, so that every token the spec names as `lifecycle.unsupported` is coded so in each table that names it.

#### CPL-09

**Low, test-gap.** The 128 MON/MGR/OSD/MDS services bound has no boundary test: no test admits 128 and refuses 129.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:1094-1102](../../specs/ceph.md) says that past 128 MON, MGR, OSD and MDS services planning refuses, coded `lifecycle.unsupported`, with reason "`CephCluster <cluster> declares <services> MON, MGR, OSD and MDS services, past the 128 one services call submits`". The code agrees: [services.go:105](../../internal/storage/ceph/services.go) refuses on `len(r.Services) > maxCoreServices` and services.go:112 sets `const maxCoreServices = 128`; the worker admits `2 <= len(services) <= 128` ([ceph_native.py:806](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native.py)). The only test of the refusal, [physical_devices_test.go:128-133](../../internal/storage/ceph/physical_devices_test.go), builds `2+maxClusterHosts*maxPhysicalDevices` (167) services, and the accept side plans the per-host shape of 35. No Go test references `maxCoreServices`, and no Python test has a 128/129 services case.

**Impact.** An off-by-one in either bound would go unnoticed. A request of exactly 128 could pass planning and be refused by the worker after registration, or be refused at planning when the worker would admit it. The worker still refuses before applying service specifications, so the consequence is a late and worse diagnostic, not a host effect.

**Counterevidence.** By reading, both bounds agree today. The count covers only mon, mgr, osd and mds because the other families are delegated ([services.go:28-35](../../internal/storage/ceph/services.go)), which matches the spec.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a table test with exactly 128 and 129 core services, checking the first is admitted and the second refused with the exact reason and remedy, and a worker-side case at the same edge. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/storage/ceph/... -run TestCoreServicesBound` passes (the test does not exist yet) with 128 admitted and 129 refused.

#### CPL-01

**Low, gap.** Ceph requires NTP-synchronized host clocks (preflight host.time and the cluster block's host-time refusal), but the spec says Storage accepts any time source that answers.

Tracked.

**Evidence.** [specs/ceph.md:472-475](../../specs/ceph.md) says "Storage accepts any selected time source that answers ... and requires no proof of its upstream synchronization", and [infrastructure-services.md:672-676](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md) says a consumer "accepts a responding source of either kind", with a managed server answering at local stratum 10 when it has no upstream ([infrastructure-services.md:639-641](../../specs/infrastructure-services.md)). Both clauses bind the selected source. The code requires the host clock to be disciplined: [guests.go:42](../../internal/storage/preflight/guests.go) passes `host.time` only when `timedatectl show --property=NTPSynchronized --value` reads "yes", and [ceph_native.py:1905-1906](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native.py) does `require(synchronized.strip() == b"yes", "host-time")` in the cluster prerequisites. `host-time` is raised a second time at ceph_native.py:2810-2820 with a different meaning, an enabled and active cephadm time unit. The token is in neither [CLUSTER_REASONS](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_core.py) (lines 67-86) nor [adapterRefusals](../../internal/storage/ceph/materials.go) (lines 411-413), so it reaches the operator as the generic remote-refusal, coded `lifecycle.unknown`, with no remedy of its own. The listing of the host "time" probe at specs/ceph.md:458-459 does not say what it proves.

**Impact.** The kernel flag the probe reads is cleared once the host has synchronized to any selected source, a local-stratum source included, so a host following an answering, upstream-unsynchronized managed server reads "yes" and the code does not contradict the spec. The 2026-11-03 run's `native-refusal:host-time` ([m2.md:2638-2641](../../specs/milestones/m2.md)) came from hosts whose clock was not yet disciplined, which no spec clause says Storage must accept. What remains is a spec silence: an operator who meets the refusal has no clause defining the probe and no remedy.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fires before any native effect. The missing remedy is an accepted constraint ([delivered.md:4675-4679](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)), and test_ceph_refusal_record.py:176 pins the generic outcome. B1079 repaired the destroy path the unknown record blocked. The original report rated this a High defect on the reading that the spec waives host synchronization; arbitration rejected that reading.

**Correction and exit evidence.** State in the plan's prerequisite probes what `host.time` and `host-time` prove, and reconcile the two code sites. Exit: a preflight test and a prerequisites test that agree on one definition, and a refusal test showing the token reaches the operator with a stated meaning.
