| [CRB-02](#crb-02) | Medium | defect | CephNFSExport admits `protocols: []` and `transports: []`; the worker refuses them only at apply, with an opaque request refusal |
| [CRB-03](#crb-03) | Medium | defect | Consumer prerequisite and key-type refusals do not name the missing prerequisite or the allowed key types |
| [CRB-04](#crb-04) | Low | test-gap | No test proves the consumer's ambiguous public address refusal on a selected MON or MGR host |
| [CRB-05](#crb-05) | Low | doc-stale | CephConsumer admission diagnostics still call the object a "managed export" |
| [CRB-06](#crb-06) | Medium | defect | A filesystem-wide SMB share is admitted beside a share of another SMB cluster on the same filesystem |
| [CRB-07](#crb-07) | Medium | defect | A CephObjectBucket named with 45 to 63 characters is admitted and planned, then refused at apply by the bucket worker's 44-character limit |
| [CRB-08](#crb-08) | Low | doc-stale | Lifecycle destroy clauses claim per-resource absence evidence and export-before-backing removal with no Not yet met line, while every Ceph resource retires with its hosts |

#### CRB-01

**Medium, defect.** A CephConsumer named with 52 to 63 bytes is admitted and planned, then refused at apply by the consumer worker's 51-byte name limit.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:1389-1391](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) says "a consumer name follows the [one name rule](../../specs/api.md#object-names)", and [api.md:249-254](../../specs/api.md) defines that rule as "a DNS label of at most 63 bytes. No kind shortens it for an internal prefix". The Go side accepts every such name: `DecodeConsumerRequest` requires only `reconciliation.ValidSegment(r.Name)` ([export.go:78](../../internal/storage/ceph/export.go)), the request name is `obj.Name()` ([export.go:172](../../internal/storage/ceph/export.go)), and `ValidSegment` bounds the value at `maxIdentifier`, which is 63 ([plan.go:27, 540-548](../../internal/reconciliation/plan.go)). The block identity is hashed past 63 bytes, so planning does not cut the name either. The worker adds its own bound: `require(len(request["name"]) <= 51 and ...)` ([ceph_export_native.py:55](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_export_native.py)). `require` raises the default reason `"request"` ([ceph_native.py:254-256](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native.py)), which is none of the consumer reasons the worker lists at line 27 and the Go side maps.

**Impact.** A CephConsumer named with 52 to 63 bytes passes `validate` and `plan`. Apply builds the cluster and its prerequisites, and only the consumer block fails, with a request-boundary refusal that names neither the field nor the limit. The remedy is to rename a frozen declaration. The refusal comes from `validate()`, which runs first in dispatch, so no principal is minted and nothing unsafe happens.

**Counterevidence.** The 51 is a stale mirror. When the check was added in 77033e8f5 the Go side validated `"ceph-export-"+name`, a 12-byte prefix, and 51 plus 12 is 63. A later commit hashed the block identity and validated the bare name, and the worker bound was not relaxed. The worker's principal names come from a digest (`prefix()` at [ceph_export_native.py:83-85](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_export_native.py)) and do not depend on name length, and the marker and custody file names stay far below 255 bytes, so nothing needs the limit. No spec, knowledge page, test or milestone item mentions it. A Go planning test of a 63-byte CephConsumer already exists ([long_name_identity_test.go:17, 47](../../internal/storage/ceph/long_name_identity_test.go)); [long_name_identity_test.go:78-97](../../internal/storage/ceph/long_name_identity_test.go) covers the 64-byte refusal. Only the worker side has no test.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Remove the 51-byte bound from `validate()`, or accept the full 63-byte label. Exit: a collection unit test that dispatches a consumer request with a 63-byte name and passes validation. The same class of ad-hoc cap exists in `ceph_native_resources.py` at lines 149 (48 bytes) and 187 (47 bytes); those two were not compared with the Go side and are worth a sweep.

#### CRB-02

**Medium, defect.** CephNFSExport admits `protocols: []` and `transports: []`; the worker refuses them only at apply, with an opaque request refusal.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:986-987](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) makes `protocols` "exactly `[4]`" and `transports` `[TCP]`, and line 1004 requires a refused member to name the field, the reason and the next step. The schema declares `field("protocols", set(integer("3", "4")))` and `field("transports", set(enumeration("TCP", "UDP")))` ([storage.go:163](../../api/v1alpha1/storage.go)), and `set()` sets no minimum item count ([schema.go:81-83](../../api/v1alpha1/schema.go)). Admission refuses a present `3`, a present `UDP` and a missing `protocols` member ([nfs_export.go:62-67, 191-193](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nfs_export.go)); an empty list passes all three, because `native.Has("protocols")` is true for `[]`. Normalization defaults `transports` only when absent, so `[]` stays `[]`. The Go request freezes `Protocols: []int{}` and `Transports: []string{}` without `omitempty` ([nfs_export.go:28, 33, 60-70](../../internal/storage/ceph/nfs_export.go)). The worker then requires `canonical(native["protocols"]) == b"[4]" and canonical(native["transports"]) == b'["TCP"]'` ([ceph_native_nfs.py:272](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_nfs.py)).

**Impact.** Validate and plan pass. The export block fails at apply, after the cluster and the NFS service ran, and the refusal does not name `$.spec.native.protocols` or `$.spec.native.transports`. Whether the worker's refusal carries the generic `request` reason was not traced to the adapter.

**Counterevidence.** The worker refuses before any export write, so NFSv3 or UDP is never served. An empty `sectype` is harmless because the frozen field is omitted when empty. A temporary Go test over the admission path returned no issues for either empty list and left normalized `transports` empty; the test file was removed afterwards. A scratch `bootwright validate` run of the NFS example with both lists emptied reported "Desired state is valid". That second probe was not reproduced by the verifiers, and the code reading alone establishes the gap.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In `nfsExportIntrinsic`, refuse a present `protocols` list that is not exactly `[4]` and a present `transports` list that is not exactly `[TCP]`, at their own fields, with the existing remedies. Exit: extend `TestNFSExportProtocolsDefaultRefusesV3` and `TestNFSExportTransportsTCPOnly` to empty lists, and show `bootwright validate` on a scratch copy of the NFS example reporting both fields.

#### CRB-03

**Medium, defect.** Consumer prerequisite and key-type refusals do not name the missing prerequisite or the allowed key types.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:1410-1414](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) says that before any effect the consumer proves its prerequisites and that "any failure refuses, naming the missing prerequisite or the allowed key types"; the table row at [line 1404](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) gives only a remedy and does not weaken that clause. In the worker, `prerequisites()` ([ceph_export_native.py:143-191](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_export_native.py)) raises one token, `export-prerequisite`, from 14 `require()` sites (lines 137, 147, 149, 153, 155, 158, 160, 169, 171, 174, 178, 181, 182 and 189). They cover the radosgw-admin exit code, the pool record and ID, the rbd application, the filesystem record and ID, the csi group, the prometheus endpoint, the quorum leader, the monitor v2 address, the monitoring host and port, and the realm, zone group and zone. The key-type checks at lines 163, 165 and 166 share `export-key-type` and do not report the allowed ciphers the worker has already read. `Refusal` is "A closed, non-sensitive failure reason" with no detail ([ceph_native.py:220-221](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native.py)). The Go side maps each token to one fixed text: `failure("lifecycle.unknown", "Ceph consumer refused: "+reason, "inspect the consumer prerequisites and its owned identities before continuing")` ([export.go:285-287](../../internal/storage/ceph/export.go)).

**Impact.** An operator cannot tell which prerequisite failed or which key types the monitors allow. [B1127](../../specs/milestones/m4.md) (m4.md:2021-2031) records a live run in which every apply refused with an unexplained `export-prerequisite` until the monitor-ID fix, and that fix changed the cause, not the diagnostic.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal fires before any credential is created, so the defect is a diagnostic gap and not a safety gap. The refusal is not entirely detail-free: the adapter appends a code-site token such as `export-prerequisite@ceph_export_native.prerequisites:<line>` as "(adapter detail: ...)" ([ceph_export.py:121-128](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/modules/ceph_export.py), [process_linux_amd64.go:394-405](../../internal/reconciliation/ansiblerunner/process_linux_amd64.go)). That identifies the check only to a reader of the source and never lists the allowed key types. The same Go loop also maps `export-foreign-principal` and `export-identity` to the fixed text, but the spec's naming clause covers only prerequisites and key types. The B86 brief lists the tokens as "Named refusals (item detail only)" ([m4.md:1139-1140](../../specs/milestones/m4.md)); that is a delivery record and not a decision that accepts the gap. The existing tests ([test_ceph_export_native.py:144-146, 238, 261, 278, 344-346](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_export_native.py)) match only the bare token.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Raise a refusal with a non-secret detail that names the failed prerequisite and, for `export-key-type`, the monitors' allowed cipher names, and give each a distinct Go message. Exit: worker unit tests asserting that each prerequisite failure names its prerequisite and that a disallowed key type lists the allowed types, plus a Go refusal test.

#### CRB-04

**Low, test-gap.** No test proves the consumer's ambiguous public address refusal on a selected MON or MGR host.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:1402](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) lists "Ambiguous public address on a selected MON or MGR host, or a shared MON short name" as planning refusals ("one address in the Ceph public networks per selected host and unique MON short names"). The address refusal is `if len(candidates) != 1 { return failure("api.invariant", "Ceph consumer requires one unambiguous public address per monitor and manager host", ...)` ([export.go:345-347](../../internal/storage/ceph/export.go)); it covers zero candidates and more than one distinct candidate. The short-name half has `TestExportRefusesMonitorShortNameCollisions` ([export_test.go:182-199](../../internal/storage/ceph/export_test.go)). No `_test.go` file under `internal` or `cmd` contains "unambiguous public address" or "one address in the Ceph public networks".

**Impact.** The refusal exists and reads correctly, so nothing is wrong today. A regression in the candidate selection could freeze a wrong or arbitrary monitor or manager address into the external details with no test failing.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a planning test with a MON host holding two distinct addresses in the public CIDRs and one holding none, and cover an MGR (prometheus placement) host as well, since the check runs for both types. Candidates are deduplicated, so the two addresses must differ. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/storage/ceph/ -run TestExportRefusesAmbiguousMonitorAddress`.

#### CRB-05

**Low, defect.** CephConsumer admission diagnostics still call the object a "managed export".

**Evidence.** Four CephConsumer admission messages still say "a managed export requires ...": a replicated RBD pool, the csi subvolume group, a prometheus service and a gateway endpoint FQDN ([pools.go:392, 396, 399, 407](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go)), all inside `(a *admission) export`. The kind was renamed from StorageExport because the old name "collides with StorageNFSExport" ([report-final.md:475](../../audits/001-spec/report-final.md), F05-05). [ceph-resources.md:1418-1421](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) keeps the old spelling only for the digest domain tag, the ownership mark and the on-host layout; diagnostics are not among them. A search outside `audits/` finds the four strings only in `pools.go`.

**Impact.** The messages name the wrong concept: an operator can read "export" as CephNFSExport. The field paths in the issues are correct.

**Counterevidence.** The spec fixes no diagnostic wording; [line 1400-1401](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) requires only that admission "names the reference", which the field path does. No spec clause is literally violated, so the record's kind, doc-stale, is a classification of a naming leftover rather than of a stale spec line. `TestManagedExportAdmissionRulesAndPassingTwin` ([export_test.go:46-90](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/export_test.go)) checks only `issue.Field` and a non-empty remediation, so the wording is untested and free to change.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Reword the four messages as "a CephConsumer requires ...". Exit: extend the named test with an `issue.Message` assertion, since it does not check message text today.

#### CRB-06

**Medium, defect.** A filesystem-wide SMB share is admitted beside a share of another SMB cluster on the same filesystem.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:1170-1176](../../specs/ceph-resources.md): "two SMB clusters never share one subvolume. Admission cannot see resolved subvolume paths, so a filesystem-wide export or share on either side refuses with the other on the same filesystem. The refusal names the CephNFSExport, or the share of the other SMB cluster". NFS versus SMB is implemented in both directions: `smbProtocolExclusion` collides on `subvolume == "" || other == "" || subvolume == other` ([smb.go:557-559](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/smb.go)). The SMB-to-SMB check is weaker. `smbSubvolumeEarmark` begins `if subvolume == "" { return }` ([smb.go:567-569](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/smb.go)), so a filesystem-wide share skips it. For a subvolume share it refuses only a peer with an equal `subvolumeRef` and `!peer.Spec().Has("filesystemRef")` and a different cluster ID ([smb.go:571](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/smb.go)), so a peer's filesystem-wide share never matches. The check compares only the CephSubvolume name, not the filesystem each side resolves to. The one SMB-to-SMB test row uses two shares of the same subvolume ([smb_graph_test.go:150-151](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/smb_graph_test.go)).

**Impact.** Cluster A with a share at the root of filesystem `shared` and cluster B with a share bound to a subvolume of `shared` are both admitted, as are two filesystem-wide shares of different SMB clusters. The manager's earmark `smb.cluster.<cluster_id>` does not fire for a share that names no subvolume, so the same CephFS data can be served by two independent Samba clusters with separate locking, which the spec forbids. The exposure is of shared data, not data loss. That planning also accepts the pair was not checked, but no other check refuses it.

**Counterevidence.** "Either side" could be read as NFS versus SMB only. The next sentence names "the share of the other SMB cluster" as a refusal target, and a filesystem-wide share covers every subvolume, so the reading that includes two SMB clusters is the natural one; the ledger records the spec wording as ambiguous, which is why the confidence is medium. Equal-subvolume collisions are refused and tested.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In `smbSubvolumeEarmark`, drop the `!peer.Spec().Has("filesystemRef")` term, resolve the filesystem of each side as `smbProtocolExclusion` does, and refuse when the peer belongs to another SMB cluster on the same filesystem and either side is filesystem-wide or both bind the same subvolume, naming the peer CephSMBResource. Exit: add rows to `TestSMBShareAndNFSExportCannotExposeOneBacking` for a `filesystemRef` share beside a subvolume share of another cluster and for two `filesystemRef` shares of different clusters, each yielding one `api.invariant`.

#### CRB-07

**Medium, defect.** A CephObjectBucket named with 45 to 63 characters is admitted and planned, then refused at apply by the bucket worker's 44-character limit.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:1626](../../specs/ceph-resources.md): "The native bucket name, a DNS label of 3 to 63 characters under the one name rule (its block identity is `ceph-object-bucket-<name>`), so always a valid S3 bucket name", consistent with [api.md:249-257](../../specs/api.md). Go admission has no upper bound of its own: `objectBucket` checks only `len(name) < 3` ([object.go:188-192](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/object.go)), and the Go test admits a 63-character name ([object_bucket_test.go:35-40](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/object_bucket_test.go)). The request freezes `Name: name` unchanged ([object_bucket.go:51](../../internal/storage/ceph/object_bucket.go)) and only the block identity is hashed ([object_bucket.go:28-29](../../internal/storage/ceph/object_bucket.go)). The worker declares `MAX_BUCKET_NAME = 44` ([ceph_native_object.py:98](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_object.py)) and requires `3 <= len(bucket["name"]) <= MAX_BUCKET_NAME` ([ceph_native_object.py:286](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_object.py)). The worker's unit test pins the refusal of a 45-character name with `"^request$"` ([test_ceph_object_buckets.py:578-581](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_object_buckets.py)). The bucket unit file ran with 85 passed, and `TestObjectBucketNameIsAnS3Name` passed.

**Impact.** A valid 45 to 63 character bucket name passes `validate` and `plan`; apply refuses it with the generic `request` reason after earlier blocks have run, naming neither the field nor the limit. The worker refuses before any S3 call, so no data is touched, and the recovery is to rename the bucket. This is the same class as CRB-01 with a different kind and limit.

**Counterevidence.** The specs disagree. [specs/api/ceph.md:428](../../specs/api/ceph.md), on the page that owns storage admission, still says an object bucket's "name has 3 to 44 characters", which matches the worker and contradicts the field record at line 1626. The delivered notes [m2.md:858](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) and [m2.md:1736](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) also carry the 44 limit as history. The 44 was the 63-byte label minus the 19-byte block prefix, and the hashed identity removed the reason. The worker's other name bounds (63 for labels, 128 for user and subsystem names) do not share the defect.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Set `MAX_BUCKET_NAME` to 63, or derive it from `LABEL`, and update the worker test to admit 63 and refuse 64. Correct [specs/api/ceph.md:428](../../specs/api/ceph.md) from 44 to 63. The delivered notes in m2.md are history and need no change. Exit: the bucket unit file passes with a 63-character name admitted, and the Go admission test continues to admit 63.

#### CRB-08

**Low, doc-stale.** Lifecycle destroy clauses claim per-resource absence evidence and export-before-backing removal with no Not yet met line, while every Ceph resource retires with its hosts.

Tracked as B491.

**Evidence.** [ceph-resources.md:1740-1747](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) states in the present tense that destroy "removes owned exports/shares, access mappings and peer links before their backing resources" and that "Cluster teardown does not substitute for per-resource absence and ownership evidence". The code does not implement that order. `ObserveRemoval` returns `observeRetirement` when `e.RetiredWithHosts` ([capability.go:543-548](../../internal/storage/ceph/capability.go)). The retirement reason is "retired with its hosts, which this removal proves stopped", and removal while hosts survive refuses with a reason that names B491 ([retirement.go:14-18](../../internal/storage/ceph/retirement.go)). The SMB retirement builds `Retirement{Action: "smb", ... RetiredWith: r.Machines}` with no native read ([retirement.go:189-224](../../internal/storage/ceph/retirement.go)), and the consumer retirement refuses unless the hosts retire with the destroy and are not physical, then emits `Retirement{Action: "export", ...}` ([export_evidence.go:204-216](../../internal/storage/ceph/export_evidence.go)). [m2.md:1416-1437](../../specs/milestones/m2.md) records that D160 moved the per-resource online removal clauses of B81, B492, B477 to B483 and B489 into B491.

**Impact.** Documentation only. A reader would take per-resource removal ordering and absence proof as enforced, while a destroy relies on the hosts' stop proof. The behavior is intentional and safe under D160.

**Counterevidence.** The gap is partly disclaimed elsewhere. [ceph.md:13-18](../../specs/ceph.md) carries "Not yet met: complete resource lifecycles, removal while hosts survive ... B491", [ceph-resources.md:21](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) carries a blanket "Not yet met: later P2 kinds and their qualified lifecycles" with no id, and the per-kind sections name B491 at lines 142, 454, 484, 811, 834, 935, 1406, 1501, 1509, 1529, 1546 and 1597. None of those is in the Lifecycle and migration gates section. [specs/index.md:50-53](../../specs/index.md) requires a clause the code does not meet to carry its own "Not yet met: ...; tracked as `B<n>`" line. The verifiers rated this Low, and the severity above follows them. Every kind's retirement was inferred from the shared `observeRetirement` path and the consumer and SMB variants; the object, bucket, client and NVMe-oF capabilities were not traced individually.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add after line 1747: "Not yet met: Ceph resources retire with their cluster's hosts and carry no per-resource absence evidence or online removal order; tracked as B491." Exit: `make docs-check` passes and `grep -n "Not yet met" specs/ceph-resources.md` shows a line in the Lifecycle and migration gates section naming B491.

The rows headed round 2 and round 3 record targeted re-examinations of sections already listed; their clause counts overlap the first rows and are not additive.

#### Observations

- Every named refusal and fix in this lane (nfs-export-path-escape, nfs-export-realm-default, nfs-export-foreign, the SMB refused-member table, the consumer MON-ID key, the CSI Secret names and the subvolume-group manager retry) has both Go and collection unit tests; the recent consumer fixes match the current spec text.
- SMB admission is unusually complete: each refused member, value rule and cross-object rule has an exact-message test, including no-echo checks (TestSMBDiagnosticsNeverEchoAuthoredValues, TestSMBFieldsOutsideTheIntersectionRefuse).
- The RGW NFS export never puts the user's key pair in a record or argument: ExportUserWorker reads it into memory and splices it into stdin only on update, redacting it from failures.
- The consumer worker's principal-name digest (prefix()) and the Go ConsumerPrincipalPrefix agree: the same domain tag, owner and name, and 16 hex digits.
- inspection.go nvmeofScopeText shows the subsystem NQN in a status scope row. That is status output, not a diagnostic, so it does not contradict 'No diagnostic echoes an authored NQN'.
- cephcluster.AddonExportFacts takes TLS from the last fronting ingress, while ceph.exportGateway takes it from the first. The two agree unless a gateway's ingresses differ in ssl; not reported.
- Critic after round 1: The finder covered all 54 CephNFSExport clauses, all 84 CephSMBResource clauses and all 45 Consumer refusals clauses, mostly at admission. Execution and adapter clauses were partly verified by grep alone, especially custody, key handling and NQN non-echo in the NVMe-oF, consumer and object workers. The Remaining families, Consumer chains and Lifecycle sections were examined thinly (12/20, 12/19 and 10/23 clauses). A spot-check confirmed several admission rules: the SMB public-address network and broadcast checks (cephcluster/smb.go:708-709) and the SMB 445, 9922 and 4379 listener set (smb.go:657-659). It also confirmed the NVMe-oF trsvcid 4420 rule, the 128-entry limit and the '*' host refusal (cephcluster/nvmeof.go:122-141). Two more checks matched: the squash token list (api/v1alpha1/storage.go:159), and the consumer worker's 51-byte name limit behind CRB-01 (ceph_export_native.py:55). The highest remaining risk is adapter-boundary secret handling and the SMB cross-cluster exposure ambiguity the finder chose not to report.
- Consumer CephX and RGW principals are minted with custody before effect, attempt records before each native add, and recapture without regeneration; unit tests cover lost replies, foreign principals and widened caps (test_ceph_export_native.py).
- Consumer caps are duplicated in Go (export.go:114-125) and Python (ceph_export_native.py:31-47) and cross-checked: validate() requires principals == caps_for(request).
- Every worker examined uses attempt records and refuses a listed resource that has no attempt record as foreign before any write.
- The NFS export worker re-applies a drifted owned export during apply, not during observation; observation stays read-only.
- Storage admission validates against the normalized catalog, so derived values such as a share's cluster_id take part in the cross-object checks.
- Critic after round 2: The finder covered the admission-heavy sections (NFS export, SMB, NVMe-oF, consumer, object user and bucket) thoroughly, and my spot checks agree: pseudo uniqueness, client canonical uniqueness, count_per_host, clustering never, the dashboard ID and the displayName bound, KEY_LIMIT 128, and the SMB ports with CTDB only when clustered. Coverage is thin in Remaining families (12 of 20 clauses: CephClient caps, replication peers and the single-reveal rule were skipped), in Consumer chains (12 of 19), and above all in Lifecycle and migration, where destroy ordering, per-resource absence evidence and the migration-error and test-matrix clauses 1740-1757 were never examined. The likeliest hidden discrepancies are in retirement evidence per resource family, in CephClient privilege derivation, and in name-length limits on the other block identities, the same pattern as CRB-01.
- Every Ceph resource kind retires through one host-stop retirement record (retirement.go), deliberately per D160; online per-resource removal is wholly B491's.
- The surviving-consumer warning and the destroy refusal share retiredWithHosts, so plan and destroy cannot disagree.
- NVMe-oF deadline constants are mirrored term for term between internal/storage/ceph/nvmeof.go:262-272 and ceph_native_nvmeof.py:59-61.
- Produced material is reachable from the CLI only through storage dashboard access (object-user, dashboard password) and client keyring export (wiring_inspection.go:51-74); CephConsumer external-details has no reveal path.

#### Limits

The SMB Python worker, the NVMe-oF worker's full budget formula, and the DNS service's publication and conflict handling were read only partly or not at all. Replication peers (B483) and the access handoff CLI (B489) were skipped as other lanes. Only one runtime probe was run: bootwright validate over a scratch copy of the NFS example. The Python consumer worker was not run, so the 51-byte name finding rests on reading the code. Go and Python unit tests were not run. Round 2: This round covered only the critic's targets. The destroy-ordering and migration clauses 1740-1757 were not re-examined. I ran no probes (no go test or ansible-check); every conclusion comes from reading source and tests. I did not trace the exact error-to-diagnostic mapping for every worker refusal reason. I did not check bounded_command's logging behavior for the radosgw-admin user info output that carries keys. Round 3: Read-only source review; no probes were run. C315 per-family test coverage was checked by grep counts and test names, not by reading each test. C149's itemized count was not derived term by term. C311 and C316 (operator evidence across profiles) need live runs and were not examined.

#### Refuted candidates

None. All eight candidates over three rounds were confirmed; no candidate was refuted or sent to arbitration.

### CPC: Ceph release qualification, feature matrix, profiles and capacity, stretch constraints, other native restrictions to freeze, unsupported combinations, physical qualification, acceptance evidence

Lane `ceph-coverage`. Spec range: `specs/ceph-coverage.md` lines 1-559. Register: 244 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 10; confirmed: 7; tracked: 1; refuted: 2.

#### Assessment

This lane covers [specs/ceph-coverage.md:1-559](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md). The code mostly does what the page requires. All nine unsupported-combination fixtures run through the production compiler and pin the code, kind, name, field, message and remediation. Every P0-P7 profile example matches its OD21 (b) RAM total and its vCPU and root+data cells. The cluster host ceiling comes from the run-deadline formula, not a fixed number. Erasure-coded realization is enforced from admission through to the apply-time `osd tree` proof. Stretch arbiter isolation and the `disable_stretch_mode` guard are both tested. Release differences go through selection variants, not version conditionals. The ledger's sections hold no clause the code fails outright. The discrepancies sit in two places. The first is the boundary between `validate` and `plan`: two fields pass admission and are then refused at plan with a generic `lifecycle.unsupported` message that no refusal table row records (CPC-01, CPC-07). The second is the evidence records around the code: a stale combination-table cell and a duplicate fixture, a missing stretch-EC row, an OD21 condition that has expired, an e2e rehearsal claim that does not match the example, and an acceptance template that omits required fields (CPC-02 to CPC-06). Nothing found here destroys data, bypasses a confirmation or exposes secret material. The single Medium finding is a refusal that fires before any effect. Live operator clauses, the physical rows and the per-family service depth are outside what reading source can prove; Limits names them.

| ID | Severity | Kind | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CPC-01](#cpc-01) | Medium | defect | Planning refuses every CephCluster that declares an admitted `spec.mgrModules` entry (`cephadm`, `rbd_support`), with a refusal no spec states |
| [CPC-02](#cpc-02) | Low | doc-stale | U06's owning diagnostic names a CephPool `$.spec.type` that does not exist, and its fixture is a byte-for-byte copy of U05 |
| [CPC-03](#cpc-03) | Low | test-gap | The combination table has no row for an erasure-coded pool on a stretch cluster, and no test pins that refusal's message or remediation |
| [CPC-04](#cpc-04) | Low | doc-stale | The catalog still says OD21 is unanswered and the budget test accepts either RAM option, but D160 chose OD21 (b) |
| [CPC-05](#cpc-05) | Low | doc-stale | The spec says the `lab-3-nodes-ceph` e2e rehearses the object example, but the e2e uses a TLS ingress VIP instead of daemon-terminated TLS and has no host-address name check |
| [CPC-06](#cpc-06) | Low | doc-stale | The Ceph matrix row template omits fields the acceptance-evidence section requires (effective-intent and plan digests, qualification tier, submilestone) |
| [CPC-07](#cpc-07) | Low | defect | Admission exempts a root cluster SSH user from `keyRef`, but planning refuses every cluster without a cluster SSH key with a generic trust-profile message |

#### CPC-01

**Medium, defect.** Planning refuses every CephCluster whose spec.mgrModules admission accepts (cephadm, rbd_support) and every singleHostDefaults cluster, with a refusal no spec states.

Planning refuses every CephCluster that declares an admitted `spec.mgrModules` entry (`cephadm`, `rbd_support`), with a refusal no spec states.

**Evidence.** The API page says "`spec.mgrModules` admits `cephadm` and `rbd_support`" ([specs/api/ceph.md:127-128](../../specs/api/ceph.md)). The feature matrix lists "qualified config and manager modules" under B490 and B80 ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:126](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). B80 is delivered through X70 with "allowlisted cluster config and manager modules" ([specs/milestones/m2.md:576-586](../../specs/milestones/m2.md)). Admission refuses only modules outside that pair: `} else if !slices.Contains([]string{"cephadm", "rbd_support"}, module) {` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/services.go:53-66](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/services.go)). A test pins that acceptance: `validate("cephadm", "rbd_support")` yields no issue under `$.spec.mgrModules` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/native_nfs_test.go:112](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/native_nfs_test.go)). Planning then refuses every non-empty list in `baseRequest`, which every block of the cluster runs through: `if spec.Get("mgrModules").Len() != 0 || spec.Get("cephadm", "bootstrap", "singleHostDefaults").Bool() { return Request{}, failure("lifecycle.unsupported", "the core adapter does not yet realize additional cluster configuration", "use only the qualified core MON/MGR/OSD profile")` ([internal/storage/ceph/requests.go:371-373](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go)). The coverage page allows a Bootwright pre-effect refusal only "for a feature it does not realize or a combination listed under unsupported combinations" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:105-115](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). The Ceph refusal table ([specs/ceph.md:541-566](../../specs/ceph.md)) has no row for this refusal, although `TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported` is meant to hold the code's `Unsupported` to that table ([specs/ceph.md:544](../../specs/ceph.md)). The message text appears nowhere in the repository except requests.go:372. No test in internal/storage/ceph exercises `mgrModules`. The expectation in [cmd/bootwright/admission_acceptance_test.go:256](../../cmd/bootwright/admission_acceptance_test.go) and [:344](../../cmd/bootwright/admission_acceptance_test.go) concerns a different module in the reference example and does not pin this planning refusal.

**Impact.** An operator who follows the API page and declares `mgrModules: [rbd_support]` passes `validate`. The whole cluster is then refused at plan with a remedy that names no field. The refusal fires before registration and effects, so nothing is damaged. The cost is a confusing round-trip on a field the API documents as admitted.

**Counterevidence.** The `singleHostDefaults` half of the same condition is not a separate defect. Admission accepts `singleHostDefaults` only for exactly one non-stretch node ("single-host defaults require exactly one non-stretch node", [internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go:171-173](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go)). Host binding requires at least three owned hosts ([internal/storage/ceph/requests.go:493-495](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go)), and the spec states "Fewer than three hosts keep their existing refusal" ([specs/ceph.md:957](../../specs/ceph.md)). That refusal is redundant but specified. A related Low oddity remains: [specs/ceph-resources.md:285-288](../../specs/ceph-resources.md) still defines a 2/1 pool default for `singleHostDefaults`, which admission reuses at [internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go:169](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go), on a topology that can never plan. `cephadm` and `rbd_support` are always-on manager modules in Ceph, so the refused declaration asks for a no-op enable.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either accept the two admitted modules at planning (a no-op enable), or move the refusal into admission at `$.spec.mgrModules` with a concrete remedy and remove the "admits" sentence from the API page. Then align the refusal table and the B80 record, or add a Not yet met line with an item. Exit: a cephcluster or ceph package test plans the libvirt-3-nodes-ceph example with `mgrModules: [rbd_support]` and either succeeds, or asserts an admission diagnostic at `$.spec.mgrModules[0]` that a refusal table row pins.

Also reported as [CEA-03](#cea-03); the entries are merged here.
#### CPC-02

**Low, doc-stale.** U06's owning diagnostic names a nonexistent CephPool $.spec.type, and its fixture is a byte-for-byte copy of U05.

U06's owning diagnostic names a CephPool `$.spec.type` that does not exist, and its fixture is a byte-for-byte copy of U05.

**Evidence.** Row U06 reads "EC CephFS metadata pool | ... | admission `api.invariant` on CephPool `$.spec.type` | tested" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:487](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). CephPool admission raises no issue at `$.spec.type`. For an erasure-coded `cephfsMetadata` pool it raises "CephFS metadata pools require replicated protection" at `$.spec.erasure` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go:284](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go)) and "pool role does not permit erasure protection" at `$.spec.role` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go:310](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go)). The U06 fixture expects exactly those two fields ([cmd/bootwright/testdata/matrix/U06.yaml:1-29](../../cmd/bootwright/testdata/matrix/U06.yaml)). `diff U05.yaml U06.yaml` prints only `1c1 < row: U05 --- > row: U06` ([cmd/bootwright/testdata/matrix/U05.yaml:1-29](../../cmd/bootwright/testdata/matrix/U05.yaml)). The harness lists "Owning diagnostic" only as a column name ([cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go:39](../../cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go)) and compares diagnostics to the fixture alone ([cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go:271-317](../../cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go)), so the stale cell passes.

**Impact.** The combination table does not name the diagnostic that refuses U06. U06 reads as an independent tested row but adds no coverage beyond U05.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal exists and its fixture pins the code, field, message and remediation, so the behavior is correct and proved. U05 and U06 are two distinct rules in the code (pools.go:310 and pools.go:284). U05's own text says "today only `cephfsMetadata`", so no role-only input exists today, and one fixture legitimately triggers both rules.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Change U06's owning diagnostic to `api.invariant` on CephPool `$.spec.erasure`. Then merge U05 and U06, or narrow each fixture to its own diagnostic. Optionally have the harness check that the field named in the Owning diagnostic cell is among the fixture's expected fields. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./cmd/bootwright/ -run TestCephMatrixCombinationFixturesRefuse` with that check in place.

#### CPC-03

**Low, test-gap.** The combination table has no rows for the stretch exclusions the code refuses (EC pools, device-class rules, NFS/SMB, NVMe-oF), and the EC-in-stretch message is pinned by no test.

The combination table has no row for an erasure-coded pool on a stretch cluster, and no test pins that refusal's message or remediation.

**Evidence.** The table's rule is "Each row is a combination that a primary source calls unsupported" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:462](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)), with message and remediation pinned by the row's fixture ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:462-467](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). The coverage page says "The same IBM page excludes EC pools and device-class rules in stretch mode" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:339-340](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)), and [specs/ceph.md:612-613](../../specs/ceph.md) refuses stretch pools that use erasure-coded pools and device-class rules. The code refuses an EC pool on a stretch cluster: `a.invalid("$.spec.erasure", "stretch does not support erasure pools", "remove spec.erasure and declare spec.replicated for a stretch cluster")` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go:306-308](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go)). The table ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:480-490](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)) has no row for it, and the U01 fixture does not mention erasure ([cmd/bootwright/testdata/matrix/U01.yaml](../../cmd/bootwright/testdata/matrix/U01.yaml)). The phrase "support erasure" matches only pools.go in the repository. The one stretch-EC test checks the field alone: `requireIssue(t, Validate(pool, catalog), "$.spec.erasure")` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/admission_test.go:384-386](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/admission_test.go)). Other EC rules raise issues at the same field, so that test does not isolate the stretch refusal.

**Impact.** A change to the stretch-EC message or remedy breaks no test. The combination ledger understates the primary-source exclusions it is meant to record. The refusal fires at admission, before any effect.

**Counterevidence.** Device-class rules on a stretch cluster arrive as a CephPlacementPolicy. U01's owning diagnostic names "each CephPlacementPolicy `$.spec.clusterRef`" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:482](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)), its fixture pins that message and remedy, and the refusal at [internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go:265-267](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/pools.go) is pinned by [internal/storage/cephcluster/stretch_test.go:168-170](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/stretch_test.go). NFS, SMB and NVMe-oF on stretch are not primary-source exclusions. IBM documents NVMe-oF in stretch with at least four nodes per site ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:344-347](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). The NVMe-oF deferral ([internal/storage/cephcluster/nvmeof.go:58](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/nvmeof.go)) and the NFS and SMB refusal ([internal/storage/cephcluster/stretch_services.go:32-34](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/stretch_services.go)) are qualification gaps tracked as B935 and B936 ([specs/ceph.md:756-759](../../specs/ceph.md)), and `TestStretchRefusesNVMeoFNFSAndSMB` pins them ([internal/storage/cephcluster/stretch_test.go:294](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/stretch_test.go)). None of these needs a U row.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add one U row for an erasure-coded pool on a stretch cluster, sourced to the IBM stretch page, with a fixture. Exit: a new matrix fixture (for example U11.yaml) that `TestCephMatrixCombinationFixturesRefuse` runs and that asserts "stretch does not support erasure pools" with its remediation.

#### CPC-04

**Low, doc-stale.** The catalog still says OD21 is unanswered and the budget test accepts either RAM option, but D160 chose OD21 (b).

**Evidence.** The catalog says "Until OD21 is answered, both RAM totals are shown" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:207-208](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)) and "Its RAM must equal one of the two RAM cells" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:237](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). The table header still carries "RAM GiB under OD21 (a)" ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:242](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). OD21 is answered: "D160 chose (b): IBM's per-guest sums plus 2 GiB ... answered by [D160]" ([specs/milestones/m2.md:264](../../specs/milestones/m2.md)), "D160 answered OD21 (b) and OD22 (a)" ([specs/milestones/m2.md:1176](../../specs/milestones/m2.md)), and the decision text reads "OD21 (b): IBM per-guest sums plus 2 GiB" ([specs/milestones/backlog.md:4476](../../specs/milestones/backlog.md)). The spec's own prose already treats (b) as the authored total ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:557](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). `TestCephProfileBudgetsMatchExamples` accepts `case int64(optionB) * 1024:` or `case int64(optionA) * 1024:` and only logs in both branches ([cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go:511-519](../../cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go)). A `-v` run logs "P0 declares 24 GiB, the OD21 (b) total" through "P7 declares 106 GiB, the OD21 (b) total" and passes.

**Impact.** A future example sized to the rejected option (a) would pass the budget gate. Several rows differ between the options (P5 24 against 36, P6 24 against 60), so the loose gate is not hypothetical. The catalog keeps a column whose condition has expired.

**Counterevidence.** Every example today matches (b), so no running example is wrong. The test follows the spec's own stale sentence at line 237, so test and spec agree with each other. No product code is involved.

**Correction and exit evidence.** In the spec, drop the "Until OD21 is answered" sentence, word the budget rule as "Its RAM must equal the OD21 (b) cell", and drop the (a) column or mark it reference only. In the test, drop `optionA` from the column list ([cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go:41](../../cmd/bootwright/ceph_matrix_linux_amd64_test.go)) and from the switch. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./cmd/bootwright/ -run TestCephProfileBudgetsMatchExamples` fails when an example matches only the (a) cell.

**Low, doc-stale.** The spec says the lab-3-nodes-ceph e2e rehearses the object example, but the e2e uses a TLS ingress VIP, not daemon-terminated TLS, and has no host-address name check.

**Evidence.** The coverage page says "the e2e `lab-3-nodes-ceph` case rehearses both" the object and NFS examples, and describes the object example as two daemons that terminate TLS themselves, accepted by an HTTPS status line from each daemon through the endpoint name, "a failed name check through a host address", and one RGW daemon stopped and started ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:268-277](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)). The example matches that description: `rgw_frontend_port: 443`, `ssl: true`, `certificate_source: inline` ([examples/ceph-clusters/libvirt-3-nodes-ceph-object/storage/cluster.yaml:82-97](../../examples/ceph-clusters/libvirt-3-nodes-ceph-object/storage/cluster.yaml)). The example's README names no acceptance procedure of its own, only "Run it with the e2e `lab-3-nodes-ceph` case" ([examples/ceph-clusters/libvirt-3-nodes-ceph-object/README.md:30](../../examples/ceph-clusters/libvirt-3-nodes-ceph-object/README.md)). The e2e renders a different shape: the rgw service has `rgw_frontend_port: 8081` and `ssl: false` ([e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/templates/storage/cluster.yaml:99-107](../../e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/templates/storage/cluster.yaml)) behind a `service_type: ingress` with `ssl: true` on a VIP ([e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/templates/storage/cluster.yaml:109-124](../../e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/templates/storage/cluster.yaml)). The runbook describes the case as "RGW behind a TLS ingress" ([e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/runbook.md:7-8](../../e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/runbook.md)), and both name checks go through the VIP, the endpoint name and `wrong.e2e.example.test` ([e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/runbook.md:445-446](../../e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/runbook.md)).

**Impact.** No case produces the acceptance evidence the spec states for the object example, namely per-daemon HTTPS and a name check through a host address.

**Counterevidence.** The e2e does rehearse the stop and start of one RGW daemon while the other answers ([e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/runbook.md:763-783](../../e2e/lab-3-nodes-ceph/runbook.md)) and a wrong-name refusal through the ingress. The NFS half of the sentence matches the e2e. The runbook labels the variant honestly, so only the spec sentence is stale.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either state that the e2e rehearses an ingress-fronted variant and give the object example its own acceptance procedure, or add an e2e variant that renders daemon-terminated TLS and the host-address check. Exit: a runbook that shows per-daemon HTTPS through the endpoint name and a refused name check through a host address, or spec text that names the ingress variant.

#### CPC-07

**Low, defect.** Admission exempts clusterSSH.user root from keyRef, but planning refuses every cluster without a cluster SSH key with an unrelated 'trust profile' message.

Admission exempts a root cluster SSH user from `keyRef`, but planning refuses every cluster without a cluster SSH key with a generic trust-profile message.

**Evidence.** Admission requires `clusterSSH.keyRef` only for a non-root user: `if fallback(ssh.Get("user"), "cephadm") != "root" && !ssh.Has("keyRef") {` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go:106-110](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/topology.go)). The passing admission fixture relies on that exemption, with `clusterSSH` user `root` and no `keyRef` ([internal/storage/cephcluster/admission_test.go:51](../../internal/storage/cephcluster/admission_test.go)). Planning copies `ClusterKeyRef` from `spec.cephadm.clusterSSH.keyRef` ([internal/storage/ceph/requests.go:332](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go)) and refuses whenever it is empty, regardless of user: `if r.ClusterSSHUser == "" || r.ClusterKeyRef == "" || ...` returns `lifecycle.unsupported` "the requested Ceph trust profile is not implemented by the core adapter" with the remedy "declare the cluster SSH key, registry entitlement and the aes CephX core profile" ([internal/storage/ceph/requests.go:355-356](../../internal/storage/ceph/requests.go)). No code path realizes a keyless root mode: [internal/storage/ceph/capability.go:95](../../internal/storage/ceph/capability.go) and [internal/storage/ceph/host.go:557](../../internal/storage/ceph/host.go) use `ClusterKeyRef` unconditionally. No spec backs the exemption. [specs/api/ceph.md:324](../../specs/api/ceph.md) states only the default user `cephadm`, the feature matrix names a "non-root orchestration SSH login" as a capability ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:126](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)), and the trust-profile refusal is in no row of the Ceph refusal table (the nearest, [specs/ceph.md:553](../../specs/ceph.md), covers coordinates and transport). `validate` owns "every independent invariant whose prerequisites are valid" ([specs/api.md:209](../../specs/api.md)), and `keyRef` presence is such an invariant.

**Impact.** An operator who authors `clusterSSH.user: root` without `keyRef` gets a clean `validate` and a refusal at plan whose message gives no JSON path. The admission rule implies a root mode that nothing implements.

**Counterevidence.** No effect runs. The remedy text does say "declare the cluster SSH key", which points at the field. The refusal at requests.go:355 is one combined condition over user, key, registry and CephX key type, not a key-specific check. No spec sentence forbids a root cluster SSH user, so the defect is a `validate` and `plan` inconsistency, not a contradiction of a stated refusal.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Drop the root exemption at topology.go:108 and give the admission_test.go:51 fixture a `keyRef`. State the `keyRef` rule among the `clusterSSH` field rules of the API page near [specs/api/ceph.md:260](../../specs/api/ceph.md). Exit: an admission test in internal/storage/cephcluster asserts that `clusterSSH.user: root` without `keyRef` refuses at `$.spec.cephadm.clusterSSH.keyRef`.

#### CPC-10

**Low, drift.** Release qualification does not state that an authored digest must name the linux/amd64 platform manifest, though the resolver refuses an index digest and B1004 cites this section as requiring it. Re-judged from tracked: B1004 (specs/milestones/m2.md:2159-2183) asks only for the example pins to be corrected and the runbook clarified, and its Delivery line says X260 put the platform-manifest rule in the runbook and example values. It treats that rule as already in "the release-resolution contract" and does not record the missing spec sentence as open work, while specs/ceph-coverage.md:66-67 says only "A direct digest selects that artifact without resolving or comparing it to a build-pinned tag", so the resolver's intentional index-digest refusal is not stated in the owning spec.

**Evidence.** Spec 66-67: 'A direct digest selects that artifact without resolving or comparing it to a build-pinned tag.' Code 718: 'require(authored is None or authored == child, "image-digest-mismatch")'. image.go:121 remedy: 'select the digest of the intended linux/amd64 manifest'. m2.md B1004: 'requires an authored digest to identify the selected platform manifest. The existing resolver refuses those selections as `image-digest-mismatch`.' Spec: `specs/ceph-coverage.md:66-67`, `specs/api/ceph.md:236-239`, `specs/milestones/m2.md:2161-2165`. Code: `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_registry_discovery.py:715-718`, `internal/storage/ceph/image.go:121`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/plugins/module_utils/test_ceph_registry_discovery.py:654-675`.

**Impact.** An operator who copies the top-level digest from `skopeo inspect` (an index digest) gets image-digest-mismatch, and no owning spec sentence explains the refusal. B1004 depends on a contract clause that is not written down.

**Counterevidence.** The refusal is intentional, has unit tests and gives a concrete remedy. The diagnostic text tells the operator what to do. There is no safety consequence.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add one sentence to specs/ceph-coverage.md:66-67: an authored digest must be the linux/amd64 platform manifest's digest, and an image-index digest refuses as image-digest-mismatch. Exit: make docs-check passes, and the sentence is linked from B1004.

#### Observations

- All nine unsupported-combination fixtures run through the production compiler and pin code, kind, name, field, message and remediation; the matrix, catalog, budget and plan tests pass at f8b15669f.
- Every P0-P7 example matches the OD21 (b) RAM total, and its vCPU and root+data cells match the authored provider profiles.
- No version-number conditionals appear in internal/storage or the Ceph module_utils; release differences go through selection variants such as `ceph.call-home-model`, consistent with D162.
- Erasure-coded realization is enforced end to end: host count per chunk at admission, the `osd tree` host proof at apply, clay, lrc, shec and non-reed_sol_van techniques refused, a non-default CRUSH root and a non-host failure domain refused at planning.
- Stretch arbiter isolation is enforced at admission, and `disable_stretch_mode` is guarded by Python and Go tests. Stretch readiness requires every osdmap pool, derived pools included, at size 4 and min_size 2.
- The host ceiling is computed from the deadline formula: 11 hosts, or 7 stretched, under the 6 h run ceiling; B79 and B890 track larger clusters.
- Image resolution is frozen and reused rather than resolved again ([internal/storage/ceph/image_test.go:61](../../internal/storage/ceph/image_test.go), [:114](../../internal/storage/ceph/image_test.go)). The registry delivery hop is tested credential-free, including on retry, and the guest pull proof checks linux/amd64 and the exact repo digest.
- Manager-to-host tunnels pin `StrictHostKeyChecking yes` with no DNS or agent fallback; the live wrong-key manager test remains B472, B79 and B80 promotion evidence.
- Admission accepts OSD filters and all-device selectors that planning later refuses; B475 tracks selectors and ceph.md records them as unsupported.

#### Limits

The registry resolution, TLS, retry and duplicate-member clauses of [specs/ceph-coverage.md:50-89](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md) were spot-checked only, because the frozen-release lane owns them. Live operator clauses cannot be verified from source: wrong-key manager SSH, HA client continuity, degraded stretch transitions, the physical rows and the measured budgets. The per-family service depth of the RGW, NFS, SMB, NVMe-oF and observability rows was left to those pages' lanes. The physical_ceph test files and the knowledge pages on IBM version constraints were not read in full. The stretch sizing of RGW-derived zone pools was confirmed only through the readiness check, and the per-guest OD21 arithmetic of each example was not recomputed by hand. The CPC-01 planning refusal was established by reading the code, not by running a plan, because planning needs a context and no probe test could be added inside the repository. The destroy and fresh-apply rule for completed Ceph clusters ([specs/ceph-coverage.md:145](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)) belongs to the reconciliation lane and was not traced here. Except for the decisive matrix, catalog and budget tests, every verdict comes from reading source and tests at f8b15669f.

What remains is dormant harness code.
- CPC-09, "ceph-coverage says M2 supports every native-accepted cluster size with no Not yet met pointer, while code refuses above 11 hosts (7 stretch)": the page qualifies its own claim ("The cluster-size, capacity and other refusals the storage pages state stay in force", [specs/ceph-coverage.md:114-115](../../specs/ceph-coverage.md)), and the owning budget section carries the Not yet met line for B79 ([specs/ceph.md:952-966](../../specs/ceph.md)), so repeating it on the coverage page would duplicate a fact.

### Group: Add-ons

### ADD: Add-on trust boundary, built-in packages and selection, package listing, instances and blocks, the cluster object program, ownership receipts, the cluster object adapter, OLM installation, readiness, owned Secrets, observation and continuation, retirement, GitOps handoff evidence and bootstrap object, refusals; add-on coverage and acceptance profiles

Lane `addons`. Spec range: `specs/add-ons.md` lines 1-569; `specs/add-on-coverage.md` lines 1-465. Register: 397 clauses. Rounds: 3. Candidates: 16; confirmed: 13; tracked: 2; refuted: 1.

#### Assessment

Assessment. The lane holds up well against its specifications. The trust boundary, package selection and namespace exclusivity, the frozen-request guards that run before any runner call, retirement from the frozen request, the ownership mark, field manager and clock-skew rule (identical in Go and Python), Secret handling and the refusal table all matched the code, and every test the spec names exists at the baseline. The prior add-ons audit (002) is remediated in the tree. The discrepancies cluster in one place: the Python cluster object engine's handling of OLM and observation edge cases, and the content of the evidence it records. One High defect follows from that: a pending upgrade InstallPlan makes an exact-policy apply refuse and makes an observation of a healthy instance read unknown (ADD-01). Three Medium items are the recorded maximum OpenShift version (always empty), the missing retry on a placed Secret, and an untested placement-type refusal. Nine Low items are diagnostic wording, evidence completeness and a stale version literal in the spec. The coverage page's absent cert-manager and GitLab packages are accurately tracked (B767, B93), so about 30 of its clauses are not met by design. Most acceptance-profile and native-fact clauses (operator gates, live-run facts) cannot be verified from source and are marked unverifiable in the ledger. Findings are bounded by that ledger.
