#### ADD-01

**High, defect.** A pending upgrade InstallPlan makes an exact-policy apply refuse and an observation of a healthy instance read unknown. Re-verified independently with a driver probe: the engine always checks installPlanRef against the pinned CSV on the exact path, so a pending upgrade plan reads unknown with the reason naming the first program object, usually the owned Namespace, and the fresh-apply refusal depends on the plan appearing before the CSV reaches Succeeded.

**Evidence.** The spec says the current CSV "is reported, never compared, and a pending upgrade waits for the operator" ([add-ons.md:341-343](../../specs/add-ons.md)). Observation is unknown only for "a foreign object, a failed read or an installed CSV other than the expected one" ([add-ons.md:444-449](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The same section also says "any other plan fails the attempt naming its CSVs" ([add-ons.md:334-336](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The repository's own knowledge records that "a newer channel head creates another InstallPlan that waits in RequiresApproval" and that "installPlanRef points at the pending plan while the installed operator is healthy" ([olm-v0-exact-install.md:35-40](../../.agents/knowledge/olm-v0-exact-install.md), [olm-v0-exact-install.md:71-75](../../.agents/knowledge/olm-v0-exact-install.md)). In the engine, the exact policy and a dependent Subscription take `plan_name = (live.get("status", {}).get("installPlanRef") or {}).get("name", "")` and then `approved = self.plan(obj, live, csv, plan_name, observe) if plan_name else None` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:265-271](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). `plan()` requires `spec.clusterServiceVersionNames == [csv]`; otherwise, when observing, it sets `self.unknown = True`, and when applying it raises `Refused(... " approval proof differs; CSVs " ...)` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:352-375](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). `execute()` then writes `readings[0]["ownership"] = "unknown"` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:454-458](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). Only the operator-managed branch has `installed_plan()` to recover the plan that installed the CSV ([cluster_objects_engine.py:321-338](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). The `upgradePending` fact is computed ([cluster_objects_engine.py:281-282](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)) but the exact path cannot reach it when `installPlanRef` names an upgrade plan. A probe that drives the engine with installedCSV `pkg.v1`, currentCSV `pkg.v2` and `installPlanRef` naming a plan that lists `pkg.v2` prints `unknown` for the observation, with the Subscription marked ownership `unknown`, and `apply` raises `InstallPlan/ns/install-upgrade approval proof differs; CSVs pkg.v2`. The unit tests that name `installPlanRef` use same-CSV plans only ([test_cluster_objects.py:275](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py), [test_cluster_objects_fdf.py:86](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects_fdf.py), [test_cluster_objects_programs.py:30](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects_programs.py)).

**Impact.** Once the catalog moves ahead of the declared CSV, a correctly installed operator on a qualified package such as nmstate or metallb is classified unknown by `diff --observe`, by the resolution of an interrupted attempt and by the B1125 interruption drills. That unknown carries the remedy "destroy and apply again" and the reason "Subscription ... is foreign or could not be read", which is wrong. The dependent engine Subscription of the ACM hub takes the same branch. A fresh apply can also refuse if OLM generates the upgrade plan after `installedCSV` is set and before the CSV check passes.

**Counterevidence.** No upgrade is ever approved, so the failure is safe. The observation and continuation half is certain once a catalog moves. The fresh-apply half is narrower: OLM creates the upgrade plan only after `installedCSV` is set, and the loop may still be waiting for `Succeeded` at that moment, so that race is plausible but unproven. A run with startingCSV equal to the channel head on a catalog that does not move passes, which may be why B755 and X302 did not see it. Nothing protects a pinned older CSV or a later observation. The spec is also internally uneven: "any other plan fails the attempt" (334-336) reads against "a pending upgrade waits for the operator" (342-343). [add-on-coverage.md:389-395](../../specs/add-on-coverage.md) supports the continuation requirement only; it does not mention pending plans.

**Correction and exit evidence.** When `status.installedCSV` equals the expected CSV, find the plan that installed it among the InstallPlans the Subscription owns, as `installed_plan()` does for the operator-managed policy. Treat a plan whose CSV list differs as the pending upgrade: report it, never approve it and never fail on it. Keep the refusal only for a plan that would install the first CSV with extra CSVs. Clarify [add-ons.md:334-336](../../specs/add-ons.md) in the same change so that a pending upgrade plan of an already installed CSV is reported and does not fail the attempt. Exit: a unit test in `tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py` where installedCSV equals startingCSV, currentCSV is newer and `installPlanRef` names an unapproved upgrade plan; observe classifies the instance completed with `upgradePending` true, apply returns unchanged with no approve write, and the dependent variant behaves the same.

#### ADD-03

**Medium, defect.** maxOpenShiftVersion is read from a CSV annotation key that does not exist, so the evidence never records it.

**Evidence.** The spec says the evidence records "any maximum OpenShift version the CSV declares" ([add-ons.md:343-346](../../specs/add-ons.md)) and that a bundle's `olm.maxOpenShiftVersion` "is recorded in the instance's evidence and the acceptance row" ([add-on-coverage.md:29-32](../../specs/add-on-coverage.md)); the value grammar and bound are at [add-ons.md:399-405](../../specs/add-ons.md). The spec does not name the annotation key. The repository's knowledge states that "A CSV annotation `olm.properties` with `olm.maxOpenShiftVersion`" blocks a cluster update ([olm-v0-exact-install.md:173-176](../../.agents/knowledge/olm-v0-exact-install.md)), and the same knowledge pages record that ACM, Data Foundation and GitLab bundles declare one. The CSV projection adds only `metadata["annotations"]["olm.maxOpenShiftVersion"] = True` ([cluster_objects_native.py:44-47](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py)) and the engine reads `csv.get("metadata", {}).get("annotations", {}).get("olm.maxOpenShiftVersion", "")`, emitting `""` when it is absent ([cluster_objects_engine.py:392-394](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). `olm.properties` appears nowhere in `ansible/`, `internal/` or `cmd/`. No Python unit test mentions the field. The Go golden showing `4.21` ([evidence.golden:57](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/testdata/evidence.golden)) covers only the Go decode of an injected value.

**Impact.** The evidence and the acceptance row lose the one fact that warns an operator that an installed operator blocks the cluster's next minor update. The spec requires a value and the record carries an empty string, silently.

**Counterevidence.** The value is evidence and never a rule, so no install decision is wrong. The Go-side validation of the field is correct for any value that would arrive. The finding rests on the repository's knowledge of OLM's typed-property format and not on a live CSV.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Project `metadata.annotations["olm.properties"]` in the CSV read, parse its JSON list in the module with a guard for malformed JSON and a non-list value, take the value of the entry of type `olm.maxOpenShiftVersion`, and pass it through `native(value, "version")`. Check that an unparsable value maps to `invalid`, which the Go validator rejects. Add one sentence to the knowledge page or the spec naming the `olm.properties` property type. Exit: a unit test in `tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py` where a CSV with `olm.properties` `[{"type":"olm.maxOpenShiftVersion","value":"4.22"}]` yields `maxOpenShiftVersion` `4.22`, and an invalid value yields `invalid`.

#### ADD-11

**Medium, defect.** A placed Secret whose create or post-create read fails transiently fails the attempt at once instead of being retried until the deadline, and the diagnostic reads 'differs at unproved placement'.

**Evidence.** The spec says a failed read is "retried until the deadline before any mutation" and that a create refused "as `InternalError` or `ServiceUnavailable` ... is retried at the next poll until the deadline" ([add-ons.md:286-295](../../specs/add-ons.md)), and that for a placed Secret "the adapter builds the object in memory and creates it as any owned object" ([add-ons.md:411-413](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The retry clauses reach a Secret only through "as any owned object", which is an inference and not an explicit Secret clause. In `place`, a failed private read returns `{"accepted": False, "unknown": True}` ([cluster_objects_secrets.py:67-72](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_secrets.py)); after `oc create` the module ignores the failure reason, re-reads and returns `{"accepted": False, "unknown": live is False}` with no `retryable` member ([cluster_objects_secrets.py:84-94](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_secrets.py)). The engine's `place` has one arm, `if not result.get("accepted"): raise Refused(model.label(obj) + " differs at " + result.get("difference", "unproved placement"))`, and does not read `unknown` or pause ([cluster_objects_engine.py:127-156](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). For an ordinary object the engine re-probes with `wait=True` and calls `self.pause` on a retryable absent create ([cluster_objects_engine.py:116-125](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). `native.create` computes `retryable` from the status reason ([cluster_objects_native.py:155-165](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py)) but refuses a Secret body ([cluster_objects_native.py:143-148](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py)), so `place` has no route to that classification. Existing tests cover native create retries and successful or differing placement only ([test_cluster_objects.py:99](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py), [test_cluster_objects.py:345](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py)).

**Impact.** A transient API failure during a Secret placement (an apiserver restart, a 5xx, a webhook window) fails the apply attempt where the spec's retry rule would keep polling within the budget. The operator repeats apply. The refusal reads `Secret/<ns>/<name> differs at unproved placement`, which suggests a content difference where the cause is a failed call. The same wording covers a failed module-side read before the create.

**Counterevidence.** The engine's probe before `place` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:131](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)) already retries the engine's own initial read, so only the module's two reads or the create itself are exposed. The refused attempt is classified unknown ([cluster_objects_write.py:41-48](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/cluster_objects_write.py)), so repeating apply continues; nothing is lost or corrupted. The object is named, so the "naming the object" clause holds. This is separate from the tracked create-path parsing question (ADD-02): `place` has no reason-based retry path to begin with.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Have `place` return a retryable or unknown flag for an unknown read, and for a create refused with `InternalError` or `ServiceUnavailable` (classified as in `native.create`) whose re-read finds the Secret absent. In the engine's `place`, pause and loop on that flag as `object()` does. Change the absent-after-create diagnostic to `create unproved: absent`. Exit: a unit test in `tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py` where the scripted `oc` fails the first Secret create with a ServiceUnavailable Status and the second succeeds, so the engine places the Secret within the deadline; and an absent result with no transient reason refuses naming `create unproved`.

#### ADD-15

**Medium, test-gap.** No test proves that a Secret placement of a type other than Opaque or kubernetes.io/tls is refused at planning.

**Evidence.** The spec says a placement's "type is `Opaque` or `kubernetes.io/tls`; planning refuses any other namespace or type naming the placement" and "A global pull-secret merge is refused" ([add-ons.md:421-427](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The code enforces it: `if p.Type != "Opaque" && p.Type != "kubernetes.io/tls" { return fail("unsupported type") }` ([validation.go:307-308](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/validation.go)). A search of the Go tests under `internal/addons` and `cmd/bootwright` finds no use of `unsupported type`, `dockerconfigjson` or any placement `Type` other than `Opaque`. `TestProgramRefusesClosedAndDeferredArms` covers the produced-source allowlist ([program_test.go:62-112](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/program_test.go), the placement at 101-111) and the namespace arm is covered in `placement_namespaces_test.go`; the type arm is not. `kubernetes.io/tls` is also never exercised as an accepted type.

**Impact.** A safety-relevant refusal has no regression guard. A change that admits, for example, a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` placement would pass the suite.

**Counterevidence.** The code currently enforces the rule. Packages are reviewed Go code, and the namespace allowlist ([validation.go:304](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/validation.go)) independently blocks a placement into `openshift-config`, so the pull-secret merge case needs a type regression inside an owned or operator namespace to matter. A produced-source placement with a non-Opaque type is refused earlier by the allowlist message ([validation.go:300](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/validation.go)), not by `unsupported type`. Creating an existing `openshift-config/pull-secret` would also meet the foreign-object refusal at runtime.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a case to `program_test.go` that places a mapped-part (Secret and Keys) `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret in an owned namespace and expects `Freeze` to fail with `unsupported type`, and one that accepts `kubernetes.io/tls`. Exit: `./scripts/go test ./internal/addons/clusterobjects/ -run TestProgramRefusesClosedAndDeferredArms` with the new cases.

#### ADD-04

**Low, doc-stale.** The spec still names the cluster object program version cluster-objects-v1 after the program moved to v2.

**Evidence.** The spec says a non-add-on block "freezes the same program section, version `cluster-objects-v1`, in its own request" ([add-ons.md:235](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The constant is `Version = "cluster-objects-v2"` ([types.go:11](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/types.go)), `VERSION = "cluster-objects-v2"` ([cluster_objects_model.py:10](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_model.py)), and the role asserts `cluster_objects_program.version == 'cluster-objects-v2'` ([apply.yml:5](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/roles/cluster_objects/tasks/apply.yml)). The move is recorded: "Add-on and cluster-network receipts carry their ownership basis (`cluster-objects-v2`)" ([delivered.md:8960-8961](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md)). The repository's guidance rule says "A spec names the Go constant of an internal version, never its number" ([guidance.md](../../.claude/rules/guidance.md)). The instance request is correctly named by its constant ([add-ons.md:178](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The M4 planning note "no M4c to M4f slice moves `cluster-objects-v1`" ([m4.md:573-574](../../specs/milestones/m4.md)) is a dated planning record and [delivered.md:8216](../../specs/milestones/delivered.md) is original delivery history.

**Impact.** A reader checking a frozen program against the spec finds the wrong version. No runtime effect.

**Counterevidence.** Only [add-ons.md:235](../../specs/add-ons.md) is live spec text; the milestone records are history.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Replace the literal with the constant `clusterobjects.Version` from `internal/addons/clusterobjects/types.go`. Optionally mark the m4.md sentence as historical. Exit: `make docs-check` passes and `grep -n cluster-objects-v1 specs/add-ons.md` is empty.

#### ADD-05

**Low, gap.** Instance completion evidence does not name the package, the cluster or the provided capabilities.

**Evidence.** The spec says "An instance's completion evidence names its package, cluster and provided capabilities, every owned object by kind, namespace, name and `uid`, the installed CSV and each readiness result" ([add-ons.md:482-485](../../specs/add-ons.md)), with no qualifier. The Go `Evidence` holds `Receipts`, `OLM`, `Dependents`, `Checks` and `Observations` ([evidence.go:89-95](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/evidence.go)); the driver wrapper adds `Absent`, `Classification`, `Postcondition`, `Request`, `Retired` and `Version` ([evidence.go:10-18](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/driver/evidence.go)); the adapter's completion adds only the request digest and the version ([cluster_objects_protocol.py:15](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/action/cluster_objects_protocol.py)). The cluster object `Program` is `Version`, `Steps` and `Checks` ([types.go:126-130](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/types.go)) and carries no provided capabilities.

**Impact.** A GitOps author building the exclusion list from evidence has to join it with the request to learn the package and cluster, and cannot learn the provided capabilities from the record at all. [project.md:79](../../specs/project.md) points to this section for the exclusion list.

**Counterevidence.** The owned-object identities, the CSV and the readiness results that an exclusion list needs are present. The request digest binds the evidence to a request, but it is a hash, so recovering the package and cluster needs the stored request.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Either add package, cluster and provided capabilities to the evidence (an evidence version move), or narrow the spec to say they come from the frozen request that the evidence digest names. Exit: an evidence golden showing the members, or a spec edit that `make docs-check` accepts.

#### ADD-06

**Low, gap.** Operator-managed namespace evidence lists later plans without the catalog they resolved from.

**Evidence.** The spec says "An operator-managed package also records the catalog of each later plan it approves, from the plan's `bundleLookups`" ([add-ons.md:346-348](../../specs/add-ons.md)). `operator_facts` lists InstallPlans with only `["spec.clusterServiceVersionNames", "spec.approved"]` and each entry holds name, csvs and approved ([cluster_objects_engine.py:339-351](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)); `OperatorPlan` is `Name`, `CSVs`, `Approved` ([evidence.go:55-59](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/evidence.go)). The first plan's catalog and bundle image are recorded through `olm_facts` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:386-397](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). No catalog is recorded for any later plan.

**Impact.** The evidence cannot show which catalog supplied the plans that the odf-operator approves for its dependencies, the supply-chain fact the clause asks to keep.

**Counterevidence.** The list is evidence only and decides nothing. The clause is ambiguous: Bootwright approves no later plan ([add-ons.md:358-361](../../specs/add-ons.md)), so "it approves" can only mean the package's operator, as the coverage row says ([add-on-coverage.md:45](../../specs/add-on-coverage.md)). The requirement at [add-ons.md:362-363](../../specs/add-ons.md) to list each plan and CSV is met.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Project `status.bundleLookups[].catalogSourceRef` for the listed plans and add a bounded catalog member to `OperatorPlan` (an evidence version move), or reword the clause to name the operator as the approver and drop the catalog. Exit: extend `test_operator_managed_namespace_evidence_is_bounded_and_sorted` to assert each plan's catalog.

#### ADD-07

**Low, defect.** A declared failure condition's diagnostic omits the condition type.

**Evidence.** The spec says "a declared failure condition fails the check at once, naming the object, condition and reason" ([add-ons.md:387](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The model returns `False, False, "failure condition " + native(item.get("reason", "")), True` ([cluster_objects_model.py:178-182](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_model.py)) and the engine raises `Refused(model.label(value) + " " + last)` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:177-178](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). The message names the object and the reason, not the condition type. The network block declares two failure conditions on one check, `Degraded` with no reason filter and `Ignored` with reason `NoMatchingNode` ([render.go:45](../../internal/containercluster/networking/render.go)). The unit test sets `failOn` `Degraded=True` and asserts only the failure flag ([test_cluster_objects.py:171-176](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py)).

**Impact.** With two declared failure conditions and an empty or shared reason, the operator cannot tell which one failed the attempt; a `Degraded` condition with no reason yields a message ending in `failure condition `.

**Counterevidence.** The object and the reason are named.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Include the matched condition type (and status) in the last observation, for example `failure condition Degraded=True reason Failed`. Exit: `test_lagging_condition_and_failure` asserts the message names the condition type.

#### ADD-08

**Low, defect.** An observation's engine-level unknown is pinned on the first program object (the owned Namespace), so the diagnostic and additive remedy name the wrong object.

**Evidence.** The spec classifies "a foreign object, a failed read or an installed CSV other than the expected one" as unknown, with the remedy to destroy and apply again or, for an additive instance, "to remove or correct the object and repeat `apply`" ([add-ons.md:446-452](../../specs/add-ons.md)); a failed read of a check is unknown in observation ([add-ons.md:392-393](../../specs/add-ons.md)). Several engine causes only set `self.unknown`: a failed read in `probe()` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:56-60](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)), a dependent Subscription that is `differing or older` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:226-233](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)), a differing primary Subscription and ResolutionFailed ([cluster_objects_engine.py:247-263](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)), and the CSV, first-plan, plan and operator-fact reads at 189-190, 312, 343-344, 355-356 and 372-374. `execute()` then rewrites the first recorded observation: `if self.unknown and readings: readings[0]["ownership"] = "unknown"; readings[0]["equal"] = False` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:454-458](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). For an OLM add-on the first object is the Namespace, added first by the operator prelude ([render.go:151-157](../../internal/addons/instance/render.go)). The Go side returns the first Unknown or Foreign observation as `<Kind>/<ns>/<name> is foreign or could not be read` ([unresolved.go:80-84](../../internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go)), and for an additive instance the remedy skips the block's own id in `declaredBy` and returns `removeUnowned`, "remove or correct the object on the cluster if no add-on of this context owns it" ([unresolved.go:12-39](../../internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go)). The overwrite also misattributes a genuine unknown read of a later object, because the first reading is the one Go reports.

**Impact.** For an add-on whose dependent Subscription drifted or whose readiness read failed, the operator reads that the instance's own Namespace is foreign or unreadable, although it reads fine. The real cause (which dependent, check or plan) appears nowhere in the evidence. On an additive instance the remedy text points at removing or correcting that Namespace.

**Counterevidence.** The classification itself is right, and the Go evidence evaluation agrees. The remedy is hedged with "if no add-on of this context owns it", and this instance owns the Namespace, so deletion is unlikely. The non-additive remedy, destroy and apply, is unaffected. The spec states no explicit obligation that an engine-level unknown name its own cause; the phrase "the observation records which object differs" ([add-ons.md:451-454](../../specs/add-ons.md)) concerns an own object that differs from its declared body. The defect is therefore against the remedy clause's presumption that "the object" is the offender, which is why it is rated Low. No unit test pins which observation carries an engine-level unknown.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Record the cause of an engine-level unknown as its own evidence entry, for example a check result with `unknown=true` or a dependent fact with a reason naming the Subscription and field, instead of overwriting `readings[0]`; have `unresolved()` name that entry and keep the object observations truthful. If a named cause is wanted as a contract, add that sentence to the Observation section. Exit: a unit test of `Engine.execute(observe=True)` with a differing dependent Subscription and one with a failed check read, asserting that the Namespace observation stays own and equal and that the cause names the Subscription or check; and a Go test that `UnresolvedAdded` names the dependent, not the Namespace.

#### ADD-10

**Low, defect.** A condition is flagged stale whenever any sibling condition transitioned later, not only when it is unchanged 'long after' them.

**Evidence.** The spec says "A condition unchanged long after its object's other conditions is reported as stale and never decides" ([add-ons.md:393-394](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The model sets `stale = bool(item.get("lastTransitionTime") and changes and item["lastTransitionTime"] < max(changes))` ([cluster_objects_model.py:185-188](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_model.py)), with no threshold; `ready` does not use it, so the "never decides" half holds. The engine copies the flag into the check result ([cluster_objects_engine.py:172-179](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)) and the deadline diagnostic prints only `check %d: <lastObservation>` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:202-208](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). The Go side stores `Stale bool` ([evidence.go:79](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/evidence.go)) but no code reads it, so it reaches no operator output. The unit test checks only elements 0 and 3 of the condition result ([test_cluster_objects.py:174-176](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py)); nothing tests the stale value.

**Impact.** On a healthy object nearly every condition that is not the most recent transition is recorded stale (an `Available True` set before a later `Progressing` change, for example). The flag is noise and cannot show that a condition is genuinely stuck.

**Counterevidence.** Staleness never decides readiness, so no outcome is wrong. Comparing timestamps as strings works for RFC 3339 in UTC. The spec names no threshold for "long after", so the clause is vague as well as the code lax. The spec does not require stale in the deadline diagnostic, which names "each unmet check and its last observation" ([add-ons.md:395-396](../../specs/add-ons.md)).

**Correction and exit evidence.** Apply a documented threshold (for example more than the readiness poll window or a fixed interval older than the newest sibling transition) and name it in the spec, or reword the clause to "older than another condition's transition". Exit: a unit test of `model.condition` with two conditions a few seconds apart asserting stale is false, and one with a gap past the threshold asserting true.

#### ADD-12

**Low, defect.** csvSucceeded reports last observation 'Succeeded' for an installed CSV that is still Installing or Failed.

**Evidence.** The spec says a failed attempt names "each unmet check and its last observation" ([add-ons.md:395-396](../../specs/add-ons.md)), and `csvSucceeded` holds when the installed CSV "reports `Succeeded`" ([add-ons.md:386](../../specs/add-ons.md)); last observations are bounded native strings ([add-ons.md:399-405](../../specs/add-ons.md)). The CSV check returns `bool(csv and csv.get("status", {}).get("phase") == "Succeeded"), "Succeeded" if csv else "pending"` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:181-195](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). The second value depends only on whether the CSV was read, not on its phase. `check()` passes it through as `lastObservation` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:160-162](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)), `checks()` joins `"check %d: %s"` for every unsatisfied result ([cluster_objects_engine.py:197-208](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)), and `pause()` raises `Refused("deadline reached: " + description)` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:40-43](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). A CSV stuck in Installing or Failed yields `deadline reached: check 0: Succeeded`. The sibling `statusPhase` arm records the observed phase through `model.native(phase)` ([cluster_objects_engine.py:176](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). No unit test covers a CSV in a phase other than Succeeded.

**Impact.** The timeout diagnostic and the observation evidence state the opposite of what was observed. The operator must read the cluster to learn the real phase.

**Counterevidence.** The readiness decision is correct: `satisfied` is false unless the phase is Succeeded, so there is no false success.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Return the observed phase as the last observation when the CSV is present, sanitized with `phase if isinstance(phase, str) and phase else "pending"` and passed through `model.native`, because `native()` returns `invalid` for a non-string. When the CSV probe itself is unknown, `unknown` is more precise than `pending`. Exit: a unit test where the CSV phase is `Installing` until the deadline; the Refused message contains `Installing` and not `Succeeded`, and an observation records `lastObservation` `Installing`.

#### ADD-13

**Low, defect.** Operator-managed evidence silently keeps only the first 16 InstallPlans and CSVs of the namespace, though the spec says it lists each.

**Evidence.** The spec says "The evidence lists each InstallPlan and CSV of the namespace, as evidence and never as a rule" ([add-ons.md:362-363](../../specs/add-ons.md)). `operator_facts` slices `[:16]` on each plan's `clusterServiceVersionNames`, on the plans and on the CSVs, with no truncation marker ([cluster_objects_engine.py:340-350](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). `listed()` sorts items by `metadata.name` before the slice, so the kept entries are the first 16 by name ([cluster_objects_engine.py:288-292](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_engine.py)). The Go validator refuses more than 16 plans or CSVs and more than 16 CSVs per plan ([evidence_validation.go:31-35](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/evidence_validation.go)). The only bound the spec states nearby is the 16 MiB output limit ([add-ons.md:240](../../specs/add-ons.md)); it states no list-length bound. A unit test pins the cap and the sort with 20 plans and 20 CSVs ([test_cluster_objects.py:296-307](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py)) but asserts no marker.

**Impact.** In `openshift-storage`, the odf-operator can create many dependent plans and CSVs over upgrades. InstallPlan names are random, so the kept 16 ignore age, and the handoff evidence can omit plans or CSVs that a GitOps source should exclude, with nothing saying the list was cut. That the cap is reached in practice was not observed.

**Counterevidence.** The lists are evidence only and decide nothing. The cap is a deliberate bound, and the validator is a second line of defence that the engine's own output never trips.

**Correction and exit evidence.** State the 16-entry bound in the OLM installation section and record a truncation count or flag in the evidence (an evidence version move), or raise the bound to cover the namespace. Exit: a unit test with 20 plans where the evidence carries 16 entries plus a truncation marker, and the spec states the bound.

#### ADD-14

**Low, test-gap.** The kubevirt package has no fake-cluster journey, and content safety is not tested at the largest admitted configuration.

**Evidence.** The spec requires every built-in package to pass, before it is offered, "a fake-cluster journey (fresh apply, continuation `unchanged`, unknown resolved by observation, a foreign object refused, a plan of another CSV never approved, retirement contacting nothing)" ([add-ons.md:121-138](../../specs/add-ons.md), repeated at [add-on-coverage.md:382-388](../../specs/add-on-coverage.md)). The full-program Python journeys are parametrized over `['nmstate', 'metallb', 'network']` ([test_cluster_objects_programs.py:85](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects_programs.py)), the failure-injection test uses the same three, and the fixtures directory holds `metallb.json`, `network.json` and `nmstate.json`. A search for `HyperConverged` and `hco-operatorhub` finds only the Go render and registry tests ([kubevirt_test.go:13-94](../../internal/addons/packages/kubevirt_test.go)). The Go journey builds a synthetic package `Package{Name: "fixture", ...}` ([addon_journey_test.go:136-216](../../internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/addon_journey_test.go)). B883's exit evidence lists "registry conformance, purity, content safety, render and plan goldens" and leaves out the journey ([m4.md:1891-1895](../../specs/milestones/m4.md)); other packages' items name it.

**Impact.** The kubevirt program (an empty HyperConverged behind its CRD gate and per-namespace access objects) has never run through the engine against a fake `oc`. The omission is an untracked exemption from the qualification rule.

**Counterevidence.** The engine and its journey arms are generic and proved by the nmstate, metallb, network, fdf and hub tests, and the operator gate covers the live path. Content safety at the largest admitted metallb configuration is tested: the `metallb-maximum` golden renders 16 pools of 16 entries (33 objects) and freezes it through `co.Freeze`, which enforces the 64-object, 96-step and request bounds ([golden_test.go:178-222](../../internal/addons/packages/golden_test.go)). Only the pure-program helper uses a single pool ([registry_test.go:113-127](../../internal/addons/packages/registry_test.go)), and no assertion by name for the maximal render checks content safety beyond what `Freeze` enforces.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add a kubevirt fixture to the parametrized journeys in `test_cluster_objects_programs.py`, and align B883's exit evidence with the qualification list (or record the exemption). Optionally assert the content-safety checks (no Secret, reserved key, status, template delimiter) on the maximal metallb render. Exit: the parametrized journey includes `kubevirt`.

#### ADD-02

**Medium, defect.** The webhook-window retry never fires because the create status reason is parsed as a JSON Status from oc's text error output. Re-judged from tracked: specs/add-on-coverage.md:409-410 only lists "how `oc create` exposes a webhook refusal's status reason" among the facts the first run should re-verify. It does not say the retry is broken or accept that it is. The open item it would fall under, B1125 (specs/milestones/m4.md:2006-2013), names every fact that rehearsal re-verifies but leaves this one out. So no open item or Not yet met line covers the fact that cluster_objects_native.py:157-166 parses oc's text error output as a JSON Status, which makes retryable always False and breaks the webhook-window retry required at m4.md:1612-1617.

**Evidence.** Spec: 'a refusal the API classified, by its status reason and never its message, as `InternalError` or `ServiceUnavailable`, as when an admission webhook is not yet serving, is retried at the next poll until the deadline' (add-ons.md:292-295). Code: `status = json.loads(text)` and `if status.get("kind") == "Status": reason = status.get("reason", "")`, then `retryable: reason in ("InternalError", "ServiceUnavailable")` (native.py:159-166). The only test scripts oc to emit a JSON Status document: `response({"kind": "Status", "reason": reason}, code=1)` (test_cluster_objects.py:101). Probe: a fake oc that prints `Error from server (InternalError): error when creating "STDIN": ... failed calling webhook` to stderr yields `{'accepted': False, 'retryable': False}`. Spec: `specs/add-ons.md:290-295`, `specs/add-on-coverage.md:409-410`, `specs/milestones/m4.md:1612-1617`. Code: `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py:157-166`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py:99-109`.

**Impact.** A create refused because a webhook is still starting (MetalLB pools, a GitLab resource, a hub's MultiClusterHub) is re-read, found absent and fails the attempt with 'create unproved: absent'. The specified in-attempt retry is lost, and the operator has to repeat apply.

**Counterevidence.** Repeating apply continues: the object is absent, so it is created. 'How `oc create` exposes a webhook refusal's status reason' is listed as an unverified native fact (add-on-coverage.md:409-410), so the format is acknowledged as unknown. This finding says the code handles only one of the plausible formats, the one oc does not print by default.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Run the create with an output that exposes the API Status (for example a raw REST request, or -o json, whose error path is then verified), or read the reason from the structured text form 'Error from server (`<Reason>`)'. Record the verified form in knowledge when B1125 meets it. Exit: A unit test whose scripted oc prints the real text error for InternalError and ServiceUnavailable and expects a retry, plus the B1125 rehearsal recording the observed format.

#### ADD-09

**Low, drift.** The cluster object reader treats oc's 'server doesn't have a resource type' error as absence, which the spec does not admit. Re-judged from tracked: B1122 is not open work: specs/milestones/delivered.md:11735 lists it as "completed", and commit 3e08c7507 ("read an object of a type the cluster does not serve as absent") is the change that moved the code on purpose, with no open item, Not-yet-met line or decision admitting the discrepancy. specs/add-ons.md:286-288 still says "only the API's not-found answer is absence, and every other failed read is unknown", so the spec is stale against code that was changed deliberately, which makes this a confirmed drift.

**Evidence.** Spec 286: "only the API's not-found answer is absence, and every other failed read is unknown". Code 15: `UNSERVED_TYPE = re.compile(r'error: the server doesn\'t have a resource type ...')`; 130-131: `if code and not listing and UNSERVED_TYPE.fullmatch(error.strip()): return {"answered": True, "object": None}`. The unit test at 180-183 (`test_an_unserved_type_reads_as_absent_and_no_other_refusal_does`) shows the behavior is intentional. A grep for 'resource type|unserved' over specs/ and .agents/knowledge found no record. Spec: `specs/add-ons.md:286-288`, `specs/add-ons.md:446-448`. Code: `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py:14-15`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_native.py:130-131`, `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/tests/unit/test_cluster_objects.py:180-183`.

**Impact.** In an observation, an owned operand whose type discovery no longer serves reads as absent, not unknown, so the instance can classify as partial or noEffect where the spec's rule gives unknown. The practical risk is small, because deleting a CRD deletes its objects. The spec states a stricter rule than the adapter implements, though.

**Counterevidence.** The match is a fullmatch of the whole stderr, so partial-discovery warnings (extra lines) still read as unknown, as the test at line 181 proves. oc runs with HOME=/nonexistent, so no stale discovery cache persists. Gates on the CRD being Established keep apply from creating an object of an unserved type.

**Correction and exit evidence.** Add one sentence to specs/add-ons.md step 1 admitting an unserved resource type as absence (no object of it can exist), with its rationale, or record it as a knowledge fact the spec links. Otherwise drop the rule in observation mode. Exit: make docs-check after the spec line is added; the existing unit test stays green.

#### Observations

- Audit 002 is remediated in the tree. F03 (whole-second timeout and wrapped render errors, X228), F04 (placementNamespaces frozen in the request, X229), F05, F07 and F19 (no name-keyed generic code, X230), F08 and F02 (add-ons info and the guide, X227), F09 (defaults never select, X231), F13 and F18 (parity and budget tests exist), F01 (additive apply, X234) and F12 (authored OLM, X235) all match the current code.
- Every test the add-ons spec names exists at the baseline: TestAddOnRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported, TestPackageTimeoutAdmission, TestSchemaMaximalPackagesCompileDecodePlanAndCoverEveryMember, TestPackageTimeoutDefaultsEqualTheirBudgets, TestBuiltinPackageRequestGoldens and TestBuiltinPackageCoverageRowsMatchTheRegistry.
- The ownership mark agrees byte for byte between Go ([program.go:79-91](../../internal/addons/clusterobjects/program.go)) and Python ([cluster_objects_model.py:28-60](../../ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/cluster_objects_model.py)); the clock skew is held at `types.go:18` and `evidence.go:125` on the Go side and in `ownership()` on the Python side, and the field manager is built in `cluster_objects_engine.py` `place()` as `bootwright-` plus the first 32 characters of the mark.
- The Go side re-derives realization from evidence (`EvaluateEvidence`) instead of trusting the module's classification, a sound defense in depth. It sets `CSVObservation.ReadKnown` true unconditionally, so an unknown CSV read reaches Go only through the engine's `readings[0]` rewrite, which is why ADD-08 matters.
- Secret values never leave the write module: reads project key names, non-secret values are compared inside the go-template, and creation output is `-o name`.
- In observation, every failed read in the engine sets `self.unknown` through `probe()`, so a failed gate, CSV or check read classifies the instance unknown, as the spec requires.
- Authored custom resources cannot name a core or built-in API group: admission refuses them before `kindBoundChecks` derives a group.
- The frozen-request guards on apply and observe (registry namespace mismatch, authored name that shadows a package, authored program reaching outside its namespace) run in `Capability.run` before any runner call and are each proved by a test; retirement is exempt.
- An additive apply that would change an existing last package's dependencies refuses through the generic "would freeze the block differently" delta.
- The audit 002 F14 suggestion to drop `--context` from the add-ons group help was not applied; every group help lists the common flags, so it is not reported.
- JSON and text forms of `add-ons info` carry the same facts, and the skeleton test covers every registered package.

#### Limits

No new in-tree tests were written and no Go or ansible-check suites were run. Two Python probes ran the shipped module_utils against scripted reads from the scratch directory. The real `oc` error format (ADD-02) and OLM's placement of `maxOpenShiftVersion` (ADD-03) come from tool knowledge and the repository's knowledge pages, not from a live cluster. The lifecycle internals were taken from delivered records and test names rather than read in full: additive admission (settleApply), lineage removal and the `diff --observe` presentation. These clauses, owned by other lanes, were not traced: the cluster network block's nmstate requirement, the CephConsumer removal refusal and Environment marker handling. Acceptance profiles and native-fact clauses cannot be verified from source, and most parked Left-out items were not opened individually. Round 2 examined only the critic's targets; package phase gate ordering was checked only for metallb (metallb.go:27-29), and whether a differing dependent should be partial rather than unknown is a spec question left open, with Go and engine behavior consistent with each other. Round 3 examined only the critic's targets and ran no probes; two points rest on reading, namely whether the JSON-patch test of `/status/bundleLookups` matches the server's value exactly, and whether a CSV list of 16 or more occurs in practice. A request just over the instance request bound would be caught by reconciliation's plan-level check rather than the oversized row, which was judged too narrow to report.

#### Refuted candidates

- The instance removal description and its empty impacts have no golden or test: refuted, because `internal/addons/instance/capability_test.go:146-148` calls `capability.Removal` and fails unless there are no impacts and the description contains "stay on a cluster", and the contract test compares the removal with the destroy plan; only a full-string golden is absent, and the spec's table row does not require the word "unmanaged".

## 7. Method and verification record

### The audit request

Date: 2026-11-05. Repository: `bootwright` at commit `f8b15669f` on `main`,
clean tree. Requested by the repository owner: "perform a full audit of code
considering specs; divide validation in sub tasks and use the best fitting
model/effort for each of them". Deliverable: this report and its navigation
page under `audits/003-code/`; no other repository change, no product code,
contract, milestone or spec change, and no command with effects.

### Division into lanes

The specification corpus (29,734 lines over 33 pages) was divided into 36
lanes. Each lane pairs one spec page, or one contiguous range of a page, with
the Go packages, Ansible roles, playbooks, action plugins and tests that own
its clauses, found through the six steps of
[Finding code](../../specs/architecture.md#finding-code). Lanes were sized so
that one reviewer could read the whole spec range and open the owning code in
one pass; the three largest pages (state reconciliation, Ceph, managed OS)
were split at their section boundaries.

| Group | Lanes |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | api-grammar, api-environment-secrets, api-machines, api-openshift, api-ceph, api-addons, cli-parsing, cli-journeys, cli-output, project-glossary, architecture, security |
| 2 | controller-host, controller-stage, contexts, secrets, reconciliation-core, reconciliation-plan, reconciliation-diff, reconciliation-safety, infra-services, substrates-virtual, substrates-physical, addons |

### Sub-tasks and their models

Every sub-task was classified before it ran and given an explicit model and
reasoning effort, following the owner's routing rule: a cheaper model only
where it produces the same result as a stronger one; Opus for finding,
verification and synthesis; Fable only for arbitration between disagreeing
agents.

| Sub-task | What it does | Model | Effort | Count per lane |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clause register | Copies every normative clause of a 200-line spec chunk verbatim with its line and heading, and lists the Not yet met lines | Haiku | low | one per 200 spec lines |
| Finder | Reads the lane's spec range in full, locates the enforcing code and tests for each clause, reports discrepancies with citations, fills a per-section ledger | Opus | medium | one per round, up to three rounds |
| Reproduce lens | Confirms the code side of one finding in its own git worktree, running an effect-free probe where one decides it | Sonnet | high | one per finding |
| Spec-reading lens | Confirms the spec side of one finding in its owning section, and searches milestones, decisions and prior audits for existing tracking | Sonnet | high | one per finding |
| Refuter lens | Tries to refute one finding from both sides, then calibrates severity and kind | Opus | medium | one per finding |
| Arbiter | Decides a split verdict after re-reading the decisive citations | Fable | medium | one per split |
| Completeness critic | Compares the ledger with the register, spot-checks met verdicts, names the next round's targets | Opus | medium | one per round except the last |
| Lane writer | Writes the lane's section of this report from the verified data | Sonnet | high | one |
| Cross-lane synthesis and citation check | Merges duplicates across lanes, orders by severity, checks every citation of the assembled report against the baseline | Opus / Sonnet | medium / high | once |

A finding is confirmed when the three lenses agree it is real, or when the
arbiter decides so after a split; it is refuted when the three agree it is
not. Each lens defaults to "not real" when its evidence is inconclusive, so
the catalog errs toward omission. The final severity of a confirmed finding
is the lowest the real-voting lenses assigned, unless an arbiter decided it.
A confirmed discrepancy that a milestone item, a Not yet met line, a decision
or an open audit remediation item already records is listed as tracked, not
as a new finding, unless the record itself is wrong.

### Rules every worker ran under

Read-only on the repository, no git write command, no `examples/wip`. No
`ansible-playbook` and no Bootwright command with effects or that reveals a
secret; allowed probes were reading, grep, single-package `./scripts/go test`
with `-run`, `./scripts/go vet` on one package, `--help`, and `validate` or
`render` over a copy of an example. Every citation names a path and line at
the baseline commit and quotes the decisive words.

### Severity scale

Blocking: on a qualified path the code can destroy data or hosts outside its
ownership, bypasses a safety refusal or confirmation the spec requires,
exposes secret material, or leaves durable state the spec says is impossible.
High: a specified behavior is missing or wrong with an operator-visible
consequence on a qualified path, or a trust, privilege or durability rule is
not enforced. Medium: wrong or missing behavior with a workaround or on a
narrow or unqualified path; a spec that contradicts intentional code; a
safety-relevant clause with no test proving it. Low: naming, wording, output
detail, documentation drift, test gaps without behavioral consequence.

Kinds: defect (code contradicts the spec), gap (specified, untracked,
unimplemented), drift (code intentionally differs and the spec is stale),
unsafe (a safety or security consequence), test-gap (a contract clause with
no test proving it), doc-stale (a tracking record that is wrong), improvement
(no violation).

### Verification record

Scale of the run: about 1,640 agent runs over four workflow runs and two
reruns, about 105 million agent tokens, all on 2026-11-05. Register agents
(Haiku) 169; finder rounds (Opus) 103; verifier lenses (Sonnet, Sonnet,
Opus) 1,062; arbitrations (Fable) 41; completeness critics (Opus) 68; lane
writers (Sonnet, or Opus after a Sonnet refusal) 45; synthesis agents 74.

| Verification statistic | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate findings proposed | 354 |
| Verifier votes cast | 1,062 (one reproduce, one spec-reading and one refuter per candidate) |
| Votes of "not real" | 62: 7 from the reproduce lens, 22 from the spec-reading lens, 33 from the refuter |
| Split verdicts decided by the arbiter | 41 |
| Refuted candidates | 29, listed per lane under "Refuted candidates" |
| Confirmed | 313 after merging; 3 more confirmed but recorded as open work (B248, B412, B99) |
| Duplicates proposed by two independent passes | 9 groups, every one confirmed by a separate reviewer as closed by one fix; 52 related pairs kept separate |
| Tracked items re-judged | 16: 13 are drift or defects no record names (the cited record was the decision that moved the code), 3 stay tracked |
| Headline findings re-verified from scratch at high effort | 10 (every High and every unsafe): all real; MOI-04 raised Low to Medium; CEA-10 reclassified unsafe to drift; consequences narrowed in 8 entries, recorded in each entry's opening line |
| Citations checked against the baseline | 4,608 across the 36 lane reports: 219 line references repaired, 0 unresolvable, 8 sentences the cited lines did not support, corrected by hand |

Limits of the method. No command with effects ran and no host or cluster was
reached: no apply, destroy, controller install or uninstall, media, context,
machine, cluster, power or trust command, and no `ansible-playbook`. Every
judgment is from source, tests, goldens and effect-free probes; live
behavior of NetworkManager, RHSM, Satellite, Redfish firmware, cephadm, OLM
and the OpenShift agent installer is unverifiable here and the lane ledgers
count those clauses as unverifiable. Each lane's "Limits" paragraph names the
files and sections it did not read. Verification defaults to omission: a
lens that could not decide voted "not real", so a real discrepancy with
inconclusive evidence may be missing from the catalog, and the catalog
understates rather than overstates. Severity errs low by construction. The
clause registers were extracted mechanically and are incomplete by
construction; the finders read the whole spec range and the critics compared
the ledgers with the registers, but a clause neither pass examined is not
reported as met. The sibling reports of earlier audits were not re-read;
their open remediation items were treated as tracking records only.
